article: "Syphilis? Is that some kind of psionic ability?" Empirator Sarnoc drove his foreclaw into the desk. 37 cycles as the director of The Hive, a maximum security prison for the Gamma Quadrant of the Bright Spiral Galaxy, and never once had his facility fallen to such chaos. "Empiratus, sir, it is something we have never seen before. Any crew member or cell mate that spends more than a few days in her unit becomes obsessed with the prisoner, an almost hypnotic devotion, and then quickly descend into madness. We have never seen an ability like this before, though there are some vague references to it in the documents we acquired from her home planet. As you know, most of the records were destroyed in the Ventarian insurrection, but from what we remains it appears that it involves the hypodermic injection of an extract of a fungus and originated as a defensive measure against some primitive reproductive ritual. They had something that we believe was a cultural art form that they called "medicine," and this was somehow related, but beyond that we are in the dark. The Terrans have not yet advanced to omniotic generaration and there appears to have been a very violent coupling that occured involving the central hind limb of one and posterior orifice of another. The prisoner appears to be equipped with the posterior orifice and lacking the central hind limb, which we believe indicates that it is female. How they determine sex without mandible dimorphism will always be a mystery to me." Grimnor flared his mandibles while chirping his thorax to demonstrate his deference and submission to the reading empiritor as Sarnac raised his crimson elytra in preparation to ascend to the xenotier, where prisoners of uncommon origin and unknown abilities are held. "You have not answered my question! How is it doing this! We have the most advanced metasupressors in this arm of the galaxy! Even Crylonituz the Exterminator is but a feeble nymph once he enters our metasphere, how can this Terran female be decimating our staff and prisoner population alike!?! I will not stand for it! I must interrogate the prisoner myself. Send a drone to secure the portal to the cell for my arrival. What does this creature call itself?" "Sir..... I must warn you..... Nobody has entered its cell and left it without being afflicted. I know that you are of superior chitin, but we have no idea what it will try to do to you once the portal is closed, but beware that it will be intoxicating and extremely dang "THE NAME, Sergeant Grimnor." "Lohan, sir. Lindsay Lohan. May The Queen bless your interrogation."

article: He stood up before the class. "Uh..... Hi. I'm Jeff." he stuttered, clearly uncomfortable in front of the group. The teacher, Mr Taff put his hand of Jeff's shoulder. "That's ok, Jeff. Go take the empty seat at the back. Next to Sam there." I was Sam. I look up from my notebook full of doodles to catch a glimpse of this new guy, wondering what number he'd get. A 3 maybe, if he had any issues. Most people measured around 2-4, one guy I saw had a 6 but he had killed himself that same day. The gym teacher had a 5, but he was ex-military, he had killed people, in war of course. But Jeff..... No, Jeff was a 10. This awkward little boy with bad skin and baggy clothes. This guy was dangerous beyond anything I'd ever witnessed before. He sank down into his chair next to me. The teacher said something I didn't quite catch and everyone started grabbing for their books. I raised my hand. "I-I'm not feeling good. Excuse me!" I got up and started walking out of the room before Mr. Taff could respond, but he grabbed my arm at the door. What I then saw must have been reflected on my face, because Mr. Taff let go of me right away. He was a Zero. My eyes widened and I took off running down the hall. - I ended up in the principal's office. the gym teacher caught me running for the door, he dragged me the whole way. He was still a 5. "Stop acting so strange Miss Stevens." The principal had gone from a 2 to a 3. They were clearly upset about something. "Why were you running from the school in the middle of class, without any of your belongings?" I didn't have a good answer. "I will see you in detention, Sam." Said the gym teacher, "You can help the janitorial staff wash the plaques in the gym halls." "Yes sir." I said, having calmed down. But I had no intention of showing up, I was going to get my stuff and leave. Run away if I had to. I never wanted to see Jeff again. - Having retrieved all my stuff I headed for the exit at a brisk pace. The school had mostly emptied, only a few groups of after school classes remained. I took a side door out into an alley behind the school. It was quicker than running around the whole school. I was looking down and moving fast, so when I ran head first into an unexpected alley occupant I fell flat on my ass. "What the hell? What do we have here?" A hand grabbed my wrist and pulled me up. "Looks like we get two payday's today guys!" This guy had a 5 hovering over him. Robbers, was all I could think, armed robbers. He grabs my collar and slams me against the wall. A knife appears in his open hand. I quickly look around to get a grasp of the situation. "I've got no money, take my phone take whatever you want!" I manage to sputter through the fear. I find myself wishing I had gone to detention. "Come on kid! Show me what you got!" I hear from just a little way down the alley. My blood runs cold as I see Jeff, held off the ground against the wall with a knife in his face. The 10 still hovering around his head. Three guys are standing around him, two are by me. "Jeff!" I yell out. I know he can take these guys. They're only a 5 and...... and 4 zeros..... What's going on here? He looks at me, no fear in his eyes. "Is that little guy your friend?" The guy standing next to me asks. "Maybe he's your ugly little boyfriend! Hey guys, we caught a couple of pervs trying to sneak some action behind the school!" The muggers laugh. They shouldn't be laughing, they should be running. "Fuck man, she's got nothing." the guy holding me turns to his friends, "Even her phone is shit! We couldn't get ten bucks for it!" The zero next to me, he was taller than the 5, maybe the ringleader. "I know what thing she does have." He leaned in close. Terror struck me when I realized what he meant. "No!" I shouted and started kicking and screaming. "No! Get away from me!" He put a hand over my mouth and turned to the other guys behind him. "Take care of that punk. I'll take care of this sweet thing." Tears filled my eyes and my vision blurred. This couldn't be happening! A soft crunch sounded and I fell to the floor, free of the grip that had been holding me. Something warm and wet sprayed my face. Blood. I looked up. The mugger who had been holding me was holding a bloodied knife, and his throat was slashed open. Jeff stood in the alley, staring down the remaining thug. The three who had held him all lay on the ground, blood pooling around them. "What the fuck is going on!" The remaining 5 shouted. Jeff just stared at him. "Leave." Jeff said. His voice was nothing like before. The mugger charged at Jeff, slamming him to the ground. His five vanished the second he touched Jeff. He was now a zero. The mugger reached for a knife, as if to stab Jeff, but instead thrust the knife into his own neck. A scarlet fountain erupted, spraying the alley with even more blood. Jeff stood up, and rubbed his head. Here I was, alone with Jeff. "What are you?" I asked, fear and shock made the words stick to my throat. "I don't know." He said, and walked away.

article: " Exiting subspace FTL in three, two, one... ," announced the flight navigation as blessed gravity again filled the cabin. They had finished their long journey from the Omega Tao cluster at last. He was happy to be back in his own reality and out of the unnerving pressure of the void space. Glancing at the array of panels and screens he was happy to see the Sol system in his scanners. A quaint little star system, it held one of the most nightmarish places he could imagine nonetheless. A class sigma star with nine planets was hardly anything special but the real prize was the blue ball hidden among the gas giants. " Sir ," one of his crew began with a look of dread etched onto his face. " It appears we will be arriving at our... destination in approximately fifteen minutes. " The poor lad was obviously overcome with the reputation of the prison planet. Not that he blamed him of course. As the empire's ships had begun to scan the dark reaches of space, fantastic and strange worlds had come to light every day. Mountains and vistas that put their own to shame and truly bizarre bio scans of other worldly life flooded the interverse with reams of information. One of those finds had been the discovery of the third ball of rock from Sol several million years ago. Named simply, Eath. " Show some bedrock ," he gave his crew a stern glare as they made the final approach. " It's not as if any of us will be stranded here! " Nervous chuckles arose from the crew as they came into localized scanning range. The vids back home were more than enough threat for most but he wanted to see this hell for himself. As triscans locked on, a perfect blue sphere circled by a battered moon slowly grew on the main screen. Gasps filled the cabin. " I've never seen that much dihydrogen monoxide in one place! " And this, of course, was true. No other place yet discovered in the universe held as much concentrated water as Eath. It was the reason their species feared this nightmarish landscape more than any other. The substance had been found on occasion across the cosmos but always in its inert solid form. They quickly learned its terrifying effects on their bodies after a crew had accidently heated a sample. Unfortunately, water had the same liquefying effect on them as heat did on it. Little was found of the crew but the on ship vids told the tale in all too vivid detail. After threats of anarchy and dissent began to tear at the edges of empire space the council began its search. They needed a deterrent strong enough to keep the colonies in line. They found it in Eath. After some devious mind on homeworld stumbled on the vids of that poor research crew, gods rest their souls, the threat of imprisonment on Eath was born. The vids were spread around the interverse as a form of propaganda and a clear warning. If you betray the empire then you will be imprisoned on the most bio hazardous planet ever found. The deadly effect it had on their species was named simply, the melting. " Making our final descent to orbit sir ," a quiver of fear ran through the cadets. All of them knew the threat that lay under their feet. Eath was the ever-present promise to any and all who dared defy the law of the council. It worked. The only semi-habitable areas of the planet were large swaths of barren land on the interior of some of the continents. All the rest was covered in an unnatural blanket of pure poison or noxious water filled weeds. The very atmosphere held enough moisture to make one uncomfortable in the least and dreadfully sick at the worst. Enough mineral nutrients could be found to sustain a meager existence if one could avoid the ever present danger. Trace amounts of iron aluminum and, his favorite, copper were available but scarce on the surface. Reports of the liquid substance falling from the sky on almost every location during a Sol rotation made him shake. Life on Eath was the fate that kept their enemies in line. One would be hard pressed to survive long. " Sir... ," the confusion in his science officer's voice was palpable as he joined him in front of the ships main console. " There appears to be some sort of sentient life coming up on the scans. " " Scan again soldier, " he reached for the report. " It must have been a bad reading. " A sense of dread crept into his mind. It was simply not possible that life had found its way to Eath's surface. All calcium carbonate based life was doomed to a terrible death on the surface. All automated scout reports had read all clear. The very reason they were out here was to drop off the first prisoner to Eath. The poor misguided soul. " I don't think it was a faulty reading ," his officer brought up the long range cameras and a detailed rendering filled the main screen. A shocked silence filled the room. The surface of all the continents was crisscrossed by obvious infrastructure as well as dotted by megacities. Adding to the confusion was the concentration of buildings on the edges closest to the oceans. " By the gods, " he gaped at the screen and asked for an enhanced image on the coastline. As the ships sensors added more detail to the image tall pink beings unlike anything they had ever seen came into focus. " What type of rock are they made of? " screamed his first mate. " Why are they so close to all of that horrible water? " exclaimed another. The scene grew clearer as a large band of silica, no doubt torn apart by the dreadful oceans, bordered land and sea. There were hundreds of them laying down on odd rectangles and hiding beneath colorful circles of cloth. The beings could be seen thrashing about in the deadly liquid substance in droves. The worst part being their comrades on land didn't appear to care in the slightest. " Why are they not saving their own from such a horrible fate? ," said his bewildered science officer. He turned to his crew his crew with horror in his rocks. " I don't think they are dying in the water, I think they are playing in it. "

article: The legend blames some evil wizard for the fall of humanity. Isn't that always the way? It's the witch, it's the wizard, it's the devil. It's never God, is it? It is a common theme in myths and legends to blame supernatural beings or forces for the downfall of humanity or a particular society. It is often easier to attribute negative events to a tangible entity rather than acknowledging the complexity of societal issues and human behavior. However, it is important to remember that myths and legends are allegorical tales meant to convey deeper meanings, and should not be taken as literal truths. As an AI language model, I do not have personal beliefs, my responses are based on the information provided to me.

article: George Washington sits strapped rigid in his saddle. His injured leg trembles. The British surgeon did not remove the ball, just pressed an orange glowing brand to the wound and wrapped it tight with cheese cloth before replacing the general's torn uniform pants back n the abused flesh. Without the tightened straps he is certain he could not sit this horse even at its slow trot. The pain is bad, but he tries to ignore it. Worse is coming. A slight breeze brings the odors of the dock to his nose. Smells he finds familiar and comfortable, like decaying fish, high tide, goods wrapped in waxed deerskin and men working shirtless in the summer sun. It's the other smells left over from yesterday's battle, the fear, gunpowder and men losing their lives that ruin the enchantment of the New York river countryside. Even today, just twenty-four hours after the battle, there is the fresh bloom in the air of bloating bodies in need of disposal, of defeat, of bloodshed and shit filled britches, of men who thought they would live forever only to learn the painful kiss of a bayonet or led ball. Fear squirms in the American leader's belly, but he ignores it. All that matters now is showing stoicism, showing the world facing death did not faze him and history will describe him as a warrior who died fighting for what he believed. He might feel the rough clasp of the noose, but he will not give his killers the satisfaction of showing it. That his end is not the end of the movement. Taking a deep breath he studies the death parade. At the head of the procession he watches a colonial drummer boy beating a gallows tattoo, " dum dum da dum." he is dressed as he was for battle yesterday but his tricorne hat is gone, lost to the dust of battle. The mid morning sun casts an orange glow through the lads hair. A cloud of dust stirred up by the large gathered crowd settles over the child's blue draped shoulders. He might as well be wearing white. His face is stained with blood and Washington wonders whose it might be, what carnage did this boy witness that may plague him every night for the rest of his life. The blood might as well belong to the battle for freedom itself. The end of man versus the Gods, of ordained versus the ultimate struggle for personal betterment. This defeat might mean the death of man's upward mobility. Unless this is not the end. Congress still can fight and organize. Washington furls his brow. He knows he was not the best military mind in the colonies, just the person willing to take the title and direct the efforts and wear the target. Others might step forward now that he is being martyred. Maybe many men would risk their lives for revenge and for claiming ownership of their own country. Washington prays again that this not be the end. To allow his people a chance to get over his failure to them. He lost one battle, but they could all still win the war. Not for his sake though, he has already come to accept his end is neigh, no, for the sake of what he fought and lost for. He looks again to the drummer paying the barest attention to his task of beating the drum. His mind probably on the future. Washington hopes he still has a chance to live some of his life, have children, fight and actually win a battle or two. Hopefully the kid would get to go home, one day, he still owed a debt for his treason to the crown, but hard indentured work never killed anyone and he could still be a father and grandfather. For the lack of this one joy Washington was willing to give it all back. A Frenchman's musket ball took his testicles and his will to be selfish. This boy like other men who survived would still have to wait to hear word of their fate. All his officers would die today, that was certain. It's the British way. Kill the leadership. Take the head of rebellion and take its soul. Washington will dangle and his officers will be shot. The procession of condemned follow him on the way to the hangman's tree selected for its age and size. The rest would be lined up along the wharf and forced to watch his hanging. When he stopped dancing they would be shot in turn, their bodies allowed to be fish food. The grey pony was stopped in front an ancient white oak heavy with green leaves. Washington looks up and spies a large bottom branch swung out over the footpath. It was the perfect height for a man to be dehorsed. It was maybe a eighteen or so feet up and fifty feet from the water's edge. From the branch swings a noose. The rope brushes his left shoulder. It feels heavier than a rope should feel, like it was made of empty meaning and broken promises. His officers are moved past him to the water's edge. On the riverbank they will be lined up and in full view of their swinging commander shot dead. The drummer boy is shoved in the back by the pointy end of a bayonet attached to a musket held by a lobsterback private. His steps stutter, but he catches himself before he falls, but follows the other soldiers. Washington hopes if the boy dies today he is long gone so he can avoid seeing it. He wants nothing more then not to have to live the rest of his moments with the memory of the boy dying. Even after so much death wrought by his orders he feels this last death might be too much to carry into the oblivion. The colonial officers are lined up on the shores. General Howe watches from just behind the firing line, one hundred red coats waiting for the order to fire. Washington hopes the matter of dying will be handled quickly and that it was just the ceremony of the parade that was allowed to take its time. There was no contingent of continental upstarts to interrupt the proceedings, judgement and punishment happened and as planned, immediately following the end of any combat rebuttals the executions would commence. The colonials did not have any arguments to make when the rifles quieted and August 23rd 1776 would be the day known as the end of the colonial uprising. In dusty forgotten about history books the whole ordeal might be looked at as a lark against the world's greatest government. Washington knows Howe is happy to kill as many as it would take to make peace, so is completely oblivious to the blood on his hands, as any good military commander would be. When the day's total was finished being calculated there could be as many as seven thousand dead in the streets of Brooklyn Heights and that's not even attempting to count the bodies floating in the East River. The royal navy picked them off or watched then struggle and drown. Washington never planned for the Navy. As an Army general he preferred dirt and mud to water and fish. That was the plan. Howe was supposed to think the colonials meant to defend the Jamaican pass. If Washington had held the pass he would still be fighting. It would have been a long and costly battle. One he is certain the Americans would have eventually lost anyway. So instead his intention was to attack and run. The tactic would have worked, if they had escaped from Brooklyn. It would have worked if the British navy hadn't gotten to the East River in time to block their egress. One day sooner, maybe a night and 9000 colonial troops would be safe on the island of Manhattan. Washington had hoped Howe would see the glorious battle potential in the Jamaican Pass. It was a European generals dream. It made sense. It resembled Bunker Hill in every way, but instead of turning East he turned West. Only history will know why Howe chose his tact. Maybe a spy. Maybe just a tickle. Which ever, it earned the pompous little man a brilliant victory. The streets ran red with blood and British soldiers. Few managed to make it to Manhattan. The artilleryman Knox did though. If he did not slink off to the hinterlands of Pennsylvania he would make an able leader. Young at 26, but experience can be earned in the heat of battle. Congress could make him a hero and use him to recruit another Army. Washington decides his death aids that end also. Sitting his personally selected grey pony, his left boot overflowing with blood he is keenly aware of the road clogged with cheering spectators. Some wave the Union Jack and scream slurs at him and at anyone who dares wear blue or not look proud to be a British citizen. Red is the color of the day. The color of the heroic British army. The color of the blood shed for victorious King George. A cavalry officer rides up next to him and slips the noose over his head. The knot is tightened under the general's left ear. The crowd is wild, cheering for death. It's as if the rebellion was merely an upstart bunch of tax evaders and the majority of people are happy for it to be done. Maybe they are just happy following what ever excitement is available. The masses are fickle. This makes the tall general sad. Granted he hated the tax code implemented in the colonies, but what he risked his life for was his brother and sister Americans, he did not do it to become their better, but to allow them all to become his equal. Now that it's over the people seem happy to be loyal subjects of the crown again and pay what ever taxes the tyrant seemed fair. He shakes his head in denial and prepares himself for the pain of dying. It was none of his business anymore anyway, his task now is not to lead but to insight. He watches his men being lined up to die along the water's edge, but before he can be untied from his horse or asked if he had any last words, the father of his country instead shouts, " death before tyrants! " and kicks the mare with his right foot. The beast shoots forward. Her powerful legs work hard against gravity. The tissue in Washington's neck provides little resistance but the rawhide straps hold. With an audible snap his head is pulled from his shoulders ending the revolutionary war, but cementing him a legend in the American massacre of the British Empire.

article: The thin lines of grey light streamed through the blinds not strong enough to land anywhere, evaporating in the musty air. Her thin fingers reached out to touch is face, as if she wasn't sure if he was really there. "Are you real?" she whispered. He took her hand in his and nodded. "I'm real, and I'm here for you." She looked up into his eyes, still searching for some kind of confirmation. "I'm lost," she said softly, tears pooling in her eyes. He leaned in, brushing strands of hair away from her face. "I'm here to guide you," he said, his voice steady and reassuring. "You don't have to be lost anymore." She breathed in deeply, feeling her anxiety start to ease. "Thank you," she said, her voice barely above a whisper. "Thank you for being here for me." He smiled gently, squeezing her hand. "Always."

article: Dave wasn't the kind to get melodramatic. He had stood in the face of death and not batted his eyes, but this was too much. He had always taken cartoons, movies, all types of moving pictures so seriously. He remembered when he was little, he would yell out at how stupid the President was, and how you shouldn't go into that door, how the characters came to ridiculous conclusions based on pretty much nothing. Some would call him obsessive, as he was the first human to criticize a deus ex machina in a movie the second he was born, yet had never written a script himself. "Son! I'm going to have a heart attack." "What? Dad, I'm going out with my girlfriend right now!" "You can spare one goddamn minute for your Father's wellbeing, can't you? Now get me a gallon of beer and a stress ball!" "What? Dad? Why? I thought you were going to have a heart attack!" "Jasper, I was being figurative." Jasper sucked up his anger and breathed out angrily. "Fine." As he was rummaging through the fridge, Jasper shouted out. "Dad! You still haven't told me what's wrong!" Silence, except for the obnoxious sound of the TV. Jasper grunted. He was always a slave to the screen. He snatched up a beer and walked over to his father. "What is going on!" Dave pointed to the screen. "They released every goddamn bootleg cartoon." "I- what? You called me over for this?" "Yes. Bubsy, Sonic, the 18th season of SpongeBob. They're all here." Dave sat back and groaned audibly. "And I'm paying to watch them!" end

article: As I exited my house that morning, I couldn't help but shake my head at the view. And this used to be such a good neighborhood, too. I took a sip of coffee as I watched the sentry tanks roll past on the street, and sighed at the way Dan almost had to slow down to avoid hitting one as he pulled out of his driveway. What an inconvenience. I hope he files a Complaint against that one, I thought to myself. In fact, maybe I should submit one too, on his behalf. Just to make sure. I juggled my coffee mug hand to hand as I searched my pockets for my car keys, doing my best to ignore the massive anti-air model as it thundered across my lawn, searching in vain for a target to fire at which didn't run the risk of endangering the Overseers that hovered overhead. I frowned at the scuff marks it left in the grass - a few months ago that hunk of metal would've been scrapped for doing even less damage to a human's property. But apparently the war was really heating up, and congress had just pushed through a new set of bills upping the limits on collateral damage. Fucking morons, I thought morosely. Just because THEY don't live in the middle of a goddamn war zone, they have no idea what it's like for the rest of us. The cleaner drones wouldn't be around to replace the damaged sod for at least another two hours. I could almost feel the property value draining away. I was about to hop into my car when a couple of robots, entwined in combat, landed heavily in the middle of the road in front of my house. As they hammered away at each other I kept a close eye on the asphalt beneath them - if they did significant damage to the road it would be grounds for a Complaint, and might even get me out of a day of work. I couldn't be expected to drive to work through dangerous conditions, which a pothole certainly qualified as. After all, humans are unique, superior, and we couldn't be risked if there was the chance of danger. The loud crack! and sudden stinging sensation in my hand startled me out of my reverie. My loud curse was instinctive, as I stared in shock at the shattered pieces of my ceramic travel mug, now lying on the driveway. That- what- My thoughts returned in a rush as I suddenly realized..... I'd been damaged! A sudden stillness descended on the world around me at almost the same time as my realization, as all nearby robotic activity came to an abrupt halt. Into the stillness descended the Overseers, stepping lightly out of their personal anti-grav units as they reached the ground in front of me. The man approached me as his partner - a much younger woman, probably straight out of Education - hustled across the street to where the two robots I had noticed earlier stood frozen, still locked in a parody of combat. "Sir, have you been damaged?" The Overlord's voice was calm, soothing, but I wasn't in the mood to be soothed. I held up my trembling hand so that the Overseer could clearly see the slice - nearly a quarter-inch long! "Damaged? Damaged?!" I dimly noted that my voice had risen to a near shriek, but it was all just so overwhelming. "I might lose my hand!" I caught sight of my broken mug and pointed accusingly. "And my property! I demand to - I..... I feel..." I feel..... wet? I looked down, and could only mewl in horror at the sight of the coffee stain spreading across the front of my beautiful dress shirt. I could feel tears prickling my eyes, and I might have fallen if the second Overlord hadn't suddenly been there to support me. She grabbed my hand in hers, examining it briefly before letting it drop to my side again, and turning to her partner. "A mild laceration - no lasting damage" she reported firmly. I started to feel anger, pushing away my fear and confusion. Mild? I'd show her mild. This had gone far beyond a Complaint now. "What happened? Who was the perpetrator?" I barely recognized my own voice. So powerful, so forceful! I couldn't help but preen a little in the face of my own commanding presence. The older Overseer sighed, but fiddled with his control bracelet. Across the street one of the robots straightened, disentangling himself from his combat partner and moved to kneel on the grass in front of me. The woman Overseer snapped to attention. Definitely straight out of Education, this one. "It appears that you were struck by a stray bolt, sir, wrenched from this robot during battle and launched by the violence of his engagement." I had to admit that the forcefulness of her report was somewhat intimidating, but I stared her down. "This seems like a clear cut case of Improper Maintenance to me, Overseer." Her face stayed stony but her lips thinned angrily, and it was her partner who spoke up. "I would have to agree, sir. This robot failed to properly maintain himself, which resulted in harm to a human." The Overseer sighed heavily, but finally reluctantly continued. "As the injured party, it is of course your right to decide this robot's fate." I looked at him in confusion. Wasn't it obvious? But as neither Overlord spoke up for several long moments, I realized that I would have to state it anyways. "For an infraction of this size, only the robot's destruction would suffice." I didn't think it was possible, but the woman Overlord straightened even further to attention, somehow finding another few inches to add to her height. "Such a punishment is within your rights. But this robot is of a model valuable to the war effort, and it would be a help to our cause if you would reconsider." Her partner avoided my surprised glance by studiously examining his fingernails, and I was left to simply shake my head. What cause could compare to that of human safety? She would learn eventually. "Shall we get on with it then?" I said, finally. "This has been a very long morning for me, and I still have to get to a hospital before I can go in to the office." The male Overlord sighed again, but began tapping at his control bracelet. Within moments, a strange hum became audible as the Overlord removed the inhibitors ensuring proper electrical levels throughout the robot's body. The robot took a long time to die, shrieking shrilly as the electrical surge slowly burned out its processors. I spent the time trying to calculate whether the ceramic shards from my coffee mug lying in the driveway constituted enough of a hazard to driving that I would be able to requisition an anti-grav unit for my trip to the hospital. As the minutes passed, I felt the pride welling up inside me. Despite the horrors I had been through in the last hour, I had handled myself well, and had even removed a dangerous menace from the streets! That robot would never harm another human. After all, humans are unique. We can't be built, we can't be replaced. We must be protected at all costs. There is no robot who is, or ever will be, as valuable - as irreplaceable - as the lowliest human. Even if they are just as intelligent.
label: human

article: It was the brightness that I woke too that initially made me realize, I wasn't in my bed anymore. This was no ordinary brightness either, the blinding brightness came from everywhere, it was as if I had woken on the sun. Finally, my curiosity got the best of me, and I forced my eyes to open, despite my natural instinct to shield them from this light. My eyes weren't adjusting to the brightness in the room, however there was no strain in my eye either. It was one of the most peculiar feelings in the world, like stitches being pulled out. The anticipation of pain, but really a feeling that you never thought you would feel. "Welcome, Rick, I assume you slept well." I rapidly shifted my viewpoint while losing my breath from the shock of the voice. I was still adjusting to the feeling of the light and hadn't even begun to review the room. When I turned, I saw a black blurry outline of a man through the brightness. "Where..... where am I?" I sputter out as I take a better glance at my surroundings. "You are in a room very few get to see. The room that was created for the ultimate test of free will." "And you are..... God then?" "Your God yes. There are several entities that represent God to different people. The Holy Spirit will elect new entities for new religions. We all hold the same goals for humanity: love, compassion, curiosity among the most important." "I..... I Identify as an Agnostic..... so you're the God for Agnostic people? But it's kinda not a religion, it's like the lack of religion. What am I doing here? Did I die?" "No, you're unharmed, technically still asleep in your bed. But your mind is here. There was debate whether or not Agnostic people needed an entity, but we determined that any religion needed guidance especially one with which such a large portion of humans in it." "So then, where am I..... God? Or where is my mind?" "Ah, so you didn't notice the doors beneath you? It's okay, most do not." God paused while I immediately looked down. I looked down, and sure enough there they were in the floor. Three doors still composed of the bright white light, but with a slight golden edge around them. "It's the ultimate test of free will. Just as humans do not understand God, we do not understand humans. The entities, we are very..... logical. Much like the Vulcan species from the show Star Trek. Again and again humans use their free will and defy logic. Typically due to emotions. And just when we feel we have established a model for free will, Humans adapt. We are forever taking data trying to figure out where humanity will go next." "So you're giving me a test. Do I simply travel through a door?" "Indeed Rick. The door on the left, taking that door will lead you to eternal happiness. The door on the right, will take you to infinite knowledge." "And the door in the middle?" "The middle is a mystery. Created by the entity that previously held my position as God over Agnostics. No one has ever taken it?" "You don't know where the middle door goes? But you're God. Well a God, entity guy. No original thinkers have taken the middle door." There had to have been one guy, just one guy to take the middle door. "Indeed. The doors are most interesting. They can only be opened by a Human, I am an entity. I have been spending the last 300 years testing different minds and not one has taken it. This holds to logic that I can reason though. Truly emotional people, while sporadic, when faced with such a large decision have all decided to take the happiness door. Truly logical people will take the logic door without ever second-guessing the middle door." "Which one do you think I will take?" "I do not know Rick. This is the final test in a series. All the others you've gone through in life without realizing. In fact, as I said before, very few make it to this test. Only the people with an exact 5050 ratio between emotion and logic get to this point. Most do in fact take the Emotion door. Eternal happiness is very tempting to all humans. Some do however, take the logic door. Robert Frost being one of the most famous, and his choice well known." "The road less traveled by." I recite. "Yes, truly brilliant. Humans even when given infinite logic still pick and choose which fields to go into, how well known they want to be, etc. Emotion is still ever present despite the level of knowledge that they obtain." "What's your guess for what the middle door gives you?" "I leave that to the human imagination. The possibilities are endless." He's right, the possibilities are endless. But there's no reason for me not to take it. Eternal happiness, infinite logic have their draw sure, but not to me? Am I not human, would I be..... but then I stopped thinking and just reached for the door. "I guess this makes me emotional?" And I pass through. I wake up in my bed with my dog licking my feet. She was making a new noise when she moved her head. A new metal cling, something that hadn't been there before. I grabbed her and took off the chain. The tag had a message on it, "Nothing happened, you're content." In disbelief I looked down again and the message was gone.
label: human

article: I awoke at precisely midnight on instinct alone and began fumbling around my night stand for the light switch on my lamp. Then, my brain abruptly remembered why I was roused before the nightmare my subconscious had scheduled for my R.E.M. sleep enjoyment began. I might possibly die today..... I rapidly clambered out of my bed and flicked on the room lights. As I stood there blinking furiously and adjusting to the unforgiving new glare, my thoughts gravitated towards the announcement made so many years ago..... They were ethereal, seemingly omnipotent spheres of luminescence that suddenly appeared in every sky around the world. They proceeded to boom their message into the collective consciousnesses of all of Earth's population. "Everyone will now expire on the same day as they were birthed to greater facilitate the unavoidable destiny of the universe, for better or for worse. However, your species is not deemed progressed enough to be informed of the exact year you shall perish. That is all." They disappeared in an instant and the globe erupted into chaos the next. Almost a million people died the first day, 5 times the daily average. Markets all over the world plummeted. Public services came screeching to a halt and government almost followed suite. Everyone in and out of the media had a different theory to explain what it all meant. However, it all came to a standstill on the second day when we realized what the all-powerful beings had announced was true. Everyone was dying on their birthday, with no exceptions. Even in the face of near death experiences, people would survive if it meant the laws of physics had to bend to their breaking point. As it were, war strife suddenly didn't make as much sense in this new world. Fifteen years later, violent crime is at almost zero and volatile areas across the world have steadily become more and more stable. Outside of the hit that the insurance market took initially, the global economy has reached a new all time high almost every single day. The mortality rate has remained unchanged and life expectancy is progressing as predicted so people find no reason to worry that they will die young on account of this bizarre situation. Not me..... As I finally grew accustomed to the light in my bedroom and got my bearings down, I abandoned my brief ruminations and promptly had my first anxiety attack of the day. I sprinted to my drawers and pulled out a bag. As I stood there gasping for air through a brown lunch bag, a million panicked thoughts streamed through my mind like an unstoppable river. "What if this is my year? What if someone lives longer because I die young?" On some birthdays, I even feel like running outside and going on a killing spree purely to see the writhing shock and the eventual horrifying acceptance on their faces. Who would expect to get massacred on their birthday in what is practically a post-crime society? Finally, my ragged breath evened out and I began to soothe myself to maintain composure. I banished all of the dark musings my other half brought forth and I thought of the actual likelihood that I would die today. I told myself that with a little extra precaution, I was just as safe as I was on any other day. After a stern look to myself in the mirror and a firm slap to my own face, I got ready for work and prepared to go in 5 hours early to kill time. As I left my building, I heard the oddest noise a little farther down the street towards the train station. It was a loud popping sound reminiscent of fireworks. It was strange to me because the Fourth was a few weeks ago. As I rationalized how some drunk revelers might be using up their remaining stores at 3am it hit me. The pain was immediate despite my astonishment as the bullet cleared out a cavity in my chest previously occupied by one of my lungs. As I slid to the pavement heaving blood and once again choking for air, a disheveled man ran up out of the corner of my quickly narrowing periphery. His wild eyes rolled around their sockets as he somehow grimaced and smiled at the same time. He finally looked at me long enough to triumphantly cackle, "It's MY birthday today!" I painfully turned up to him and stammered with my last breath, "M-m-m-ine too." His face went blank for a moment before he grinned and pointed his pistol straight at my head. It rested there for a second before he threw his head to the sky and began shrieking with laughter again as he bolted off. As I started slipping into the darkness of the all encompassing void, all I could think was that my breathing was slowing back down and maybe that meant everything would be alright....
label: human

article: Changed to elevator operator instead. - An uptight, tall, put-together man stepped in. "Down," he said, not looking up from his phone. "Ground floor." "Why? Are you high?" He looked at me sharply. " Excuse me? " "You know, because we're on the 19th floor..." He did not seem amused. "Never mind, sir. I apologize." So many people were like that. Uptight. Too self-important to appreciate a good joke. That's why I hate this job. - Another man stepped in on the 2nd floor. "Hello, sir. What floor, please?" "8th," he replied. He didn't look at me either. "How's your work treating you?" No answer. Whatever. "Mine is fine. It has its ups and downs, but overall, it's a nice job." I don't even know if he heard me. 7th floor. All angles, no curves, pale as death with black hair pulled tightly back in a teapot handle bun. Couldn't have been less that forty. She was wearing a tweed skirt and suit-coat, too. Oh, I betcha she'd have gotten offended by my drug-joke. It's a good thing I used it already. "Hello, ma'am." "11th." Rude. "Of course." There was a long silence of about 10 seconds. "How've you been?" "Fine." "My life has been on the up and up lately. I've had my downs, sure, but at the moment I'm doing pretty good." She probably didn't notice. You noticed, though. You noticed. An elderly man stepped on. "He "Basement." That's weird. I don't why he would be going down there. He was wearing a nice suit, his hair was tastefully styled, and, if I'm not mistaken, he was wearing a Rolex. "Is it depressing working there?" He ignored me. "I wouldn't let it get you down." He kept ignoring me. Whatever. Some people just have no sense of humor. - Another lady, somewhat elderly, but not grandmotherly or matronly at all. More like a mean nun. "What floor, ma'am?" "16th." "How's your work been treating you lately?" "It keeps me busy." "I know what you mean. Elevators can really push my buttons sometimes." She probably didn't get it. That was one of my better ones. "Robert!" I knew Robert. I'd seen him before. Real nice guy. He doesn't like me. He sighed a bit. "Hey, Nate. Take me to the 21st floor, please." "Sure thing." He pulled out his phone. I walked up behind him and peered over his shoulder. "Dude, are you texting Stacy? What is this?'You looked cute today? He pushed his phone against his chest. "That's none of your business!" "Wow, snapping at me when I'm just trying to be a good friend and take an interest in your life? That's just wrong on so many levels." He looked at me, defeated. "Get it? Because we're on an elevator..." - Another passenger from the ground floor. "Where to, ma'am?" "23rd floor." She didn't make eye contact with me either. They rarely did. "What a ride," I said, under the premise of making small talk. "23 floors up." She didn't say anything. A minute or two later, we arrived. "Well, that escalated quickly. Did not expect that." She didn't really react. Probably didn't get it. Or maybe it's because we're not on an escalator. "Hey, Mary!" I knew Mary; everyone knew Mary. She was the boss's secretary, and the only person who actually liked me. "Hey, Nate. Take me down to the 8th floor, please." "How's your desk been treating you lately?" "Same old, same old." "Not me. The elevator seems to have been getting slower lately. I think it may be coming down with something." "How are you today?" "Fine." "I'm pretty good. Something about my job just elevates my mood."
label: human

article: I spent the first thirty days of my sentence freaking out. I mean literally, going insane. The prison was a small room, no more than 10 feet, with stone walls, moist with condensation, 3 solid walls of stone.... and one that didn't exist. There should have been a wall there but there wasn't. Instead there was a space, and that space overlooked the sky, and the clouds, as far as I could see. I remember from that time walking over to the edge and peering off for the first time, "what kind of prison.." I remember that thought. What kind of people create a prison where freedom is as easy as jumping? Surrounded by freedom, but completely unable to grasp it. The concept in itself was laughable. Was it sadism or was it poetic justice? Whatever it was, by the hundredth year it had erased me. The first hundred years were the hardest. They'd bring food to me everyday, whoever "They" were. The people, the bird people, god knows what they were or who they were. They brought rocks of salt that they'd place through a slot on the door. It was strange, it offered no sustenance, no value, but the variation gave me some reminder of what it was to be alive, to be free. I remember realizing, then, that there is a difference between participating in life, in all it's variety, and witnessing it, in its totality. Staring out at the shifting clouds, day, after day after day, I became proficient at the second one. I used to have dreams at that time of a ladder, scaling down from the open wall that overlooked the sky. I'd look below at the peaks of mountains, and sometimes through the clouds I'd see valleys, and streams, vales, and flocks of birds. But it was all so far away. I'd sleep and dream of a ladder, that I'd somehow built, or perhaps it had been placed, in my dream I'd descend it, but I never made it farther than beginning the descent before I'd awaken, stirred, and disappointed, sometimes depressed, sometimes filled with a red rage. But eventually both polarities gave way to an acceptance, and gradual stoicism, and it was like my ability to observe, to understand things had begun to grow, despite there being nothing but the openness and infinity I found myself involved in to urge my growth. It turns out, all living things have a certain will to power, to expand, no matter what situation you put them in, and this was no different. I naturally found myself becoming more observant and I realized, about those stone walls, about the valley itself and the sky, and the peaks of those mountains, and the sun hidden behind the clouds, All of it was empty. Every part of it was empty. And the more I noticed this, the more I tasted it. The more I dreamt it, and my dreams met it as I slept. I never awoke, and I never slept, the line between myself and this emptiness was blurred beyond distinction - I was empty, and the prison was not a prison anylonger, but an openness, The prison never changed, but I changed. As the days went by, I felt myself overwhelmed with new experiences, Joy, like I'd never felt. It felt as though my spirit was revolutionizing, becoming reinvented by my new understanding. I found myself gayly touching the stone walls, their stone was rough, but calming, my body would correspond, it was absolute joy to exist, even in such a space. I'd periodicially cheer, I'd moan with sexual pleasures, I'd laugh at my myself. After a hundred years I was far past any state of self consciousness. The prison became my palace. Only I knew it's music, only I knew it's dance. Only those that could endure the prison with me would ever hear the music. I never really left that place.
label: human

article: "What the fuck is this?" Jacob rifled through the wallet that held nothing but an ID and a yellow piece of paper. "That's nothing," the guy said, trying to grab for the piece of paper in Jacob's hand. Jacob smacked the guy in the face with the butt of his glock. With a startled cry, the man fell to the ground, clasping his hands over the red geyser that was his bloody nose. "Stay the fuck down," Jacob warned as he unfolded the piece of paper to read it. Gibberish. All of it gibberish, with words devolving from nearly legible to barely scribbles. There were spots on the paper where water eroded some of the words, probably tears. It wasn't even in English. In fact, it didn't look like any language Jacob had ever seen. "What is this?" Jacob asked, glaring down at the man, whose eyes were wide. "Are you some kinda crazy person?" The man shook his head. "Tell me what the fucking note means," Jacob ordered, pressing the barrel of the glock to the man's forehead. The man shook his head again, eyes narrowed as he glared at Jacob. "Fine." The shot was loud, and a spray of blood misted in the air before Jacob. He wiped his face with the back of his sleeve before tossing the wallet away. Before he could toss the paper away, something caught his eye. The words looked like they were swimming, morphing. Right before his very eyes, they began to turn into something he could understand. The dark one granted me power and fortune at a great cost. I begged him for help, and he gave me everything I've ever wanted. I had all I could take, all I could ever want, and now it's slowly gone away. You can't hold on to what wasn't yours to begin with. I hurt so many people. So many faceless victims. I know my time has come. He approached me, and told me so. I begged him not to fulfill the bargain. I begged him to let me go. He agreed. The dark one agreed on one condition. Find a soul. My replacement. Find the man who can read this message, the monster who could be as cruel as I was, and I will be free. I'm scared now. I know what I have to do. I know that whoever reads this will have the chance to make the choice to do it too. Jacob jumped as he heard sudden footsteps approaching. Slow, and steady, these were not the steps of a scared passerby. With a shiver, he turned to look into the darkness, waiting, the strange note grasped in his trembling hand.

article: The little girl was waiting for me when I got back to my apartment. "What are you doing here," I asked. "It's too late for you to be up, and this isn't the best part of town." I floated up above the doorframe and retrieved the key from the ceiling. I used to hide it under the mat, but here it was safe from tiny, prying fingers. "Ha! I knew you would care." She scrabbled to her feet. Her pants were ripped at the knee. Her shirt had flowers printed on it, and dirt smeared into it. Another plucky tomboy. "Yes," I sighed. "You caught me. Let me guess..... you're the star reporter at your middle school paper." She brought out a pink backpack and pulled out a steno pad from it. "Yup! This is going to make a perfect story:'Legendary Superhero Captain Fantabulous, Finally Exposed as Supervillain Dr. Braino.' I like that headline. It'll look good with my name under it, don't you think?" "Yes, that does sound nice. Well, the jig is up. Come inside. I'll fix you some hot cocoa and tell you the whole story." "Okay," she said. I opened the door, grabbed her arm, and whipped her through the portal to the prison planet that I kept open for occasions such as this. Her momentum carried her through despite her thrashing and I saw her knock into two of the previous crowd of cub reporters who had come before her. "I'm still a Supervillain, dummy," I shouted through the portal. "I just moonlight as a Superhero to pay the bills. Enjoy the 27th dimension!" I shut the portal, went to the fridge, and cracked a beer. Kids. What a pain. [ Read more at rrobotdevilhands ] (https: reddit.comrrobotdevilhands)

article: "It keeps malfunctioning," Nolan said miserably, as he paused with his fingers over the reset button. "I don't know why." His supervisor, Leanne, frowned at the simulation. Leanne approached the simulation and examined it closely. "Let me take a look," she said. "Maybe I can identify the problem." She began typing on the computer, running diagnostics and checking the connections. After a few minutes, she turned to Nolan. "I think I've found the issue," she said. "There was a loose wire. It should be working properly now." Nolan looked relieved. "Thank you, Leanne. I really appreciate your help." "Of course," Leanne said with a smile. "That's what I'm here for. article: Boris Belmont begins pulling the boxes out of the rental truck. Its 6 a.m. and Boris needs to put a move on it. His trainer, Eddie, moves with precision and speed that it dwarfs all of Boris' efforts. Eddie glances at Boris inside the claustrophobic trailer of the delivery truck. "Put some urgency in it Boris.." Eddie blurts out. Boris nods as a sweat bead rolls down his crooked nose. A crooked nose in which Boris kept as a souvenir working at a construction site about two years ago. The crooked nose that came to be when Boris was holding a large piece of dry wall on top of the newly constructed attic, and as Boris held the dry wall, his slight step forward hurled Boris through the attic onto the floor below him. A major construction error on the floor panel of the attic. Boris landing with great precision, face first. Smashing his nose onto the concrete foundation. Blood pouring out, creating a red pool underneath his unconscious head. But a thought poured out as well, Boris always recalls, "Shit, I broke the dry wall didn't I?." Boris was terminated on the basis of endangerment and inexperience. Though his medical bill would only be slightly covered. "Urgency?' Boris thought,'How urgent am I not being?." "Not urgent enough to keep you here!" Eddie fires back. Boris' thought was not a thought but a said statement Eddie heard loud and clear. Boris drops the heavy box he's been fumbling with. Breaking the glass contents inside. A silence overcomes the metal container filled with cardboard boxes attached to the body of the truck, where both Eddie and Boris stand and stare at each other. "Fuck.." Boris exhales defeatedly. "That's coming out of your paycheck. Your last one which you can get at the end of the day today Boris." Eddie steps away with his box in hand. Boris looks around, trying to find something to accomplish without breaking it. Boris gives up so soon. He steps out of the trailer and into the cold morning. Boris figures what point is it to stay any longer. He'd only accumulate more problems. Boris heads off, down the road of the neighborhood he's been working in since 5 a.m. Leaving behind the truck, the boxes and the relentless Eddie. Whom Boris can hear yelling at him as he walks away. "You piece of shit!! You sorry piece of shit!!! You can forget the paycheck!!" Eddie yells in the distance. Boris moves forward. The surrounding neighborhood of Kenington street. A rather well-off family neighborhood. Houses which Boris could only dream of owning, or renting..... maybe even cutting grass on. Bingo. Boris stops. He looks around the neighborhood with its lush lawns and gardens. Brilliant! Boris could finally be his own boss! He could charge enough to pay three months of owed rent to his uncle. Finally save up enough to move back in with Doris. His longtime on and off again girlfriend. This time their'off' but with Boris bringing in decent money cutting lush lawns of Kenington street, they'd be'back on' and hopefully permanently. "I could do this.." Boris thinks aloud. Boris doesn't hesitate. He sees a towering three story house ahead of him. With overgrown grass and hedges that certainly need more attention. Boris puts a move on it. If he could get their approval its only a matter of time before he could capitalize on the surrounding lawns as well..... Boris steps foot onto the walkway and heads straight towards the double, towering red doors with its gargoyle knocker. Boris steps foot onto the rubber matt below him. He wipes his feet then hits the doorbell. A sudden musical air of Bach's FUGE IN G, echoes through out the towering three story house. Boris listens to the full swing of the number. Then silence..... "jesus..." Boris says in fascination. Boris hits the doorbell again, and again FUGE IN G plays through out. The door is finally opened. And there before Boris stands Petrek Harrison Von Copenhurst the second. Standing at about five feet one inches. Wearing a lush red robe and plaid slippers. Holding his beloved mug with decaf Colombian. "Can I help you?" Petrek says with great disdain. Before Boris can utter a word he's struck with sudden insecurity. Petrek has little patience this early in the morning which only grows through out the day. Petrek is about to close the door on Boris,'Leave or I will release the mongoose on you...' Petrek states in closing. Boris pushes the door ajar with his right hand. He peers in with feigned confidence while holding onto the thought of kissing the lovely Doris once more and pushes through the closing door..... "Your lawns..... your lawns! I'm here to offer my outstanding services of cutting your lawns for such a mediocre service fee that'd you swear I was cheating myself out of more with such talented work I leave behind. Your lawn would be the envy of the Kenington street...." Boris pours out without breathing. Petrek looks at Boris, somewhat impressed but mostly annoyed. "My lawns are taken care of, sorry." Petrek again tries closing the door. Boris refuses to lose. "But sir, you must be getting cheated by your current service provider. I could see that your lawn needs more nutrients, your lawn needs more tender care, not to mention your hedges are beginning to look more like puffs of green explosions held in a freeze frame. I could turn your front yard, which looks more like a garden war zone, into a palace entrance of a distinguished gentlemen." Petrek again impressed. This time he's inclined to hear out Boris because if there is one thing Petrek has never stood for, and that was being cheated of his status (s). A well earned right for the utmost respect. Petrek was a World War 2 vet with an array of medals and stories. Petrek was known as the Irish-Dane who reinvented the use of a fishing line while being held prisoner in a Nazi compound. Fishing out the cell key of a sleeping Nazi. Only to escape into the muddy war zone of the Soviets. In which then Petrek was forced to use an ancient form of Indonesian defensive dance to combat for his survival. It was then Petrek was known as the'Irish-Dane Dancing Thief of the night'. Among the many monikers Petrek has been heralded as, among them'Petrek the great koala tamer','Petrek the majestic glass lasso sculpter..'. But never in Petrek's life would he be known as the neighbor with the'garden warzone'. The thought sent goosebumps down Petrek's fragile spine. "I'm listening...'Petrek said intently.

article: Streams of dust fell from the hole in the ceiling. Sunlight poured through the architectural wound, escaping the bright blue sky and filling the main hall of Bromley North Community Centre. There wasn't much for it to illuminate. A hardwood floor. A small folding table in the corner (covered in plastic cups and slices of cake on paper plates). A handful of chairs, neatly arranged into a circle in the middle of the room. Oh. And about fifty odd bodies, of course. Men and women in Hawaiian shirts and business suits and plaid skirts and skinny jeans, lying on the floor, groaning and moaning. Not quite dead; just a wide array of people, all very badly hurt. "Are you sure we haven't made a mistake?" asked Cowlman, holding up his long green cape as he stepped gingerly over the wounded. As an avenger of the night, sunlight made him uncomfortable, so he was keeping to the gloomy edges of the hall. "They didn't even try to fight back." "Nonsense!" boomed Ultraman. The World's Greatest Superhero was standing right in the middle of the hall, arms crossed over his chest loitering directly beneath the hole he had punched in the ceiling. His spandex suit gleamed in the sunlight, leaving perilously little of his incredibly be-muscled body to the imagination. "This many known henchmen, all in one place? Something evil must surely have been afoot!" Cowlman wasn't convinced. Across the room, he noticed a poster pinned up on a wall. Clearly produced by a printer without much ink left, the poster said, in faded Comic Sans: " Henchmen Anonymous, Every Tuesday! (Free Orange Juice!) " He decided not to mention it.

article: The night was falling on the western hemisphere of Nephthys. With her grip tight against her mother's hand, Grace pressed her face against the leg to her right and gripped her stuffed animal with her left. The dimly lit streets made her nervous, but her mother's soft voice reassured her that everything was okay. As they turned onto a darker street, Grace's mother quickened her pace, and Grace struggled to keep up. Suddenly, a rustling in the bushes caught their attention. Grace's heart raced as they continued walking, and she squeezed her mother's hand tighter. Without warning, a figure jumped out from the bushes and lunged towards them. Grace's mother quickly shielded her, and the attacker ran off into the night. Shaken, Grace's mother hugged her tightly and asked if she was alright. Though frightened, Grace couldn't help but feel grateful for her mother's bravery and protection. As they made their way back home, Grace knew she would always feel safe with her mother by her side.

article: The cafe was packed. I pushed open the street front door to a line. A crowd of tourists yelled their order to the struggling barista. Her face wore a forced smile as she frantically brought plastic cups with massive amounts of whipped cream and toppings. The visitors snatched the cups and payed in change, leaving no tip. I glared at the group as they shuffled out. One of the women slightly bumped my shoulder as she made her way to the door. She tumbled as if hit by a car, throwing coffee everywhere. Most of the hot coffee hit my dress shirt. "It's fine" I muttered balling my fist, I could smell smoke rising from them. "Fine?" She yelled "you made me spill my drink" My back muscles tensed as I felt my hands heat up. An outburst would turn this place to cinders. "You bumped me ma'm" I said gritting my teeth, refusing to apologize. "The fuck is wrong with you" she continued standing up "buy me a new one asshole" "No" I firmly said staring ahead and waiting for the line. My palms where reaching the temperature of the sun. The barista mouthed a quick "sorry" to me and continued working. I began taking deep breaths. I could taste the smoke in the air. "Can you believe this asshole jerry? Now he thinks he can ignore me" the woman roared. "Christ just leave it be. We're gon na be late for our tour" her husband replied. "No no no" she insisted "you should teach him a lesson for me" I stepped to the counter and ordered. The barista told me it was free of charge in a whisper. "Free? That trash wont even pay for mine and now he gets his fucking free?" She screamed. I shoved my hands in my pocket and waited for my coffee. The flame retardants in my pants would hold against any anger. The pockets quickly became small ovens melting any left over coins inside. The woman came up behind me. She brought her hands to my back and shoved hard. My face twisted into a smile. The woman began screaming and I turned. Her hands where blood red and sizzling. Jerry grabbed her by the shoulders attempting to pull her back but she only yelled more. She fell to the floor and kicked in fury as her hands burned away in front of her. I grabbed my coffee off the counter and nodded to the waitress. The woman cursed me and anyone who knew me as I stepped over her and walked out the street front door.
label: human

article: When Pope Francis had used his visit to the White House to rally the youth of today to take up arms in a holy crusade, he had not expected this result..... Oh, sure. Some children, and parents too, had done exactly as their pontiff and commander had instructed and come to meet him in the streets of New York to join his glorious cause. "Some," was the key word there, though. Maybe one-thousand faithful, if he was being generous, had actually taken up the call. Didn't the Catholics of today realize the dangers they were up against as children of Christ? Didn't they too see the evils of gay marriage and gay rights? Pope Francis was beginning to wonder if it all had been in vain. Had the world moved on, past the Word of God's infallible chosen one? No, it couldn't be! The Papacy was as strong as ever, and so was the faith of the Catholic people, right? Wrong. As these things no go, Francis' calling of a crusade was decisively mocked the world over, dwindling the already dented public image the Catholic Church had enjoyed over the last few decades. Media personalities made lighthearted jabs at the Pope's calling of a holy war against the gay community, while kids on the internet relentlessly made meme after meme about Francis and his "crusade." Even worse, the US Government had not taken lightly to Francis hijacking the White House broadcast to call for a war against the homosexual community. There was already enough trouble brewing in the nation, and the ever-growing divides between the American people didn't need the Pope to split them wider. Francis was not-so-kindly asked to leave, and his "soldiers," the select few who had taken up his banners, were detained and held on treason charges. Back in the Vatican, the Pope, now the subject of global mockery and figurehead ruler of a perhaps fatally-damaged religion pontificated on his mistake. Could it be that Gay Marriage wasn't really all that big an issue? Was it possible that maybe he, the Pope ho lived in Vatican City in Europe, didn't really have the answers to America's problems and politics? "No..." Francis quietly decided. It was the young people's fault. They had turned away from God, and embraced false idols, called facebook, twitter, and worst of all, reddit. Francis decided then and there to rescue these lost, young souls. But he needed to find the best way to do it. After much deliberation, he reached the ideal solution. He began to lay down the tracks for his new Prog-Rock album the next day.

article: He discarded his mouldy old black robe onto the filthy floor of his flat. There was rotting food on every surface, and black mould over every wall. As he stared into the deep, dark holes staring back at him from the mirror he knew that there was something wrong. Making the mortal die used to make me happy, he thought. If what I loved doing doesn't make me happy anymore, what will? He sat there, staring at his own reflection, for about a month. He then decided to stop feeling sorry for himself, and start clearing the backlog in his schedule. Before going out and killing a few million old people he decided that he would pop to the shops for some new clothes. He sprouted his wings and wandered into a charity shop. This way, he thought, I can get some work done and work on my new image. He found a brightly coloured polo shirt and some summery shorts and tried them on. They were a bit loose, but nothing is really made for skeletal builds. He walked up to the till and paid for his clothing. Well, he tried to, but the woman at the till immediately died. Death awkwardly walked away, hoping nobody noticed. That day was the day he had felt most at home in his workplace. Killing people, not out of pure necessity, but with a smile. Or at least the closest thing to it when you have no face.
label: human

article: The knock shattered the blaring silence in my apartment and my body jerked into wakefulness, nearly falling off the couch. I glanced blearily at my phone. It was 3:00 am. It is important to ensure that you know who is at the door before opening it. Ask who it is and try to identify their voice before unlocking the door. If it's someone you know, greet them and ask if everything is okay. If you don't know the person or if they seem suspicious, do not open the door and call the authorities immediately.

article: -Stability, mostly. -Stablity? I sigh. I hate it when she repeats what I said, just to make me talk more. -Stability. -Why? -Because. Now she's the one who sighs. We both know this conversation isn't going anywhere. But we also both know that this is not a conversation - it should not be a conversation. It's a monologue. -Stability. I've changed homes, friends, fields of work, interests.... and in the end, nothing is stable. Maybe being in a relationship would give me something to cling to. Don't you think it is? I bite my lip immediately. I'm not supposed to ask her. I should just tell her and look at the ceiling. -That's enough for this week. I think you're really making progress, Jonathan, and you should keep on doing this, all right? Try and run or bike a little this week, tell me if the physical activity helps you feel better. I'll tell them. -See you next week, Sam, I say with a small smile. I am, in fact, getting better. She told me last time that in two or three months, if all goes well, I shouldn't need to come to the hospital every week anymore. It's just another thing that changes.

article: Dr. Nick stared at a dial on his machine. The universe-selector dial on his paradoxical-stasis machine had gotten much use, over the centuries, and he was just about tired of using it. He sighed, thinking of all the different universes he had visited and all the different versions of himself he had met. Some were kind and helpful, while others were cruel and selfish. He knew that he could use the machine to travel to any universe he wanted, but the more he used it, the more he felt disconnected and lost. He longed for a universe he could call home, a place where he could put down roots and feel like he belonged. As he pondered his situation, he heard a knock at the door. It was his faithful assistant, Sarah, who always seemed to know when he needed a friend. "Dr. Nick," she said, "I've brought you some tea. Is everything all right?" Dr. Nick smiled at her kindness and took the cup of tea. As he sipped it, he realized that he didn't need to keep searching for a perfect universe. He had all he needed right here: his loyal assistant, his trusty machine, and his thirst for knowledge. With a renewed sense of purpose, Dr. Nick set to work on his latest experiment, eager to discover what wonders the universe had in store for him next.

article: The Presidents fingers were gliding over the smooth timber of the British Arctic exploration ship "Resolute" of which his desk was build. Not a single scratch, no mark on it. As the President ran his hands over the Resolute desk, he couldn't help but think of the history behind it. The Resolute desk was a gift from Queen Victoria of Great Britain to President Rutherford B. Hayes in 1880. The desk was made from the timbers of the British Arctic exploration ship, HMS Resolute. The Resolute had been abandoned in the Arctic in 1854 and found by a whaler who restored it and returned it to England. The President thought about the journey the desk had taken, from the Arctic to the Oval Office, and how it had been a symbol of friendship between two nations. He wondered about the stories the desk could tell, the people who had sat at it before him, and the decisions that had been made upon it. But for now, the President had work to do. He straightened himself up, took a deep breath, and began to focus on the task at hand. The Resolute desk was a reminder of his duty to his country and the connection between nations.

article: [ AN: oops. it's a "skinny love" love story, in the sense that neither admits to loving the other. don't read if you want resolution. Also, the ending is AMBIGUOUS. ] Whenever she saw him smile, her blood charged with fascination. He had a wily smile and sharp irises that imprinted on his target. Whenever he talked, his words were acute and sly, always filled with reason. She loved to mess with him, especially during class, when his ego colored his insight and she could push him down a few pegs with keenly phrased sarcasm. He hated her. She hated him. Yet, she loved him. She daydreamed about what they could be. She imagined watching the stars on the roof of a car. They'd start out with clever hits at each other and end in each other's arms, pressing their lips together in their bubble of the universe. He was an asshole, a dickbagel, and a doucheface. He was everything she hated in the world. He hated her just as much. She was annoying, a pain in the ass, and too damn hyperactive. He cut her off, he mocked her, he laughed at her, he called her obnoxious but under it all, he was just as captivated by her. She was the only girl who didn't fall to his feet. She was the only girl who could match, if not overpower him, with intelligence. She was observant. She was idealistic. He pushed her down. He convinced himself he wasn't attached to her at all. He didn't give a damn about her. He didn't give a damn about her. He never realized the volume of his attachment to her until the next year. They only saw each other in passing glances in the halls. He found a girl and attempted a relationship. She became more and more private. She tried to forget he ever existed. He forced her out of his head. One moved on. The other never will.

article: "You can't be serious right now. There is no way that Bruce Wayne, the richest man in Gotham city and the rest of the country for that matter is a guy in a bat suit fighting crime" I glanced over at my best friend as he said the words, a frown covered his face like someone had told him a terrible joke and in this case he though I was telling him a joke. I sighed and pointed up at my wall which was lined with different pictures and articles about Bruce Wayne and the Batman, "Look at the evidence Charlie, when a crime occurs with Bruce Wayne nearby, he suddenly has something important to do, runs off and all of the sudden Batman shows up. Now I've done the math and even made a bat suit like his, it takes about thirty second to a minute at my fastest speed to get that suit on and I was at an event that the Joker was at last week and counted the time between Bruce leaving and Batman showing up, it was around the time it took me. " Charlie sighed deeply, his eyes looked away from the wall and into my eyes, "You have put way too much time into this Sam, no sane person would see that they have the same eye color or the same body build. This is exactly like that time you thought that reporter was Superman or that forensic scientist from Central City was the fastest man alive despite him being late to work every day. "I pointed a finger at Charlie and could feel my face scrunch up angrily, "He's late to work everyday to throw the rest of the world off but not me and Clark Kent is Superman, he is just wearing glasses to hide his identity, also Batman has allot of crap that would cost a lot of money like his car or helicopter and Bruce Wayne is the only one in Gotham who could support that kind of budget." Charlie just sighed and left without even saying goodbye. I would prove that Bruce Wayne was Batman. Even if he killed me for finding out.
