article: Michael Controller and Geoffrey Remote were duking it out in the court room. A battle of wits, you ask? Why, of course. A battle over guilty vs. not guilty, a case of true legal proportions? Not so much! You see, Attorneys Controller and Remote were experts in their field. In fact, the famous closing argument scene in To Kill A Mockingbird was based on a closing argument that was originally given by Attorney Remote. And Attorney Controller is so persuasive when standing on the stage on which he was born to perform, that some people actually believe that he has the power of mind control (even a couple of jurors believe this!). These two attorneys among men, these gods among mortals, these whales amongst minnows, these two were sick and tired of boring court case after court case. They'd seen'em all! And won'em all, too! Once again pitted against each other as they had been so many times in the past, Remote and Controller came to an agreement. They would remain rivals in the courtroom. But rather than argue over a case of legal rights, they would instead try to get thrown out of the court. And not just told to leave, either. Literally thrown out. Think Jazz in Fresh Prince of Belair thrown out. The winner would receive a 100 gift card (bought by the loser, of course) to a pastry shop of his choice. And the game was afoot. - THE COURT CASE - ON A NICE, WARM, SUMMER DAY "Attorney Controller! Please stop dancing during Attorney Remote's opening statement!" The request came at the behest (enjoy that rhyme!) of the calm, yet swift Judge Baboon. This judge was so respected that when he entered the room, people wouldn't just rise in his honor, but they would sing The Hymn of the Baboon, as well. And in case you're not aware, The Hymn of the Baboon was a song created by the City Council in honor of Judge Baboon. Anyways, after Judge Baboon had finished his request, Attorney Controller gave his swift reply. "But Your Honor, sometimes you just got ta let your moves do the talkin'!" Judge Baboon looked down at Attorney Controller fiercely, eyes bulging and everything. Baboon knew how to look frightening when he needed to. Caught off guard, Attorney Controller quieted. "Now please, continue, Attorney Remote," requested Judge Baboon. Attorney Remote spoke up. "Ah yes, as I was saying before the prosecution interrupted me, my client is..." Suddenly, Attorney Remote stopped talking and started dancing! "What in heaven's name are you doing now?!" demanded an irritated Judge Baboon. "I'm letting my moves do the talking!" came the reply from a carefree Attorney Remote. "Aaaarrrgghhh!!!!! Order in the court!!!" Judge Baboon yelled while banging his gavel. Suddenly, Attorney Controller piped in! "Odor in the court?! I don't smell anything out of the odornary..." "Damn..." Attorney Remote thought to himself. "Controller really capitalized on my moves. Well he's got another thing coming to him..." Looking at Judge Baboon, Attorney Remote politely asked, "Your Honor, may I get my evidence?" "Why yes you may," replied Baboon. Finally, this court case was getting somewhere. Baboon was tiring from old age. His mind was still sharper than all of the world leaders combined, though. Can you imagine being that old and still having to live with a mind so sharp?! Baboon sure could. It was happening to him! But noticing a creeping coldness in the air, Judge Baboon snapped out of his thoughts. He had a court to run. Attorney Remote brought in a freezer. "Well this better be something pertinent," Baboon thought to himself. "Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, I give you Exhibit A!" announced Attorney Remote. Suddenly, Remote whipped open the freezer door, snatched up something inside it, and threw it at Attorney Controller. What was that something, you ask? A snowball, unbelievably! Attorney Remote had kept it saved up for months in case he ever needed to surprise someone with it on a nice, warm summer day. And today was that day! Attorney Controller was looking angry. "Your Honor..." Attorney Controller grumbled. "Gim me that gavel." "Why, Attorney Controller?" asked Judge Baboon. "Now listen here Baboon! I'mma take your gavel and throw it at Mr. Remote!" insinuated Attorney Controller. In the blink of an eye, Attorney Controller had grabbed the gavel and thrown it at Attorney Remote. But as if he had true cat-like reflexes, Attorney Remote dodged! "That's Attorney Remote to you, Controller," Attorney Remote claimed smugly. Judge Baboon was getting sick of this. He looked over to the defendant. The defendant gave Baboon an innocent shrug. "What in the name of The Law is going on here?" Judge Baboon wondered. Even with his sharp mind, he just couldn't completely figure out was his courtroom was currently being made a mockery of. But Baboon knew one thing for sure. He had to put a stop to it. ...

article: Death poked at the olives floating lazily in his martini, drifting slow circles through the drink. He imagined they felt much like he did right now, mostly useless, washed up and not doing much more than imagining what it might feel like to be an inanimate fruit, and with that full circle stream of thoughts he sighed and slumped lower in his barstool. His first day off and he'd ended up at a bar, a location with which he was very familiar (the shadier ones were hotspots for souls needing to be reaped), and he understood why they so frequently carried an atmosphere of heavy depression, hanging like a weight on their patrons' shoulders. Bars were depressing places for depressed people. He'd tried to call planet Xenor's reaper. Demise, her real name was, but a coworker told him that she insisted on being called Denise, which he thought was the most adorable thing he'd heard all decade. Unfortunately, their conversation had gone like this: "Hey, Denise." Muffled giggles. "Stop, stop it!" Shuffling noises. "Hello, who is this?" "It's Death." "Oh, hey, Death. Hold on a sec..." More laughing. "Could you stop, I'm on the phone! Hey, Death, sorry. What's up?" "Um..... are you busy today? It's my day off and I guess I was wondering if you wanted to..." "Death, I'm so sorry, I have to cut you off, I've got company and work is on the other line, I'm on call. I'll catch you later!" "Right, that's fine." But Denise had already hung up, and Death could've sworn he'd heard her shout, "I'll be there in a sec, babe!" before the line went dead. He'd wandered Earth's streets for a while after that, New York City, to be exact. Then he'd checked into a hotel and taken a nap. Now he was here. It felt like the epitome of a wasted day. Not that that surprised him; he was the reaper of souls, after all, a decidedly morbid job. It was fitting that even his days off would be lackluster at best, right? "Right." Death confirmed to himself, and then glanced around nervously as he realized that he was talking to himself. He wanted to order another drink, but he could hardly afford groceries as it was. Just as he was about to throw in the towel (literally, he had moved to toss down the cocktail napkin he'd been toying with), a petite looking thing slipped into the seat next to him. She was thin and pretty with long, incredibly pale blonde hair, so pale it almost appeared to be a glowing white, and skin that was oddly radiant. "I'll have whatever he just finished. And get him another!" She turned her big brown eyes towards Death with a lopsided smile. He absentmindedly dropped the cocktail napkin to the floor. The woman's features were quirky and not traditionally beautiful, but something about her automatically made Death feel simultaneously soothed and nervous to be in her presence. He also felt incredibly out of place sitting next to her, so clearly out of her league. "Uh. Hi. Do I know you?" Death spoke in his usual deadpan voice. He was already figuring out excuses to decline the drink she'd ordered for him and book it out of there before he had to fabricate an identity to this human. She was strangely ethereal, though, and something kept him there. For just a minute longer, he told himself. He'd see what she wanted. "Nope, but I know you. You're Death, right? Why aren't you reaping?" Death startled upon hearing his own name, too shocked to ask her how the hell she knew who he was. Well, at least she wasn't human, then, but he wasn't aware that another unearthly being was scheduled to be on Earth at this time. An Angel out of place, perhaps? "It's..... it's my uh, day off." Vick being the senior in age and superiority made the introductions. " Cadets Vick Bastion and Oracle Krass reporting as ordered, Grand Fleet Admiral. " Vick found it appropriate to use the most formal of titles for the host. Garret smiled. He enjoyed seeing the life in their eyes. Both were exquisite soldiers and leaders. Often, he saw them working together in the classroom and the field exercises. Is it Fate that they could work together, or the fact that they came from the same area? Garret Kane didn't care. Both had hailed from the homeworld of the human race, as did he. Different upbringings between the both. Vick was a juvenile delinquent in his youth but came out as a gentleman and a scholar in the end. Oracle was experienced in the academic field, but wasn't as street smart as Vick. Apparently, from what Garret understood, they were great friends before enlisting and often helped one another in many ways. Garret wondered if they had some form of a personal relationship. The way they spoke to one another brought the thought into his mind. They teased one another in such a way it was obvious they were a couple... Maybe they had tried a relationship at one point in time? Regardless, they were the best Garret Kane had seen. " Rest, Cadets. Please, have a seat. " The Admiral motioned for them to sit in the chairs in front of the desk. As always, Cadet Krass took the offered seat and Bastion stood. " Please, Bastion, have a seat. " " Vick, you know you're going to sit down, " Oracle chimed in looking up at her comrade. Reluctantly, Vick took the seat. She was right after all. He just preferred to stand until he needed to sit down. " You're both the most brilliant cadets I have ever seen walk through these halls, " the admiral started. " I have never seen anybody as genius as you two. I don't know if it's because of your combined minds or because of the fact that this is in your blood. Regardless, you're more than likely wondering why I have called you two down here. " He paused, waiting for some sort of confirmation. Oracle glanced at Vick. He was more suited to speaking to the top brass with his formal way of the silver tongue. " As a matter of fact, Admiral, we were. I assume that it is for recognition? " Another smile appeared on the old man's face. " Recognition? Possibly. " He took a deep breath. This would be his finest confession. Never would he admit it to anybody, but them. This situation deemed it so. " I'm getting too old for this, Cadets. My time for retirement has been long past, and it seems that I must do so. However, before I can officially sign my retirement and end my contract I must find a suitable successor to this... legacy. " Oracle and Vick looked at each other with side glances. They were both shocked at the news. " Sir, " Oracle said, " I don't understand what you're implying. " " Admiral, forgive me, but could you stop beating around the fucking bush? " Vick asked bluntly; not to Oracle's surprise. Garret grinned. He had chosen wisely with these two. " I'm recommending you both for a full commission and promotion. Both of you will be taking my place in the academy and - God help us - on the battlefield. I have literally taught you both everything I know, and both of you have passed with exemplary colors. Nobody has even come close to your scores since I've been teaching here. " He stopped there letting the news sink in to the two cadets. After a moment of silence Garret spoke again. " So, do you accept what I have to offer? " Another tense moment passed and in unison as if some form of telepathy was spoken between them they saluted the Admiral. " We accept, Sir! " Nodding, the admiral said: " Good. Good. Now, we have a lot of work to do before this all finally takes place. "

article: She wandered around her school, anxious, confused, depressed. Her glassy, lizard like green eyes darted around, looking at all the people passing by. As she continued to walk, she suddenly found herself outside in a small courtyard area. The sun was shining down, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. She took a deep breath and slowly began to calm down, her anxiety ebbing away. It was then that she noticed a small plant growing in a pot by the wall. The plant was wilting and drooping, in desperate need of water. Without thinking, she reached over and watered the plant with the bottle of water she had been carrying around all day. As she watched, the plant slowly began to perk up, the leaves lifting and turning green once again. A small smile crept onto her face as she realized she had helped something grow and thrive. article: "The stars flew past me like little cosmic pebbles as I helplessly careened through space, my escape pod destined to become my coffin. Unfortunately, it looks like no one can say for sure, although it's starting to look like I'm going to put the "terminal" in terminal velocity. In my little fugue, I think about how happy I am that I'm just going to crash into a small planet and die quickly, as opposed to suffocating or starving to death out in the blackness of space." The children gaze at me, all spiffed up in my brillant space suit, sitting in a cul-de-sac taken out of time, all in fascination as I let loose a loud sneeze. The human children, I might add, on this definitely alien planet. One of their mothers, having just diligently delivered some full cans of Coca-Cola (alien planet, remember) watches vigilantly for any sign of trouble, but they were certainly more trusting than I was expecting. At least, I certainly know my mom would never let strange men near their children. Little things like that, in addition to the architecture that I've seen, as well as the clothes, really give off an "early 60's" vibe. "Show us the trick again!" a little boy squeals. "Yeah!" pipe a few more. It makes me feel like a badass, anyway. I glance at a freckled boy who looks like a little bit like the bully from "Recess," and in my most authoritative voice, "Hey, chuck your can in the air!" As the can gains more height, I aim my glove at it and nail it directly with a laser beam, much to the awe of the children and shock of the mother. She grabs the arm of the Gelman look-a-like, and starts heading into what I presume is her house. Insulting, but I can understand. A grunt from behind alerts me to the presence of the police behind me. He tells me that "they've" arrived, whoever that means. I figured my best bet as soon as I landed in this suburban paradise was to contact law enforcement, maybe that could give me a way out, or something. It wasn't very difficult to find someone, considering I crashed into someone's fence. I figured being proactive, as opposed to waiting the decades it could potentially take for my people to come back here, would be a much better use of my time. A very slick looking car stops next to us, the back door opened by a rather dapper young woman. The passenger window rolled down slowly to reveal a man in his early 40's. "Please," he starts, a grin going across his face, "we've got quite the tour for you..."

article: An estate sale's a hell of a thing, cleaning out someone else's garbage and wondering, the whole time, whether any of it's worth a damn to them or to you. All a matter of preference, I guess, but this place, far as I could tell, didn't have a single thing worth preferring. Down in this fella's basement, ran into a stubborn old sheet of plywood stuck against the wall. "Nothing left behind," the client's worksheet had said, but this goddamned board wouldn't budge. Last bit of junk always ended up a pain in the ass. Why couldn't it have been a Rolex. Or a rare painting. Who am I kidding, though? God knows a dope like me wouldn't know good art if I painted the damned thing myself. Art curator could send me a letter, proclaiming perfection, and I'd still probably junk it. Had to go out to my truck and grab a crowbar to pry that wood board from the wall. Damn near bent the thing on my first tug, though. "Determined son-of-a-bitch," I said, my lips pursed as I pried at it again. "For the love of Christ," I yelled out, "get off the fucking wall!" I guess that final pull was a real good one, because just then, as I wailed out curses that would've made my daddy proud, the wood flung free and the lucky guy I am hit me smack dab in the forehead. I laid there, half-conscious, whispering angry little things to myself. Fucking estate sales. A Rolex. Just once, a Rolex, please, you sadistic gods of estate sales, just once give me that watch. Even if it's one of the cheaper ones, a used one, silver even, I'll never ask for another thing again. I noticed the crowbar next to me, lying there, bent right down the middle. Never seen wood do a thing like that. Matter of fact, I don't even remember pulling the board free. I guess a blow to the head'll do that to you. As I got up, right where the board used to be, I saw what looked like an elevator: two chrome doors, cut right down the middle, with a set of buttons on the side. Went up and tired the buttons. Nothing. No lights, no click, no ching. Weird. Looked like it might be some visual art, something you'd see at one of those contemporary art museums. You know, the ones with the upside down toilets and stuff. Maybe, I thought, this was like that. Thing is, behind those doors, through that little crack right down their center, I could see the slightest bit of light. Real feint. You could easily miss it. For a second, I thought that maybe it was coming from the outside, but then I remembered that I was in the basement. What a dope I was. Blow to the head'll do that to you. If that stupid crowbar hadn't bent so far, I'd use it to pry those doors open. Who knows, though. Maybe it would. I walked over and examined the thing. It looked like a crooked spoon at this point. There was no way I could get enough leverage with it to open the doors especially not these ones, heavy as they looked. "Ding!" The fucking shit? Behind me, just like that, with a ding, the doors opened. It was fully functional had lights and everything. At this point, I was thinking, "you know what, keep the damned Rolex." Too weird for me. But the thing is, it's a lot easier to say'no' to another roll at the craps table when you're back home sitting on the couch; when you're in Vegas, though, temptation, more often than not, says, "c'mon, lucky number seven!" That's why, God help me, I stayed the hell away from Vegas. I found myself in a remarkably similar situation, though. And while my gut said, "walk away," the gambler in me rolled the dice and walked inside. It was pretty nice in there swanky, even. Had these little designs, looked Greek, running along the edges of the mirrors. Red carpet, too. There were only two buttons: "UP and DOWN." And I figured since I'd already seen upstairs, why not take a look down below. "Oh..... well..... fuck it!" I said as I pressed the down button. I started smiling nervously. Almost a laugh, really the kind a meth head gets as he waits his turn, watching as his buddy lights up and gets off. A "hand-it-over" smile. Wait a minute..... What the fuck was I doing? The doors closed and I felt the elevator jerk. "Ohhh!" I screamed out, looking around for someone to share the fear with, but finding only my reflection in the mirror, terrified and smiling like a meth head. EDIT: Making some coffee. I'll work on it some more in a few.

article: "CAPTAIN!" The commander bellowed as was his usual. A man approached in full combat Kevlar and saluted, "Sir?" "We've done it, we've broken their backs. Sergeant slap nuts over there found the key to feeding the machines false information. Its an ancient form of communication called sarcasm," the commander explained. "Sir, I'm not familiar," the young man replied. A puzzled look passed over his face before the battle hardened captain wiped it off. "Neither had I, from what I understand you say the exact opposite of what you mean, but you say it like a whiny scum sucking weasel private would say it." The Captain held attention, "Perhaps a demonstration sir?" "I'd be happy to give you a demonstration numb nuts," the tangy sweet taste of sarcasm dripped from his words. The Captain waited for almost a half a minute before replying, "Sir?" "That was it Captain, I'm not actually happy I have to demonstrate it for you, but I did." "I think I understand, if I may sir?" The Captain prompted. "Give it a try son." "Sir you're nothing but a fat bloated whale's vagina, and you're the biggest asshole in this entire battalion. If not for our rationing of ammunition one of us would have killed you months ago." "Sergeant Slap Nuts, was that it?" The Commander turned to look at the man in the thick round glasses feverishly typing on an improvised keyboard. "For the last time Sir, my name is Sleven Nootz. Joe was nervous at first, but he knew he had to get what he needed. He decided to approach a friendly-looking person and ask for directions to the nearest store. The person directed him to a nearby market where he found all the supplies he needed. However, as he was about to leave, he realized he didn't have any money. Not knowing what to do, he explained his situation to the cashier. The cashier, moved by Joe's story, decided to give him the supplies free of charge. Joe was overwhelmed by this generous act and thanked the cashier profusely. As Joe made his way back to his home in the woods, he realized that despite living a simple life, there were kind people in the world willing to help him out. article: I was pacing all around my room. "I love that man" was all that I could think of over and over again for the last hour. His voice made me tremble and his gleaming smile infected me with pure joy. He was worse than nicotine. He was the type of drug that would kill me. I couldn't hold this any longer, I couldn't hide this anymore. I stared at the pill, it was taunting me. It laughed at me, pressuring me to ingest it. In that split second I said to myself, "fuck it," and I took it. I gulped. The moment of truth would come any minute, when the screeching doorbell would ring. What happened after this would determine everything. It was either a win or a fall. And it was then when I found myself standing in front of him. His physique impeccable. I opened my mouth to talk, but no words came out. It was as if something had obstructed my airway. I choked. He was waiting, waiting for my response. Last night I made a promise that earlier I had regretted, but now it was all my body wanted to do. "You said you would answer my question." He stated in a monotonous voice. "I did, didn't I?" I responded, stupidly. "Do you love me? "It was there, no running away from the truth anymore. My mouth spoke before my mind could analyze. Every word I poured out of my body was like I was spitting out water after being drowned. I was walking closer to him by the second. "I do, I have for the past three years and probably will fore the ones to come. I love you so much. I love your voice, and the way you say things with much confidence. I love the way you hold my hand gently and pet my hair. I love the way you kiss my nose and when you stare at my eyes as if we were the only two people in this universe. I love the way you tenderly grasp my head while kissing my lips. When I'm with you I can't even imagine anywhere I'd rather be. With you, I peak. You know every part of me and I know even the smallest freckle in your body. I can't imagine a world where I'm not with you, much worse, a world without you. It's nonsense. It's unreal, a nightmare. I love you, do you? Do you love me with the passion that I do?

article: "So..... you're a vampire. And I'm a vampire hunter." She sat primly on a boulder across him. "But you know, not all vampires are bloodthirsty monsters," he replied, raising an eyebrow at her defensive posture. "Yet, you feed on human blood," she countered, her grip on her stake tightening. He sighed deeply, "It's complicated. But know that I only take the blood of willing donors who understand the risks and benefits, and always in moderation. I have no desire to harm anyone." She studied him for a moment, taking in his calm demeanor and sincere words. Finally, she lowered her stake and relaxed her stance. "Alright. But if I ever find out you've hurt anyone, I'll be back," she warned before turning to leave. "Thank you for being understanding," he called after her, silently relieved that the encounter had gone smoothly. He knew it wasn't over, though. As a vampire, he would always be hunted, which was why he appreciated the occasional rare conversation like this.

article: I woke up at 6am for work, and it was hell getting out of bed. I only work three days a week, so the rest of the time I wake up much later. Here are some tips that might help you wake up easier in the morning: 1. Try to establish a regular sleep routine: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, including weekends. This can help regulate your body clock, making it easier to fall asleep and wake up naturally. 2. Avoid electronic devices before bedtime: The blue light emitted by electronic devices like phones and tablets can suppress the production of melatonin, a hormone that regulates sleep. Try to avoid using these devices for at least an hour before bedtime. 3. Practice good sleep hygiene: Make sure your sleep environment is conducive to sleeping. Keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet. 4. Use an alarm clock: Waking up at the same time every day can be difficult, so use an alarm clock to help you establish a regular sleep routine. You might also try a wake-up light or a gentle alarm clock that gradually wakes you up with light or sound. 5. Get moving: Exercise during the day can help you sleep at night and feel more alert in the morning. Even a short walk in the morning can help you wake up. 6. Avoid caffeine and alcohol before bed: Both caffeine and alcohol can disrupt your sleep. Try to avoid consuming these substances before bed, or limit your consumption to earlier in the day.

article: "Go. I'll hold them off." I could feel my life ebbing away from me around the hastily applied bandage. Daniel hesitated a moment, the shrieking of the alien horde drawing near. "No," I insisted, gritting my teeth in pain. "You need to go. Get to safety and call for help." Daniel looked torn, but eventually he gave in. "Alright," he said, turning and bolting down the corridor. I sighed in relief, knowing that at least one of us would make it out alive. I could hear the aliens getting closer now, their chittering language sending shivers down my spine. But I wasn't going to let them take me without a fight. I reached for my trusty blaster, praying that it still had some juice left in it. As the first alien burst into the room, I lifted my weapon and fired. The creature howled in pain, its body disintegrating into a cloud of acrid smoke. But there were too many of them, and my blaster was quickly running out of power. article: As Alia made her way through the crowded bookshelves of Gould's Emporium, she inhaled deeply, its particular musk calming her. It was the scent of old paperbacks, two for the dollar; the perfume of aged tomes with cracked leather binding, " one of a kind, " the equally aged proprietor would say. Old textbooks caused shelves to sag under the weight of their combined knowledge; biographies of people once famous now piled in the corner gathering dust. The shop was only small, though contained more books then Alia had ever seen in one place. The rows of shelves rose from the creaking floorboards to the chipped plaster ceiling, any natural light that made it through the grimy windows was quickly lost amongst the labyrinthine library. Rows of outdated incandescent lights hung from their wires, illuminating their small section of shelf. At the end of one of the rows, an old bookshelf, unlike the rest, stood. The light above flickered temperamentally, briefly illuminating the intricate woodwork of the odd shelf. Even in while lit, the wood was almost black, the figured carved into its sides too hard to distinguish in the dim light. On this bookshelf lay only one book - an unremarkable book by the standards of Gould's Emporium - leather bound, old parchment, no title on its cover. A single rune was embossed on the spine, though Alia didn't recognise it. As she approached the bookshelf and it's book, she felt a peculiar sense of unease, one she had never felt while in the walls of her beloved bookstore. She rebelled against the feeling, and curiosity drew her closer to the book. Her stack of books she had been looking at lay forgotten on another shelf as she picked up the strange book. It was heavier than it looked, the pages made of thick parchment. She opened it - a page had already been marked by the previous owner no doubt. The page was filled with handwritten passages in different languages: one was Latin, another Alia recognised as Greek, the rest remained a mystery to her. What struck her as even stranger was the object that had been used as a bookmark - it was a long, thin piece of metal marked with strange runes, like the one on the cover. The metal was so dark it was almost black and was shaped like a blade, though there was no clear indication as to which end was the hilt and which the blade. Studying the strange runes, she soon realised that a paragraph on the marked page was written entirely in the strange runes. Directly underneath, in Latin, was another paragraph, about the same length that Alia could only assume was a translation. She began to read aloud: " Qui vult vocare diaboli..... " She picked up the blade obscuring the rest of the line, accidently cutting herself on the cold razor. It seemed the blade was sharp along its entire edge. A single drop of blood fell onto the page as she continued reading. The lights along the entire row of shelves began flickering, the Alia's surroundings grew cold and dark. She looked up from the page, and realised she was not alone.

article: At last, it was complete. The painstaking work, the attention to detail..... While not a lifetime, way way too much time had been spent on this project of mine. The city of New York, in glorious detail. Thousands of tiny little trees, gallons of latex paint, millions of toothpicks, buckets of glue and newspaper for the papier-mache. And the lights! I lost count a long time ago. The streetlights, the building lights, and all timed for the correct time of day and everything. It was a beautiful sight to see it at night. Businesses would go on and off, home windows would illuminate and then be turned off as the imaginary residents went about their daynight cycle. I even put in a few lines of magnetic track to allow the buses, cars, carriages, and even those courier bikes to run about. It was a little much to ask that people move around, so I just put them about in static positions. There's a Waldo in there somewhere, and a Santa, and of course, the entertainer denizens who populated times square, all littered about the place as needed. There was even working water. Oh, not for plumbing or sewers, but any fountains? Yep. Ponds, running water? Yep, everything worked. The water surrounding Mahnattan did flow, to keep it fresh, a nice slow pace. And the ferries all worked too! Heck, I even had the tunnels. Everything I could think of. Everything I could make or acquire (or both!) It was all there, and current to today. I had at last put the final touch on the model. The spire of the Chrysler building. One would have thought the Empire State or the new WTC would have been the most challenging, but no, the Chrysler building's art deco top was indeed a long time in creating, but even it too was at last finished, and in place. I sighed. Contented. It was Done. But alas, it was nearing time. Not yet, but soon. I took a few flying shots with my gyro stabilized drone camera, to simulate flying through the city. Different angles, different approaches, different times of day. I took static pictures with my camera. Same thing. Different angles. I had, of course, documented the build itself, but this is different. It's one thing to see it being built, the magic behind the finished product..... but it's quite another to just stand there and take in the beauty of it all. When I'd done all I could to preserve the moment, the perfection that was my scale model..... I stared at it. A long time. So pretty. I really didn't..... "Now?" I turned to my sister, sadness in my eyes, but exasperated that she'd ruin the moment. "God, Jenny, will you hang on a moment?! This took forever to.." "Yeah, yeah, whatever, Jake. Dan's coming over, and I'm not waiting for you." I rolled my teenage eyes. "Fine." I set up the few video cameras in their positions. I didn't want to do this. But I had to. For Art knows no sympathy. And Jenny has her date with the loser. And Sparky, the reason for all this. I turned the cameras on. "Ok, let Sparky loose." The Massacre of New York took only seconds. Sparky, our Dachshund, tore into my masterpiece with the rabidness of a deranged lunatic, bent on destruction. The little smoke bombs, harmless and noiseless, went off in each building as the dog proceeded to dig and find the little morsels I'd hidden in them. Of course, he didn't need much direction, as he was trained, since I started this vision, to destroy Papier-mache things, and this was just his moment. After a minute, sated, he stood in the middle of what was once New York..... then sauntered off, satisfied that he'd done his job. "Wow. He tore that up pretty quick," remarked Jenny. "Seems like a waste of time, Jake, you ask me." I turned to her, smug in my overall satisfaction. "It's Art, Jenny. You wouldn't understand," I said with derision dripping from my words. She looked at me with daggers. "Whatever, Jake. For a 13 year old, you sure are a snot. Grow up." She turned away, going, I assumed, to swap spit with her newest boyfriend of the year. I didn't really care. I got what I needed. Now to the editing for my short. I thought to myself, I'm going to be the next Spielberg, or Abrams.....

article: When I was only seven, my father left. My mother used to tell me he went to save children in a third world country. After I turned fifteen, she figured I was old enough and finally admitted that he left her after an argument, went to the bar, and died on his way home. It was a sad story. But it wasn't the truth. I remember that night so vividly. How could I forget, when every dream is always a replay of what happened. He came home that night. He walked home from the bar so he wouldn't be hurt, leaving his keys on the table. I can only assume a drunk stole his car. There was too much damage to identify the body after the car exploded. As for my father, however, he came home. My bedroom was right next to the door, so when he knocked, I heard it, and let him in. "Where's your mother?" He asked me. I told him she fell asleep a while ago. He mumbled a frustrated response, then told me to go to bed. "But I'm scared," I replied. "I can't sleep until you scare the monsters away!" He never rolled his eyes at me, and never told me to stop imagining things. This night, like all others, he carried me to my room, tucked me into bed, and leaned down to tell the monsters to go away. But this night was different. As soon as he started to speak, I saw it. A skeletal hand, with nails long and dark, reached out and wrapped around his neck. He started to choke, flailing trying to escape. At seven years old, all I could do was scream. By time my mother got there, he was gone. I told her what happened, and she said it was just a bad dream. But there was no denying the headline the next day. In their defense, I wouldn't believe me either. Even the therapist my mother took me to almost convinced me it was a dream, and he would come home years later from Africa to see me again. One Friday night, when I was ten, I finally gathered the courage to find my father. I grabbed my stuffed teddy, my unicorn flashlight, and a chocolate bar I got at school earlier that day. I lay flat on the floor, staring into the abyss underneath my bed. "Don't be scared," I told myself. After an eternity, I finally shimmied under the bed. I wasn't prepared for what I saw. Hell would have been more pleasant than this. Monsters, demons, and creatures I didn't have a name for. But no father. Every night for a month I went back, hiding behind piles of bones and detached limbs. The world there was stained with blood. I watched every night as monsters pulled in new victims. I never found any of them again, but I could only assume the worst. I thought that was behind me when I moved to university. Until last night. My roommate was out with her boyfriend, so I was by myself. I heard a thump that was familiar. The sound of one of them coming out from under the bed. "Can I sleep up here? It's scary down there." His voice was so familiar, one I hadn't heard in years. I rolled over, and handed him my teddy. "I know," was all I could say before we fell asleep. I woke up this morning and he was gone. I hope he comes back tonight. I finally didn't dream of that night. The monsters were finally scared away.

It wasn't easy, but we fought for each other, even when it meant putting our own needs aside. And slowly but surely, we started to rebuild what was broken. We learned to communicate better, to trust each other more deeply, and to love each other more fully. And while we may still face challenges along the way, I know that we'll get through them together. Because that's what love is all about: never giving up on each other, no matter what obstacles come our way. That's the beauty of our love story - it's not perfect, but it's real. And at the end of the day, that's all that matters.

article: I cant do this. I cant do this. I cant do this. I cant do this. Help. HELP. No one is going to help me. I should just end it all. This is my own fault, I'm an idiot for even existing. They should have killed me. I'd rather be dead. I could just do it myself. No one left to care. Not even I care. I'm alone out here. Not even sure if my writings in the dark are straight on the lines of this tattered notebook. Its so cold and dark. No more tears left to shed. I hope I die tonight. I survived the night. Shouldn't that mean that I am the one that needs to care? What does anything even mean anymore? Why am I discarded like someones trash? The Dwelling could be in any direction. There's no point in even trying. The thick leaves make it cold. I want to freeze. It rained in the night, I was more cold than I'd ever been. I didn't want to move, but my body got up and did everything anyway. I found a hollow tree trunk and shoved it full of leaves. In the morning I was still alive so I guess that means something. Year 19, Day 363 I've come a long way from the scared little girl in the jungle. A long way from finding my first birds eggs to eat and tiny springs to drink from. I've searched high and low for The Dwelling. I never have found it once. Wherever they took me, it is remote. I've been thinking a lot about the coming days. In my past I cherished the idea of these final days, as this whole journal could detail. But now as it lingers very near, I don't want to return. If they come for me, I already know I will be wary of them. Perhaps I could hide and they would never find me, I have often thought, but by now they have the technology they desperately sought to find me anywhere. My punishment is no longer the banishment, but the return. Year 19 Day 364 Nothing much to do today. I thought too hard on what could be and what might be. My stomach is sick despite the full belly of iguana. It should be a good night, but the hair on my neck is standing up, I'm ready to run. Year 20 I WAS WRONG. I WAS WRONG. Forgive me.

article: Arceus was always a bit of a coot. As smart as he is, he was also considered insane. So when Marcos entered the lab after a month of vacation, and seeing his dead body, it did not surprise him in the slightest. "Please do not disturb, OR OTHERWISE TAMPER WITH my body! The experiment would be irrevocably ruined!" Marcos read the red ink aloud. He places the note back where he found it, even making sure it was tilted the same way, just a centimeter from the scientist's nose. Whatever Arceus does, keep your head down, and obey. This was the best advice given from the last scientist who worked under him. So Marcos went on his work as normal, before once again stepping over him to leave. "God dammit Arceus, couldn't you at least stuff yourself into a closet, instead of being right in front of the doorway?" He curses, making sure not to disturb even a finger of this limp body. He returns each day, for the next week, and Arceus is still as dead as ever. Is he even dead? Marcos would not even dare check for a pulse. He simply went on about his work, until he heard a scream. He had forgotten to close the door, and someone walked into the sight. "SHIT!" Marcos turns, tackling down one of the old scientist before he had a chance to dial 911. No one has the slightest idea of how demented Arceus actually is. "WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?" He wrings the phone out of the geezer's hands. "HE'S DEAD! L-LOOK AT HIM!" He stares up at the balding, middle aged man with eyes welling. "Listen to me! If it's Arceus' dream to be dead in a hallway. Who are we, to take it away?" Marcos pointed to the note. 'YeS! WhO hAs ThE rIgHt!?" Suddenly Arceus' body starts coughing up dust, making the poor old man run with fright. Once again, Marcos was not surprised. "I DID IT! SUCCESS!" He whoops, mumbling that he has to write the results down and publish it immediately. "Write down what? What is it you were doing?" Marcos had to ask, only for the doctor to pat his fellow scientist on the shoulder. "Marcos, Marcos! I never intended to hide it from you, I was just afraid it would not work is all. Now I know it does." He pulls out a rather large needle, filling it up with a strange fluid. He gently taps the bubbles to the stop, and pressing on the plunger to release it, along with a few drops of the liquid. "What was the one thing, that you wanted to do?" He sneers, this demented man is still in his early twenties, his youth and energy, as well as unsurpassed intelligence; this made the middle aged man envy him, but not once did he complain. And bringing up what he wanted to do? What a cruel joke! Everyone knew what he to ride a spaceship, and explore the universe; but he will not live long enough to see the technology- the needle was driven though Marco's neck. As he fell, he heard Arceus chiming out. "SEE YOU IN A MONTH, YOU ARE GOING TO EXPLORE THE COSMOS!" He cackles, picking up the do not disturb note, and putting it right next to Marcos' fallen body. "Happy birthday, old chap! You are the best co-worker that I could as for!" Arceus is crazy, the sort of crazy to test the elixir of immortality on himself.

article: "So you're the one," he said. His bald head reflected the impersonal fluorescent glare of the hospital lighting. I nodded. "That's me," I said. He smiled. It took effort, I could see that. The lines that aged him told a story as if his face was a page from a story that ended too soon. "And you have nothing to live for?" He asked, his breath escaping from his fading lungs; his voice incidental. I shook my head. "In honesty, I said, no. My story isn't the important one here. What about you? What do you live for?" "I want," he started. His frail voice descended into a racking coughing fit. "I want..." I offered him a glass of water and rubbed his back. "It's OK," I said. "I'm here." "I want to stop the White Genocide." "And I'm here to - wait, what?" He passed me the water back. "Those damn blacks," he said. "They're destroying the country. Someone has to stop them." I stayed very still, hoping that maybe - just maybe - his vision was based on movement. It turned out it wasn't. "The..... white genocide, you say?" "You've only got to turn on the TV," he said. "Go ahead. Turn it on. See the future that those fucking anti-white bastards have wrought upon us." Dutifully, I turned on the TV. It was a re-run of Full House. I looked over at him, hoping he'd have changed his mind by now. He waved a hand, aggressively. "Change the channel." I did. It was a Taylor Swift music video. "Again! stupidsonofabitch." I did. "What's this?" he asked. "Breaking Bad," I said. "It's good. You should..... should have..... watched it." He gestured at the screen. "Who's he? The darkie?" "I..." I said. "He's a drug dealer." He snapped his fingers. "Ah! Ha! See?" "Yeah," I told him. "But they kind of all are. It's probably not representative of whatever point you're trying to make." A coughing fit. "Forget the TV. You read the news?" "Of course," I said. He pointed a gnarled finger at me. "You've seen them, then?" I nodded. "I guess," I said. "I mean..... yeah. I've seen black people. On TV." He looked satisfied. "So you know what I'm talking about." "Not really," I said. "No." There was a moment of silence between us. It was uncomfortable, in that we were clearly at odds on this issue, but comfortable - in that he wasn't fucking talking any more. "So..." I said, eventually. "I think I'm going to go." "You've found something?" He asked. "Something to live for?" I caught myself shaking my head before I even said anything. "No," I said. "I'm just..... I'll try next door." He coughed, spluttered, raged! "Race traitor! Race traitor! You'll be sorry about this! I'll be back! You should know better. It's goddamn propaganda, filling your brain! You know who the good guy here is? You know who the good guy is?" I opened the door. "Here? In this case? Yeah, dude. I know. It's cancer."
label: human

article: I had driven past the decrepit, shitty building at least a thousand times since moving into the apartment complex it sat next to, constantly polluting the space in which I lived. I had always assumed it was abandoned, as the windows were boarded up and there was no sign of life inside. But one day, I noticed a small flicker of light coming from inside. Curiosity getting the better of me, I parked my car and approached the building. As I got closer, I could see that there was indeed someone inside, moving around with a flashlight. Fighting the urge to turn away and forget about what I had seen, I knocked on the door. After a few moments of silence, the door creaked open, revealing a man in his 50s with a wild beard and unkempt hair. "What do you want?" he growled. "I just wanted to make sure everything was okay," I replied, trying to sound as friendly as possible. "I've never seen anyone in here before." The man eyed me suspiciously for a moment, then shrugged. "I'm just fixing some stuff up," he said gruffly. "Nothing to worry about." I nodded, feeling relieved but still uneasy. "Well, if you need any help or anything, just let me know. I live right over there," I gestured towards my apartment complex. As I turned to leave, the man called after me. "Hey, kid... thanks." I smiled and waved, feeling like I had made a small difference in someone's day. From then on, I often left a friendly note or a plate of food by the building, just to let the man know that someone cared.

article: With a disgruntled sigh, Jack Evans collapsed into his 2007 Ford Mustang GT, completely blacked out from headlight to spoiler, which he had done so many times before, signifying the end of his shift at the San Francisco Daily Bulletin. Each day he would struggle to cope with the constant harassment and ridicule that he experienced almost habitually. Being the rookie journalist not only signified that he would be the butt of all jokes, but that he would be stepped on, as he never spoke up or defended himself. Everything had led up to the moment when he witnessed his boss welcome his fiance into his office, where they exchanged conversation, and ultimately handed her a key to his hotel. Jack, immediately pent up with anger stormed into his cubicle, a small, dusty corner in the otherwise large office. He was taking matters into his own hands. No longer would he be the butt of jokes at his office, being known simply as "Lonesome Jack." He was going to make a name for himself, and take down everybody who lacked belief in him; all those that had stepped on him. As he blinked out of his reflectance of the day's events, he started up the charcoal muscle car, and his headlights flickered into a bright white existence. He squinted through his windshield of a thousand tears, the usual rain pouring endlessly, as it had each night this winter. It seemed to reflect his mood, always gloomy and full of despair. His gaze paused at the bay that lay before him. He could just make out downtown San Francisco from here. That is where he would begin his hunt for vengeance. His coworkers, boss, ex girlfriends, parents, everybody, would feel his wrath and be forced to take him seriously from this moment on. As Jack cruised across the silent, melancholy streets of downtown, he watched as civilians, potential witnesses ran for cover under haunting facades of hotels, shops, restaurants, a reminder of the history that still lived in this city. He quickly came to the realization that he would need a weapon, but simply walking into a gun shop and buying a gun would be too suspicious. So he came to the conclusion that he would hunt for them as an animal would, simply with his bare hands. The growling engine of the Mustang fell to a silent conclusion as Jack stopped the car and opened his door slightly, as if to let the cold air into the furnace of hate that was contained in the cabin of his vehicle. He looked up at the cement tower that lay before him; "The Roosevelt." Specifically, the residence of his boss, the one who made him an exile at the office, who declined any attempt at him moving up in the business; the one who stole his fiance from under him. As he jogged into the Art Deco themed lobby of the hotel, he found the elevator opened, as if giving him an invitation to fulfill his prophecy. The numbers on the golden wall read "1..... 2..... 3..." all the way until it stopped at "25...." The doors creaked to an open position and he found himself alone, in complete silence upon the crimson carpet of the penthouse. Jack paced towards room 1990, the "President's Suite." To his surprise, the door lay open as well, a small crack of light escaped into the candle lit hallway. Taking this as further proof of his divine right of vengeance, Jack lust forward into the room, throwing the door open with ferocious might and made two large bounds right into the suite's master bedroom. As he thrust the two ancient oak doors of the room open, he witnessed his fiance holding a knife to his bosses throat, as well as three bags filled to the brim with unmarked bills, gold china, and other priceless objects near the window to the balcony and ultimately, the fire escape. In moments that seemed to live in complete slow motion, Jack analyzed each detail of the event as if he were the late Sherlock Holmes himself, tracking down precisely what was happening. As the two struggled in death's embrace, Jack jumped over the side of the immaculate drapes lining the bed and threw the woman to the ground, where she found herself soon swimming in a pool of crimson. The knife lay, 4 inches deep in her chest, where she had fallen. In complete shock, his fiance, whom he had nothing but anger up until now for, looked at him in the eyes and whispered "thank you" as she faded into an everlasting slumber. And in this moment, Jack realized, as he looked at the knife lying on the floor, the faint words "Phantom" etched on the hilt, that his fiance, who would often be gone late nights into the early morning hours was working for the mob, specifically the "Phantom Mob." This group of barbarians were feared throughout the entire bay area, and to his complete dismay, his own fiance was a member. In complete disgust he turned away. Jack's shoulders heaved up and down in animalistic spirit as he struggled to catch his breath. As he slowly looked up, fiery cauldrons of lava glowing in his eyes, he met gaze with his boss. The man lie complete fear, not even the slightest whimper escaping his pale white face His boss, who was nothing more than an angry man in a business suit had come to realize that his life had just been saved, as this woman's mission was to end his life, and take all that he had. And as Jack disappeared down the fire escape into the foggy San Francisco night, he came to the conclusion deep in his heart, that he would not kill for vengeance, but save those that had attempted to corrupt him from themselves.

article: Irradiated? Well that puts a spin on things..... And I thought the job went well..... "Well..... Fuck." Don sighed after he heard the news anchor. He stopped cleaning his favorite coffee mug and sat down at the kitchen table, staring at the TV screen. "I'm sorry to hear that, Don," I said sympathetically. "Is there anything I can do to help?" Don shook his head. "I don't know. I just need to process this. I can't believe I've been exposed to radiation. What does that even mean for my health?" I could see the worry etched on his face, and I wanted to ease his anxiety. "Maybe you could talk to a doctor or a specialist about this. They might be able to explain what the risks are and what steps you can take to protect yourself." Don nodded slowly, his mind racing with possibilities. "Yeah, you're right. I need to get some more information on this. Thanks for being there, I really appreciate it." "Of course, anytime," I replied with a smile. "Take care and let me know if there's anything else I can do to help."

article: And yet, the city remained. There used to be so much light. Driving down Broadway felt like flying through space, with each passing light another star in the galaxy. Everything was so vibrant and alive. But now, there was a dimness that had settled over the streets. The neon signs that once glowed bright were now flickering and dimming, their letters partially missing or scrambled. The buildings stood tall and stoic, but somehow hollow and empty. It was as if the city had lost its soul, and was merely a shell of its former self. People still went about their business, but there was a weariness to them, as if they were resigned to the city's decline. The hustle and bustle that once defined this place had been replaced by a quiet, eerie stillness. As a helpful assistant, I wondered what I could do to bring back the energy and vitality that once characterized this city. Maybe it was time to encourage community events and gatherings, or to initiate public art projects. We needed to find ways to ignite the spark that once set this city ablaze.

article: "The sun just flickered." "What?" "No seriously, it flickered." Of course, this was not something easily believed. The sun was..... the sun. It didn't flicker. It just gave light. An d yet, the person who noticed it was insistent. Perhaps it was just a trick of the eye, or maybe some kind of atmospheric anomaly. However, as news of the sun's flickering spread, scientists and researchers around the world began to take notice. They set up telescopes and instruments to monitor the sun's activity, and soon discovered that there was indeed something strange happening. The sun was experiencing a series of massive solar flares, bursts of energy that caused the sun to briefly dim and flicker. While this was a fascinating development for scientists, it also raised concerns for those on Earth. Solar flares can cause disruptions in communication and electrical systems, and even pose a threat to astronaut safety in space. As the sun continued to flicker for several days, people around the world watched with a mixture of awe and anxiety. It was a reminder of the immense power and unpredictability of the universe, and a chance for scientists to learn more about the mysteries of the sun.

article: "See, there are a thousand ways to be dead. Real dead, fake dead, undead." He chuckled mirthlessly at his own joke. Myra rolled her eyes. "In your scenario, though, thinking about fake dead, it's easier and harder than you think. Easier because all you need is a fat wad of cash and the right contacts which I am offering you and harder because," Mr Black paused to take a breath, lips pulled against his remaining teeth. "Because giving up everything from your old life is a real son of a bitch." "That'll be no problem for us," Josh replied. Myra loved his smooth voice. He could convince anyone of anything. He could sell the proverbial ice to eskimos. She nodded, hoping she didn't look too enthusiastic. Or desperate. Mr Black wasn't even looking at them, though. His gaze was fixed to the far wall of the KFC, at a cheap pastel print framed in brass. "Yep. Harder than you think." Myra glanced at Josh, feeling his impatience. "Look, Mr Black. We understand exactly what we're getting into here. We called you because we want to do this, not because we want to fuck around over shitty food. Can we dispense with the boring shit, and get on with the practicalities?" Mr Black's gaze returned to Josh's face, and he grinned suddenly. It didn't make him look any nicer. His eyes were set so deep in his head, Myra saw only a hard glint in shadowy sockets. Combined with the rotted stumps of the last three or four teeth in his mouth, she would have been happy to run out of there screaming. But Josh needed to do this, so she needed to, too. "This is what you need. You need to meet me tomorrow morning at the park bench on the Grove Street side of Fenster Park. There's a letterbox beside it, so you know which one. I'll pick you up in a Honda Odyssey. Bring nothing, except one hundred fifty thousand cash. When I say nothing, I mean nothing. Only the clothes you're walkin' in." Josh nodded as Mr Black spoke, taking it all in. He didn't flinch at the price. But he had expected it; his associate Kronfeld had warned him, had divvied up the proceeds in advance so Josh was prepared. Myra's breath hitched, but she kept as quiet and agreeable as she could. She didn't want to mess this up for them. "What will happen next?" Josh asked. "Passport, social security, drivers licenses all the ID you'll need to travel. My crew will take care of that. Then we take you south as far as we can. You'll end up in South America, but you won't know where until you get there. Once you're there, we're gone." Josh and Myra nodded. Myra felt butterflies flitting around in her stomach. It was a good thing she hadn't touched her chicken; she didn't think it would have stayed down. They needed this. Keep cool. They spent that evening at the movies, sitting near the back and whispering under the cover of the film's soundtrack. "What about my parents?" "What about them? Forget them! They'll figure you ran away. That's true." "I want to say goodbye." "No. No goodbyes." Myra slouched sulkily in her chair. She knew what would happen if she disobeyed Josh. She couldn't be left behind. She couldn't live without him. She'd already quit high school and spent every night out with Josh and his associates. They looked after her as well as her parents had. And school was pointless, anyway. Although maybe she should have taken Spanish classes. They stood together the next morning, Myra gripping Josh's arm tight enough to leave a red mark when she let go. He had a cheap suitcase in the other hand. It was full of neat piles of twenties, straight from the ATM. Kronfeld had set them aside from the last job, the one where Josh left his flashlight behind. A grey Odyssey pulled up down the street and Myra jerked on Josh's arm. "Is that it?" she hissed. He shook her off. "No. Shut up." They waited on the seat for another twenty minutes before a silver Odyssey came to a stop in front of them. The back door slid open and a hand waved impatiently. Josh pulled Myra in after him and closed the door. Mr Black sat in the passenger seat in front of them, stonefaced, and another man with a shaved head drove. Myra couldn't see his face, but his eyes in the rearview mirror were blank, staring straight ahead. "You ready?" Mr Black said to Josh. "Ready." He leaned back and fastened his seatbelt so Myra did too. Josh sat with one arm draped across the seat back, touching Myra's shoulder in what she figured was reassurance. Josh was so caring and protective. She loved him so much. "Let's do this, then." Mr Black gestured forward and the driver pulled away. Myra didn't pay attention to their surroundings she was imagining herself and Josh lying on beach towels somewhere in Brazil until she realised they were deep in the redwood forest. The road had gotten narrower, really only one lane wide. She guessed there was a cabin out here where they would get ready to go south. She was right. They pulled off the road when the woods were so thick there was no sun, only shadows. The van followed a bumpy dirt track for a mile or two, then stopped at last in front of a hunter's hut surrounded by the trunks of vast trees. They climbed out, Myra first, Josh close behind. The driver got out too and went to the trunk to get something. Myra was looking up at the treetops swaying, seeing the sun just hitting the tips of the conifers and slanting a little ways down, when she heard a popping sound. She hadn't even processed it when she felt the pain in her chest. She looked down and saw red on her t-shirt, and touched it. It was wet, and warm. She looked at Josh, standing beside her. He looked apologetic. "Josh?" "I'm sorry, babe. It wasn't going to work." She collapsed to the ground, feeling soft needles under her. Eyes open, she saw the driver standing over her with the gun pointed at her face. Before he shot her again, she heard Josh say, "You're right, Mr Black. It is harder than I thought."
label: human

article: "Finally, we have discovered the fountain of youth! At long last eternal youth is wait, what does that placard say?" "Whosoever drinks from this fountain shall be as they were from the beginning. So I guess we'll be babies if we drink it." "Well, let's take turns then, every thirty years one of us drinks, and then we raise each other. It's not what we thought, but we'll still live forever!" "Yeah, that's an idea, but first we can bash our heads a bit with these fist sized rocks, because that is what I would rather do than raise a baby every thirty years. We should bottle it, and sell it to rich people who can afford to hire themselves a nanny. Then we'll be rich and can hire nannies for ourselves." "Oh, yeah that's a much better plan. I really don't know where mine came from. I'm glad you have such a strong mind for business." "Besides, we both know I would drink first and then betray you when your turn came about." "You're kind of a bastard, aren't you?"

article: It all started when I was 100k in debt during my second year of medical school. You don't realize how demoralizing that is until you pass into six figures of debt. That was when I realized I had the skills and training needed through my classes to beat the snot out of all these punks in street fights. Not a single one of them could possibly tell the difference between the flexor pollicis longus and the flexor hallucis longus (Hint: one's in the hand the other's in the foot), much less know how to properly fight someone. Since starting to fight, I was now in the mid 50k of my debt, but there were more loans that were about to come in September. Why did I have to go to a private school as a middling member of the class without any scholarships? On top of that, I was just starting my third year, which meant gone were the days of sitting in lectures and having time at night to fight. Now I was starting to grapple with being in the hospital up to 16 hours a day, 6 days a week (yay for those 80 hour maximum workweeks) doing the impossible task of trying to look good to attendings, residents, and the entire medical community at the expense of the patients sometimes. Working so hard and then going to these street fights was really cutting in on the six hours of sleep I could physically get between being in the hospital, coming back from the hospital, and the human tasks of living (like showering). Somehow I had managed to work out a deal such that I could get to fights at least once a week, right before my one day off, but that meant that my debt was going to sure eke its way above the 100k mark again this year. That evening I was coming off an afternoon of getting mightily pimped about everything from the branches of the celiac artery to what sort of prophylaxis should be given after blood exposure of someone who is HIV positive, but it was about time for me to go back to something I truly enjoyed. Making the money that would keep me from feeling the insurmountable loans that were all around me. What I did not know was that I was coming against someone who knew more about the human body in a different way. I might have known what could go wrong and how to fix it. My opponent though knew how to make it all go wrong in the first place. Neither of us looked like much. We were both skinny twenty-something men that appeared to spend too much time on computers. I could see the extra pressure he was putting on his cervical vertebrae from poor posture. His SCM looked so overdeveloped my testing for CNXII might break my hand. On top of that, I could see him stretching out his hands before the fight began, and I bet he would have had a positive Tinel's Test and probably a Phalen's test that went positive at 30 seconds. We were both examining each other to the point where neither of us heard the bell to begin. Once that happened, both of us could not move for a few seconds, largely because we recognized each other. He had been in one of my classes in undergraduate as a TA. Which class was that? Oh, physics for non-physics majors. Shit! He came at me with a series of kicks that all seemed to go after knees, a weak point in my body in the first place, as well as fulcrum that sure could bring me to the ground. He was also coming from the side, trying to get at the " Terrible Triad " of the medial meniscus, MCL, and ACL all getting torn at once. That was all I could think about with these kicks while he was thinking about using the right amount of force to destabilize me. His punches came next, but I was just dodging them sporadically. I wanted to get him close enough to one of the wooden sides. That did happen, and he punched the wall so hard I could hear the bones breaking. A boxer with a boxer's fracture, that's something you don't see all that common. This fight was going nowhere, so it was time for me to finish this. So long as I knocked him out, I would win some of the money. That was when I remembered something about our lectures. He was deathly afraid of blood. I even remembered one incident during a lab. A sly smile came across my face as I got my nails ready to dig into his leg. I swiped enough to draw blood. As soon as my old TA saw his own blood, he had a syncopal episode. He just vasovagal-ed in front of my eyes. That is what happens when you pit a physics graduate student against a med student. Someone's going to faint, and it's not going to be me.
label: human

article: "I will live forever" I said to myself. I donned the helmet, God help me. It powered on. I felt pain. My neurons were being wiped out one by one. Please stop! article: "All those years?" I was crying. "I missed you so much. I hated everybody. I took out my loss for you on them. Now you come back. Finally." "Yes," she said firmly. "I promised I would always love you. I have fought everything to save the people I found myself amongst and when we made it they wanted to make me queen or something but I refused. article: 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marines; quantity force: 2 It was only the Squad's Automatic Rifleman and the Designated Marksman that were left. article: It's just the rain. It shouldn't be able to hurt James. James had been sitting in the rocking chair for about an hour. Instead he resigned himself to his grandfather's living room, content knowing he was safe. James'grandfather had passed away nearly a year ago, leaving James with the home and enough money to cover the homes expenses for a few years. Although the home was in his name now, it still belonged to his grandfather. Looking out into the street he watched a cat run up the sidewalk taking shelter on the porch. Running around outside playing with the animals The cats and dogs were faster than him even then but it never mattered to him. James had a way with animals, always able to bring them to him. Through treats, soft words, and patience James always had someone to pet or talk to. Although he couldn't keep the animals he could have them on the porch. On the porch, James would spend his days petting the strays that he befriended. Often times he would hear their stories of hunting for food or playing with their litter, but mostly smiled and enjoyed being pet. It's just the rain. James'eyes opened again. Nodding off in the rocker gets easier everyday. Getting out of the rocker had gotten harder. Its contours smooth and neat created a special sort of comfort that can only be found in oak. James however preferred a simple throw pillow under himself. It is still understandable. James felt at his age it didn't matter how perfect the chair would support him, the feeling of down feathers was plenty comfortable for his seat. Thinking back to his grandfather, James remembered the mountain of a man. Stronger than a man could possibly be even at his great size. Carrying what looked like a hundred pounds of wood he set them on the porch next to his rocker and prepped them for the fireplace. He would always pat James on the head and tell him he's a sweet boy. It's just the rain. James carefully stood up one hand on an arm of the chair, the other his cane. Thunder slammed against the windows and against James'shaken body. He considered his choices for the remainder of the day. While he thought about heading to bed early a second Blast of thunder caught him off guard enough he fell. The pain sent him back to the hospital. He remembered that first fateful afternoon. Sitting on the bench waiting for the doctor to return with the results of the blood work. It wasn't what he wanted. He wanted to go home and play with the animals. Instead he sat there as the doctor came in and revealed that James wouldn't be able to run even at his struggled pace much longer. Terminal, but not fatal. It's just the rain. To James it felt as though all the bones in his legs had gone on vacation. He crawled best he could to the phone. Pulling it by the cord he could hear over the pellets hitting the siding of the home the line was out. He inched his way with his arms to the front door. He slid down the step into the foyer and pulled the door back. Perhaps on the porch he could get attention from a neighbor. It's just the rain. Using everything in his arms James righted himself against the house and sat on the hardwood porch. He touched his legs and he knew it was bad. The sensation tore up his weakened legs through his hips and chest to his brain and James howled. The cat from across the way hopped onto the porch and wandered up to him. James coaxed the little cat into his lap. Wincing in pain James called out in his strongest voice for help. A woman takes her eyes off her shiny new cellphone. I turned to the first page of the book and saw that it had been inscribed with a message. "May this book bring you the peace and hope that you deserve. With love -A." Suddenly, I realized that "A" might not be a mysterious stranger after all. It could be someone who cared about me, someone who wanted to help me heal. With a renewed sense of purpose, I decided that I would use this gift as a catalyst for change in my life. I would read more, explore new worlds, and maybe one day, even write my own story. I'm here to lead you to the other side." He held a hand out, as though to assist me. As I tried to stand, I found I couldn't move more than a mere twitch in many direction. I pushed as hard as I could, but I couldn't get out of that shaky metal bed. "What's wrong with me?" I whispered to myself. "You'll soul is still trapped inside your body," he explained. "You must've been in here for a long time. Here, I'll help you out." He reached towards me, but he didn't exactly touch me. It was as though his fingers passed through mine, I was being pulled out of myself. The world felt so much lighter now, like I was floating. "There you go, feeling better?" I turned to him quickly. I nodded, unnerved. "Whenever your ready" he said, clasping his hands, waiting for me to lead the way. I took a half step forward, and turned back to him, "The other side" I inquired "what's it like?" He gave me a reassuring look, "It's peace, friend." article: Tom awoke uncomfortable in his chair. He had fallen asleep in his living room for the third time that week. Groggily he pulled himself up, but groaned and quickly hunched back down to avoid the morning sun. Three weeks since he moved out of that basement studio apartment and he still wasn't used to the sun. Another groan as Tom's neighbor revved up their lawn mower. Tom still hadn't introduced himself. He hadn't warmed up to the suburban idea of friendly neighbors yet, but he knew he would have to eventually. "It won't be so bad," he thought to himself. "Maybe I'll actually need a cup of sugar one of these days." Tom worked nights, another idea he hadn't fully warmed up to. It certainly paid well, and he still made it into the city on weekends to maintain a social life, but the backwards schedule was still an adjustment. And he needed better blinds if he was going to sleep during the day. "Just a year or two," he told his friends, "to pay off my student loans and get some good experience." They called him boring, but he didn't mind. He didn't have parents who could help him pay for school, and he knew what he had to do. "Maybe I am boring," he thought, "at least I won't be in debt." Tom was halfway to his bedroom when his doorbell rang. He hesitated, thinking he might just ignore it so he could get some more sleep. "I guess it's as good a time as ever to meet the neighbors," he grumbled to himself. He opened the door to an overly bright day, and before his eyes could adjust, he was greeted by one of the two large shapes standing in his doorway. "Hello-rrrrr vrrrrr-eet-rrrvvrrrrvrrr-present the-vrrrrrrrrrrrrvrrr..... " Tom couldn't really hear anything over his neighbor's mowing, but at least the shapes had settled into two well dressed men with name tags, carrying backpacks and aggressive smiles. " I'm sorry, what? " Shouted Tom. He knew the polite thing would be to invite them in, but he really was tired, and decided men with name tags and backpacks were not likely to leave quickly. " vrrrrrrrrr-om the chu-rrrrrrvrrrrrrr vrrrr-onder-rvrvrrr rr-epted Jesus into yo-rrrrvrrrrrrrr? " Tom could tell by their expressions that this was a question, and pretended he understood. " OK, what can I do to help? " Tom yelled over the mower. " Rrrrrvrrrvvvrr-looking for Jesu-rrrrrrvrvrrr vrr-urch of Jesus Ch-rrrvvv-o help us tr-vvrrvrrr..." At this point the man who hadn't been speaking handed Tom a pamphlet. It had a picture of a sunset with a halo, and Tom was more confused than ever. " Alright, so you're looking for Jesus..... because he's on the run? Am I in trouble here? " " No, no, no," shouted the first man, still smiling aggressively, " we're just here t-rrrrvrrrrrrr-ould like to a-rrvvvrvrrrvv vrrrvvrvvr rrvvv..." At this point Tom had given up, and just wanted to get some sleep. " Thanks, I'll keep a look out. Neighborhood watch and all..." he shouted as he closed the door. He felt a little bad, but they weren't exactly neighbors anyway. Tom dumped the pamphlet into the trash, and headed back through the living room to his bedroom. The house was much more cozy and comfortable without the direct sunlight, and the mower was just a soothing hum through the windows and walls. "Still five hours until work," he thought, and climbed into bed.
