article: A small blur caught the corner of Kate's eye. For a moment Kate was scared, but upon seeing the familiar orange fur she relaxed. And then she immediately felt weepy. It was only yesterday when Patches was euthanized. Her parents, to their rare credit, had been forthcoming and honest about the poor cat's condition. Kate's BFF had reminded her that Patches was in pain and this was the best. Parents and friends, in that rare collision of conformity, had prevailed and Kate had spent the better part of the night crying. But there she was. Patches, a not-so-aptly named kitty, was a striped orange and white cat that Kate had begged and pleaded for when it turned up inside the garage that had been left open overnight. The missing miter saw took a backstage as Kate's pleas had led to a new beginning for the kitty and the family, and for a few years, they had lived in blissful harmony. It was only a few short weeks ago that the vet had told them the news and, despite a positive prognosis, Patches had unexpectedly taken a turn for the worse. And when she turned up in the corner of Kate's bedroom Kate was speechless. Patches stared at her with yellow eyes, intent but not threatening. Kate's breath held in her throat. Patches blinked, turned her head, and began washing her neck while siting on her haunches. Kate hesitated, but then slowly pushed the covers from her bed and, ever so slowly, put her legs perpendicular to the bed. Ever so slowly, Kate moved in measured movements, not wanting to scare the kitty. It didn't make sense - Patches had never been skittish, yet Kate couldn't help but to be too cautious, if only to stave off another loss. Patches continued washing, oblivious to the grieving girl. Ever so slowly, Kate's feet met the carpet. As her feet hit the floor Patches froze. Kate and Patches stared at one another, as they had in years past, so many times in the living room. Cat and Kate were motionless. Eye to eye, Kate couldn't hold on anymore, and she began to cry. Patches continued to stare at her as her tears hit the dark wood floor. Kate was lost in herself, crying for her friend, her fried she knew but barely knew, a friend she would never see again. And then a paw, a lick, a knowing butt of a furry head against the side of her hand, and there was Patches. Kate's head lifted, and the yellow eyes stared back, longingly. And slowly, as Kate lay on the floor, she fell asleep, a furry ball of heavenly orange fur beside her. Joshua had sinned before. He had done bad, he had definitely made mistakes, and he had chosen pleasure over every sacrifice in his life. Yet, as he died, he wished that, just for once, he could make someone happy. He had done so bad, and, just this once, he wanted to do good. A shadow approached, Josh's head lifted, and someone had a plan.

article: The words scroll across my wrist, offering up the daily incremental adjustments that supposedly help advance society. Some people seem to be destined for greatness. My friend Joe has followed his adjustments and grown into one of the foremost cancer researchers on the planet, respected by the people and funded by seemingly everyone. My cousin was prompted who to meet at just the right time. Almost everyday she would meet someone significant and form a network of relationships which led to her becoming the first female mayor of what used to be known as London. She's coming up for re-election, and is practically a shoe in at this point. I sigh as I read the words scrolling across my wrist. I've never seen a tangible benefit for humanity in my actions. I remember the excitement when my wrist lit up with the name of my first girlfriend. I remember the confusion when both of our wrists lit up on the same day and told us to break up. That barely happens anymore, why would it when the AI knows what's best and can suggest solutions that fix everything? Especially when it advises both people..... My prompts have led to situations where I've crashed my car, skidding on black ice, to offending people and making them cry. I've questioned the prompts, and wanted to ignore them. It's hard to explain what it feels like to be the only screw up in a sanctified community, an evolving world. Once I woke up and glanced at my wrist to see the words "Trust me." It was exciting, unusual. But then it simply reminded me to get some food from the store. Since then, though, I've trusted the daily prompts - no matter how inane or counter-intuitive it's seemed. (And by counter-intuitive, I mean stupid and outright wrong - how on earth does going for a hike through the mountains to watch the stars help humanity? I was lucky not to die of hypothermia that time.) Today's words: "Just stay home." This has been happening more lately. At first it was great. Permission to not go to work? Heck yeah! Getting fired from work? Not so grand. The more it has told me to stay at home, the more I've done. I've redecorated; twice. I've watched all of the simunarratives that appeal to me. I've cleaned and tidied. I've withdrawn from the social consciousness gatherings. Overlapping experiences with another through the neural interfaces is one of the most amazing things I've ever done. But when you're a screw up like me..... it's uncomfortable to see just ho wonderful everyone else's lives are and, I sense, it's uncomfortable for them to experience my disappointments. I overlapped with Joe once, he quietly told me afterwards that he didn't understand what good I was doing before muttering something about guessing we should trust the AI. A couple of days later and he'd made a break through in development of a humanized monoclonal antibody directed against some protein in brain cancer. I felt oddly proud of him, at least he was making the world a better place. Just stay at home. Okay, I'll stay at home then. Let's do something different. Let's find that old-tech library. With one last glance down at that message scrolling on my wrist, I click in the box and start writing for rwritingprompts

article: He pulled her out of the creek. He wasn't sure how he did it, but he managed to pull her onto the pebbly shore. She was so heavy. Her lips were slightly blue in the afternoon sunlight. His chubby little hands tried to pat her face, but she wasn't moving. Her chest didn't seem to be moving up and down, but he wasn't really sure what he was supposed to look for anyhow. He started to sob. "Shhh, it's all right," The voice took him by surprise. "Wh..... who is it?" he said through blurry eyes. "Don't worry, I'm a friend." A fuzzy paw touched his cheek. It was a tiger. He stood on two legs, lean and fluffy, with a human-like quality to his feline face. "Who...?" the boy trailed off as the tiger came over to him and touched his older sister's chest, leaning down so that one ear rested over where the boy imagined her heart was. "Let's help her together," the tiger said, sticking his tongue out sideways through his teeth and winking at the boy, "It appears her heart is still beating, but we need to get the water out of her. Can you help me roll her to her side?" The boy sniffled and then helped the tiger roll his sister over a bit, propping her up against a small branch that had lodged itself into the sand. "Very good, hold her there," the tiger said, "Now I need you to stand back." The tiger stepped back twenty feet and crouched down in a way that made his spine look impossibly long, coiling like a spring. He wiggled back and forth for a few short moments before....CRASH! He barreled right into the back of the boy's sister and the force caused her to immediately cough and vomit up water to the side of her. The young boy's eyes brimmed with new tears, and he tried desperately to wipe them away so she wouldn't see how scared he had been. He ran to her, held her hair back and sobbed her name loudly as she coughed and retched on the bank. "Sis!" he cried, as her eyes opened and she began to move her arms and legs, feeling back to the side of her head where a large bump was beginning to swell. "Ugh," she moaned, but the color was coming back to her face, and she was able to get up, "Hey bro. I know mom said that I had to look after you, but it looks like you looked after me instead." That was when he realized something. The tiger! He whipped his head around, but he didn't see anything on the shore- just his sister and himself. It was totally deserted. After a few minutes of resting, his sister pulled herself up, still slightly shivering and they walked over to the log where they had placed all their stuff before swimming that afternoon. They gathered their things, and she made a call with her cell phone to their mother to be picked up. He poked along at the edge of the water, still within her sight, but still trying to process what had happened. 'Maybe it was just my imagination,' he thought to himself, poking at some moss with a stick. But then, as he walked around a waterlogged tree, he saw a tuft of orange sticking out. He pulled at it a bit and a soggy stuffed tiger came into view where it had been hidden in the hollow wet wood. He pulled it out and brought it to his sister who was calling to him with a voice still hoarse and grated from being recently sick. Their mother's car had just arrived at the roadway and she was honking the horn impatiently. "Look, Sis!" He called. "That thing is kind of.....gross," she replied, but she wasn't strong enough to argue. He wrapped the toy in a towel and they clambered into their mother's Subaru. His sister sat in the front and endured her mother's frantic fussing. They had to go to the local urgent care to be checked out for a concussion, but luckily, there wasn't any lasting damage. But as he sat in the waiting room, he heard a little growl to his right. "Say, this towel sure is nice," The tiger looked down at him, lankier than before with his soggy fur coat, "But do you possibly have some tuna available? A hero tiger such as myself needs proper nourishment." The boy grinned shyly and nodded, "And I'm sure a hero tiger such as yourself also enjoys defeating monsters under the bed and likes to sleep on a warm bed, right?" The tiger nodded, his eyes closing thoughtfully, "Such is the proper way to care for a tiger, you know." They shook hands. "I think this may just the beginning of a beautiful friendship," the boy replied, and the two of them looked through the comics section of the day old newspaper in the waiting room until his sister and mother came out and announced that tonight was impromptu pizza night. "I hope they have anchovies," he said from the back seat of the car. "Why? You don't even like anchovies," his sister said, irritation seeping into her voice. "They're not for me," he said pointing at the stuffed tiger sticking out of the towel next to him, "They're for him. After all, he's earned them."

article: Caroline's eyes slowly opened to a new day. Sun rays flickered through the curtains of her bedroom window casting doubt on another dark day of remembrance. She pulled herself out of the bed and struggled to gather her thoughts as the doorbell downstairs rang. Mr. Tolk delivered the mail every day to 331 Sunnyvale Drive for twenty years. He was never late and today would be no different. A woman came to the door who had clearly been up all night crying. Her pupils dilated through bloodshot eyes as the morning sun cast his shadow over her as if intentionally blotting out the light. "Good morning Miss. Debby, I have a delivery for you." Mr. Tolk handed over several small boxes to Caroline and withdrew a tablet for her signature. Caroline signed for the packages and brought them back into the house. Her first thought was absentminded as she discarded the packages on a small table in the foyer and wandered back to bed. Six hours later, sirens pierced the peaceful absence of her dream state awakening Caroline into a world of chaos and confusion. Latoya Mendez was screaming and crying at a police officer in the kitchen of the Debby residence. Detective Fantino was called over to help calm her down. "Just tell us what you saw Mrs Mendez. Slowly this time." said Fantino. "Miss Debby has been so depressed for the last year that the mail piles up. I decided to help sort her packages for her and found four boxes with...." her voice broke into uncontrollable sobbing as Caroline Debby was led away in cuffs to a police car. The steel surface of the interview table was cold to the touch. It was an unnerving chill that reverberated through her bones as Caroline sat waiting for the footsteps outside to stop at her door. Muffled voices in the hall could be heard arguing moments before the door swung open. "What are we doing here, Caroline!" Fantino lamented. "This is not the first time we've been forced to bring you in. Do you even remember what you did this time?" "I have been asleep for every hour of nearly every day for the last week. This is the one year anniversary..... I just want my son back. What am I being accused of this time?" said Caroline as she adjusted the braces of her cuffs uncomfortably. "You have body parts in your house Miss Debby. Detectives are going over the evidence but it does not look good for you. Look, anything you can say to help the states attorney and find closure will only help your case Caroline. Do you have something that you want to confess?" Fantino stared down at Caroline as if trying to piece together her mock composure. "I did not kill my son before. I did not kill my son now!" Caroline said angrily as she glared up at the detective. In Maville, criminal investigations are a long drawn out process that can take years unless a detective can convince a criminal that it is within their best interests to confess, usually for a shorter sentence. Hugh Hills works in the study of DNA a new cutting edge scientific breakthrough that can identify any person, their relatives and relations with just a single drop of blood. The phone rings in the lab..... "The Hills have Ayes, how may I see for you." Hugh said as he answered the call. "I am calling to get your report on the Debby murders. article: The flood of perfect white raging outside forced my windowpane-like eyes shut every time I tried to open them. The bleaching luminance however did have a warm embrace; it settled over my shaking cold face like graceful feathers poured from a sun-baked pillow. My breathing floated and settled like dew within my deathly lit bowl. All of the scratching, tapping, creaking and thumping objects from before the countdown seemed to have been wrapped in soundproof wool. The only discernible sound from the overwhelming white noise was the scratch of the atmosphere stabbing at any thing resembling a crack. I guess it was trying to be the first to execute my unforgiving sentence. The usually lively ecosystem of species spread through my limbs seemed to suffer some slight dismay with my penalty. I felt scattered tingles as most of them burrowed, scuffled or shook back into the small retreats and cracks. My body was giving up already..... and I've barely left orbit. As things quieted down I started to smell the blood on the dirt of Mars - oh the irony of the starry dream I had in my time with toy trains, cotton candy, dirt and drunkenly formed fatherly discipline.

article: A city, its mountains. The office towers lighting up in the evening haze and the smeary pale of a cloudless sunset. The tiny headlights of cars with sweaty passengers unseen, idling in traffic, smelling the hot food cooking in restaurants. The world shifts as the woman behind the camera adjusts her footing, muttering in English to her boyfriend. A light like the sun over the horizon, there and then gone. Silence, but for the wind in the trees. She asks what that was. The clean, shaved, washed, waxed people in suits at desks read facts and information like sports commentary. They narrate animations with moving arrows and lines like football plays. They report on characters and captains. They discuss. They debate. They nod solemnly. The light flashes in the sky and fades but the afterglow remains. They update, they check-in, they go-live, they re-Tweet. Wounded civilians scream and coddle loved ones, rewind. Look right here: loved ones die. Rewind. The light like the sun. Stay tuned. A city, its mountains. The office buildings lighting up in evening haze. Tiny headlights and unseen drivers thinking about food. A mutter in the sunset. A light and its afterglow. The wind in the trees. The troops are bad cameramen. They laugh or they scream or they joke nervously. Trucks and tanks and armoured vehicles on tall tires carry them down empty roads where sometimes cars have been abandoned or craters from bad arty shots force detours. The videos capture the sounds of war. Pops and crackles of overhead bullets. The shake and snapping of stalks and branches. Rivers idling over rounded stones. The scritchety clatter of the camera tumbling after bomb concussion shreds the canopies and dust swirls in mottled sunlight. Winged insects flashing momentarily in their arcs. A city, its mountains. Buildings, drivers. Sunset. A light. People speak in hushed tones. Somewhere, over the horizon on the other side of the world, everything has changed. There are no videos of the darkness that came afterward. A light like the sun. A motorcyclist pulls over to the side of the road in the clear, humid evening and reaches down to turn the petcock to OFF before quieting the motor. She's out in the country, flat fields of corn and wheat on either side of the old road. Above her the stars are out and bright in the sky. One of them, brighter than the rest, moves slowly toward the Earth's penumbra. The rider flips up her visor and sits back, hands behind her on the seat, watching the little light move, thinking of the people inside looking back. When those astronauts look down at Seoul, what do they see? The light fades and she is left alone. She listens and hears only crickets and a soft waxy rustle of a breeze in the corn. No guns, no artillery. No marching. No wet gasps from ruined faces. She shifts and works a hand into her pocket, pulling out a phone made in South Korea. She wonders if the people who screwed and soldered its pieces together are still alive, whether they could have seen the flash from wherever they were. Her friend has texted her, asking when she will get to the party. She responds with " A few minutes " and puts the phone away. The bike starts up fine once it's warm and after a moment of further staring into the stars she kicks the engine over and rolls away. The bright red of her tail light flashes as she slows at the intersection, then winks out.

article: "Better not wuss out too early now," the doctor leered. Sang nodded despite the chin strap. For a long while, he was a happy spectator. The Heart Charge Tuesday of the hospital was always an interesting affair. However, as the night wore on, Sang began to feel uneasy. He wondered how much longer he could endure the seemingly endless stream of patients coming in for heart-related issues. Eventually, Sang had to take a break, and he slipped away from the chaos of the emergency room. As he walked down the quiet hallway, Sang felt a sudden pain in his chest. He clutched at his chest, gasping for breath. He managed to stagger to a nearby bench, where he collapsed. His chest was tight, and he couldn't catch his breath. Frantic, Sang pulled out his cell phone and called for help. Within minutes, medical personnel arrived on the scene, and Sang was rushed to an examination room. The doctor there examined him, and after some testing, diagnosed him with a heart attack. Sang was shocked. He was in his thirties, and he had never experienced any heart problems before. But as the doctor explained the potential causesstress, a poor diet, a sedentary lifestyleSang realized that he had been neglecting his health. From that day on, Sang made a commitment to care for his heart, both physically and emotionally. He changed his diet, began exercising regularly, and sought counseling for his stress. And as he sat in the hospital, recovering from his heart attack, Sang realized that sometimes, it takes a wake-up call to remind us of what's truly important.

article: The new queen slew the last defender to the throne room and stepped through the wide entryway trailing blood from her stained white dress amid a chorus of gasps from the King and his body guard. She had regicide on her mind, loathing in her eyes, and the dripping blood on her sword to mean it. " Kill the bitch! " roared the king atop his throne his voice reverberating. His loyal protector needed no urging. He stomped down from the dais in splendid full black plate his longsword drawn angling for his diminutive prey. She didn't stand her ground, instead rushed headlong as though a demoness possessed, her voice wailing like a banshee to meet his charge. The knight stopped, lifted his gleaming weapon readying a deadly blow. At that moment, time seemed to stand still as a pillar of moonlight streamed through the ornate stained glass window striking his blade in holy resplendence and sending shards of bright glory around the room. Surely the old gods were with him now thought the young handsome king as a smile crept upon his face. The young queen did not slow her stride as the knight roared and rent the air with his blade in a perfect arc. She instead dropped and slid feet first on the polished marble floor made slick by the blood-soaked dress. The momentum transformed her into a blur as she slid between the knight's legs and thrusted her small sword upward with all her might. It sunk to the hilt through a slit in his armor and choked off the man's dying scream. The knight staggered forward, dropping his sword with a clatter, and crumpled with a discordant crash. Silence arose save for the king's heart beat thundering in his ears. The queen, a bloody sight ripped from hell, yanked her sword free, wiped away the gore on the only clean spot left on her formerly white dress, and walked to the throne all the while dragging her sword tip along the marble marking the occasion with an ominous screech. Her sword didn't need to be sharp any longer. The king drew his royal dagger in a futile attempt brandishing it before her. The air whooshed and his hand lay on the floor still clutching its dagger. In a moment, she was upon him with the sword at his neck. " Why?! " he cried. " You and I have brought peace to our long warring kingdoms, my beautiful queen! " She spat in his face. " Ask my father who lies dying from poisoned drink. Ask my people whose throats now suddenly labor beneath your army's boots at their doorstep. " " How did you - " " My spies are prettier than me. You dishonored me on our wedding night no less. " " No, please, let us consummate our - " She drove her sword through his chest, the dulled blade stopping at his heart. His eyes bulged. She kissed him on the lips as she drove the sword the rest of the way with tears streaming down her face. He exhaled his last breath and fell across the throne.

article: I have never expected to savour the taste freedom again. After all, when I was bound and stuffed into this metal casket - having been burned, stabbed, poisoned, drowned and subjected to every imaginable murder method available - buried deep beneath the earth, I had expected my captors to not mark my grave. Best to leave me forgotten, I presume. Their laughter as they lowered me down, mixed with the sound of the dirt crashing unto the metal, haunted me amidst the deafening silence. How long was I confined to this hell, unable to move or speak, unable to die, with only the damning silence as my companion? All because they did not understood my kind, allowing their actions to be driven by fear instead of enlightenment. If only they had the slightest inkling of the gift that I was sent to bestow them. But the directive from the Sage was clear. Were humanity to reject us, we too would reject them. But to condemn the emissary to a metal grave? It was unheard before. It was tantamount to war. I vowed to repay the favour that was done to me. - Dave heard a dull thud as he brought his excavator down. Perhaps it's a rock, he thought to himself, as he carefully dug the soil around it. To his surprise, however, a metal casket gleamed from beneath the dirt, not just any rock that he was expecting. He quickly turned off his machine, before motioning for his supervisor to quickly come over. "Hey Mike, did anyone said anything about this place being a burial ground?" Dave asked as he pointed towards the casket. With the dirt gone, the casket looked much more intimidating. The head portion was carved in the shape of a skull, with two red rubies on the eye sockets. Beneath the skull, rows upon rows of ancient text adorned the casket's body. Mike however, seemed to distracted by something else. "Are those what I think they are?" He ran quickly to the hole that Dave dug, sliding towards the casket at the bottom of it. Both his hands reached greedily for the shiny gems. Dave stood at the edge of the slope, looking at what Mike was doing. He wanted to inform someone else about his find, but he was unsure if it was the right thing to do as Mike was his supervisor. He wondered if it was right for Mike to disturb a casket that looked so omnious. Just as he was about to call out to Mike, he heard a series of a mechanical clicks from the casket, followed by a terrified scream. The last thing that he remembered, before his vision turned to nothing, was a bright flash of light, followed by a robotic voice proclaiming that "I have finally been freed. It is now time for revenge." - rdoritales

article: "Have you seen the revision yet?" "Revision?" Arthur looked up from his holotab, the program automatically collapsing his program back to two-dimensions in order to save power. "Of the great galactic guild guidebook. They put out the first new volume since they re-branded their entire company in order to stop lawyers from contacting them so easily." Arthur's friend flopped down on the couch and threw his own holotab at Arthur, who failed to catch, or even flinch at the action, and thus took the device straight to the chin with the accompaniment of a distressed yelp. "Why'd you do that?" Arthur's friend said after enjoying the impact and the reaction to said impact. "Because you bloody threw it at me!" Arthur picked himself, and the chair he had been sitting on, back up from the floor and glared with whimpering intensity at the uncaring assailant, "So why am I supposed to care about this..." "Great galactic guild guidebook." The reply came with expected amount of smugness. "Why don't they call it G4?" "Because then they'd get even more lawyers after them!" Three arms were thrown up into the air in mock exasperation, "Grawling greep, it's a wonder that brain of your can even move that jaw with the lack of processing power it is forced to lumber about with!" "Whau?" "Ah, I no longer wonder." "I'm so confused. "You say that a lot." "It happens to me a lot." "Just read the damn thing." "What button do I "Oh, give it here you ridiculously fur-free primate. I think I would like you better if you had fur. Hitting you would be more satisfying that way, and probably less disgusting. Here, this. Your planet..... well, the second one, you know. The ones the "I GET IT!" Arthur pulled the device over to where he could read it. He quickly digested the contents, and then slowly digested his feelings about it, ending the moment with a sigh that was both heartfelt and displaying that everything he had seen was both expected and an extreme disappointment. Which, indeed, was a particularly unique emotion that Arthur had become well acquainted with over the course of his life. "Earth: Abandoned because of human nature." "And rightly so." Two arms punched Arthur in the arm with far more force than was ever necessary, "You should be happy. It's three more words than'Mostly Harmless." "It must be Thursday."

article: I'm late to the party with this so it is unlikely to be read. But I worked hard on it, so..... I gained consciousness with an aching head as two men entered this small, windowless room. Both carried a folder under one arm and a cup of steaming black coffee in hand. They sat at the wide, stainless steel table across from me. Beneath their black blazer jackets, I noticed each carried a side-arm. " Hello Dr. Roth, " said the older of the two. " I'm Detective Monroe, and this is Detective Cambridge, " he said, gesturing to a balding white man. Monroe's expression was impassive, while Cambridge seemed to scowl without effort. I reached out to shake their hands but a sharp tug at my wrist caught me surprised me. I was handcuffed to a loop attached to the table. My dry mouth opened in shock. I can't remember being handcuffed. " What am I doing here? Why have you handcuffed me? " " I understand you've got questions - we'll get to that. But first, we need to talk about last night, " Monroe said. " Sure, I've got nothing to hide. Look, do I need a lawyer or something? " I'd seen enough TV to know that I had to ask for one as soon as possible. And with this headache, I might say something stupid. I need aspirin. They cracked a reflexive smile to each other while the one named Monroe leaned forward. " No Dr. Roth, you aren't currently being charged with any crime, " he said. " However, that can change depending on how you answer my questions. And then, " he emphasized, " You may indeed need a lawyer. Not that it would do you any good. " A shiver ran up my spine as I contemplated his words. I might need a lawyer. What the hell did I do? " If I'm not under arrest, why am I here handcuffed to a table? " Monroe held up a hand. " Let's talk about last night Dr. Roth. " " Fine, " I said like an indignant child," I went out drinking with my buddies from the lab. That's Fred, Tom, Katie, and Peter. I'm sure you want their full names? " He was writing while I talked. He looked up at me and shook his head. " Look, I don't normally drink because I used to have - uh - problems I'd get drunk. I've been sober 4 years now, but we were celebrating our first set of successful trials. So I figured it was a bonding experience for the team. I could handle it. " " And where did you go? " Monroe said. " Uh - The Last Laugh, I think it was? We had a few bottles of champagne - moved onto shots after. We didn't make any trouble. When they were closing, we finished our drinks and left. We went back to Fred's and kept drinking. I guess I passed out. It's not that clear. Say, do you guys have aspirin on you? I've got a killer headache. " Detective Cambridge crossed his arms in front of him and smirked at me. " Stupid prick, nobody gives a shit about your headache. This one is a goddamn liar if I've ever seen one Monroe. " " Shut it Cambridge. Let him talk, " Monroe turned back to me. " We'll see about some pills shortly. Dr. Roth, do you remember anything else that happened after you returned to Fred Maver's home? Please be absolutely certain. Your life depends on you telling us the truth. " What the fuck did that mean? " I - I - it's very blurry. I was really fucked up. I'm sorry. " Monroe nodded. Cambridge made a disgusted sound, but said nothing. " Very well Dr. Roth. We'll give you the information we have on your night. " Detective Monroe opened his notebook and flipped over a few pages. " Your party did arrive at The Last Laugh around 8:35 PM and left at approximately 2:15 am this morning where you returned to Mr. Maver's home. Mr. Maver indicated that Peter Kent and Tom Richards left at around 3am. " I nodded. I remembered Tom and Pete bailing on us. " From that point in the night, you became increasingly agitated with Katie and Fred Maver. You made sexual advances toward Mrs. Maver in particular, which greatly upset Mr. Maver. He became upset and attempted to remove you from his home, where you became enraged. And you hit him. Hard. According to our notes, it was with a large blunt object. Frying pan, most likely. This rendered him unconscious. " He looked up at me. Had I hurt Fred? " Please tell me Fred is okay and that I didn't hurt him too badly, " I said. My voice wavered. " He's fine. He's the one who gave us the information before the incident that led to you rendering him unconscious. He's concussed, but he'll live, " Monroe said. I breathed a large sigh of relief. Thank goodness for that. Monroe continued, " However, the same can not be said for Mrs Maver. At this point in time based on the evidence gathered, you raped and murdered her. " My head was pounding harder as my blood ran cold with fear. " No," I said shaking me head, "I - I didn't do that." Tears pricked my eyes. " Of course you did, you fucking scumbag. Your clothes had her blood. We extracted multiple sources of her DNA in addition to her blood. From your genitals. And you left us a little surprise inside her to find. You came inside her, you psychopath, " Cambridge said. Cambridge set the contents of the folder open for me to see. Inside was a photograph of a bedroom with a limp body on the bed. The battered remains of Katie were meticulously captured, eyes-wide with a swollen, purple cheek. Her flowery-blue button up top was open, exposing her breasts, and her pencil skirt was raised up to her waist exposing her naked flesh to the world. Around her throat were distinctive marks of bruising where she had been strangled. I sat stunned as the tears came. Katie was once the woman whom with I thought I'd spend the rest of my life. When she broke my heart, I threw myself into my work and the hurt allowed me to focus like never before. Every breakthrough made, I've thanked her for it. We're on the verge of curing cancer, and her rejection of me is the reason. And now, she's dead. They think that I raped her. And then killed her. Or oh God, maybe the other way around? I shuddered as bile burned at the back of my throat. I swallowed hard to keep it back. " Look, I didn't do this! I've always had a crush on Katie and we dated a long time ago. But I was best man at Fred and Katie's wedding. I let my feelings for her go. She helped save my life. Focus me on my research. She's been my muse. I would never hurt her, " I could feel the thump of pressure in my head grow stronger. My heart was pulsing in my ears louder and louder with each beat. Tears began to leak from my dry, irritated eyes. " I - I would never do something like this. " " Of course not, Dr. Roth. You're hardly the first murderer to deny a crime of passion. We'll give you a few minutes to digest this knowledge and we'll return to continue this discussion. " They both rose and left through the same door. The florescent light from a fixture above cast an irritating light that intensified the wallop. I shut my damp eyes but the pain remained. THUMP. I couldn't bear to see Katie's lifeless form pictured in front of me - but I couldn't look away. And my brain, where before it was fuzzy and unfocused, had now begun to rebel. It beat rhythmically to escape from the cell of my skull like a caged animal vying for freedom. I focused on my breathing. In and out. THUMP. In and out. THUMP. Eventually, the throb quieted enough for me to think. I tried to recall last night. Let's see. Tom and Pete left. We drank more. Katie looked amazing. I remember telling her. And - And - Fred got angry and - I... oh god. All my research, the cure was so close. So close. I wiped a tear away. And I'd thrown it all away because I was a stupid, drunk fuck. This is why I quit drinking. Because I'm not stable when I drink. Monroe and Cambridge returned during my pathetic stupor. Their hot coffee curled wisps of steam into the air. They sat quiet until I opened my eyes and looked at them. " I think I raped and murdered Katie, Detectives. " Although spoken in a defeated monotone, each word was heavy on my tongue. Cambridge broke into a wide, unsettling grin. " Yes, we came to the same conclusion, " Monroe said in an even tone. " Dr. Roth, will you recount your experience for the record as best as you can? " " Where should I begin? " My gaze remained fixed on the picture of Katie. What the hell had I done? " After Mr. Kent and Mr. Richards left is fine, " said Monroe. He sipped his coffee again. " Well, we were lounging in their basement at their home bar. We were playing pool. And Katie leaned to hit her next shot and I was struck with an old memory of us playing together in college. So I told her that she was beautiful. Fred said to knock it off, but I swear I saw Katie smile I at me. I could tell she appreciated it, you know? Neither Monroe nor Cambridge made a sound to answer me and I refused to look up. "Go on," said Monroe. "We went upstairs and Katie made us a quesadilla. It tasted amazing. And I was still buzzing, so I wanted to tell Fred that I loved him and that I was sorry that Katie looked so amazing tonight. That it was a complement, you know, nothing more. " I nodded, agreeing to my own statement without looking at them. " But no, Fred was being such a dick. He got even more upset. I tried again to explain that I was just telling Katie she looked great - like she did in the old days. Fred really went off. He tried to shove me. I - I got angry because I was just trying to be nice and he shouldn't have pushed me. I remember just wanting him to stop. And then I had that pan..... " The each word rushed out without any consideration of what I was saying. Of what I was describing. The burn of bile had returned, but I owed it to Katie to finish. I owed it to society to see myself locked away. " I did hit him. With the pan. And then Katie ran away. She was so upset because of what Fred did. I wanted to hold her and tell her it was okay. I remember chasing her. I was crying because I didn't want her upset. I didn't want her mad at me for stopping Fred. And I just wanted to tell her more that she was so pretty - So pretty to me, " I said, trailing off. Continued below.
label: human

article: "Am I under arrest, officer?" I stressed the last word, knowing that it would get a rise. Agent Lassiter looked at me hard. "Agent. Police are officers, I'm an agent." "Right,'Agent'. Anyway, if you're not going to arrest me, then...." "You know, once upon a time, before I went into law enforcement, I went to college. Iowa State University. You know what I studied there?" "No, what." I answered as bored as I could. Play their game, keep asking to leave. They've got nothing. "Physics. Iowa State actually has a very good physics department, not many people know that. Ranked 50 in the country by US News and World Reports." "Uh huh." "I was interested in astronomy, see. Always loved looking at the stars. My old man would take me out to the country when I was young, away from the lights of Mason City - that's where I grew up, Mason City, Iowa - anyway, with this nice 12-inch telescope he had, and we'd find Mars, look at Saturn, and stuff." Stall tactic. He's trying to get me off guard, hoping I'll say or do something. "Listen, Agent Lassiter, that's fascinating and all, but I...." "As it turns out, astronomy wasn't for me. The math got to be too much for me, I never could get my head around calculus. But I did enjoy the physics classes that I took, especially the General Physics courses we took, which hit on a variety of subjects. Including time travel." Shit. Wait, there's no way he can know. My ID is rock solid. I've got nothing on me tying me to the future. I planned this down to making sure my wallet is vintage. He's just trying to keep me talking. "Agent...." "Time travel was fascinating to me, especially travelling back in time. The Grandfather Paradox. Butterfly Effect. Stuff like that. Is that something you're familiar with?" "Agent Lassiter, unless you are placing me under arrest, I'm going to get up and leave now." The door was locked. Shit. "See, the Butterfly Effect says that even minute changes you might make in the past, could have drastic consequences in the future. A butterfly beats it's wings in Japan, and a storm hits in Chicago, that kind of thing. But with time, right? So you travel back in time, and..... oh, I don't know..... bet 100k on the Lions to win the Super Bowl." I sat back down. "If anyone can hear me, I am officially asking to leave, since as far as I know I am not under arrest. It appears that I am being held against my will. I would like to speak to an attorney, and I am going to excercise my right to remain silent." "But when you make a bet, you don't make that bet in a vacuum, right? Bookmakers constantly shift the betting lines based on the action they are getting. So if you make a large bet on a long shot, that might slightly shift the odds. Not much, mind you, maybe just a point. But if that line shifts, other books might shift as well. And this shift might encourage others to bet, further shifting the line." OK, Agent Lassiter, now you're interesting. I have to admit, this is something I had not considered during planning. "But money tends to come in on both sides when a betting line moves. Unless there is known information, like a QB getting hurt or whatever, any movement usually ends up correcting itself." Lassiter's eyes sparkled. Shit, why did I engage? Stupid, stupid, stupid. "That's right, it would. But it's interesting you bring up'known information'. Because that's true as well; if some piece of information is made public that would affect the outcomes of games, the lines swing dramatically. If the information is important enough, the odds are taken down entirely." I tried my best to look disinterested, and I'm sure faily miserably. Where was he going with this? "And that's just for information related to the game itself. Injuries and what not. It makes you wonder, what would happen if really shocking information got out? Something that would call into question the integrity of sports betting itself? Something like, you know, a time traveller coming back and placing bets based on future knowledge?" No. This can't be happening. He can't know; he's fishing. So why am I the one crapping my pants? "What....what....." "It would shut down sports betting alltogether, I'd wager. Every bet of any significance would be questioned. Lines would swing wildly as people chased bets with their own money. It would start affecting the games themselves. If big money came in on the Lions to win the Super Bowl before the season even started, the Lions would figure'Hey, we're gon na win the Super Bowl!' and play differently. It would also affect the play of other teams." "You.....No....No one would believe you!" "It's a wild tale for sure, I'd need proof. Proof like a certain individual that no one remembers meeting until a few months ago placing many large wagers in many different Vegas casinos, for example. Those cameras in the ceiling see everything, you know. Every person walking in the doors. Every bet placed at every window at the book. All nice and time coded and in full HD, just waiting to be found by some poor junior agent. It's not definitive proof, of course..... maybe you really are just incredibly lucky. But it's enough to get the idea out there into the public. And once it's out there, it's never going away, right? You know how people love a good conspiracy theory." I feel like Wile E. Coyote with a tiny umbrella, under a looming shadow. "And that's not even the worst part, is it? If people are coming to the past to bet on sports, what else are they doing? Are they playing the stock market with future knowledge? Are the subtly influencing elections? Are they bringing future tech back with them and giving it to certain world leaders, or terrorists? The implications would be devastating." Now I've got a little sign that says "Help." "Imagine the effect that would have on the future as well. Never mind the Butterfly Effect, this is fucking Godzilla tearing up the entire world. Nothing would be the same. Millions, perhaps even billions of people would never exist. Anyone going back to such a future, even if he still existed, would be going back to an entirely different future." Crunch. This man has just outlined how he can utterly destroy me by throwing a couple of rookie agents into a windowless room with a bunch of video tapes. He probably doesn't even know how right he is; in retrospect, I can't believe how sloppy I've been. It would be childs play for him to do exactly as says. Doing this would potentially throw this timeline in chaos as well, it's difficult to believe he would actually do this, even if he really believes any of it. But there's no way I can take the chance. Everyone I've ever known, my entire family...... "Uh....what would you say if I told you I have a sudden and overwhelming desire to return..... home?" "I'd say click your heels together, Dorthy."
label: human

article: "You always were a coward." She said, as she held my hands, tears starting to well in her eyes. "When we were little, and I tried to fight older boys, you were the one who would grab my hand and run away with me. When we started elementary school, and the bullies tried to pick on you, you were the one to quietly walk away." The hands that were holding mine squeeze a little tighter. "When we got to highschool, and those girls started spreading nasty rumors, you stood up to them, and when their boyfriends threatened to beat us, you were the one who went to the principal and told." "When college came, and I wanted to drop out, you got so scared at my Dad finding out that you talked to me all night, and in the morning things didn't seem so bad." She looks up, into my eyes, and lifts her veil. "You always were a coward, except when it came to me. So that's why, today, I can say to you..... I do."
label: human

article: I shook two pills out of the bottle and into my palm, looking out the window at the only vaguely familiar town as I swallowed them dry. The action I'd performed daily for the last three months felt far more familiar and friendly to me than the scene out the window. Retrograde amnesia. That's what the doctors said I had. My memory went back ten months, to when I'd woken up in a hospital bed surrounded by strangers who'd apparently found me in the woods outside of town. Before that, nothing. I had to live with strangers who called themselves my parents as I tried to get to know them. I had to re-learn my own goddamn name. And as I went back to a school I didn't recognize in a city I didn't recall, I had to deal with the consequences of a life I didn't remember. See, those pills? They aren't for the amnesia. No, that's'treated' with the stupid therapy sessions I have to go to three times a month in an attempt to get out of me memories that simply aren't there. No, the pills are anti-depressants I started taking to cope with the reality of being'the crazy girl' of the city. Social ostracization is not a pleasant thing. I apparently had friends before the incident; many people over the first two months had come to demand to know if I'd recovered. Some even stuck by me for two or three weeks, helping me orient myself in the city as they waited for my memory to return. But they all left in the end, when it was clear I wasn't going to go back to how I was. Now people cross the street to avoid having to deal with me. Now whispers follow me wherever I go.'There goes crazy Christine', they whisper.'Remember her two years ago? now she doesn't recognize her own parents'. Oh yeah, my name's Christine. Apparently. npsb; But I do what I have to and I deal with it. I go to the highschool I go to and I listen to the gossip to try to figure out the workings of the place. Annie's the Queen, head of a big group of Mean Girls who run the school. Marlin and his crew were the guys you didn't want to cross - people like me were the ones who ended up going home with a shiner if one of Marlin's gang caught them. As for outcasts like me, there were the smokers in the smoke pit; they seemed like pretty nice folks, if a little smelly. There were the nerds playing Magic: The Gathering in a corner in the cafeteria and praying done of Marlin's gang decided it would be funny to flush their cards down a toilet. There were the weirdo anime freaks with cartoon characters of their laptops talking about which fictional character they wanted to marry or whatever, and then there was Marionne. Even I, the depressed social outcast, wasn't desperate enough to try to hang out with Marionne. Everyone knew she was weird. She dressed like some kind of housewife or doll, but with certain things wrong: today a pink dress that stopped above the knee, looking like it ought to have an apron in front of it, with a red sweater tied around the waist and her hair cut into a bob. The girl curtsied to say hello, for crying out loud! And yet, outcast of the outcasts, Marionne wasn't picked on. People were scared of her. Rumour had it she could do anything, even the blatantly impossible. When they were truly desperate, people would go to Marionne for help. One kid who asked her to raise his grades got straight A's for the next three semesters. Another wished for money to help cover their parents rent and found a winning lottery ticket in the trash. Rumour had it Marlin used to be 6'4" before someone asked her to knock him down a peg and she shrunk him by a foot. No one crossed Marionne, not if you valued your life. But no one wanted to admit they'd gone to her either, especially as she didn't do this stuff for free. So every student steered well clear of the creepy Marionne. Including me. nbsp; I put the pill bottle on the counter and ran out the door to get to school. Walking was always an ordeal because I sometimes forgot the way, but my parents didn't yet trust that I'd re-learned how to drive. I was dashing up the street with still another ten minutes to go when I heard a soft, wavering voice behind me. "Excuse me, miss Christine?" I turned around. Behind me, Marionne was in mid curtsy, inclining her head towards me. Great, now I'd probably been seen with her. As if my social situation needed to be any worse. "What do you want?" I asked warily. "I assume you've heard about the favours and assistance that I've granted other people?" Her voice was light and sweet, like a taste of cotton candy. I didn't trust it. Sweets can cause cavities. "Yeah, I've heard. And I don't need any help." I told her. "I understand." She answered. "See, I'm the one who is requesting help in this situation." Her large, strange eyes lingered on my face. "You see, Annie has taken something very dear to me. I thought if anyone could help me get it back, it would be you." I rolled my eyes. While I felt bad for her, it would be social suicide to be going up against Annie, let alone with someone like Marionne. Not that I had much of a good reputation to begin with, but I wasn't going to throw my chances away. "And why would I do that?" "Well, I would pay you quite well." She responded. "Not in money, of course. How about this; You get my possession back from Annie, I will return your memories to the way they were." I twitched. "What?" I forced out after a moment. "Did you have something to do with my memories disappearing?" Was that what happened when they found me in the forest that day? Did Marionne do that? "It was the agreement. I have something done for me, I erase your memory so you can not function well in this town again." Heat was rising in my chest. "You expect me to believe that?" I snapped. I thought about all the awkward moments with my parents, all the desperate attempt to point out I really did not know who were my friends were, all the times I'd gotten lost in my own hometown "You expect me to think I agreed to this? That I asked you to take my memories away from me?" Marionne laughed; the sound was like wind-chimes. "Oh, Christine. Whoever said I made the agreement with you?"
label: human

article: I sat down drinking my coffee waiting for the all clear to return to my apartment. I thought I'd give her space while she packed, although she just barely unpacked after a short and exhausting two weeks of living together. I couldn't help but be impressed by how quickly I wreck my relationships. It was at the end of this thought that a gentle nudge kept me from continuing another. The patron sitting next to me had bumped me as he got up. He looked down at me almost pitifully as he said his apologies. I was shamed into looking down as I mumbled my acceptance. When I looked up his pitiful stare was replaced with subtle amusement. " Have a great day. " He said with a confident smile. I was stuck with an odd sense as I watched him leave. It was like being visited by an old mentor or teacher. I looked to where he sat and resting close to me on his table was a pair of simple of black sunglasses. I looked toward the exit and thought a good deed wasn't worth the trouble of making a scene. Instead I opted to get in line for a refill with the glasses in hand. Looking at them more closely on the inner side of the arms were odd golden glyphs depicting a scene of eyes looking into a heart. I couldn't make out the rest. I slid them on and almost fell over from a sudden episode of dizziness. Above the man in front of me text began to come into focus. John Guudly As I looked around the room names began to form and disappear as I scanned the patrons. I returned my attention to Mr. Guudly and wondered what other things these glasses might tell me. John Guudly- 29 year old in a relationship with Jennifer Tanner I was amazed by these sunglasses as they showed me whatever I wanted to know like a teleprompter scrolling matching my reading pace and curiosity. As we both got to the front of the line I knew John was everything I wasn't. He was financially thriving as realtor, confident, and content with his life. I was struggling month to month as a cartoonist and in a wreck mentally. I envied John and I didn't need the glasses to tell me why. He was better than me. " I'll take an ice coffee. Creamer no sugar, Sugar. " He said with a wink. " Coming right up. " The barista, who's name tag and text showed as Victoria Lower, said with a professional smile. " While you at it why don't you put your number on the cup? " John asked leaning on the counter. I let out an audible scoff earning a glance from Victoria as she looked back at John. " I'm flattered, but I'm in a relationship. " She replied seemingly sincerely though her mood read irritated and relationship status single. " I don't take no for an answer. " He pressed. I knew John superficially through the glasses, but I couldn't imagine why a guy with his life would want more. " But you do take you coffee on ice with creamer and no sugar, and I have other orders to take. " She said placing his coffee on the counter and looking back towards me with the same professional smile she gave John. John's failure didn't linger on his face when he took his coffee and looked back at me. He grinned as he moved past me and his mood changed to superior. " Just a refill on plain black coffee for me. " I said shyly, feeling more feeble in John's previous space. " Sure thing. " Victoria said and turned to work up a cup. " So do you deal with men like that often? " I asked in hopes of forgetting John's mood at seeing me. " Yeah, even some women. " She joked though her mood read uneasy. I could guess she thought I might hit on her too. I could bet with theses sunglasses it might be easier than going in blind. But was that okay? Was it cheating or sleazy, knowing what answers to give and what topics to bring up? If I didn't use the glasses for this what would I use them for? Victoria's cough brought me back to the moment as she held out my coffee. I could feel my body relax as I took off the sunglasses, took my cup and returned to my seat. I put the sunglasses down on the table. What troubles will this funky pair of sunglasses bring? " Coffee Black for Mr. James Hughly. His favorite drink when he's feeling emotionally exhausted. " Playfully said the handsome owner of the sunglasses as he sat down next to me with a bemused grin. " I'm sure you can guess why I know that. "
label: human

article: You know that feeling just before you wake? Hovering between dream and life? That moment just before you open your eyes and you don't want it to end? That's when the magic happens. It's nothing special. Imagine every emotion you experience durring your day, condensed down into a moment. A blink. A thought. A flash. Thoughts and feelings transfered instantly. Thats what this was like, except it happens on the other side. The dream side. Most people don't remember their dreams. Those that do, it is just a few moments. Some fade quickly. Some you remember forever. I'm a bit different. Everytime I dream, I take pictures. Photographs, if you will. Sounds lame right? Well, these aren't your normal photographs. These transcend consciousness. They transcend time and space. The things I photograph in my dreams, they are still there when I wake. I know what you're thinking, "He's one of the lucky ones." You are wrong. Everyday I wake, never remembering the night before. Everyday I open my camera and everyday I dread the next. Everyday I make a choice. Everyday I wonder if this will be the day I don't wake. You. Are. Wrong. The thing people forget about dreams is that most people don't remember them. The thing people forget about dreams is that there are also nightmares. Things that even the most sadistic person wouldn't conjour durring consciousness. Things that would leave you questioning your sanity. Things that would leave you questioning your mortality. The thing is..... they aren't just on the camera anymore...

article: I learned at a young age that I was gifted. I'm not talking the good grades kind of gifted either; I'm talking super gifted. I was 7 when I first learned of my gift, or, at least, that's the first time I can remember using my gift. My momma was sick with something special that a doctor couldn't fix. I remember my paw took to drinking'cause, at the time, we was gon' lose her. He couldn't cope. How could he? I remember sitting at the edge of the bed looking at momma. She was sleeping. Her breathing was funny, kind of shaky. I remember feeling scared, the kind of scared that makes you angry. I was full of fear and I didn't know what to do. I couldn't lose my momma, I mean she was my momma! No boy ever deserves to lose his momma, and I wasn't'bout to lose mine. I leaned over the bed, placed my hand on her head and began to breathe. I didn't know what I was doing, but it felt natural, instinctive really. I could feel a power surge through me. It was like a shot of adrenaline soared through my body and into momma's! She jolted like she had been hooked up to one of them medical boxes, the ones where the doc says "clear!" She was alive, and not only was she alive but now she was healthy. It was like she had been reborn. A pure soul put on this earth with no malice inside. Whatever I did to her, it saved her. But, whatever I did to her also drained me. It was like that time I had fallen out of that tree and landed square on my back. Pain was all up my body, almost like death himself was giving me a bear hug and didn't want to let go. I had never been in so much pain. I learned I had a power to save people. I was scared of the draw backs. But any time my momma got sick, I was there to make her better. And every time I did the pain got worse and worse. Every time I saved her I was that much closer to meeting my maker. It grew closer and closer until one day I got a call from Paw. Momma died in her sleep. There was no signs of illness, nothing out of the ordinary. She just passed on..... gently in her sleep. I never used my gift after that. Not because of the pain that came with it, but because there was no one else left I needed to save. I only ever want momma safe, and I did that. But even with this gift I learned that sometimes you can't escape death. Sometimes it's your time and you can't be saved. I saved momma for as long as I could, that's all I needed.

article: Hank's attention was glued to the pin on the dead man's shirt. He had seen such a pin before, back in college - his friend, then what one would call him, a "hipster," wore it proudly on his plaid jacket. "Eat the rich," the little tin disc said. Eat the rich. His friend's father was a Morgan Stanley analyst, that's how the little shit even got into MIT in the first place. Then again, by the time Hank celebrated his 20th birthday, the notion that the majority of the population suffered a permanent and debilitating, cognitive dissonance, had become old news to him. Amidst the unfolding Mexican standoff, the dead body of the unlucky Purger lay on the oak floor like a demarcating Rubicon. The ragtag team of masked Purgers that managed to break through the automated defense system of Hanks' villa versus three GreyForge mercs (embellished by SWAT, SAS and some Russian inner security), including Hank himself. None dared to cross the line again for the time being. Hank calculated the odds, quickly - four against at least ten, with who knows how many outside in the yard, and automatic weaponry making it all the more unpredictable. Aside from the mortal fear that coiled like a metal mattress spring in his stomach, Hank felt a growing anxiety over the fact that too many incalculable variables were involved. Such unstable systems were his forte as an analyst, but when his own life was at stake, his resolve slowly crumbled under the pressure; the bigger picture fell apart, not letting him think as clearly as he really could. The leader, Chicken Head, pushed forward, a shotgun held confidently at the hip. Something in his lazy gait, in the red, goose-bumped large hands, in the light-brown eyes that Hank still could see under the ridiculous get-up, whispered into his ear with a faint familiarity. Shifting on his tongue like a hair that got stuck to it. "You've heard of me, I think," the man rumbled with a clear Boston accent from within the cockerel rubber mask. "We come to restore justice. Make life a bit more fair. No need to be so inhospitable. People out there want to eat, they need housing, shelter - and fairness, of course..... So few have so much in this country, while so many suffer..... We'll correct that." A man in an Obama mask nodded vigorously by the Chicken Head's side. "Got ta redistribute the wealth, twitchy! Got ta fess up'fore you die!" Hank's lips spread in a wide, shark-like grin that made the contrast shadows under his brow grow deeper, strengthening the similarity with a deep water predator. Sure, he heard of him. The town's two last devastating Purges ripped through the wealthy suburbs, all orchestrated by a particularly clever Purger in a chicken mask - he even managed to build something of a loyal mob in the process. Not like that required some effort, in Hank's eyes - bit of populist slogans, a tiny drop of charisma, and some above average intelligence to keep ahead of your followers. Still, notoriety or not, talk like that never sat well with Hank. Not after what he has been through to get where he was, with this house, these artifacts, these GreyForge grunts. They had no idea and no right. Purge or no Purge, he won't be fed pre-school morals to. Life was not fair, oh yes. Hiring ex-military to survive wasn't among Hank's ideas of life being fair at all. "Spare me the bullshit," he motioned towards the dead man with a gun he got from one of the mercenaries. "Poverty is, for the most part, a social maladaptation, a mix of mental deficiency and purely human desire to brush off responsibility. It's nice to think that someone evil steals you from so that you don't have to face the possibility that maybe it's you who's a pathetic waste of space with nothing to contribute instead!" He chuckled, but his shoulders sagged. Idealism was such a joke. "You, however, are resourceful. Cut the power to my house, managed to shut down and reboot the SafeHouse OS, took the cameras out..... brought a whole mob of welfare leechers, fired up, no less, by a rousing speech on how "the man" owes'em everything for all the'ard work!" Got ta use the Purge to fix "da injustice"!" Hank's mocking tone didn't bode well with the "hardworking masses," eyes glistening menacingly from within the masks, weapons rising. Vladislav, one of the GreyForgers, lay a hand on his boss's chest, trying to push him behind their armored backs, but Hank couldn't help himself. He was tired. He waved his pistol around, accentuating the motion mostly on Chicken Head. "If any of you fuckers ever worked a real job that you earned with your brain and brawn, if your parents were smart people and not drunkards that left you with no capital, but with a shit school and shit education, guess what - maybe you wouldn't be such miserable fuckers, ey? Novel concept, isn't it?" "Shut your trap, pig!" "Yeah, you fucking piece of shit! I'm gon na fucking cut your head off, try to take that to your insurance company, asshole!" "Get him, chief!" Hank held the gun to his face, wiping his nose with the top of the pistol in a nervous tick. He could feel the other man smiling, feeling the power of the mob behind him, rifles, hatchets and axes raised, eager for blood, fueled by misplaced righteousness. The leader was the locus of it all, for certain. "Oh, and your leader! Wonder where he has such profound knowledge of the SH OS, of all my villa's systems, of the type of bots we use for patrol - no, do it! Anyway you spin it - if he worked in the company, if he was a repair man, or - oh my, what a twist! " , Hank's face contorted into a mask of pretend horror. "If he was a customer himself, means that you little rabble-rouser is a capitalist swine himself! Is he not?" Chicken Head shifted on his, his stance changing just a fraction, but it told Hank that his shot was true. It was no disgruntled war vet or an Appalachian farmer raging against social economic inequality during the Bloody Night. No, there was intellect, one that took advantage of free resources without shame. Hank could almost respect that, if his life didn't hang on the line. The police-grade body armor he wore felt paper-thin still. "My men are placing charges under the west wing of your mansion, Mr. Norris," he drawled. "The only thing that's gon na change here, is if you'll be dying quick or slow..... You fellas included. You're outnumbered." Ah. His name, in that voice. Hank's job was to have a good memory, and not just of numbers. His name, in that voice. In a split second, it all clicked into place. Mr. Norris. The Boston accent, the county golf club, the awful lobster-red tan only an Irishman would get, the shreds of a conversation caught in the men's room about hunting trips. Hank licked his lips, and turned his head from one invader to another, from one grinning Purger mask to the other, from one gun barrel to the other. article: "Sarah, wait!" I beg. "I swear, it's not what you think it is!" Sarah looks at me, tears streaming down her face. "Oh, it isn't, is it?!" "Anyways, I don't judge YOU just because your family is "Is what, Paul?!" she demands. "Jewish?! Oh, I'm soooo sorry, you must have so much to deal with. Meanwhile, my fiance literally WORSHIPS RICKY BOBBY!!" "All I'm saying is the Church of Will Ferrel teaches love and laughter, and Judaism teaches to cut your son's foreskin off, so which religion is weirder?!" Sarah lets out a humorless laugh before sinking to the floor. "My God," she mutters. "I'm engaged to an anti-semite who worships Will Ferrel!" I open the locket to see my Lord Ferrel's loving face beaming up at me. This isn't right, Paul, he whispers to me softly. Forgive her, for she knows not what she does. I sigh before closing the locket and putting it in my pocket. "See, this is why I didn't want to tell you," I say softly. I take one tentative step towards Sarah. She doesn't move away, which I take as a good sign. "I knew you'd think this was weird, and I didn't want to scare you away." She wipes the tears from her eyes. The Church of Will Ferrel gave me a reason to stay on the wagon and get my life together. If it weren't for the church, I wouldn't be the man you fell in love with when we met." "I guess you could say things'escalated quickly'?" Sarah goes deadpan. "You're lucky I love you," she groans, plopping her head back down.

article: The chatter of the townsfolk in the courtyard below was drifting through the tiny window at the top of my cell and echoing around the small, dank chamber. I listened to the small-talk of the washer-women, interspersed with the screaming of playing children and horses hooves while I watched the latest drip of moisture make its slow journey from the high window to the floor. Half of the mouldy bread roll I'd found next to the door three days ago still lay in my hand; I'd been forcing myself to ration, but daren't leave it on the floor for the rats. The twentieth drip had almost reached the floor now, soon I could allow myself another bite of the roll, but not before I'd shifted my body across the floor, placed my head beneath the drip, extended my tongue and savoured the sweet, cold moisture. I ate my next portion of the damp, green bread as slowly as possible, savouring every chew. Nobody had visited my cell in three days, and god only knew how long it would be before the next. - Wikipedia The Prisoner of the Eastern Tower (Person) The Prisoner of the Eastern Tower refers to the unknown man who was taken captive by the forces at Galdor Castle for unclear reasons during a particularly bloody civil war. He went on to remain captive in the castle for over three years after the war finished. There is little literature regarding the identity of the prisoner apart from excerpts of his diary, written while in captivity, discovered in 1994 between the pages of a book in the castle's library. Originally the source of controversy, they were eventually proven authentic when the ink and paper were subjected to radio-carbon dating in 1999. The fact that the man could read and write, a rarity among the majority of the population at the time, has led some to suggest that he was a member of the clergy, although this is disputed by historians who cite the strange style of language used, which was closer to modern English than any other document from the time; the clergy at the time wrote exclusively in Latin. - When I next opened my eyes there was nothing but blackness. I must have finally slept. That's when I heard the sound of scraping metal and footsteps on stone, faintly echoing through the narrow corridor outside. Gradually an orange flickering glow became visible, shapeless at first, indistinguishable between reality and a dream, the silhouette of the archway which formed the entrance to my cell began to take form, growing brighter and brighter with every heavy footstep. Instinctively I reached for my weapon, and for the hundredth time cursed myself under my breath for losing it in the manner I had. The scraping of metal armour and the jangling of keys grew louder until two large figures stood blocking the light in the doorway. The iron bars screeched as one of the men dragged open the heavy iron doorframe. More strange words were angrily barked in my direction, presumably an order to stand and follow them. An order I would have happily followed if only I'd had the strength. Instead I was dragged out of my cell by my feet and back into the darkness of the corridor. As we began to descend the stairs, still being dragged by my feet, I lost consciousness on the first step. - The diary and written literature are not clear on what became of the prisoner; some accounts from the time refer to the'disappearance' of a long-term prisoner from the castle, but whether this refers to him or another prisoner is unclear due to the entry being undated. Historians argue over how he wrote with ink and paper while in captivity, most have indicated the possibility that he was given the freedom of the castle when it was liberated by the King's troops, although not granted full freedom for some reason. While many wild theories abound as to the eventual demise of the prisoner, the general consensus is that he either died in captivity or soon after release. - My head pounded from behind, the world span, I touched the back of my head and screamed in agony as I made contact; my hair was matted with blood and I could feel it trickling down my spine. I tried to open my eyes but immediately dry heaved, with no food or water for days I had nothing to vomit. The head injury combined with the dehydration meant that I hadn't even noticed my broken ribs or ruptured spleen. - The Prisoner of the Eastern Tower (Movie) The Prisoner of the Eastern Tower is a cult movie released by previously unknown director Stephen Quinn in 2017, premiering at the Cannes film festival of the same year and based on the controversial diary excerpts from Galdor Castle which are held at the Museum of London. The movie stars Jesse Eisenberg as Richard, a young post-grad history student in the future who, in order to complete his degree, has to visit his chosen historical event in the past and successfully pass himself off as a local. The movie has been praised for incorporating local myths and spoken legend within the plot, which have been attributed to the movie ammassing a huge cult following. - I awoke to cold water passing over my lips, I eagerly drank, licking my dry, flaking lips as I tried to divert every drip of moisture into my mouth. I peeled open my eyes and peered into the blurry half-light, trying to focus on something for the first time in what felt like months. A kindly face, a woman. As my vision cleared, I noticed it was an elderly peasant woman, her wrinkled skin and hands showed a life of hard work, but mostly they had the typical elderly peasant look of hard-earned wisdom. I tried to utter hello in my best accent, but all that came out was a gargled croak. " Hush now. " Spoke a kindly voice in unfaltering modern English. " Drink and rest, swallow this, open your mouth. " As I obliged, she placed the bread onto my tongue. It was wet, and tasted bitter and rancid on my tongue. " Now swallow, " she ordered in a stern yet gentle voice. I swallowed the bread, took another drink of the water and stared back at her. Her eyes looked younger than her face. " Who are you? " I croaked, unsure if she'd understand my rasping attempt at speech. " A friend. " It only hit me now that this woman had been speaking modern English to me. I had no words, my mind was still reeling as I tried to understand what was happening. She looked into my eyes, as if hearing my thoughts. " They moved you here to be presented before the King tomorrow. I know you have questions, but this isn't the time. " She was staring at her palm, swiping her fingers across it as if it were a tablet. " The guards won't come past again for 12 minutes, and the diversion team will be here in 4. " She grinned at me now, suddenly much more relaxed. She looked much younger than she had, her wrinkles seemed to be fading away. Whatever she'd made me eat was starting to work, my bloody and bandaged head felt almost normal, I could breathe easily now without pain and my legs already felt stronger. I cleared my throat, licking my parched lips and took another sip of the water. " You're from the future too, right? That's why you can change your appearance like that. So this is a rescue mission? " " Oh it's definitely a rescue! " Grinning from ear to ear, she took my hand, her wrinkles now all but gone and her hair now shimmering blonde, " but I'm definitely not from the future. " She giggled. - The Prisoner in the Eastern Tower (2017): Plot Synopsis Arriving a few weeks before the famous siege, Richard (Eisenberg) becomes side-tracked rescuing a young girl from the hands of a group of soldiers in the woods. The men return to kill him and he is forced into hiding with the girl and the local villagers. Eventually captured, his equipment is hidden by the girl's family, who attempt a rescue with the help of other villagers. While the rescue ultimately fails and Eisenberg's character goes on to become the fabled'Prisoner in the East Tower', his various interactions with the villagers and their attempted rescue turns the common public against their dislikeable feudal lord. The commoners' uprising coincides with an attack on the rebel castle by the King's troops and becomes the deciding factor in the battle, subsequently ending the war. Like the diary, the movie's conclusion is unclear on what later becomes of the protagonist. The closing scene shows the young girl digging up the time-traveller's equipment, fiddling with the controls, and staring up at the castle.

It was outside of James' usual order of business to get to the lab without taking a shower first, but the fact that it actually had come to him in a dream made it all the more imperative that he get it down on paper, formed into a prototype, something to make sure it was not forgotten. By the time James was halfway through building the thing from parts he realized that he could have just dictated the idea into his phone, but no matter, the prototype would do the trick and he'd have it ready by the time anyone got there. As it turned out he wasn't quite done when Linda came into the lab. It was clear from the way she stared at him that the fact that he'd rushed here as fast as possible was obvious. "What happened to you?" she asked with a hint of concern. "I had an dream-.... uh.... an idea..... in the middle of the night. I had to put it together before it.... uh..... fell out.... yah know?" James could barely glance away before the urge to keep going drew most of his focus. "Uh..... huh. And what-..... what are you making, anyway?" Linda stepped closer and stared. James paused for a moment, too, to look at his work. A flush entered his cheeks as he realized how terrible it looked. Between the colander, the frayed sock, and the tangle of wires it looked more like something extracted from a junk heap than a science experiment. "It's a field generator." Linda would know what he meant as they had been working on the project together for months now. Linda slowly nodded her head, glancing between James and the contraption slowly. "How breathtakingly precedent of you." She said sarcastically. "To think the answer lay in our kitchen cupboards and hampers this whole time." "No!.... No..... wait.... look." James finished wiring the motor to the base of the colander and hurried over to the adjacent work station. "See, I realized that static electricity was the key.... and.... well.... watch." A few more seconds of furious typing later the colander began to spin, brushing against the sock as the mess of wires began to jostle and shake. "James..... this..... can we please." "Just wait!" Linda glared sharply at James, then drew a breath before humoring him for exactly as long as it took to count to ten 1....2.....3.....4.....5.....6..... The ceiling tiles blew outwards.

article: Most mornings I wake up a few minutes before my alarm goes off so I doze as I wait for seven am.
