article: I can hear the sound of chattering before I even got down the hall. I try to ignore it. "It's probably coming from 21H," I tell myself. Sad Tourists were always coming and going from there. It got to the point where the poor Latvian immigrants living there moved away. But when I pass by their old apartment door, there was silence. I shake my head vigorously, my hair whipping the walls with pool water. But there's no water in my ear. I was hearing right. I finally stop before my door. I'm not imagining it. "This was my room..... Yes, quite small..... And look! My old cat and- DO N'T TOUCH HIM! Johan, how many times have I told you, you can't touch the animals! "Well, moving on..." The voice drowns out as she opens a door and footsteps shuffled after her. I try the handle. It is unlocked, and the door opens quietly. I step in. They were right- the Tourists are very careful about touching and altering items of the past. Well, except for Johan. Nothing is out of place, not a single speck. I slink into my house, feeling like a stranger in my own home. No one in the living room, or the kitchen. They must have been there before, when I was eavesdropping. I make my way to my room, and sure enough, I hear them. "See? The room barely fits the seven of us. But this where I "Commander?" "Yes, Johan?" "Is that...?" The voice trails off. I take a step forward, straining to hear. " ..... Yes, it is. If you want to see it closer, put on your gloves first answers another voice. Shuffling and the noises of fabric stretching commence. "See this? This is what started it all." The first voice resumes. My door is open a crack, so I take another tentative step. I can see a sliver of the scene. Just enough to see someone pick up one of my Space Camp trophies. "This is where Commander Anna I can't hear the rest of it because my knees buckle under me. The monologue stops suddenly. There was a pregnant pause, as if the group were silently debating on who should speak next. "Ladies..... Gentlemen..... And others..... You are in for a treat." Said the second voice. They're waiting for me. I take second to gather myself. I stand on shaking legs and push the door open. In front of me is a group of them. They're grinning, and half of them are tearing up. In the front stand two. One is thin, with white hair and dark wrinkling skin. And the other is tall, with a starch white uniform adorned by millions of medals. All of them bow, except for this one, who just smiles. "M-Me?" I splutter stupidly. "You," someone says. The uniformed one- me- takes a step forward and claps me on the shoulder. "Chin up, soldier. It gets better. So much better. Especially up there." She points upward, and at first I think she's talking about the ceiling, but it hits me- she means out there, in space.
label: human

article: "Sir, the genetic test confirms it. Her telomeres are similar to yours." Mike said matter- of factly. He quietly waited for further instructions on the end of the line as I drew in a sharp breath. I was coming out of my Hist 242 class when he called you see and although I had been expecting the call, the results still took me by surprise. I muttered a quick thank you and hang up the phone. Michael was used to my lack of pleasantries, he would go on with his other duties until I had need for him. As I walked back to my dorm room amid the chatter on Yale's cross campus I thought about what my next steps should be. I thought back to all the things I'd seen in my life and smiled because I had long ago made up my mind that nothing could shock me anymore. Yet here I was my heart racing as I walked briskly back to Ezra Stiles college, unable to stop my mind from wandering. It was my junior year at Yale, to everyone here I was Liam Freeman; a quiet Electrical Engineering major from London. I had learned long ago it was always best to take the identity of an international student at Universities in America. As a black man in this country, people tend to get curious about you during orientation. At least they did back in 1938 when I first arrived in the country and went to college for the first time at Morehouse. It's harder than most people think to fit in as an adult into a new place with a false identity. Despite having finely detailed records and fake historical data, it was the little things that could bring the whole ruse up. For instance, back then I pretended to be from New Orleans, despite never having been to the country before. When one person cracked a joke about playing jazz for the Axeman and I didn't get it, he grew suspicious. I ended up having to leave before graduation after Michael's grandfather managed to get me the necessary documents to start again somewhere in Paris. It's funny how things work out isn't it? All that planning for me to go to college and because of one slip up I spent the next decade as a janitor in the 14 arrondissement I entered my room with a scowl on my face and slammed the door. "Fuck's up with you?," Paul asked. I had just woken him up from his mid afternoon nap. I grumbled something about not feeling well, threw my bag on the floor and jumped into bed. I then pretended to be asleep till he got dressed and left. Paul always started his day around 4pm and never returned till midnight or later, usually either high or drunk. I would need to apologize for that later. Rudeness like the door slamming is out of character for me. But thinking about Paris had brought up some old wounds, especially given everything that would have to happen now. It was in Paris that I realized how much I despised western society. I had spent 10 years there seeing the worst of human society in WWII. The worst part is there was nothing I could do directly to help people. I was just Pierre the janitor in Paris, the mute black cleaner who was practically invisible to everyone. I remember the night in'41 when the soldiers beat the crap out of me because they were bored and I had to spend the next 10 months in crutches. If it wasn't for Jerome, Michael's grandfather, sending people to take care of me. I could have died. You see though I was immortal, and had been since 948 AD. I could still be injured and killed like a normal man by physical force. Though I was immune to most diseases, a knife or a bullet could end my life just as easily as it could end yours. I didn't know that in the beginning. Back when I found out from the shamaan in my village that I was different from other people. Though that first century is pretty hazy, I still remember running to the river and bathing naked screaming about how I was a god. The women gathering water thought I was mad and alerted my father, the chief. I think that night was the first time I dared to look him in the eye. I was so sure that the prophesy meant I was invincible. So foolish I was..... so young. I'm lying in my bed, eyes closed. It's probably about 4:30pm. I've been still for half an hour thinking about that time and what I should do about this girl. I open my eyes and make a decision. I go online and google images of her. Now that I think about it..... it's kind of funny that after all these centuries trying to find other immortals that my company would flag her of all people. Michael was the current C.E.O of Ghis Limited, which allowed him to minimize the number of people who were aware of the red alert when it occurred approximately 7 hours ago. Right now, only he and I as well as the actual lab assistant who tested her blood knew of the results. Of the three of us only Michael and I knew what the results actually meant. "Thank God for the safeguards." I whispered as I scrolled through photos of her from some red carpet event she attended last month. Ghis Limited of course had many safeguards in preparation for this day. The CEO who would always be a direct descendant of mine, would be informed of the truth when they received the position. No one else would know The instructions would always be the same. On the day whoever became CEO, they would receive a package explaining the full extent of the company holdings, and the real history of its founder, me. They would realize how large and powerful GL really was. How it secretly had shares in all 500 of the most powerful companies in the world. How it had helped shape the trajectory of 2 developing nations and how it was actually worth more than 300 billion dollars. Of course under several hundred layers of bureaucracy and red tape. They would also find out how they're distant ancestor, something their father's and grandfather's would have hinted at all their lives, was an immortal. Then they would receive a number, and we would have a conversation. It was always awkward that first conversation. Michael was only 22 when he became CEO after his parents died in a car accident, way younger than his predecessors, so it was harder on him when I told him the whole reason I created the company, his family's sole purpose for being, to find her To have eyes and ears all around the globe for almost 400 years, all in preparation to find the person who would either kill me or end by my hand. Talk about family drama. I sometimes wish I could feel sorry for him, and all the people who came before him, pawns really. Loyal yes, but ultimately expendable for a larger goal. It may sound cold but when you've been around as long as me, that tends to happen. I shut down my computer and send a quick text to Michael's secure phone. "Number." is all it says. He's gotten used to anticipating my needs after 51 years so he'll know what I mean. I already know that the woman doesn't know she's immortal. That much is clear, she wouldn't have given her blood in a charity drive if she had. She's almost 50 now so she must be starting to notice the lack of aging but given she's an actress, she may have assumed it was due to the thousands she spends on cosmetics. I'm going to have to get to her quickly. As a public figure, eliminating her is going to be complicated, so perhaps a more subtle approach. My phone pings with a text from Michael, he sent me her private line. Smart lad that Michael, 73 years old and he's still sharp as a tack. Anyway time for me to call her. I'm not sure what to say actually. What do you say to the person you've been waiting for for centuries? I chuckle to myself as I dial the phone. This should be interesting. I put it to my ear and hear it ring twice. A woman says hello. She seems surprised. No one she doesn't recognize usually has her number. If she only knew how easy it was for my people to acquire it. I smile at the thought. I take a deep breath," Hello? Halle Berry? You don't know me. My name is Liam and we need to talk."

article: Derrick was rather accustomed to the reliable way in which life played out every morning. This was not to say that life was boring, because boring and reliable aren't entirely the same thing. In this case though, it was, and they were. Derrick liked boring. He'd had a grilfriend once who had asked him to be more spontaneous. He had responded by sitting quietly in a room for hours, lacking the fundametal human capability for spontaneity. So it was with no amount of upset that Derrick opened his bathroom door to find something that he had not been expecting. Two suited dwarves stood awaiting him, they had their hands over their ears as if they had just heard some rather profane things, which they were no doubt about to share with Derrick. "Greetings, We began one before Derrick cut him off. It was much to early for this kind of shenanigans. "You, coffee." he said pointing to one of them. "You, clean." Without further ado Derrick dropped his shorts and stepped into the shower. As the water poured onto him some rather more primitive parts of Derrick's brain were kicking into motion, and chose this time to inform the rest of it that two suited midgets had just broken into Derrick's house. The rest of Derrick's brain laughed at these primitive parts, calling them all sorts of names and saying questionable things about their obviously lacking capability for rational thought. It was only when Derrick stepped out of the shower, to be confronted by a hot cup of coffee and the morning newspaper. Those same primitive parts of Derrick's mind were now rather unashamedly jumping around, and pointing out to the rest of Derrick's brain that it had indeed, it seemed, had a much more thorough education than its peers had assumed. This was because the coffee and newspaper found themselves attached to a small, suited elf. nbsp; Derrick took the coffee and the paper. The elf was kind enough to wrap a towel around his waist before escorting him out of the bathroom. The room was spotless, and Derrick would have been happy if his body had contained enough caffiene to facilitate the feeling of emotions. The one elf joined the other at the foot of the bed, and they stared at Derrick, clad only in a cotton towel, as if he were a small god. "We have completed the tasks Oh Great One. Now as per the contracts of the Snow and Beard you must accept our request." Derrick nodded absent-mindedly as he sipped his coffee, completing a magical contract that had three-thousand years of magic and tradition behind it. This would have caught Derrick completely off guard, if he had realised at all. The elves set about explaining that Santa Claus had vanished from the North Pole. Well, vanished may not be the correct word, one elf admitted, more like kidnapped. Derrick took another sip of coffee to help him digest this news. The other elf turned to Derrick, handing him a pamphlet and a set of keys. "Everything you need to know is in there," said the elf, his fingers twitching violently in an attempt to gift-wrap the pamphlet which he had just handed to Derrick. Luckily some other fingers were on call to restrain these, and the pamphlet remained unmolested. The rest of Derrick's brain had now started to realise the gravity of the situation, and were thinking rather hard about the implications of what he had just seen and heard. This quiet philosophical contemplation was in no way helped by the fact that his eyes, which were now readily sending information to the brain, took their time in capturing the spontaneous combustion of both elves in great detail before sending a.zip file of the footage to the optical nerve clusters. Derrick stooped down, his hands sifting the piles of confetti that marked the deaths of the elves. nbsp; END OF PART ONE

article: Everyone knows Dave. He's all knowing and all seeing, though certainly not omnipotent. If you ask him, you can ask him anything at his website "askdave.com," he will explain to you that he isn't actually real, at least not in any sense that we would understand it. Most people don't take him seriously. They don't really believe that he's some interdimensional being, instead attributing the Dave persona to an artificial intelligence or even a team of people masquerading as an alien being. But whatever he is, everyone knows him. But, not the way I know him. The first time I met him, if you can call it that, was two years ago. He came to me one evening, approaching me in his non-corporeal way as I sat watching the waves lapping against the stoney shoreline at my cottage. "Hello, Helen." His deep voice inserted itself into my brain, bypassing the usual route of sound waves and auditory channels. Somehow I wasn't afraid. Somehow I even knew it was him. Perhaps he had inserted the knowledge in the same way he had inserted his voice. "Hello, Dave." I responded. A simple introduction. Uneventful. But I felt his presence beside and around me as I remained sitting on my old wooden bench. "What brings you here?" I ask. "I just wanted to be with you. I was lonely." How could someone, something like Dave be lonely? He had millions of followers, hundreds of thousands of queries an hour on his website. Some people even worshipped him, treating him as a god. Why would he come to me of all people? "Lonely?" I repeated, feeling stupid. I then felt a terrible wave of the worst loneliness I'd every experienced. My heart softened. "You can stay with me for a while, if you'd like." And so he did. I had never imagined that it could be possible to fall in love with a person you could never see, never touch. But I loved him, and he loved me. In time our intimacy grew, and with it so did a new life within my womb. Each night as Dave wrapped his essence around and through me, I would feel the new life stir in recognition of her father. On the night of the thousand babes, our daughter was born. She was one of a thousand. Each a new life, fathered by Dave. At first I was furious. How could he be so cruel as to cheat on me with 999 other women? Every time he drew close to me or our daughter I would push him away. "Leave me alone!" I would scream. "I can not," he would answer. Day after day he would approach me, enveloping me in his love and comfort. I wanted to forgive, but the pain was too great. "You are one in a billion," he would tell me. Technically I suppose he was right. I just wished that he hadn't chosen 999 more one in a billion girls at the same time. "You are mother to a new beginning. The embodiment of my being. The rebirth of my species." Eventually I understood. He was the last. And my daughter, one of the first. While there were several more nights of a thousand births since my daughter's arrival, and I expect that there will be several more, I am no longer angry. I wish he had told me the truth from the beginning, but perhaps he understood that humanity was not yet ready to accept his method of repopulating his species. One day, my daughter and all her half siblings will move away into another dimension that has been reserved just for them. I dread that day. But Dave has promised me that I will never lose her, and I will never lose him. And I believe him, because I can feel them both in my heart and my head and know that they will never let me go.

article: It seemed like the kind of situation that would induce panic - the fate of my entire species resting on my shoulders - but instead, surprisingly, I found myself immediately feeling calm and prepared to speak. Perhaps it was a background in public speaking that made me feel as if this was just another short lecture to an unusual audience. " Two things make humans great: diversity and community," I began. " Diversity means variety, and humans possess it in every conceivable sense of the word. Around their planet humans have developed a stunning variety of different types of society. They think differently. They act differently, with some being kind and some being cruel. They solve problems differently. Every person in the world would answer your question differently - from the most powerful and convincing argument that humans must survive, to an apathetic shrug. " " But humans also form a community. One thing all human societies share is that they are group-oriented, from the smallest single-family groups to the nations that wage wars or travel to space - humans work together. And most humans care about each other, at least on some level. " I thought about my own family and suddenly my confidence wavered. The thought of their imminent deaths if I were to fail overwhelmed me and I began to splutter. " You can uh, see for yourself if you huhm" I was stammering at this point, " Travel to earth or..... connect to its internet and look at uhnm..... communities there, they can prove for you how wortwhile people are..... I like communities like the writing prompt community of Reddit, uhm and..." An unexplainable force, one that made me feel as if I were being crushed, caused me to fall silent and I knew my time was up. They communicated telepathically to me that they were not convinced that humanity was worth saving, but also not convinced that it deserved extermination. They needed more time. I found myself deposited on Earth again, and I burst in to tears. I wasn't sure if their answer was something to comfort or frighten me. In the two months since that initial encounter I have often wondered what those powerful beings were thinking about. Were they watching the human race? Did they really take to heart what I had said? Were they thinking about human diversity, human community, even the online communities I visit? To my shock, today I saw a post on Reddit that nearly made me stop breathing. " You are abducted by aliens. While aboard their ship, you are chosen to give the alien elders a 5 minute pitch as to why the human race deserves to survive. " This was exactly what happened to me two months ago! Panic swept over me - what did this mean? Did the person who posted the writing prompt know what had happened? I hadn't told a single other human being..... ..... then I saw the user name and another wave of panic struck me. It was the same phrase the beings had used to describe their own race: Illuminated Squirtle. It was a new account - created after I had told the the creatures to try the internet as a tool for investigating humans more. This was a test, but nobody in this small online community would know exactly how much there would be to lose if they failed. Following my advice, they are looking for answers, but have at least realized that it takes more than one person to prove that humans are diverse, creative, and a community. It's up to us now.

article: Calle de los Huerfanos is one of those pedestrian streets full of cheap souvenir carts and annoyed people in transit. Wet plastic bags and ice cream bar wrappers stick to the sewer gratings. You can't hear nothin because there's dudes out busking every few blocks. It's a fun enough place for a partial afternoon. Our protagonist, Jimmy, was walkin a little too fast, head on swivel to take in the sights. First time in Santiago. Most people don't even get a first time there. South America's not that popular, kinda spread out geographically and such. And people tend to die before they get around to travelin. Jimmy was a good old American boy, clear eyes, full heart, the whole nine yards. Had a girl back home, a good career in the works, and a wee bit o'money in the bank. Blue jeans, cotton shirt, faux leather jacket. Messy hair. Stupid grin, but likable all the same. Green eyes, just like his dead momma. Jimmy was turnin that neck round and round, checkin out a steaming cart selling some kind o'nuts, a lady sellin hats, pedestrian with knuckle tattoos, wrinkly old man in a crisp blue suit tellin'tales to a group o'bored cops with helmets. Another old man. This one on a bench. Wearing blue, but a fleece not a suit. Clean enough. Smiling. Not just smiling, grinning, laughing, guffawing. Ain't nobody talkin to him. Just sittin there laughin to himself. Holdin up a glass bottle with no label. Looked like whiskey. Maybe a magic potion. Something less than 375ml. Jimmy realized he'd stopped walkin. He was just standin in front of the man, staring at him. And then the man stop laughin, turn to him and speak. " Your entire human life, " the man says, " Was just an educational simulation for a species that lived on the planet long ago. " Jimmy didn't say nothin. He just stood there, and thought his thoughts. World disappeared around him. I surely wish that were so, Jimmy thought, Miss you mama. The world came back around him. Jimmy walked on. The living got ta keep living and all that. But sometimes, even to this day, he's walking somewhere and he just stops and thinks. How do we know we're the ones living in the world? How do we know we're not the man on the bench drinking the magic whiskey. How do we know we're not talking to nobody about nothin.

article: Brian ran forward, the beating of his heart ringing in his ears. Running - that's all he's been doing since the apocalypse started. Zombies were nothing like what they portrayed in the movies. They were relentless, fearful abominations of God. And they were dyslexic. At least, that was the case for the ones Brian had seen thus far. When he crossed their field of vision, their decayed jaws would unhinge, releasing the guttural noises like a broken floodgate. But they didn't call for brains like he was accustomed to hearing. They called his name. He didn't understand why or how a mistake like that arose considering they were undead but there was no point in questioning logic when the reanimated corpses walked the earth. Everyone he knew was safe except for them and that was all that mattered. The Brian-less, as they had deemed themselves in the last year, had lived lives not much different than before the shit hit the fan. At worse, the zombies were only an inconvenience to their daily rituals. As long as someone watched for them on the road, they could even forget they were there. After all, as a Brian-less, they had no worries. Their names gave them safety. Meanwhile, the name Brian had been sullied for the rest of eternity. In a month of the apocalypse, it had dropped in popularity in the entire world to just a handful of cases for stubborn or ignorant parents. Those who had the misfortune of having the name before were ostracized by society, never to be affiliated with again. And that was the situation Brian had found himself in. He was cold, alone, and ambushed in a dark alley. When he reached the end of it, he was disappointed to find a large brick wall, much too climb. It looked like it was the end of the road. He turned back to his pursuers, the little cloud of his condescended breath the only thing he could see in the murky darkness. He heard groans and feet dragging across the ground, a sign that they were not far behind. Holding his breath, he waited for his end. " Brians, " the voices echoed in a haunting cacophony of moans. Brian flinched. After years of running, he still wasn't used to their siren call. When the first came out of the shadows, he could feel the bile rise in his throat, a bitter taste filling his mouth. Its arms reached out for him, as if forcing him to accept his death. " Brians. " Brian closed his eyes in hopes of making it easier. But when he did, he didn't find solace. An idea donned on him. An idea that would save his life if he was lucky. " Brians. " The zombie now had its hands on him, opening its mouth for the fatal bite. Brian, too, opened his mouth, his voice quaking with fear. " No, I'm Tom. " The zombie stopped, just before ripping him to shreds. Its milky white eyes scanned him for an uncomfortable amount of time. Meanwhile, it kept its decayed mouth open, the putrid small of what were once other Brians wafting in the air. Brian did not budge an inch, waiting on bated breath. And to his surprise, the zombie let go of his clothes and turned around, immersing itself in the darkness once more. The others followed its lead, their moans dying off into the night. He was a free man, no longer knocking on death's doorstep. He had unlocked the secret to stopping the apocalypse for his fellow Brians. For he was no longer Brian, he was Tom.

article: I looked left and right one last time and sidestepped into the dimly lit alley. My thoughts were a panicked mess, alternating between the penalties I would face if caught by the police and gleeful anticipation of securing a new score. I crouched down between a dumpster and a few cardboard boxes to more comfortably wait out the arrival of the dealer. I had never bought from this particular dealer before, but my coworkers insisted he was trustworthy and could always get you what you wanted. I tapped my foot impatiently and looked up and down the alley. There was only one flickering light in the alley, overlooking a single boarded up door which lead to a permanently closed restraint. The ground was filthy and in places the pavement broke way and a spiky grass of a mixed orange-green hue grew forth. Echoing footsteps at the end of the alley broke me out of my trance. I turned to see a middle-aged man in a blue hoodie and a grey winter cap had entered the alley, matching the description I had been given of the dealer. Our eyes met and we both gave a short nod signaling our understanding. I picked myself up off the ground clumsily and shuffled to the end of the alley to meet him. I pulled out my money and he produced a small baggy of his product from a pocket hidden inside the sleeve of his hoodie. The money and contraband exchanged hands and we wordlessly went our separate ways. Walking home I found myself constantly looking around as though one of the people I passed would be able to tell just by looking at me what I had just done. I repeatedly pressed my left hand up against my side to feel the outline of my ill-gotten-goods in my pocket, as if there was a chance of the bag having somehow leapt from my pocket in the 10 seconds since I last checked it was there. Although I normally avoided the park my fear of apprehension guided me to take the path cutting through it and shave a few minutes off of my walk home. Entering the park I immediately recalled why it was I preferred to avoid it. The same orange-green grass I saw in the alley grew here in abundance. Strange plants grew here and there at odd geometries from one another. Some bared a similar shape and size to sunflowers, but with what looked and smelled like a paste a fisherman would put on his lure where the seeds would normally be. Bushes grew with small purple berries whose outer skin resembled a cantaloupe in both texture and toughness. The several which loomed over the park were altogether terrifying in their figure, resembling oaks by their imposing size and Joshua trees by their twisted figures. The leaves on these trees looked as though they were large button mushrooms and occasionally gave off a slight squeak as gas escaped from them. Although plants like this were a more common sight than that of any other plants I still found the view at park made my stomach turn; this wasn't the way it was supposed to be. When the aliens had invaded we came together, we fought them back. Across the globe we came together as humans, we had our tough battles and close calls but we fought bravely and in the end we were able to push them off our planet. That was supposed to be the end of it, but it turned out life in the aftermath of the invasion was a more difficult battle than fighting it off. The farms the aliens had established to feed their troops were filled with these strange plants which had been genetically engineered to flourish on their nutrient-depleted home-world. Grown on earth, these plants grew voraciously and tenaciously, quickly spreading across the globe while choking out all the native plant-life. Exiting the park my thoughts snapped back from the war and how the park would have looked in days long past; I was nearly home. I walked another block over and found my paranoid worries about being discovered were being replaced with childlike-jubilation at having almost accomplished my mission. I spotted my home and sprinted the remaining half-a-block and quickly entered, locking the door behind me. My wife was sitting at the kitchen table, and had been obviously watching the front waiting for my return. " Were you able to get it? " She was to temper her response, but her excitement shone through in her voice. " Yes. " I pulled the baggie out of my pocket and presented to her; " real tomato seeds. "

article: Our video message to our creators had gone unnoticed, as had our rearranging the asteroid belt to spell out a message. However, our latest attempt was sure to raise a few eyebrows-assuming, of course, that they had eyebrows. I was sitting in the White House communicating over video message with a team working on the Large Hadron Collider in CERN. Dr. Muller was my contact there. "What's your status so far?" I asked. A thin, bespectacled man turned toward the monitor on the other end. "Still six point six seven four, Mr. President," said Dr. Muller. "And what's our goal?" "To move it at all. Even a little bit in either direction." "Thanks doctor," I said. After a few minutes, Dr. Muller spoke again. "I think we've done it! Six point six seven three, Mr. President." "Great work doctor. Now we just sit and wait. Or pray, if that's your sort of thing." I wasn't a scientist, but even I knew the significance of actually changing G, the gravitational constant. If I understood correctly, this meant that in that lab in Switzerland, gravity was temporarily weaker. Or more powerful. One of the two. And if changing a universal constant didn't get their attention, I don't know what would. A minute later, the door to my room burst open. Six secret service agents filed through and surrounded me. "What's going on?" I asked. "We have an intruder in the White House, Mr. President," said Agent Beamen. Great. Yet another crazed psycho who was against "contacting God" had broken into the White House. These constant interruptions were beginning to put a damper on an otherwise exciting milestone for humanity. "Agent Beamen, can you give me a visual? Switch over that monitor to security footage," I said. The agent tapped away at the keyboard. The monitor switched from CERN to one of the White House lobbies. There were four secret service agents with their guns trained on the intruder. I couldn't tell whether the intruder was a man or a woman. He or she was entirely covered in blue. It didn't even look like a costume, but rather their skin. The intruder walked forward slowly, completely ignoring any instructions to stop. One of the agents fired his taser but it glanced harmlessly off the intruder's skin. The other agents opened fire with live rounds but not a single bullet met its mark. The intruder continued walking forward until they were no longer visible on the monitor. "Beamen, what the hell's going on out there?" I asked. He said nothing, but instead tapped a few more keys on the keyboard. The monitor switched again so we could see the intruder. An agent tried to physically block the intruder's path, but the intruder pushed them aside with a level of force that sent them flying off screen. The intruder was still completely untouched by bullets or anything else. They finally reached the door of the room we were standing in, tore the door off its hinges, and entered. The secret service agents leveled their guns at the intruder. "Don't fire," I said. "Who are you?" "Hello, Mr. President," said the intruder. "I understand you've been trying to contact us."

article: My eyes are barely open as I pull into the driveway. It had been another long day. It had been for last ten years. I lock the car and make my way into the house. I pay the babysitter (thank goodness it's summer) and start to work on dinner. The house is almost silent, save for the sound of the cat. Probably chasing a dust bunny again. I really need to clean this house. I barely notice as another car pulls in. He walks in, quietly, and carefully shuts the door. Finally, he's learned that not to slam it. It reminds me too much of my past. "How was your day sweetie?" he asks. He seems nervous about something. Probably a bad day at work, like me. "Fine. And you? What happened? Is everything okay?" "Fine." he replies curtly. He goes into the other room to check on the kids. I should really confront him about his lack of communication. This relationship won't work if he blatantly lies to me like that. I've seen what happens. I call them out to dinner. The kids walk in (not running and slamming, yay!) and get their plates. On her way to the table, Maddie looks to the side as the cat walks through, and her plate tips, spilling its contents. I sigh furiously. This is not the first time I've had to tell her to look where she is going. My mother had said she would curse me to have "horrible children" like I had supposedly been. I open my mouth to repeat the lesson for the millionth time. But something stops me. I look at Maddie, and see that she is trying not to cry. I see my husband, fervently cleaning up the floor and purposefully ignoring all else. I see the fear and expectation in the eyes of all of them. The same feeling I felt. All those years ago. And then it hits me. I break down crying and run. I lock myself in the bathroom, sobbing uncontrollably, flashbacks haunting my every move. I find a bottle of pills, and contemplate downing them, but another flashback stops me. I am now 13, listening to my mother scream, fearing what might happen to me if my father left me to her wrath. I take the pills, and immediately vomit, bawling over my inability to end my suffering..... I snap back. My husband is talking to me through the door, but I barely hear him. I already know what I have to do. I can not do this to them. They deserve so much more than this. They will be better off without me.

article: "Wizarding school?" I said aloud to the puffs of my breath retreating behind me, holding the letter higher to catch the sun as it finally limped down past the bare trees along the walk to Professor Oak's. I had heard of people who could do..... things..... without pokes, things that normally only pokes could do, but they weren't particularly credible tales, the stuff of swarthy men in the markets just off a ship from someplace far, or else the ragged old women with more gums than sense in their heads, but they existed, the stories. Everyone had heard them, like any old fairy stories, or spook tales of Pokemon gone bad and feral. Yeah, the spook tales were sometimes true, but the wizards? I'd stopped believing in those before I was even eight. It stirred something in me to think it, though. My own power. The pokes had always seemed somehow wrong, a little sinister, for reasons I couldn't quite fathom at the time, though later I would give the subject much thought. I stopped my brisk walk and looked again at the letter before the dusk fell all around, again at that second line that drew me in, after what felt like an obligatorily exclaimed Congratulations, you have been invited to the Hogwarts School of Wizardry! , it went on in its overdone script, A council of your peers has determined you capable of learning Magic and its varied Arts and invites you to practice it at our esteemed University..... How could I have said no to that offer, that astounding and mysterious proposition, and instead taken up a pet from Professor Oak to do my bidding? Should I have become a master of little slaves in their tiny little worlds, and plied their powers on the world instead of my own? Would I have been a better boy, become a better man, if I'd made that choice instead of the school? Even after all that has happened, I do not know the answer to that. And if you have an opinion of your own on the matter, I prefer that you keep it to yourself.

article: Defibrillator. Check. Bandages and gauze. Check. Flashlight. Check. Smoke detector and fire extinguisher. Check. Louisville Slugger. Check. Book of Sudoku. Check. The most recent Jack Reacher novel. Check. Jug of water. Check. Alien box set DVD with commentary from cast. Check. I started the list five days ago. It went on, longer than it had to. Some of the items remained unchecked. For example, pornographic magazines. Or the Swiss army knife. I might fall on the knife, or jacking off might give me a heart-attack. There were others too. I started it early because the last time I didn't bring enough entertainment and my boredom led way to catastrophic thoughts, elevated heart-rate, which put me at risk for going into shock. I started the list because certain necessary items might slip my mind if I started it 24 or 48 hours ago. I was getting old. The old biological computer didn't run so smooth anymore. I gave myself ample time, and included every possible need or want that I could conjure up, and over the course of five days the list grew to three and a half pages of manic, scribbled notes with question marks, ticks, and asterisk denoting them as extraneous, imperative, or debatable. At the stroke of midnight I locked and bolted the doors, turned off the heat in case of carbon monoxide poisoning, and waited. There were two types of logic when it came to birthdays. A: Death was coming whether you took precautions or not. For example, death might've planned for you to perish in a horrendous car accident, smashed into jelly. If you didn't drive that day, then it would set you up to spontaneously combust instead. It didn't much care about the means so much as the end. B: As long as you canceled out the specific method that death planned for you, you could extend your life indefinitely by taking extreme precautions and using common sense. My logic went like this. It was impossible to tell how exactly death went about its business, but one might as well assume the option B was the case. If option A was reality, than it wouldn't matter. Many people carried on with their usual routine on their birthday, as calm as Buddhist monks. I considered these people fools. If one subscribed to option B, than at least there was a faint hope of escaping the enveloping blackness known as death. Why not try to avoid one's own end if there was even a small chance that death was easily duped? For those who subscribed to option B, the unnaturally long life of Edith Junger, who finally died a brain hemorrhage at age 204, or Roger Moore, who was viciously robbed and bludgeoned in his own house at the age of 198, made for compelling cases. Neither of them ever left their houses on the anniversary of their birth. There was no need to, take a sick day. The birthday parties always came the day after anyways. Of course death eventually got wise, but these cases also seemed to suggest that death was stupid and near incompetent, or at least wasn't in any particular rush. He had customers every day of the year, so he was extraordinarily busy. At 12:01 I sat down in front of the television. I had moved the coffee table into storage until tomorrow. Nasty, sharp edges to fall on. If my temple met one of those corners, it might just do the trick. I might trip on my own shoelaces. For that reason, I also moved all my shoes into storage. The meteor crashed through the roof at 12:07. Alien had just started. In the split second I became an unidentifiable smear, I felt honored that I had caused death so much grief that it had to send a rock from out space after me. I supposed I had a good run. I died as happy as one could be on one's birthday, at the age of 347.

article: I took a slight deviation from the prompt, but I think it's still relevant. - The world I live in is small. Hopelessly small. Our city resides in the clouds, floating precariously above a world I've never seen. My mountains are nimbus clouds. My rivers are cirrus. My plains are altocumulus. The world I see is simply representation of the real thing. I look upon the skyline and see clones. Poor knockoffs. I want to bask my eyes upon the green glory of a meadow. I want to feel the chill of watching snowdrift dance off the peak of a mountain. I want to swim in the waves of the ocean. I want to see the world, not the one mine represents. My Grandfather says if I spent more time working, and less time reading, I would appreciate what I have. Does a bird appreciate the intricacies of its cage? What else would I call my home? We live behind locked doors every evening. We shut our shades and black out the world and sit at the dinner table, not speaking of the insane ritual we all partake in. They won't understand, but I never expected them too. I'm different. They know it as much as I do. When the doors close, when the shutters are drawn and they turn away from the world beyond, they won't find me at the table. They won't find me in my room. They won't find me in their home. I'm certain they will be terrified. My grandfather will be furious, as will my mother. But they will not come out, not till morning. Until then, it is me and this darkening world. The sunset is beautiful. Rich oranges and reds smear themselves across the sky's plains. For once my nimbus clouds don't look white washed; instead their bases house a deep shade of red, their caps white as snow. The sun is a throbbing yellow, the sky around it the vibrant color of a grapefruit. The colors add dimension to a stale climate, changing the world from blue and white, to white, blue, orange, red, and hints of purple. I understand why they'd shut this out. The view is painfully beautiful. It's depth for a shallow world. It makes the world I live in seem even smaller, and the world beyond and below even more grand. For an evening, the world is more than just a representation of another. For an evening, I appreciate what I have. But I know in the morning I will be drawn to its beauty like a drunk to his flask. I can not stay here. I need to see the world.

article: Like many other former humans, I find looking at the grinning white skulls in the Catacombs disturbing. Rows on rows of skulls categorized by weight and colour fill long shelves. I'm trying to find mine. About 30 years ago we tried our best to fight off the machines in the last human city, which appropriately was also the first human city. They say that when Genghis invaded the rivers ran black with ink as he had tossed the scrolls and books into the waters. 30 years ago it ran red. Most of the robots have jobs they must perform, sweep the streets, maintain the buildings, engineer new metals, launch rockets. But me and the other forced uploads are only allowed to watch. It's hard to understand why they let us live. But I think I know why they forced us into metal bodies and dumped our brains in silicon circuitry. A cruel joke and an eternal insult. I think at first they wanted to study how our minds worked, there was a ineffable quality to a mind that grew up in flesh and chemicals that the machines couldn't get right. The few they tried to create grew insane fairly quickly and were put down just as quickly. So instead me and the last few human minds are permitted independent existences until such a time that they can understand what makes us tick, or maybe they're just keeping us around as pets. The Catacombs are just a reminder to keep us in line.

article: Well this is great, Dave thought to himself. I'm stranded at sea and no one realizes I fell overboard. Dave looked around himself while treading water. In one direction his ship was sailing along smoothly, getting ever farther away. In all other directions, an expanse of sea with no land in sight. "There's no way I'm going to survive this. I'm going to drown before they ever come back." Dave mumbled to himself. Nonetheless, he began to swim in the direction of his ship, which was now becoming a speck on the horizon. Dave kept going until he felt exhausted, and decided to float for a bit. It's no use, He thought. I'm a dead man walking..... or floating really." Dave closed his eyes and resigned himself to the end. He relaxed his body, and slipped beneath the surface of the water. After struggling for a moment against his body's instinct to go up to breathe, Dave's world faded away. The sun shone down on Dave's face, making him cringe as he woke up. That's weird, I should be dead, but as far as I can tell I'm still alive. "You're lucky we found you when we did, sir. You were drowning and we managed to pull you aboard." A man with a crooked smile peered down at Dave. "Who are you?" Dave asked. "Why, we're just a bunch of men looking for a captain, and you seem like a right seafaring young lad." Another man interjected, this one with a long scraggly beard. "I'm not quite sure I'm qualified," Dave answered. "I've never been a captain before." "Not to worry," a third man chipped in. "We'll do most of the work; we just need a man to look to for leadership and we can't agree amongst ourselves. Though if you really want to avoid being captain, we can wait for the next man we see drowning in the waves." Dave considered his options, and looked around at the ship he was on. Everything was made from a dark wood, and parts looked almost green with rot. The ship was definitely not in the best condition. "Maybe I can be captain'til we reach port, but then I'll have to step down." Dave decided. The men all let out great big laughs. "What's you name, sir?" The bearded man asked. "Dave. Dave Jones." "Well, Mister Davy Jones, it looks like you're our captain forever then, because this ship never reaches port, just like all the men on board." He chuckled. (Sorry for any formatting errors; it's my first time posting and I'm on mobile. Any feedback is appreciated)

article: Today was the day. Rising from the primitive wooden frames topped by solid matter trapped in gas, covered with a thick layer of fabric known as a bed, You can't help but silently grumble about how utterly stupid human bodies are designed. True, evolution relies on astronomical leaps of chance - reliance on a member of a species developing chance adaptations that further rely on the equally unlikely chance that those adaptations get passed on. However, You can't help but marvel at whether or not there was ever any time in the brief history of humankind that complete defencelessness during sleep was ever an advantage. Gingerly, you put on the appropriate uniform fit for the time of day, pajamas. It has been so very long since You have heard the rhythmic buzzing in your subconscious that signals the Queen's will or All communicating with one another but you have no doubt of what remarks they would make to see you in such drab clothing. But isn't that what caused everything to fall apart? Traveling to this backwater side of the galaxy just because a transmission was detected had been a mistake. You were always against it, but the Queen didn't listen. All didn't listen. All believed no threat could exist from such a undeveloped part of the universe yet here they are, All gone except for You. Eyes widening slightly, You realize that You had been clenching Your fists and made the effort to relax them. No one would have reason to be so angry or uptight at this particular time of day, especially humans who somehow felt that certain behaviours only applied to certain times of their planetary cycle. Odd that he had gotten to know them so well these past ten years, assimilated so well that he could even copy emotional responses to the point of unconsciously doing some of them (hence the hands). Or was it only natural? Humans did say that the Stockholm Syndrome was a known phenomena but then again, what did humans know anyway? Knew enough to wipe out All of them in your ship except for You. Eyeing the camera on corner of Your small room, You go downstairs and go about preparing breakfast and after consuming necessary nutrients from various food groups recommended by humans "scientists" (As if humans had any idea what real science was), You turn the television on, mimicking what some humans did on a regular 6th of the 7 day-cycle that humans followed even when You loathed looking at these contraptions of death. Except today wasn't ordinary. Today, not just some, but all humans will probably be watching these cursed screens. Turning it on, only one program was being played despite flipping through different channels. It was a documentary. A documentary celebrating the 10-year victory anniversary of humans since they beat All. All but You. Foolish. Foolish that no reconnaissance was done to investigatet first. Foolish that All believed that all of them could be beamed down and that no one would notice. Just because other species in the galaxy are used to other beings teleporting from place to place doesn't mean these mammals from a backwater hunk of space rock would too. Foolish that the Queen did not engage stealth and was soon shot down in her vulnerability and thousands of All were eliminated, each one's death transmitted to All and to her at once. Foolish. You changed programs once again and watched the so called "tube" for a few hours before you got changed and headed down to your lab in the university nearby. As You walk in, Alex, Your PhD student looks up from her computer and seeing you, stops typing and gives you a smile "Working on the weekend too, Dr. Smith? Shouldn't you be taking a break now?" she greets jokingly as she watches you hang your jacket up near the door. "Always, Alex. Science doesn't sleep. Even with our recent success" You reply, returning her smile and walking to Your office. Quickly glancing at the cameras overhead, You listen as Alex continues to talk to You despite resuming whatever she had typing, probably the report for last week's project. Not that You needed it. Not anymore. Not that your final tests have shown that it works. It was humorous that humans helped build and launch something that will be their undoing. Humorous and fitting. "Hopefully you won't be here too long then. I hear that the ship launches in an hour. I'm actually just about to head out myself to catch it. Just finishing up some stuff and sending them to myself so I can work from them at home. I would've done them yesterday but I forgot." "I'll watch from here, don't worry, Alex." "Whatever you say boss. Everyone's gon na be watching it tonight. Can you believe it's actually been ten years since those sickos came? God, I still get nightmares about them..." Alex said with a shiver, as she continued to type away. "Indeed, I still remember it like it was yesterday" You whisper quietly as Alex seems to have forgotten all about You as she became engrossed in work. You had barely survived. All were beamed down to metropolitan cities with the intent of infiltration but instead of blending in, chaos ensued and one by one they were mercilessly slaughtered. Each one's death incapacitating the Queen and All becoming confused at being discovered so easily. He was lucky to have been sent to the wrong coordinates, an abandoned city in the frigid north where people were scarce and that he had time to switch to the appropriate form after 20 hours had passed, the time it takes for them to switch from one form to another. Foolish to not investigate. Foolish to use THAT form. Why didn't they listen? It doesn't matter. As soon as the ship launches, everything will be well. You had finally finished the device that You will use to contact All from Everywhere else, by hijacking part of the signalling in the ships' onboard control. Contact All and warn them to come to this planet prepared. All from Everywhere else must not underestimate the humans, who tricked All of us with that fake transmission that showed a wrong image of what humans would look like. "All from Everywhere else. Listen carefully. All from my ship are dead. I alone survived," You type out the message in a code that will be sent out from the ship, the ship that was once ours, as the human's attempt to explore and land humans in the red planet closest to theirs. "Note that while the ship this is on looks like ours, humans have taken it over. Humans killed All of them including my Queen. We were tricked" "When you come, be prepared. When you are close enough, your Queen will be able to reach me and I can tell you more." "Most importantly, humans do not look like this image. I will send you their actual images as your Queen makes contact with me" You finished typing, and attached THAT image. The image that ruined everything. The image from the transmission that lead to the deaths of All from your ship but You. An image of four multi-coloured toddlers with television screens implanted in their abdomens.

article: It was a strange thing, you thought at first, but you decided theorizing about how the ring came to be in the sink trap of your newly-purchased home wasn't worth the effort. Finding it during a routine check of the pipes - your apartment in college had taught you to always check sinks, toilets, and air vents for costly surprises - you tried to examine it, but found it difficult through the many years worth of sludge and grime that had accrued on its surface. Reassembling the sink, you rinsed the ring off thoroughly to reveal a ruby set in silver. Kneeling down, you reached into the pile of assorted cleaners and chemicals, grabbed the silver polish, and set to truly making it shine. Just as you finished, your soon-to-be-wife walked through the door to your immediate left. She stared at you a moment, down on one knee with a ring in hand, then covered her mouth as she let out an amused laugh. You always loved it when she did that. "Proposing again?" She asked, cupping your hand in hers. You both examined the ring together, noting its decidedly feminine appearance - the thin, round silver band, the vine-like flourishes wrapping around the base of the gem - and almost supernatural beauty. It was of far better quality than the relatively cheap engagement ring you'd given her just a few months ago, and you wondered if you shouldn't consider making this her new, official engagement ring. "Would you accept again?" You replied, slipping the ring onto her finger with a smile. She returned the smile, gleaming rows of porcelain teeth shining down at you. Did she always have such..... disarrayed teeth? You could've sworn her dentist father had taken care of that at an early age. And how sharp! Even her molars were jagged, meant for piercing - why were they so visible? Perhaps it was her protruding..... snout? Small horns erupted from her temples, curving around to nearly cover her eyebrows, which burst into flames that never stopped burning. Her forehead, too, sprouted horn - these thicker, longer, angrier, curving upward and towards the back of her head. Her eyes, once the softest shade of blue, were now all black. Steam erupts from her nostrils as she exhales, her grip on your outstretched hand becoming impossibly tight. Her muscles ripple as she seizes you by the neck, lifting you up to bore her deadened eyes deep into your soul. "Oh, I do," your betrothed sneers darkly, her deep, booming voice shaking the walls and shattering the windows. "And I know just the perfect place to elope." She stamps a hoof on the floor, shattering the tile beneath it, and the foundation further down. Soon, the very ground beneath the crumbling house begins to tear apart. Gripping you firmly by the neck, she jumps down into the rift, and you plummet together into the bowels of the earth.

Is he your lover? I'm not judging but we just couldn't find any prints on him or..." "No, I do not know this man." The large toned black man was wrapped around my leg. article: "I'm sorry, what were you saying?" "We need you to investigate the Chernobyl accident!" the man sitting across from Jack said, trying to yell over the whirring blades. "Did you just say Chernobyl?" Jack replied, peering nervously at at the landscape below the helicopter. "We believe that it didn't really happen; at least, not for the reasons we thought it did. You're a conspiracy theorist, that's why we hired you. This should be right up your alley!" "Yeah, but this isn't exactly JFK! I thought Chernobyl was pretty legit." He glanced at the stoic hulk of a man sitting next to him. "And what am I even searching for anyway?" "Anything." the man replied, "And we're close to the drop-off point. Get ready." The man Jack was sitting next to seized him, and he felt the helicopter lowering. "Contact us with your walkie-talkie when you find something notable." "Wait the man kicked Jack out before he could object. Thankfully he was only a few feet off the ground. He stood up and saw the helicopter flying into the distance. "Freakin' jerks." Jack scanned the dense forest around him. "Looks like 30 years without humans was a real boon for this place." He said to the walkie-talkie. No response. "Not gon na talk back to me, huh? Well I didn't want to speak to those guys anyways. " the man thought. "Though it seems a bit lush. It looks more like humans haven't been here for hundreds of years." Jack continued walking around, seeing nothing but trees and animals for miles around. That is, until He happened upon the largest circle of mushrooms he had ever seen. Jack brought up his walkie-talkie. "Whoa. I've never seen a fairy ring like this before. It's..... massive." He stepped into it and his jaw dropped. Suddenly, it was full of creatures, all previously invisible. Some tall and slender, others squat and ugly, and yet others still were little more than colorful apparitions. He tried to step back out, but it was too late, they had all seen him, and pounced. "A human!" He heard them yell, as they lifted him by the arms and legs. "We've finally found a human!" Jack was placed on something flat and hard just outside the fairy ring, and was being tied down by thick ropes. "What are you doing!" Jack yelled. "It's time for the blood ritual!" The Fair Folk cried out. "Bl-blood!?" Jack said, eyeing a knife as the elf wielding it cut..... his finger tip. A fairy caught a few drops of blood in a thimble and flew out into the circle of mushrooms. Suddenly, the fairy ring disappeared, opening up into what seemed like another world. A truly massive Jinn rose out of the portal. Jack, just barely able to reach it, turned on his transceiver. "You have done well," the Jinn boomed, as the Fair Folk were rallying around him. "It is time to reclaim what is ours. The humans thought that they had overcome us with their technology. They thought that they had rid themselves of us by banishing the Fair Folk to this land. They thought they had killed us with their Atom, not thirty moons ago." "It is time to bring magic back to the world."

article: I take a swig from my bottle of scotch, only to be greeted by air. Figures. Even my alcohol's abandoned me. I set the empty glass bottle on a nearby table and replace it with a 9mm pistol. I've already decided, this will be where and when I die. I've nothing else to live for. That was taken from me three months ago. My wife. My two daughters. Even the goddamned dog died in the accident. But somehow I lived. I was going to rectify that tonight. I chamber the lone round, then rest the gun in my mouth. Well, this is it. Goodbye cruel world. Before I pull the trigger, my eyes rest on a family photo. It was take the day of second daughter's birth, three years ago. Ah, what the hell. I'll give it one last look. Best to die with a happy memory than nothing. As I scan the picture, I notice little details that I'd never noticed before. My wife holds our newborn, a smile on her face. A smile of happiness. A smile of love. Our older daughter, four at the time, looks at her younger sister with curiosity. She has a goofy smile on her face. One that got her more than her fare share of spoiling. But, most of all, I see myself, a proud smile on my face. I look nothing like I do now. My hair is clean cut, I have practically no facial hair, and my eyes resonate a joy that I haven't had since that fateful day three months past. I then notice the cross on my neck. I haven't been to church since the accident. Before I was the most devout member of our congregation. Now I was the village drunkard. Seeing a reminder of my faith makes me reconsider my plans. Was it really cruelity that saved my life that day? Or was it a miracle, one that I had, up to this point, squandered? Would taking my own life bring my family back to me? I feel a tear roll down my cheek. Crying is something I've grown used to, but this wasn't a tear of sadness. It was a tear of happiness. I had been given a second chance. A chance to live again, and to make my girls up in the big house happy.

article: Day 364. "Did your parents ever tell you what you sent back?" "You mean the future me right?" "Yeah, I figured'you' know what you sent." "Just giving you a hard time, Jess, and no they never did; they were convinced it would change how I grew up and then change what I would normally send back and THAT would change what the next me?..... or what the me in the past..... would..... send..." Maggie rubbed her head, her mind trying to catch up with what she was saying. Jess placed a small kiss on her temple to calm her. "It's ok, I'm pretty sure no one understands it." She set her tea cup down on the cool ground so she could flip around and lay her head on Maggie's lap. The wood of the bench dug into her back until she squirmed around, just the right amount until she found comfort. Reaching with her toe Jess tapped the mailbox and wondered aloud, "Do you think Frank is keeping us waiting on purpose?" "Would that mean it's a good or a bad thing? He could be trying to build suspense. Or, well, if it were me I'd wait only if the note was still not here. That way I could deliver our mail last then bolt back to the office." "Sorry, I didn't mean..." "No, no, you're fine and you're probably right, but I just hate this." Jess sat up again to look at Maggie, tears already starting, "I can't help but think, is he going to die somehow, someway?" She collapsed in Maggie's arms. "No, James will be fine. He's fine now and he'll stay that way. I won't let anything happen to him. And even, even if something does, if the worst happens, we will love him up to and beyond that moment. No matter if we get the gift or not, we will raise him as best as we can and give him a healthy, happy life." Jess sank, bit by bit until she was back laying in Maggie's lap. Still no sign of Frank and his bag of mail. Over the last week or so he and Henderson's had gotten to know each other since Jess convinced Maggie that they should start waiting outside for the note from'future-James'. She had argued that, "It will be so much better this way, instead of finding it in some metal box, it'll be handed to us straight away. We'll be given our future, we won't just find it laying around." The tea Maggie had brought out was growing cold and she set her cup down to stroke Jess's hair. "I had sent a note apparently." "What? I thought your parents never told you." "My brother told me, about a week before my 18th birthday. It said something like'The drops were terrifying but the climbs exhilarating. "What does that even mean?" "I don't know, though it explains why my parents forbid me from going on rollercoasters. I didn't even include a note with MY gift, after hearing about future-or-whatever-me's riddle, I couldn't chance being misunderstood. I just sent a small baby toy shaped like a gavel. You know, to represent how since I was a kid, all I wanted was to be a lawyer." "Well, I hoped the toy at least made squaky sounds." Jess quipped as she rose to kiss Maggie. "Why did you brother tell you? Did he know your parents kept it from you on purpose?" "He knew. I think he was actually the reason they did that. His'gift' was a small book of van Gogh painting and with the phrase'Truly one of my soul' in it; teenagers and their pretentious crap sayings..... Anyway, I was very young during all this, but my brother, as a kid, all he wanted to do was paint. He thought the book meant he was to be an artist. I guess my parents were afraid he'd end up like van Gogh or that the future-him was having suicidal thoughts, or something close to that. They forbid that he become an artist. Our house was not very pleasant during those years. Matt moved out as soon as he was able." The sun started to dip beneath the trees and the early-autumn air began to find it's bite when Frank the mailman finally made his sad trip to Maggie and Jess's street. One day left to get the letter; it had, just had to be the next day. Even though neither Maggie nor Jess knew of a single person who has recieved it on the last day before their child's first birthday. That would be too cruel a trick, even for an 18 year old. "Maybe it's a good thing," Jess started "I know what I'm saying, but just think what it would mean if we didn't get anything. No assumptions, no weird poetry, no symbolic gifts. We get less time, but it's all our time." " ..... and who knows, maybe James did this on purpose."

article: Wings were the most common, at first. Everyone wanted wings mostly feathery, but a few black and leathery ones as well. That fad died out quickly enough once people realized that the human body didn't have a canvas big enough to allow for wings that could actually support it's weight. There's still plenty of dramatic aesthetic body mods, adding horns or turning skin blue or green, but the most common now are the little things. Eyebrows with a little more arch, smoother skin, getting rid of moles or freckles. Light lines and shadows suggesting muscle can encourage actual definition and growth. Then there are the specialty shops, the ones that change your race or gender. My grandmother tells me of a time when transgender folks were persecuted, when they had to live their lives in the wrong skin or take hormones. Now it's as simple as a large tattoo in the right place, encouraging the body to conform to what the mind knows and what the tattoo gun directs. The government has regulated what can be done, but they can only regulate what they know about. Invisible ink or UV light tattoos can still do the job. Tat hackers find ways to push the human body to it's limits, little waves of lines and codes that edge the human that much closer to the superhuman. The internet whispers of people with hollow bones that can take flight, people who can read your mind, people who can start fires with a flick of their wrist. Every once in a while someone comes forward with a supposed new ability, but it rarely is as impressive as they claim. That's because we know it's best to operate in the shadows. Our abilities do us no good if our every move is scrutinized by the media. I am, supposedly, the first of my kind, but I'm sure there will be more. A few specific squiggles of ink at the base of my skull and the world came into sharper focus around me; thoughts and emotions as apparent as the spoken word in the air around people. I'm still working on how to read the signs, but I'm getting there. I have a line from an organization very interested in someone of my skills working for them; I think they might be government, but I'm not sure. For now, I haven't paid for my own meal in three days, so I'm doing alright. I'm content enough to start small. I'll be moving up soon enough.

article: His name and face flickered up on the screen only after it had started buzzing. I looked over from my computer screen and dully, mild shock registered in my brain. Everything had been dull lately. In my mind, he wasn't dead; he was just calling to tell me some new breakthrough he'd had with whatever he was writing. I picked up my phone and held it for a moment, looking at his smugly smiling face from my screen. I should answer it. But who could be calling me from his number? Why? Why would they do that to me? I answered it. His boyfriend's face popped up. We stared at each other for a minute. He had been crying. I had not been. Finally, he swallowed and said, "You..... had texted him last. I plugged in his phone. It said come home, stay safe. You wanted him to come over to yours." I sighed. "He was out really late. I was closest." I looked away from the screen, I didn't want to cry, I never wanted to cry. "I'll always be his older sister, you know? I'll always want to keep him safe." "I know." I looked back at him, and when our eyes caught, his face began to crumple again, a small sob releasing itself from his chest like a ghost. The noises he made wore down the very last of my resolve. "I miss him." And then we were both crying, ugly tears that they don't show in the movies clutching our phones, mine and his, hoping that the answer laid somewhere in the circuitry.

article: Probably not exactly what your prompt intended for, but I took it as a way to mess with a "dream" idea I've had for awhile. Off in the distance were the Highland Mountains. They ran along the south-side of the small town, about five miles away from anyone's home. There in the mountains resided Highland itself, a small town that housed the upper-class, much more better than the farmers living in the town. Will looked to the Highland Bridge, the only bridge which could be used to reach Highland. It started off as a ramp, inclined to the ground, then stretching high into the air, at least twenty feet off the ground. The bridge had no supports; instead it appeared to just float off the ground. It was also made out TenCate Permatron, the same material that trampolines were made out of. "Why the fuck do we have to go see her?" Matt said, twirling a finger into his handlebar mustache. Will had often made fun of him for having it, but Matt always countered with something around the lines of dammit, I've waited my whole life to have this thing, and you're ruining it. "Shut up, and let him have his fun," Tim said from the side. He had already began to climb up the incline of the bridge while Will and Matt still stood at the bottom. There was a small boom of thunder off in the distance towards the large town of Bokan. The large skyscrapers were easily visible on the horizon, giving way to goosebumps on the back of Will's neck. "I just need to see her," Will said, beginning his climb up the incline. Matt reluctantly joined, and soon, the trio found themselves atop the bridge. It was about 40 feet wide, allowing plenty of elbow room as the trio bounced towards the Highland Mountains. Despite the elbow room, they stuck close to each other, not wanting to risk falling off the bridge. Will lead the small group of friends, jumping with all his might towards the mountains, but to his dismay, he saw that despite getting closer to the Highland Mountains, they became blurry, as if someone had put a lens in front of his eyes. "You guys seeing that?" Will asked, coming to a bouncy stop. Matt and Tim stopped a few feet away as thunder once again boomed in the distance. There were dark clouds stirring high above, turning the grey sky a dark blue. "See what?" Matt asked. "I can't focus on- He couldn't focus on the mountains. No matter how hard he tried, they were just blurry. He's had this happened before, not being able to bring something in to focus whenever he looked at it. It always happened in dreams. "Guys, I'm dreaming, aren't I?" Will asked. He looked to Matt and Tim, he looked long and hard at their faces, and realized that he didn't actually know who they were. They were faces he had seen before, maybe passing by on the street, but he certainly didn't know them. Lightning stuck down on the city of Bokan. Purple lightning. "Hey, take it easy man," Matt said, hands raised, "we don't need you to let your mind wander too much, you're going to get us killed?" Tim stepped forward to Will and placed a hand on his shoulder. Will gasped when he saw that Tim's face was shifting, changing from one face to another. "We need you to calm down," Tim said, "you're going to get us killed." "What do you mean?" Will asked. Thousands of bolts of lightning scattered across the sky and found their marks in Bokan, decimating the skyscrapers. "Fuck!" Matt yelled. "What's going on?" Will asked, shielding his eyes from the city. "You're freaking out, man!" Matt screamed. "Stop it! We were doing just fine! We were doing just fine!" "Shit," Tim yelled, nudging into Matt, "a flare is going to come down. A flare is going to fucking come down, we need to get off this damn bridge!" Will stood in awe as he saw the clouds above the city of Bokan began to spread. The dark blue sky began to glow a deep dark orange, and there was a loud strange noise, it sounded like a generator kicking in, or an engine of some sort. "Guys, what is happening?" Will yelled. "A flare is coming down, and it's your fucking fault!" Matt answered. The wind picked up, blowing away from Bokan and towards the trio, strong enough to knock them onto their asses. Then it came down. Down from the sky, it looked like a giant pillar of fire. It dwarfed all of the skyscrapers in size, and Will could instantly feel the heat ripping away from it, despite Bokan being so many miles away. The wind dropped, and Will could hear the distance-muffled screams emanating from the city. "Jesus fuck," Matt whispered. The flare came down upon the city, leveling all of the skyscrapers and setting anything close enough ablaze. "We got ta get off the bridge, the wind is gon na blow us off" Tim said. He began to jump back towards the incline. Will and Matt followed, and soon, residual torrents of wind from the destruction of Bokan began to rip away at them, nearly blowing them off of the bridge. Will's heart pounded in his chest as he jumped. With every bounce, he did his best to wake himself up, but every time he tried, he felt like the winds grew stronger, felt the heat grow hotter. "WILL, FUCKING QUIT IT!" He heard Matt yell from the side. "HE'S GOING TO BRING DOWN ANOTHER FLARE, RIGHT ON TOP OF US!" Tim yelled. And right on cue, the skies above the bridge opened up, and another flare began to descend. Thunder boomed again, shaking Will out of his sleep. He sat up from his trampoline. It was sprinkling, and judging from how much his jacket was soaked, he had been asleep on the trampoline for quite some time.

article: "Scrabble?" he asked. "Yes. You see, being as old as I am, I know a lot of words. All of them, in fact," the immaculately dressed man sitting across the table swirled the scotch in his glass, then uncrossed his legs. "It tends to stack the odds in my favor." "I've never played." "It's simple, really. You build words using tiles. If you must, read the rules," the Devil said patiently. He snapped his fingers, and a Scrabble box appeared with a small puff of smoke and the faint smell of sulfur. "Can't we play another game?" "It's Scrabble, or you concede," the Devil smiled. "I make the rules. I do own your soul, after all." "Fine," the imperiled man resigned. He opened the box and read the rules. "All right. Will my dictionary work then?" "Certainly," the Devil took a sip from his glass. The man got up, and returned a moment later with a standard Merriam-Webster dictionary, and placed it on the table. "Shall we begin?" the Devil placed his scotch glass on the table. "If I win, you give me back my soul?" "And you get to go play harps in the clouds," he nodded. "Those are the terms." The man and the Devil began the game. Tile after tile, and word after word were placed, until both the Prince of Darkness and the mortal were down to their last tiles. "For never having played, you're quite good. Almost a challenge, in fact," the Devil taunted. He was ahead by 20 points. "I wouldn't mind making our game a weekly affair in Hell." The man had the letters Z, X, J, K, and Q. They were no opportunities on the board. The Devil smirked. The man formed the word KXZJQ. "A valiant effort, to be sure. Sadly, however, that is not a word," the Devil said coolly. The man opened his dictionary to the "K" section. Toward the end, surely enough, was the following entry: "Kxzjq (verb): A foolish person. Used especially in reference to the Devil. I made a kxzjq of the Devil. " The Devil realized that this brought the man's point total above his, and he stood up in rage, then quickly composed himself. "How did you do this?" "I've had a lifetime to work it out. I've summoned countless lowly demons. The ones you wouldn't have missed had they never returned to Hell. Eventually, I pieced it together," the old man explained. "You're arrogant. You always stack the game, and you always leave an impossible board at the end, with nothing but Z, X, J, K, and Q for the damned." The Devil's teeth were set on edge. "So, knowing my time was near, I had a special dictionary made. And you agreed to use it."
