article: I counted the socks many times now, ten went into the dryer and ten came out, but they were different. Af purple sock with red stripes was now a red sock with purple stripes. One of my kitten socks turned into a fish sock, a fish sock had turned into turned into a real fish. It's been months of this, my socks were not just disappearing, they were being replaced. People deal with lost socks all the time, but having them replaced felt like something was mocking me. Having a fish flop out of the dryer was just ridiculous. I'd have kept the fish but my cat, Mr. Kitty, ran off with it. This was unprecedented and I needed to figure it out, where were my socks going and why they being replaced? Of course the plan was simple, I could just tape a wireless camera onto the door of the dryer and catch the culprit in the act! The plan was so devious and clever I hardly believe I came up with it on my own, but it just goes to show how smart I am. I gathered up some of my least favorite and most soiled dog face socks and threw them in with the camera. All I had to do was watch the screen and wait. What could it be? Will they just vanish, maybe little hands will come out of the holes and pull things in. This was more exciting than the day my Mom left out the channel block password. The timer was set, sixty minutes, certainly plenty of time for whatever was going to happen would happen. I sat down at my computer and brought up the camera's feed, the light was bright enough to see everything, absolutely perfect. Now I just had to wait. For the next forty five or so minutes I spent my time between watching the feed and perusing my many dating profiles, no hits yet. Perhaps some more of my Supernatural Dr. Who crossover slash poetry will pull in some guys; men love that kind of stuff. As I was coming up with my next masterpiece I had realized my neglect, the camera feed! No longer could I see the inside of the drier, instead it was a ceiling and some walls. A room! This was it, the feed must have caught the culprit and now I could see where my socks had gone. I waited longer than I could count, maybe twenty seconds, when a flash of movement caught my eye. Whatever it was, it was big and furry and getting bigger. This monstrosity reached out for my camera, no fingers, just claws. This terrifying visage of meat destroying claws had been stealing my socks, what monster could it be? No sooner had I asked myself this question I had my answer, a horrifying face came into view. A flat pink nose with two holes, obviously to smell it's victims from afar. A smiling face hiding it's sharp teeth. Two big eyes to look into its victim's soul, two triangular ears to listen to the heartbeats of people hiding from it. The monster opened its mouth and let out a roar, " Meow? " Meow? Wait, I recognize that monster, it's a cat, my cat! Now I realize where I had seen that room before, my bathroom! I rushed in and found the camera sitting in the litter box, Mr. Kitty trying to bat it around. I had been fooled, whatever this was caught onto my brilliant plan and placed it in the litter box. Obviously signifying that my plan and therefore my entire life belonged in it, my blood was boiling. I had not been this angry since my parents forced me to do my own laundry and discover this terrifying truth of the dryer. What I did next might not have been the smartest thing I had ever done, but it was certainly the most brilliant. I would just have to sit in the dryer myself and wait to be whisked away by the thing stealing my socks and telling me my plans are poopy. I super glued some of my old body pillows to the inside of the dryer, set the timer and jumped in. Using my brilliance I simply broke out the plastic window on the dryer so I could press the start button. The next hour I was a rolling ball of emotion, round and round I went, part angry and part terrified. What if it didn't take me? What if it really was a giant monster that liked to eat socks and perfectly normal women like myself? The ideas rolled about in my mind, and just as I was about to call it quits everything stopped moving. Looking around I found myself in a dark place, a place I had always feared, the attic. For years I had heard scratching up here. My Dad told me it was just rats and maybe I could get a job to help pay for the exterminator bill, but I knew he was just trying to keep me from knowing the truth. I was too scared to find out the truth, but I was here now, there was no going back except through the open door next to me. On the other end of the attic was a small light, an old night light I had thought was thrown out. In the same area there were cat toys I thought we had lost. The monster wasn't just stealing from me, it was stealing from my cat. Who would want to steal from a cat? In front of me was the answer, a book that looked like a journal with words written in it, almost like a diary or a log or some other way to keep records. Strangely they were not just any words, it was written in all meows. I knew cat fluently and began to read. " I have brought the toys paid to me, the fools will never see their socks again. " Ah ha! Here it was, proof that somebody was taking socks, paid in cat toys for services rendered. I skipped a few pages for no reason and read on. " I finally have all the cat toys and catnip I want, but was it worth it? The spell is getting out of control, socks are changing color and one of my fish vanished. I was able to get it back before Sarah could take it. " I know that name, it's my name. And the fish, my cat found the fish and took it. This was so awesome, I have a cat that knows spells! I rushed downstairs and found Mr. Kitty sleeping. " Mr. Kitty, I have some socks for you. " His ears perked up. " And I found your book about taking the socks. " He shot up and stared at me, he was frozen in place. " Meow? " He asked. " No, I think it's so cool you know how to cast spells. Next week is the Cosplay convention, we're both going. " Mr. Kitty stood up and jumped through a closed window, sending glass flying outside. Mom heard the glass breaking and ran in. " Sarah! " Mom yelled, " What happened? " " Mr. Kitty was using magical spells to steal socks but then he started transmuting them instead and then he put my camera in the litter box and then he put me in the attic after I got into the dryer and then I told him I knew it was him doing it and we were going to the convention next week and he ran away. " Mom narrowed her eyes, " Good for you honey. " She walked out of the room and could hear her sobbing over Mr. Kitty running away. I never saw Mr. Kitty after that, but every now and then I find a lump of cat poop in one of my socks, a little reminder that he still thinks about me.

article: "Those fucking kids!" The butcher said as he saw my bike. It was chained up of course but the seat was stolen. This wasn't a good neighborhood everyone knew it but in our own way we tried to make it better. "I can just pedal standing I said. The man was far too fat to get worked up over something so small. He was bought to give himself a heart attack." I worked at the chain bending over to do so. "Nasty scar." The man said. I reached up to pull the shirt back down where it had ridden up. "I donated a kidney." I said bashfully. I didn't do it for recognition, but because I had two and only needed one. Like the bone marrow donations I made. Twice. I could help so I did. The butcher nodded to me and helped me slid into the backpack he was carrying. It was my backpack but he always insisted on helping me. He donated the meats for the soup kitchen, and even the ribs for the homeless shelter art gallery we did each year to raise money. When I brought my "little brother" by to teach him about pride in your work and how the body was put together, the man never blinked at having a fifteen year old gang member in his shop. By giving the boy a job he helped change his life. Hell the man even donated money for the paint when I organised the park clean up. He was a good man. Socrates was a wise man, but even he, one of the great thinkers, said that every man should know the limits of his body. Should know the joy in being physically fit. I took a lot of the man's words to heart but those doubly so. By the time I reached fifteenth street my legs were burning. Fire raced through my veins and my lungs strained. I heard the sirens of course. How could I not. But stopped before I shot through the intersection wasn't possible. The kids that stole the seat clipped the brake lines. I watched the car come flying at me. "BPM at fifty-seven. Pressure good. Check the levels of..." "Those Fucking kids!" The butcher said. He was always like this. angry at the world. ..... ..... ..... I watched the car approach, but there was no impact. "Two CCs of Norizepa. Where is that EKG reading?" "Those Fucking Kids." There was the car. "Mister Tolin?" Someone asked. I realized my eyes weren't focusing correctly. They kept talking to me but everything was a bit off as if I had been staring at one of those magic eye books. "Mister Tolin?" Hospitable. Smells of steel and sterilite. Woman. No nurse. "What?" I manage to say. She stands up and looks at the big mirror. "Mister Tolin?" She asks again. "Yes that's me." I manage to say. It seems my legs are okay, though one foot is in a cast. She is writing something down on her clipboard. I finger my ear. Something sounds odd. A weird background noise I can't identify. "Do you know where you are?" She asks. "Hospitable." I say. My throat is extremely dry. The door flies open. A man tackled by three others as he burst into the room. "Abomination!" He screams over and over as they men drag him out. The nurse leaves for a while then returns. "I'm sorry about that." She says. "Some people just need more help than others." I say. She stops writing and looks at me for a long time, then glances at the large mirror and back to me. "I can see why they choose you." She says. Then she leaves again. Suddenly I have to piss so badly I cringe. I make it to the small bathroom and take two seconds to hit the bowl I'm pissing so hard. I'll clean it up of course. The nurses have enough on their hands, like that disturbed man, that they don't need to clean up my piss. On the way back to my bed I identify the sounds. They are coming from outside. The curtains are pulled of course. but when they are opened the sounds grows louder. There are people stretched out as far as I can see. Picket signs and candles burning in the near dawn light. I open the window and the sound crashes over me. Angry loud noises. This isn't a crowd of happy people. "Come away from there sir." A male voice says behind me. I turn to see what can only be called a private security man. The guys they pay ten dollars an hour don't stay in that good of shape or wear that many items on their belt. "What is happening?" I ask. The man maneuvered me to the bed and closes the window. Then he picked the TV remote up and slips it over to a channel. "Road to hell is paved with good intentions!" A man screamed. "And that's why we can't have a discussion with these religious types." Another man says when that person was muted. They still are frantically waving their arms but no sound is coming out. "If you thought there was a war between those people too ignorant to read their history and see this isn't a christian nation before Mr. Lazarus, we actually have these people, who say they believe in Christ and his teachings. Mind you turning the other cheek was one of those teachings. We have these people killing people. Day three, the man still sleeps and we are at six hundred and forty three deaths. The fringe Muslims are saying this man may be the son of god. While the fringe Christians, and even the soccer mom Christians are saying he's the Antichrist. People this was simply a medical procedure. I mean come on. In a hundred years they are going to call this Detroit's witch hunt. So they bring a dead guy back to life. Why aren't we as a nation celebrating." "Have you read about this guy? Shit this is the guy the should bring back, I mean..." He picked up a piece of paper form his desk. "This guy served in Iraq, took seven bullets pulling his interperter from a burning truck. He donated over a gallon of blood in his life, gave a kidney, two bone marrow transplants. All for strangers mind you. He helps out in the soup kitchens and homeless shelters. He fucking volunteers to do peoples taxes. Are you kidding me. This guy deserves to live! And they are arguing in court about whether or not to pull the plug on him. I mean "Hold on folks. We have confirmation Mr. Lazarus is awake." The image cuts over to an old brick building with a lot of windows. The video is shaky but he can see one of the curtains pull back and then the window open. "That's me." I say slowly.

article: Would you have believed that it could happen, if you'd been in my place? I've seen countless heist movies and even experienced a couple of armed robberies firsthand as a teller. But a 4 year old little girl? How would that even be suspect? We like to give back to the community and kids who love their parents bank are likely to stay customers when they grow up. So, any kid whose parent opens a Junior Saver account with us can ask me, the head teller, to be a junior banker for the day. We start the day off with a tour of the place - you know, behind the counter to see the computers, running a stack of hundreds through the counters, and then back to the vault. Then the kid picks a teller to work with all day. The teller is in charge of the kid, and oh, do the parents love a day free of their sweet children! Today was the day that the Smythes brought in little Susie for her junior banker day. We've had it on the books for a couple of weeks, since they opened her Junior Saver account. After I gave her the grand tour, I handed her off to Danielle for the day. Little Susie was just full of all sorts of questions, according to Danielle. Normal kid things, like how high each teller can count, how much can we hold in our vault, and how many silly people came through each day. After awhile, Susie lost interest in all things banking and went to the area we keep toys and entertainment in for when our Junior bankers go back to being kids while they're parents are still away on their day off. I had forgotten Susie was even with us today, until I heard the vault alarm going off and Susie wailing from behind the door. When we got the door open, Susie sniffled and cried out for her mommy, whom we called post haste. We made sure Susie had her things - her dolly, her blanket, and her backpack with her snacks and juice boxes, which she hadn't touched. It was hours later when we realized that the problems with the computer system weren't just software glitches - money was actually being funneled from our account holders' accounts into an off-shore untouchable account belonging to a "Mr. Bear." When we reviewed the security footage, it became obvious. Susie watched Danielle login in to the system and scribbled down the letters Danielle typed. Same thing with Michael, Julia, and even myself. She hid out in the vault and no one noticed, we closed the door after a client was done with his safety deposit box, not realizing she was in there. When she woke up from her nap, she started crying for mommy and daddy. When the Smythes picked up their daughter, I heard her state plainly "I want Mr. Bear!" Her father shushed her and said "Now, now pumpkin, you know we're leaving on a plane this evening to go see your beloved Mr. Bear. Did you have a good day at the bank with the nice bankers?" "Yes daddy, I want to be a banker when I grow up!" "I'm sure you'll be great with money, kiddo."

article: It's been 3 years since the explosion that ended my life. I was one of the lucky ones, killed instantly, didn't feel a thing. What I couldn't figure out at first was why I was still around. I soon realized that I was a ghost, bound to the place where I died. It was a strange feeling, being invisible and unable to interact with the world as I used to. But I found that I could still observe and learn about the living, and sometimes even influence their actions. Over the years, I've watched as my family and friends struggled to move on without me. I've seen how they've changed and grown, and it's been both comforting and heartbreaking to see how much they still care for me. I've also witnessed the aftermath of the explosion and the impact it had on the community. It's a tragedy that never truly goes away. Despite being a ghost, I've found ways to occupy myself. I've become an observer of human behavior, watching people in their daily lives and trying to understand what makes them tick. It's been fascinating, but also frustrating to not be able to interact with them directly. Sometimes, I've tried to make my presence known, to reach out to my loved ones and let them know I'm still here. But it's never quite worked out the way I wanted it to. They can sense something, but they can't see or hear me. As time passes, I wonder what will become of me. Will I be stuck here forever, watching the world go by? Or will I eventually find a way to move on, to find peace and rest? It's a mystery, and one that I hope to solve one day.

article: Richard shivered as the sun rose on another bitterly cold February morning. He looked out over the castle ramparts, past the burned and snow-covered fields, to the French army that surrounded the remnants of the castle's garrison. Sharp pangs of hunger lent a temporary distraction from the frigid and peaceful dawn. And then the screaming began. He didn't want to look. Indeed, his empty guts churned at the thought of what was about to happen, but Richard owed it to the boy to bear witness. It was Richard himself who had asked William to flee the castle in the night, and against impossible odds, attempt to slip unseen through the French lines. Richard had given the boy a small dagger, and had made him swear a sacred oath, that if capture seemed imminent, he would turn the blade on himself. It now seemed that William had faltered at the fateful moment, and now, God have mercy, he had been captured alive. The trio of French soldiers had paraded him out into the open field, directly in front of the castle's portcullis. They were close enough that the starving men within could see, but too far away for an arrow to reach. Richard watched them drive stakes into the frozen ground with heavy mallets, and then, stretch the boy's gaunt arms and legs wide, where they methodically tied his limbs. Richard saw with growing despair that the boy was still fully clothed. A pity. If they had stripped him naked, the boy might have only suffered until the cold stayed his heart. The French soldiers had brought no wood, so William could not even hope for the swift death of being burnt alive. To his credit, William faced his fate with bravery far beyond his meager years. Even when one of the men knelt between his outstretched legs, he neither flinched, nor wept. Richard couldn't see exactly what they were doing from atop the castle, but judging by the way William's voice jumped in pitch from screams to shrieks, Richard knew they were slowly mashing the boy's genitals between two stones. Richard had seen the bodies of men that had met a similar fate after being injured, but not killed, on the field of battle against the French. After emasculating him, they would probably use a metal file to grind William's fingers down from fingernail to palm, only pausing when their victim fell unconscious. Richard turned his back on the savagery below, and began to loudly sing the song of his namesake, Richard the Lionheart. The other men on the rampart quickly joined in, their voices nearly drowning out the horrific keening that pierced the still winter air. They sang, and they sang, and they sang, until their chorus was joined by every man yet breathing within the castle walls. Their brotherhood lent them a measure of courage in the face of utter hopelessness. William had been their last chance of relaying a message that might have brought hope of reinforcements. At midday, the French soldiers untied the boy, and dragged him back to their tents. Richard prayed that William's immortal soul had fled to the comfort of Heaven, but Richard was not naive enough to believe the boy could so easily escape from being made a carnal plaything of the French soldiers. After the atrocities the English had inflicted on the French following the Third Crusade, (and again after the Battle of Gisors) Richard could hardly blame them for their cruelty. It had been six long months that they had been surrounded and besieged within the castle. Even with strict rationing, their food ran out within the first month. Then they ate the dogs. Then the horses. Then the rats. Then their leathers. Then the frozen bodies of the men that had not died of disease. And at last, they were left with baked dirt and dung wafers. That night, the surviving castle garrison, and the handful of unlucky mercenaries who had found themselves on the wrong side of the castle walls when the French arrived, decided they would mount a frontal assault on the fortified French encirclement. They would be outnumbered 5 to 1, with many of them too weak to swing a heavy weapon with lethal force, but it would be better to die with steel in hand than to starve, especially if they could take some of those French wound-fuckers with them. That night, the men within the castle slept with the surprisingly comforting knowledge that tomorrow, if they were lucky, they would see their last sunrise. Part II to follow.

article: Sprawled on the bathroom floor, my body slumped in submission. The crackling of centuries finally catching up, grey hairs sprouting where clumps of brown now disintegrate. My muscles tremble as the skin around them loosen, wrinkles arching and sagging. I become barely bones and the skin that covers. Weakness overwhelms as I struggle to look at them. It was never a dream, they did exist but their influence was beyond what I could have comprehended. I cursed the voices that echoed in my head, that pushed away everyone around me, that ensured I would end up in an asylum. The years spent arguing, rationalizing their presence and pretending everything was fine eventually became too much to bear. They drove off my greatest love, and I finally took my stand. I told them to leave, their occupation was not welcomed, and they agreed. I lie now on this bathroom floor as the spirits of my past evacuate, leaving behind the husk that shunned them. The life rushes from my body as I am left to stand on my own, and all I can utter is "please..... Please, don't go."

article: I was diagnosed with clinical depression in my late teens, though it was likely a part of me years before. I knew about the conversations with my younger self every ten years (everyone did it), and fortunately with the help of therapy and medication I lasted until I was 20. I woke up, eager to see what word I would have on my arm. Looking down, I saw what would keep me going for at least another ten years: "LIVE." From that moment forward, I did my best to keep a positive attitude. Through college I volunteered at every chance, and though it took me a while, I eventually graduated with a degree. My parents were thrilled, and things were looking up. I got an internship at a local start-up, started dating a girl I knew from school, and would make sure to look at my arm at least once a day, as though to say "I will." When I was 26, my girlfriend dumped me. It hurt more than you could imagine, and the depression came back in full force. It affected my job, and I was eventually let go. I wound up moving back in with my parents, which didn't help anything but I had little choice in the matter. There were several times I thought about ending it all. But every time, I would look down at my arm and see that four-letter word that always kept me going. Thinking on it, I realized I would be in a better place in my 30s, enough so that I would make sure I'd use the one word to keep my past self alive to see it. Things turned around again when I was 28. I got a new, much better job, and could finally afford a really nice one-bedroom apartment in the city. My colleagues and I got along great, and I wound up dating a coworker's roommate for a while. It didn't last, but I was back out there again, feeling better. The depression retracted, albeit slowly, but it was enough to get me to 30. Seeing my 20-year-old self, I simply instructed him to live. The next day I woke with a smile, pleased with my conversation to help my past self and obsessively curious as to what new word I'd have on my arm this time. Only, there wasn't one. For more eerie stories, check out rZchxz!

article: How long had it been since the first time? Ten years? Twenty? How long had it been since I decided that the world no longer needed me? My entire life has been one mess after another. My parents were killed in a car accident early in life. I was the only survivor; a young child with a severe limp and a scarred face. I was tormented by other children, unable to walk, play, or even interact with other people. I grew up in a foster home dreaming of escaping my own life. Of being somebody. Anybody. It wasn't until I got older that I realized that I wasn't. My intelligence? Mediocre. My talents? Commonplace. My luck? Abysmal. The clock ticks. A sharp, nagging reminder that pulls of me out of my reverie and reminds me of all my failures. The universe taunting me in short measured increments, goading me to try again. How many times has it been now? 48? No..... 49. Maybe 50 will be my lucky number? I feel the cold metal of the revolver in my hand. It's been so long, but I vaguely remember the first time I ever lifted a gun. As I pressed the barrel to my temple, I remember being surprised at just how heavy it was. Maybe it was just the weight of my actions. Back then I still believed they meant something. I remember steeling myself for what I was about to do. I was so tired. I couldn't stand it any longer. As I began to squeeze the trigger, a sharp rap at my door startled me. I flinched and the gun went off. The bullet whizzed past my head, leaving a red line across my forehead and a hole in the wall of my apartment. The UPS man stormed through my unlocked door. The fucking UPS man, a look of terror and disgust on his face as he saw me sitting alone in the living room holding a gun with the scent of singed hair and gunpowder filling the room. He immediately ran screaming for help. It was only a matter of time until my landlord and the police showed up. The worst part? I never did get my security deposit back because of that damn hole in the wall. The cops took me away because I needed "help." That wasn't the case, though. I just needed release. I needed escape. I was institutionalized for two years. I learned to play the part of the recovering patient, but every night all I could think of was the sweet freedom of death. They didn't understand. They couldn't. I was finally released from that awful padded prison and I managed to get a small rented room. A week later I was ready to try again. To make attempt number two. I took a razor blade to my wrists, laid down on the carpet, and tried to die. As I slipped out of consciousness, I felt this sense of pride as my essence formed a warm puddle beneath me. I finally achieved what fate had denied me two years ago. I woke up in the hospital with bandages on my arms. Apparently my landlord found me and called for an ambulance. I never got the security deposit back for that place either. Fucking carpet. I managed to get myself out of bed before the doctors could notice I'd left. I walked alone and defeated through the night. I felt miserable. I felt like a failure. What type of sick loser tries to kill himself twice and can't finish the job? I was never good at anything, and apparently suicide was no exception. The next few tries were quicker, simpler, and more discreet. I went to a pharmacy and stole as many boxes of pain pills as I could put my hands on. I swallowed them all in an alley and passed out. I woke up the next morning feeling fine. I saw a few weeks later that the company recalled the drugs. Bad batch. I snuck into a stranger's garage and hotwired their car. I passed out in the driver's seat, only to be woken up the next day by a man yelling at me and banging on the windows. Apparently all I did was wear his car battery out. He kicked the shit out of me but left me alive. I tried and I tried and I tried again. I jumped off of a bridge. I woke up on the shore nearby. I set myself on fire. The sprinkler system turned on. I tried to freeze to death. I woke up the next morning covered in snow but very much alive. I tried to hang myself. Three times actually. Two leather belts and one synthetic braided rope. All three snapped in half and each time I fell unceremoniously onto the ground in a heap of tears and shame. No failure hurt more than the bus. That fucking bus. I waited for the perfect time and leapt into the roadway with my eyes closed. I felt a sharp impact and heard a sickening thud. The kind that gets you right in the gut. I opened my eyes when I realized I was lying on the pavement. A bystander had pushed me out of the way and been crushed by 14 tons of merciful steel. That lucky bastard. That should have been me. How many times was it again? 49 tries. 49 failures. I stare at the wall in front of me. The stock white of another empty apartment. It's almost funny that I still live like my life is temporary. Fate has proven otherwise. It feels like the universe is Kathy Bates, breaking my ankles over and over again until I write some story that I don't have in me. It's like God wasn't satisfied taking my happiness; he also needed my free will. Lucky number 50. Maybe this time it will stick. I look down at the plastic tarp underneath me as I crack a rare smile around the barrel of the gun. Maybe I'll at least get the security deposit back on this place. Edit - Typos
label: human

article: It felt surreal. Cloudy. Like nothing was actually real, all a figment of my imagination. But there I was, waiting to stand before the world's media to announce the decision that our government had come to. The decision that would result in the deaths of millions. There would be riots and mass chaos, and I'd surely be the victim of dozens of planned assassination attempts. Me being president and all. But in a few days, nothing would matter. For the survival of the Planet and for all Humankind, the United States of America would allow itself to be destroyed by foreign nuclear attacks. If we fought back, no one, not one single life would survive on this rock we called earth. "You're on in 10!" I walked forward, step by step, mak - FLASH! An unbelievable light blinded all. The rumbling started. All went black.

article: I spread my hands apart in a pleading gesture, "We tried to do good, didn't we?" He agrees in silence. I returned my arms to the negligible warmth of the blanket we huddled under. The darkness was like a blanket itself, tightening around us. Soon it would crush us. The air is so thick. I mumbled through numbing lips, "We were great. Humans, I mean. We did so many great things." Silent agreement. I continued, desperate for one last moving speech, one last legacy of our race. "We were great. We learned so much about our world. About space." A whispered, "Too much," gave me pause, but I battled on relentlessly, despite the darkness clutching at my throat. "We built great civilizations. We cured diseases. We were great." My companion rasped, "Too great," before breaking off to give a strangled cough. The air is so thick. I tried to continue. The human race deserved so much more than I could offer, in this last breath of humanity. I can not breath. We were so great.
label: human

article: For the seventh day straight it rained. This was no passing shower but a massive, unending wave of driving rains that flooded everything in its path. Karen and her family were on the run to the Colorado mountains where she hoped her new family would be safe. The problem was that everyone else in the U.S. was trying to get to high ground as well by any means necessary. Roads were clogged with traffic as millions of people fled the low areas of the country like rats from a sinking ship. On the clacking emergency radio Karen hear the automated message system give the latest reports on the flooding. "Florida is now completely underwater along with most of the east coast. Please evacuate Mississippi as the state will be underwater within the hour." The reports had been coming in more and more frequently. Millions were dead already. Yesterday the upbeat announcer had been replaced by the automated system. The president had stopped giving updates on the situation around the world and had last said that prayers should be said for Australia.

article: The old Cartex clock on my credenza loudly drops the 9 flap, indicating 10:59 - one minute to make my decision. I've already measured it out - 23 feet from my doorstep to the street light under which I'm to meet the cab. 302. Yellow. Driver, I'm assuming, to take me..... somewhere. The letter itself was nothing special. Handwritten with a fountain pen in a flowing script. Looked a hundred years old, but no matter. All it said was, "He's gone now. I know you've been watching. Your turn. 11 pm, cab 302." Nothing special. Just, y'know. All of a sudden a letter shows up, no postmark. I think I'm trying to convince myself not to go as I walk out the door. In a yellow pool of sodium vapor light, the white light of headlamps wipe my shadow from the face of the earth. All I can think in that moment is that this could be the last I see of what I thought up until now was a pretty good life. The cab stops. 302. The door opens. I pause, my heart pounding. I realize that I haven't taken a breath since the headlamps swung around the corner. I also realize that I can hear someone breathing - it sure as hell isn't me. Hell. Uh-oh. I get into the car. There is a driver. He says nothing. Figures. The cab moves away from the curb. Away from my normal little life. Job, bike, food, music, friends..... trends. Maybe this is why the last guy did this every night. The sudden realization that his life sucked. I didn't think my life sucked until I was invited into cab 302. Whatever the hell that means. Hell. I did it again. What is the deal with my gut when I say hell? I look out the window of the cab - it is the natural thing to do in a cab. But I can't see anything. Windows must be blacked out - not sure why I didn't realize that earlier. Pretty sure my mother taught me better than that. Maybe not, since I'm in the back of a cab, with a driver of unknown..... origin, headed to wherever I was invited, and..... hell. That's where I'm going. It's suddenly clear. I'm going to hell. "So, when do you kill me?" I ask the driver. A deep, throaty laugh echoes in the cab like it's a cave. The driver stands up and turns to look at me. First thing I notice is that the driver is standing up in the cab. Second thing I notice is that we aren't moving. Third thing is that the driver isn't human. Fourth is that I'm not scared. The Driver invites me in the deepest voice I've ever heard to stand up and step forward. I do so, because, well, really, why not? He asks if I'm sorry I came. I tell him no, although I'm not sure why. I'm not sorry, I suppose, but I sure as hell am wondering what made me come. Hell. I don't swear as a rule, but something about this stupid place is bringing out a strange side of me. I'm filled with a bizarre calmness that is terrifying. He asks me if I'm happy with my life. I tell him no, although I was until 20 minutes ago; I assume that's how long we've been gone - really I have no idea. He asks me if I want to know the secret to a happy life. I tell him no - in a split second I realize that if I know the secret to happiness it will rob me of happiness. He asks me if I want to go home - I'm starting to wonder what the point of this is. Maybe this is actually hell - stupid questions from some guy..... thing..... ad infinitum. I tell him yes. Figured I should change things up a bit. He nods and walks away. With him goes any traces of light. In the bizarre world of whatever-the-hell-this-is, I'm plunged into darkness. My mind races, my eyes dart, my blood pounds, and I desperately wish I would have said "no." Being somewhere unknown with someone unknown is one thing. Being somewhere alone with no one in utter darkness is totally different. The Driver's voice echoes through the cab-chamber-cave. I can't tell what he's saying, but his bass voice is accompanied by a treble hiss. The hiss gets louder and louder. The voice gets quieter and quieter. The darkness starts to lift, like a fog; the hiss doesn't go away. It gets louder. It's my fridge. What the hell? I'm back in my living room as the Cartex drops its flaps and hits 11 pm. My fridge is hissing. My eyes are heavy. As I fall asleep I know I sure as hell will be under that street light tomorrow at 11 pm. What in the world was that?
label: human

article: Freddie and Helen Kissinger had lived on 15 Elm Street in the small town of Nottingdale, Indiana, for the last forty-five or so years of their lives. Freddie was a school principal at the local elementary school, Helen taught music at the same school. Freddie had advanced cirrhosis of the liver that was expected to be untreatable at his age, and Helen had been coughing up blood from the tears in her stomach lining that had come up as a result of some parasitic infection or another. They were ready. Sort of. Helen squawked from the bed, " Did you leave the letter for the kids? " Freddie quavered, " Yes, dear, it's behind the screen door. " " What about the dog? " " The dog died two years ago. " " Leave some cookies out on the porch for the kids when they stop by. " " I did at noon. " " What-what about the garden? " " Helen, who gives a shit? We're going to die. " It was a beautiful day outside. The petunias swayed in perfect formation, the sun beat down through the windows of the little isolated house on the lonely road coming out of town. Freddie kicked the dog on the way upstairs, with his sleeping pills in hand. Four of them would kill an adult human, and Freddie wasn't exactly sure if either of them still qualified as either of those things. He wore his dress blues, while Helen wore her Sunday best. He had to coerce her into taking off the plumed hat before she settled down. He gave eight pills to her, and eight to himself. Little nuggets of death lying in the dusty bowl of his time-worn palm. He was ready, and looking at Helen, his wife of sixty-three years, he knew she was ready too. They mouthed the words together. One. Two. Three. Freddie palmed the pills. They lay clutched in his hand, and he sighed and leaned back as if he had done something momentous. He stuffed them under the covers. He lay down and waited for his wife to die. Fifteen minutes later, he heard his wife's breathing slow. It was time. He carefully got out of bed. He didn't have cirrhosis. He just drank a lot and hated his wife. He looked outside. He was ready. He stepped out of the room with a boundless energy he hadn't felt since he graduated high school. He clattered down the stairs and clicked his heels. Suddenly, " YOU DICKLESS BITCH, I KNEW YOU DIDN'T TAKE THOSE PILLS. " Fuck. He grabbed the shovel and went upstairs.
label: human

article: When the cold splash of water hit my face, I felt as if I just returned from a distant place. My eyes opened to see Pastor Roland holding an empty bucket and grinning at me. "Good morning, sleepyhead!" he said, handing me a towel. I groaned and wiped my face. "What time is it?" "It's time for breakfast, and we have a big day ahead of us," he replied, still smiling. I rubbed my eyes and followed him out of the room. As we walked down the hall, I couldn't help but feel grateful for Pastor Roland's energy and enthusiasm. Even though I didn't always share his beliefs, I admired his spirit and kindness. As we sat down to eat, he told me about our plans for the day. We were going to volunteer at a local shelter, helping feed and care for the homeless. It was something I had done before, but I was glad to have the opportunity to do it again. After breakfast, we loaded up the van and headed to the shelter. As we worked, I felt a sense of purpose and fulfillment. It was a reminder that even in the midst of difficult times, there were ways to make a difference and help those in need. As we finished up and drove back to the church, I turned to Pastor Roland and said, "Thank you for helping me remember what's truly important." He smiled and patted my shoulder. "That's what I'm here for."

But sometimes it can be tough to stay positive when I see the immense challenges that these birds face. Habitat destruction, climate change, and poaching are just a few of the threats that they face. However, I remind myself that every bird that we release is a small victory, and that every life that we save is important. I also seek out support from my colleagues and friends who share my passion for bird conservation. Together, we can make a difference and help protect these amazing creatures for generations to come.

article: The last thing I remembered was a massive explosion and the lights going dead, followed by scream of terror outside the prison bars. I squeezed Leeroy as tight as I could and then something hit me in the head and I blacked out. I woke up and kept my eyes tightly shut, muttering over and over "Forgive me, forgive me, forgive me." Eventually the building stopped shaking and the lights began to flicker back on. Daring myself to open my eyes, I peeked through my hair that was hanging in front of my face. They were all dead and my cell door was hanging on its hinges. Looking around I saw that all the prison cell doors were ripped off or hanging open. There was no one else in sight. "We need to go" Leeroy whispered to me softly, "Don't look down, just walk I'll tell you where to go." He said calmly. Thank God I had him, I don't know what I would have done. I didn't look at anything, not even at Leeroy, but I listened intently to the sounds around me. "Wait." Leeroy said as I stepped over one of the guards on the ground, I tried hard not to look but I couldn't help it. The guard was very dead, his insides spilling onto the cold, hard concrete. "Oh God, Leeroy, what happened. They're all dead..... Leeroy, they are all dead." I whispered, my voice harsh and trembling. "Shut up- listen." He said quietly. I did as I was told, after all Leeroy always led me straight. I could hear music playing somewhere below me, and as I stood over the dead guard listening, a voice could be heard, a man, singing along with the music. The voice was growing louder, getting closer as I stood, squeezing my eyes shut again to avoid being sick from the sights around me. Everyone had been ripped to pieces. Then I heard a door swinging on its hinges and footsteps getting closer every second, the pace of them speeding up. "Move, move now, get behind the wall. Someone's coming." Leeroy said urgently. I jumped over the corpse, and dodged a few others and hid behind the south facing wall. There was a hole blown out through the stone wall, I could see army vehicles over turned, more people lying on the ground outside, blood everywhere. I held my breath, clutching desperately at Leeroy who was presumably also holding his breath. How he always remained so calm in these sorts of situations always blew my mind. "Oppa is Gangnam style!" The male voice shouted, only feet away from me on the other side of the wall. I shut my eyes tight, willing him to stay where he was and leave me alone, I had had enough, I didn't want to be used like this anymore. The music got louder and the quality of it was more defined, it sounded like it was being played on a cell phone with a low grade speaker. "I know you're in here, come out come out where ever you are!" The voice said coyly. I knew it was pointless to try and hide from Wolfgang, he was a menace. A tyrannt who had discovered what I was and had manipulated me to the brink of suicide..... unfortunatly, nothing I had tried had ever worked..... it only ended in death for everyone but me, and Leeroy of course. Wolfgang jumped out from around the corner, I had been expecting it, but it startled me none-the-less. "Ah ha!" He proclaimed, "I knew you wouldn't be too hard to find." He said happily, "Come on little miss, and bring you're little friend, we've got some more work to do." He said. My stomach dropped and I felt sick. This was torture. I followed him down the stairs carefully, the entire building was in shambles, the foundation barely holding the whole thing up. I knew as soon as I would exit, it would all crash down behind me, and it did as I stepped out what was left of the door. He made for the gate and the only vehicle that was still standing upright, motor running. "Forgive me, Forgive me, Forgive me..." I repeated out loud, over and over. Wolfgang didn't even bother to look at me, he was used to this by now. "It's not your fault Mecca, you know it's not your fault." Leeroy said softly, only loud enough for me to hear him. I looked at the stuffed yellow duck in my hands and realized that once again, my hands, along with most of the clothes I was wearing, were covered..... soaked, in blood. I wanted to scream, I wanted to do what I had done to all those people in the prison to Wolfgang, but I knew it wasn't possible. He was too smart, too cautious, he had made me into what I was and he knew damn well how to control me. So, I did nothing. With tears welling up in my eyes I walked towards the amphibious green army range rover. Wolf opened the door an I climbed in, sliding over to the far seat. I didn't want to be anywhere near that monster. He smiled as he saw my disgust. "Don't be upset Meccy, it's all for the greater good, you know that. You want all of these phsycos to be in control of the worlds deadliest weapons? Global pandamonium, you've seen it, you know what happens when contires possess technology they can't handle." Wolfgang said casually as he climbed in beside me. I inched away further, clutching Leeroy tightly to my body, he was covered in blood too. "Well, that's pretty fucked up if that's what you want..... these Koreans don't know how to handle this kind of thing. They needed to be taken out of the picture, you know that." He continued. I said nothing, just sat gripping Leeroy as tightly as possible. "Next stop, Washington." He said with a smile. I knew immediately what he had planned, he was going to use me again, to take out the president and his entire elect team. The white house would be reduced to ruble by the end of the week. "Why are you doing this..... Why did you make me kill them..... I don't want to kill anyone any more, please. Please let me go." I whispered. Wolfgang started laughing a maniacal laugh, then his face grew serious. "Don't ask stupid questions." He said bluntly. I wanted to rebel so desperately, blow up the Range rover with all of us inside, but Lord knows I had tried that before and it didn't end well. He had built me to be resistant to myself, he was resistant as well, and Leeroy..... well, I never really knew what Leeroy was. I imagine he was only for comfort..... and he was, I never let him out of my sight, let alone my grip if at all possible. Wolfgangs phone rang in his hand, he was still listening to Gangnam Style when the song stopped and rang. It scared me and I flinched. A stupid move, Wolfgang saw it out of the corner of his eye. "Don't be scared little pretty, only the telephone." He said as he slid a finger across the screen, unlocking the phone then putting it to his ear. "Ya, what's going on?" He asked. "Ya, I got her..... all of them. Dead, no survivors, the place looks like Chernoble." He said with a smile. "We'll be boarding in less than an hour, we'll see you tonight. Yes, everything is in order. Did you manage to replace those Secret service dicks in Washington? We can't have any flaws on this one, we'll only have one shot." He said calmly. "Okay, I'll see you later. Let's go supernova on that asshole." He finished, then hung up and looked at me and Leeroy. Then he reached in his pocket and pulled out his trusty Berkeley Nucleonics Isotopic Identifier and scanned me. "Well little miss, you did it again. Good job." He said as he read the calibrations and confirmed that I was in no way harming any of us. He had turned me into a nuclear weapon..... and used me against anyone who posed a threat..... he WAS the threat..." All in the name of the greater good, right?" I whispered. Before I could react he smacked me hard across the face. "Now that's no way to talk to your Daddy is it..... you little bitch." He said bitterly. Leaning forward to address the driver, he said quietly, "Get us to the airport, I've had enough of North Korea for the rest of my life I think." Smiling he turned to me and whispered. "Next stop Washington."
label: human

article: I hold the phone to my ear in disbelief. "Bullshit." The voice in my ear keeps talking. "In Times fucking Square?" Let me give you a bit of backstory. I'm John Kilburn, and I work for the Bureau of Paranormal Activity. And today there's an honest-to-fucking-god dragon flying around Times Square, and I'll bet you any sum of money that people are standing around taking cellphone videos of it. My phone rings one more time. "What is it now?" The desk agent responds, "You can't use your usual equipment. This is too public." "What, you want me to kill a dragon with my bare hands?" I have a multitude of other options: Grenades, plasma rifles, stun guns, a railgun, and a dart gun. Lots of goddamned sci-fi guns to not use. With a slight chuckle, he replies, "No. With a sword." "How in the fuck..." I put my face in my hands in disbelief, "How in the fuck is killing it with a sword any better?" "It'll look like you're putting on a show. Tourist attraction or some shit. We'll get you the sword on your way there." I'm only a few blocks away, so I start running towards Times Square. A block out, an agent stops me and hands me my weapons- a sword and shield. "Press the button on the sword to energize these." I don't even respond- I'm already too pissed off that it's the twenty-first century and I've got to go fight this thing like King fucking Arthur. I just pick up the weapons and go, sprinting until the dragon is in my field of vision. And this is one ugly son of a bitch- brown scaly skin, frail wings, black teeth the size of my hand. I prime my sword and shield- they both hum with blue energy, probably some kind of plasma tech. I hear a voice in my earpiece- "John. The sword is broadcasting an infrasonic signal to attract the dragon." "Why in God's name would that be a good idea?" I glance at the dragon as it starts lumbering towards me. There's no response, so I start charging at the dragon, swinging my sword at its chest and making a gash two inches deep. The crowd around us cheers, probably thinking this is some kind of show. The dragon charges again, this time raising a claw against me. I hold my sword straight up, stabbing the dragon through the foot and eliciting a roar of pain, accompanied with a breath of fire. Of course this asshole can breathe fire, I thought. The dragon decides to try a new tactic, breathing a bolt of fire at me. I barely raise the shield in time and the flames disperse around me, just barely deflected. The dragon starts to flap its wings, slowly but surely rising up into the sky. I jump off an information stand to try and stab it, but it's out of reach- I fall and skid to the ground, my sword scraping the concrete. I look around, wondering how to attack the dragon. I decide there's only one way to win this fight before anyone gets hurt- I reach into the inside of my leather jacket, pulling out a small, collapsible gun that extends into a longer rifle. I get on one knee and aim upwards, my eye aligning with the sights. Taking a deep breath, I hold down the trigger, a sustained bolt of plasma burning into the creature's skin. It starts falling slowly at first, then dropping like a rock, crashing to the ground. "Sword and shield, my ass. It's the twenty-first fucking century." A helicopter comes in to retrieve my quarry, and I disappear into the crowd. A voice comes on in my earpiece, and I can't believe what I'm hearing. "A fucking werewolf? It's the middle of the day!"
label: human

article: Gram is a bit of a legend in our world. She's only one of a dozen or so known mind readers in all mutant history, and one of only a handful who used those powers for good. She spent decades of her long life thwarting the deeds of dictators, preventing killing sprees, and steering technology toward the betterment of humanity. She is considered a priceless gem by mutants and humans alike. And I just want her out. Don't get me wrong. I love her. But the dementia seems to have unleashed a certain rebellious side of her that is completely out of control. Luckily she hasn't done anything dangerous, and it's actually closer to impetuousness than anything else, but it's driving me crazy. But, she's a freaking legend. Apparently she's allowed to do whatever she wants and people find it charming. She could commit murder right in front of a police station and they'd manage to justify it. " After all the good she's done... " then lead her by the elbow into the station and feed her tea and cookies. Doesn't sound so bad? Well guess who gets the brunt of it. She thinks it's hilarious to mess with me. She'll respond to my thoughts as if I were saying them out loud, and will provoke me into thinking weird stuff just so she can declare it to the world. She literally points at me and laughs. I've grown up an only child, but when Gram moved in it was like I inherited a mean older sister. Last week she made me leave the house with my underwear on top of my clothes. The worst part is that she's sneaky. People don't even realize half the stuff she does, because she's a master of entrapment. On Friday I had a girl over while my parents were out to dinner. I snuck her in, hoping that Gram wouldn't open her mind and sense what was happening. That was a mistake. Five minutes into a heavy make-out session we could hear her creaky voice on the other side of the door: " Aaaand up comes the little guy! " How am I supposed to live like this? I love her because she's my Grandma, and I respect her because she was an incredible woman. My parents tell me I need to be patient. Sometimes they even get frustrated when I complain, and remind me that I'll be leaving for college in three years and I'll probably miss having my Gram so close by. But I can't wait for college. There are challenges that come along with being a mutant in a prominently human environment, but at least I won't be the only kid in school with an 80-year-old bully.
label: human

article: Am I dead? A few mornings ago - I'm not even sure how long ago - I woke up. I felt very much alive. The sun was bright, the trees swaying in the breeze, the sky was blue, and not a person was there. There was an unusual silence through the empty streets. At first I had thought that maybe, for some unimaginable reason, the neighbourhood was evacuated, and they somehow forgot about me. I don't know what happened. I rang every doorbell in town, knocked at more doors than I have ever in my entire life. And at each doorstep, that gut-wrenching feeling of being..... left behind, became more and more concrete. Where are the Smiths? The Jacksons? The Rhodes'? At each doorstep, at each unfamiliar name, I would pray that someone would open the door. I thought - am I stuck in a twisted dream? Is this all one huge, merciless joke? Have I gone insane? I walked, and walked, in hope of finding some other desperate soul, searching like me. Now I realize. I have died, and I'm in Hell.

They both stood up and resumed their escape, moving quickly through the empty streets until they reached the outskirts of town. It wasn't until they were safely in their car that they finally allowed themselves to relax. As they drove away, James couldn't help but think about what they had just witnessed. The shadows that had been following them were unlike anything he had ever seen before. They were dark and twisted, almost alive in the way they moved. He shook his head, trying to clear his thoughts. Whatever it was, they were safe now. They could put this behind them and move on with their lives. But deep down, James knew that whatever had been following them was still out there, waiting for the opportune moment to strike again.

article: "Liam..... Liam, honey, wake up," The bed was beginning to shake, "Honey, you really have to get up now, okay?" "Just, like, 20 more minutes Ma," The shaking slowly subsided. "Honey, we don't have 20 minutes, you have to get up now..." Liam's mother poured water on his head, causing him to spring up with enough violence to knock over his bedside lamp. "What the hell Mom, what is so goddamned important that you had to wake me up with," he glanced at his clock, now on the floor beside the broken lamp "3 hours of sleep?!!? Geez Ma..." After a few calming breaths Liam settled back onto the bed, the wetness of his wake up call seeping through his pajama shirt, and he looked over at his mother, who had retreated to the door, knowing full-well what reaction Liam would have to her chilly good morning. Liam's concern over his bed's wetness turned to dismay as he took in what his mother was wearing, an army green tank top with forest-camo cargo pants and a massive backpack, loaded down so completely he was surprised it didn't burst it's seams. "Liam, we have to go, now, your father is already preparing the truck and, knowing him, it'll be ready by the time you're changed," she said, in that scary calm way that mother's use to avoid panicking their children. "But, is it real this time, it is, isn't it, please, please tell me it's a drill, tell me I'm wrong," Liam wasn't quite panicked yet, he was still trying to work through the dread at what was about to happen, he knew what the camo meant, it meant they were leaving, and probably wouldn't be back for a while, if ever. He couldn't figure out why though, it didn't make any sense, before he went to sleep there hadn't been anything in the news, either mainstream or back-channel, that indicated anything apocalyptic was happening. The economy was generally stable, as stable as ever in fact since the crash a few years ago, and the only wars, cold or hot, were in Asia and Africa. "Honey, NOW!" his mother yelled, he hadn't realized he'd been sitting there stunned. Her yell snapped him back to reality where his training kicked in, he sprung from his bed, far more controlled now without the ice water spurring his movements, and was inside his closet almost instantly. With a pleased nod, his mother hopped the banister behind her to the first floor and was gone, likely to toss her pack in the "truck" and grab anything they may have extra room for. With a swift kick to the side, Liam popped open a false wall in his closet, revealing a bugout bag, his own camo gear, his AK-47, and a decently sized box of pre-loaded magazines. He tried to don his gear swiftly, the way he'd been taught, but nervousness had an icy grip on his chest in a way his training hadn't prepared him for. As such, he tripped while trying to pull his other pant-leg up, landing in a pile of dirty clothes, with his cap on, his green shirt around his neck like a scarf, and an 80lb duffel bag over one shoulder making him feel like a turtle that some petulant child had flipped. He quickly thanked God, Buddha, and The Flying Spaghetti Monster that his brothers weren't here and used his indignation to quiet his nerves, if only for the moment, so he could at least dress properly. Exiting his room, Liam glanced around to find quite a few of his parents knick-knacks out of place, this was disturbing considering his father's borderline OCD concerning his, so-called, "finds." "There must have been a tremor or something, was that what shook the bed?" Realizing he was standing like a doe in the headights, Liam mentally berated his internal monologue. He prepared to vault the banister as his mother had done when he stopped again, looking at himself in the floor-length mirror at the end of the hallway, and he liked what he saw. A vision of the action heroes from the old movies his parents had introduced him to as a child, decked out in his survival gear and AK, all now properly donned, despite his earlier mishaps, if it weren't for the circumstances, he could've stared at himself all day. Instead, the windows began to shake violently and the ear-splitting sound of a sonic boom cascaded through the house, snapping Liam out of his self-reverie. He hopped the banister, landing on the floor below in a crouch, feeling the impact shockwaves cascade through his lower extremities and wishing he had thrown his bag over first, the extra weight made the landing unexpectedly rough. Liam stood and looked around, taking in his childhood home for, most likely, the last time. The couch where he'd had his first kiss, the wall of old gaming consoles he had repaired with his dad, the bathroom where he crawled out the window the first time to sneak out, the liquor cabinet he'd repaired after some friends wrecked it during a party, but it was time to go, he'd always have those memories, even if he wasn't there, Liam turned and bolted for the open front door without looking back. Upon emerging from the house, he stopped, dropping to his knees, mouth agape, staring at the sky in horror. What appeared to be a huge tear had formed in the sky, like some god had unzipped the heavens, but what Liam saw didn't make him think of heaven, no, it was nothing of the sort. Huge tentacles were knurling and whipping around the edges of the tear, almost like they were trying to force it open farther. He couldn't make anything out inside the tear, however, it just seemed to be a mass of purple and black darkening the formerly clear, blue sky. It almost felt as if it were sucking him in, not physically, but mentally, dragging his mind away from his body. As he noticed what was happening to him, the tug on his mind intensified, the more he fought against it, the more agonizing it got and, before he knew it, he heard screaming. But, where was it coming from, he couldn't look away to find the source though. It was close, maybe one of the neighbors? Then muffled speech, but, why was it muffled, and why can't I look away from this damned rift. Rift? When did I start thinking of it as a rift, that implies it leads somewhere, doesn't it? The muffled speech came back again, louder this time, he could almost make out the words now, but they were so distant, and couldn't really be important could they? Damn I wish that screaming would stop, it's driving me..... insane?
label: human

article: I lay in my bed with tears streaming down the sides of my face, staring at the ceiling. "Oh my god," I groaned. My crow fluttered from its perch on my bedpost and cocked its head to look at me with a shining eye. It hummed a sharp note as if asking me what was wrong. I slowly sat up and wiped my face. "This is a disaster. An absolute disaster," I whispered. "Too many emotions," an unexpected sob broke through my voice. My crow looked inquisitively at me. I threw on a dark robe and rushed out of my chamber and down the tower steps. I tore into the kitchen and stretched my hand out, the freezer door slammed open and ice cream flew to my hand immediately. I summoned a spoon and turned it over, looking at my reflection, stroking it with my fingertips. "I charm thee spoon, behold my command, let that love potion fade with every turn of my hand." I stuck the spoon and rotated it through the ice cream, taking a bite after each turn. After a few times, I looked up at my crow who was now pecking at my potted plants on the table. "I think it worked," I breathed. I pointed my spoon at him. "Remind me not to use my enemy's blood in beauty potions again. I accidentally stirred it counterclockwise at the end and it turned into a love potion!" I laughed, aware that I looked completely insane. "Thought it wouldn't affect me because I hate her so much. In fact, I was going to kill her tonight but nope. There I was, in sitting in my room, crying and composing music instead." I ate a large scoop of ice cream. "Absolute disaster," I said again with my mouthful. I heard a loud rush of paws coming down the hall outside the kitchen. Three of my hounds appeared in the doorway, their tails wagging furiously and their ears laid back. They whined high pitched breaths as their bodies trembled. I stood up. "She's escaped?" I asked. The hounds barked and turned to run back down the hall. I scooped a large spoonful of ice cream into my mouth before rushing out to follow them. They led me out of the castle and into the courtyard.Storm clouds blanketed the night sky, hiding the moon. The hounds barked at a muddy hole beside the stone wall of the dungeon. "She tunneled out," I said aloud. My silver staff appeared in my hand. "Find her!" I commanded, pointing the rod at my hounds. I turned into a black mist to follow them as they ran into the darkness of the woods. They howled to each other, communicating as they split off to search the wide expanse of the woods. In the distance, one of the hounds, Checkers, yelped in pain. The other hounds turned immediately in their tracks to find her. We found Checkers laying in a wet puddle on the ground with pain on her head. She whimpered, telling me that the Hero had clubbed her before running forward into the woods. I summoned a blanket over her and did a healing spell over her body, pressing dirt into her fur where she had been hit as a charm and drawing a sigil in the ground beside her. "You will be okay," I whispered. "When you can walk, come back to me." I turned back into mist and the remaining hounds took off in a run, following the scent. The scent suddenly ended in a clearing. My dogs sniffed the air, pawing at the ground to smell the leaves. Rain began to fall. Then, I spotted her. She was trying to hide in a tree but her leg was wounded from a bite from Checkers and the branch she rested on was wobbling. Twigs and leaves were falling, attracting the attention of the hounds below. They barked loudly, locking their eyes on the Hero. I returned to my human form and raised my staff, "Come here," I said in a low voice. The Hero struggled with all her might as I brought her down. She tossed her wet blonde hair aside as I brought her face to face with me. "Stop kidding yourself," she hissed. "You know your powers are weak against me." She was so furious her white teeth were bared at me in a grimace. Her brown eyes were shining and her cheeks were dewy with rain. I felt my chest begin to feel warm as I looked at her. My makeshift antidote hadn't worked afterall. My rod's power did indeed weaken she was dropped the remaining distance to the ground. She let out a cry of pain as she collapsed on her injured leg. I turned away, my hounds tilted their head in confusion at me as I hid an emotional glance from her. I walked a few steps and stared at the ground. "I have to keep you in prison until I can kill you," I said quietly. "You know this won't stop until one of us is dead." I couldn't look at her. "You could never kill me," I heard her say. "You never have and you never will. Your powers are useless against me and you're nothing without them. You're a pathetic, lonely, hag who will never have the power she wants. The only reason I've never killed you is because you're too much of a coward to fight me without protection." She spit at my dogs. I smiled at her fiery response and looked at her at last. Her hair was now completely soaked and hanging over her face, her clothes were almost see-through and she leaned weakly against a tree. She was the only creature in the world to ever match my beauty. I had been blind to it all this time. "Come willingly," I told her. "I can make it worthwhile." "Never," she said savagely. I walked closer, towering over her. She looked up at me with fierceness. My heart ached, looking at her soft skin. I had a wild thought of erasing all of her memories and holding her in my arms as my companion. I imagined us having a life together, ruling the kingdom as one, never being apart. Hearing her laugh and smile at me with affection rather than disdain. I reached out and held her chin in my hand and she flinched. "I can be different for you," I told her softly. Thunder rumbled overhead. "I would change to make you happy. No more dark magic. No more prisoners." She reached up to shove my arm away. "You are a prison. You could never change that." I reached out to her again. "You would never be alone. I would give you anything you ever wanted." She suddenly cried out in pain and fell in a heap against the tree, clutching her wound with both hands. I stood above her, stroking the silver of my staff. "Having you is all I want," I whispered. "If I can't have that, I don't see the point." "What?" she snarled. She looked up from her wound. Her lips were turning darker as the cold began to affect her skin. "I know that I can't bring your family back. Or bring back the people I murdered. I know that you'll never love me," I said loudly. Her stony glare broke for a moment. Her eyes studied my face. "But I know what would make you happy." I summoned a sword with a golden handle that appeared in the hand of the Hero Then, I pointed down at her leg and soothed it with a pain-easing charm and a clean bandage that's magic would keep it dry even in the rain. Her eyes rose to mine and her thick lashes blinked at me. "What kind of trick is this?" she asked quietly. "I could be everything you ever wanted," I said, my voice breaking. "But I know you'll never give me the chance. You'll never want me." "Why would I?" she yelled. "You're a monster!" "I just healed you and gave you a weapon! Isn't that proof that I have your best interests in mind?" "It's too late for any of that. You will never have my mercy." Her last statement hung in the air as it continued to rain. A chill swept over me. Instead of fighting back, I stood before her resolutely. "You've killed me a thousand times," I said in my softest voice. "Not having you is death itself." She stared at me as tears streamed down my cheeks. "Do what you will." She stood for a moment, then looked down at her sword. She picked it up, shifting her weight from her bandaged foot and adjusted her grip. With our eyes locked, she let out a roar and lunged toward me with a burst of frenzied energy. I watched her body, naked through her clothes, as her arm thrust the sword. I only raised my hands for defense at the last moment. She stabbed the sword deep into the left side of my chest and I fell to the ground beneath her. Pain that had been unfathomable to me before tore through my entire being and I coughed blood, grabbing at the soaking leaves on the ground around me. "I love you," I breathed. "I did this for you." She panted, holding the bloody sword for a moment before passing out on the ground beside me. We both lost consciousness from blood loss. But my hounds only brought one of us back.

article: I didn't have time to think before I slammed my foot to the floor. The engine roared loudly, jerking forward with enough force to press me against the leather seat. The loud crunch of the car crashing through the bridge railing and the thunderous sounds of the passing train fell silent as the water quickly approached the train had missed me by inches. When the car hit the water, I felt the seat belt jerk tightly around my chest, knocking the wind out of me. With the phone now submerged underwater and dying quickly, I could hear small crackling of the voice still shouting, but the sound died with the light of the screen. As the car slowly began to sink, I couldn't help but feel more and more panicked, as the water began to rise above my mouth. My first breath burned my lungs with the fire of a thousand suns; I had spent two minutes underwater, struggling to break free. article: (First time writing here. Very slight variation on the prompt. Based loosely on real events.) The last year had been the hardest of her life. Only one person had managed to earn her trust, and he had spent most of the previous months using it against her. He always looked at her with disdain, but by now she felt this was more kindness than she deserved. At least he looked. No one else did. She now sat with him on a balcony, watching her frosted breath diffuse out into the cold night. Her focus, as usual, was on appearing outwardly to be okay, while on the inside she had finally reached the end of her rope and was hanging on by a thread. After a long silence, she looked at him, and asked a question, trying to sound not unhappy, but still serious. "Do you think there's anything in me worth trying to save?" He looked at her with a mixture of confusion and annoyance. He always seemed offended when she showed any sign of having emotional needs, or emotional pain. After a pause, but not too long of one as to require any real investment of energy to have been put into thought, he answered. "Meh. If I can't say anything nice, I shouldn't say anything at all." Silence hung noticeably in the air for a moment, until it slowly transitioned back into the usual, common, un-noteworthy silence. She said nothing, and he perceived no reaction from her. Quietly and unnoticed, her eyes slowly glazed over as she stared out into space at nothing in particular. The light that had struggled for so long to find a way or a reason to remain had finally left them. As the spark faded from her eyes, so faded the tattoo from her ankle. As it slowly appeared on his wrist, he didn't take notice. He didn't even notice it until the next day. He was sure there had been some kind of error, perhaps a drunken mistake made while blacked out. He had the tattoo removed. Her body caught up to her spirit a year or two later, heart failure at an oddly young age. The doctors failed to understand the death of her body, just as he had failed to understand the death of her soul. At least now it was over.

article: I'm not afraid, I know I'm supposed to be, but I just can't help being excited, finally a chance to see the great beyond. Who wouldn't be excited, I had an entire list of things I wanted to get done. My guards were silent and stoic as they escorted me from my cell to cement room with a large plexiglass window, one I recognized from movies. Once in the room I hummed a little tune as I walked ahead of the guards and climbed into the gurney, impatiently waiting for someone to strap me in, as I know they would. "These will be tight," a male wearing a white lab coat patted my arm and placed straps across my arms, elbows, chest, legs, and then my ankles. "Right, Right, Get to it," I said as I waved my hand. "Small poke for the IV," said another man in a lab coat on the right side of me. "Of course," I chirped back to him, pumping my arm a little bit so a good vein popped out. "Button up your shirt, fix your boots," snapped the warden as he entered the room. "I will not be all over the damn news with you men looking unprofessional!" "My dear," said an older chaplain of an undetermined religion, bent over me and spoke softly "would you like to pray with me or confess your sins. Jesus forgives all sins and wrongdoings, if you believe." He must have been to his fair share of bed-side death watches, he looked fatigued and tired but truly wanting to help and maybe he had a hint of pity in his eyes. I thought the least I could do was put his mind at ease. "You know the people in here have done a wonderful job, truly they are top notch professionals, don't you think? They have this killing people down to a science, I feel really good about my situation! I've never done this before ya know," I motioned to my body strapped strategically on the gurney, smiling widely up at him as I continued, "the Lord and I couldn't be any closer and I have never done a thing in my life to offend Him. I think you know that," I winked at the clergyman. He licked his lips, looking a bit unnerved, "Well..... I'm glad you are not under more duress then.... what.... is.... required.... in.... this..... situation," his voice trailed off at the sight of me smiling and nodding to him. He turned and nodded to the warden, and then quickly walked off. The warden said nothing and signaled to the guards and medical staff. The curtains covering the plexiglass window opened. The bed rose and tilted me forward so I could see my audience. There were quite a few more people than what I expected and my eyes took in the crowd. My, my! Aren't I the popular one - standing room only! Grinning in approval, I attempted to nod my head towards many of the faces I recognized as my followers. I saw some cry and others call out.They were going to miss me, but I was content knowing they would carry on easily without me. The speaker crackled, "Prisoner Katherine T. Jenkins has stated that she would like to address the room with final words," the warden's voice filled both the plexiglass room and the viewing room. I could see my followers lean forward to hear my last peals of wisdom, and it warmed my heart. I do so love them dearly! "You may speak," the warden allowed as he pinned a small microphone to my shirt. "Thank you all for coming," I feigned solemnly. It took everything I had not to smile, look at all these people here to see me off! I was beyond thrilled! Some of the audience in the room giggled, others smiled, and still others openly wailed at the sound of my voice. I didn't say anything for a long moment, trying to think of what would be best. There was nothing to be sorry for, so an apology was off the table. I didn't have enough time for a sermon like my followers would want, and then I decided honesty was definitely the best policy. "I have truly enjoyed my time here. And since this is just the beginning for me, I know I will see all of you again....very soon." I smiled with sincerity and honesty in my voice. The roomed hushed for a split second before pandemonium broke out in the viewing room. All at once my followers rushed to the plexiglass window, others started bashing their heads against the wall, while still others had found sharp objects and were stabbing themselves. I laughed in delight! This is how someone should die! Together with the people they loved and as the main event at a party! "I'm ready warden! Stick it to me!" I called over my shoulder as my eyes flashed in merriment, excited for what would come after I left this decaying body of mine.
