Can you tell us anything else?" The bartender shook his head, his voice muffled by his arms. "I'm sorry, I can't.. I just can't.." The officer nodded, his expression filling with sympathy. "It's okay, take your time. We'll try again later." As the policeman turned to leave, the bartender lifted his head slightly. "Wait.. I remember one thing," he said softly. "There was a man, he.. he was acting strange.." "Can you describe him?" the officer asked, quickly pulling out his notebook. "He was tall, wore a dark coat and a hat.. and his eyes.. they were.. they were.." the bartender trailed off, grasping for the right words. The officer waited patiently, his pen hovering over the paper. Finally, the bartender spoke in a hushed voice. "His eyes were like.. like the eyes of a snake.. cold and unforgiving.." The officer scribbled down the description, his eyes narrowing in thought. "Thank you. We'll do our best to find this man." article: As a kid, he haunted my dreams. My worst nightmare was him being in my bed when I woke up, but this wasn't a dream. This was real wasn't it? I back away from the door, but the King kicks it open. It has to be a man in a mask. It has to be, but he is adorned in the entire getup. Not a word is spoken by either of us. He points to the bathroom. What did he want? Maybe this is a prank. Hopefully, it is. I walk into the bathroom and wait for my fate. "What are you going to do to me? Please don't hurt me." The King points to the floor. I sit. He holds his hand in a stop motion. He heads back to the main room. Shotgun blasts rattle my ears. Other gunshots ring out. I peek out the door and see the King blast the Hamburglar in the face. The King turns to look at me, a blank unchanging expression on his face. He leans down and picks up the Hamburglar's handgun and hands it to me. He waves for us to go. "Can't I stay here?" The King shakes his head. He pats me down and finds my car keys. He heads to the parking lot and finds my car without any help. I hop into the passenger seat, and he takes off to an unknown location. I look behind us, and I finally understand what he's running from. Ronald McDonald, Gidget the Taco Bell chihuahua, and Colonel Sanders give chase, and they're catching up to my Prius. The King motions for me to take the wheel. I slide over and start driving. He leans out the window and fires at the mascots who chase us. I watch in the rear view mirror as Gidget has a front tire shot out and crashes. The clown sneaks by the King and drives along side of me. The King pushes my chest back and fires a few rounds into Ronald's van. The clown just laughs. The Colonel holds back, and the clown tries to run us off the road. The King sees a safe haven. He motions for me to pull into the nearest Burger King. I have no reason to doubt him. I veer off of the main road, nearly killing us. My back driver side tire explodes from a gunshot. I keep driving and pull into the BK parking lot and stop near the door. The King pulls out of the car and shields me as he fires more slugs into Ronnie's van. Colonel Sanders pulls in behind us. I grab the handgun from the King's waistband and fire at the Colonel. Two in the chest and one in the head, the Colonel is down. The King gets hit by the clown, who is enjoying the hell out of this. The bullet has gone through his arm. He'll be okay. I grab his shotgun and fire at the clown who has exposed himself. The first slug hits his thigh, the second in his chest. He falls to the ground, a bloody mess. I drop the shotgun on the ground. The King stands and pats me on the back. He motions to go inside. I walk to the door. He opens the first door for me, and I head to the second one. I return the favor. The King returns home triumphant. He takes one step inside when his back explodes with blood. He falls to the ground. I race to catch him. I turn to look at the culprit. It's the one I least expected: Wendy. Yes, that Wendy. She just laughs and walks outside into the parking lot. I walk out behind her and pick up the King's shotgun. She turns to look at me. "You helped to take down the bad guy in all of this. We're going to be heroes. Good job on the Colonel and the clown. Now, it's all mine." She pauses. "Hear those sirens, that's the police coming." I can hear sirens in the distance, but I can't let her get away with it. article: War..... war never changes..... until you invite the Terrans. At first, I was reticent. Even though I had used my position on the high directorate to'guide' the high command's opinion. It didn't take much, a simple nudge here, a whispered word there; soon enough, my subordinates had garnered the support of the majority of both the high directorate and high command's staff. With a heavy heart, both the directorate and command agreed that we would attempt to wrangle the humans into assisting us in our war. It all began simple enough, we bumped into them nearly by accident - while both surveying the worlds surrounding H-9957-B6, what the humans call Alpha Centauri A. The first contact went as awkwardly as one might expect. The captain of the Dau'Nithai'Ien being awakened by his first lieutenant and told that they were receiving a communique. By all reports, it took the ship's AI over six hours to translate all five of the languages in which it was sent. All five languages seemed gutteral and harsh to us. The emphasis seemed to be place on the first transmission, however, a language known as English. Our engineers and geneticist immediately began working on instantaneous translation solutions. Of course, as usual, the engineers won out with something they called the'babelfish'. Apparently, the name had been stolen from a text made available on a crude repository computer made available by the Terran. At this point, with my personal babelfish fit into my neural receptacle, I was sent aboard the fastest ship in our fleet. By now, it was no small secret that I had suggested this plan. As such, I was eventually ordered by the head of the directorate to reach an understanding. Boy, if only he had understood exactly what that would entail..... Upon my arrival to Alpha Centauri A, the very nervous and perturbed captain of the Dau'Nithai'Ien practically cried with joy. After a little prodding, he began to explain that his entire crew were four weeks deep into a binge session on what the Terrans called'TV'. He continued explaining that, his crew had begun using vernacular picked up in TV. Pretend'gun fights' broke out during time meant to be reserved for quiet contemplation. Crewman and under officer alike were reciting lines from films such as'Dirty Harry','The Good, The Bad and The Ugly','The Godfather' and by the captains words, an "utterly deplorable" film called'Clueless'. According to his lieutenant, the Captain was "like, totally over this whole humanity thing." I remember remarking to myself, "Just what have we found?." Boarding the small escape craft, I recall telling my son, who had accompanied me, "If I don't come back, let your mother know I love her." The flight over to their craft was the longest 10 minutes of my 763 year long life. Through my semicent as a child, to my bicent - two hundred human years served in the military, to my 513 years as high ambassador to the trade coalition, I have never been more terrified in my entire life. The fate of our race, nay, the galaxy lie in the yet unknown goodwill of a race we had met little more than five weeks ago. As we pulled to the ship, the pilot began playing clips from American TV shows to communicate. It started with, "why howdy partner," followed by, "we come in peace." Finally, after receiving what I now know is a human laugh, their ship's captain replied, "welcome aboard." Just then, the cargo doors to their ship swung open and our ship was pulled in via a crude system of'lead lines' - attached to our ship via magnets. After testing to confirm their air was hospitable, the captain popped the hatch and wished me luck. With a hopeful heart and a dreadful sigh, I stepped out into the dimly lit flight deck. With sweet smelling air, and a bitter chill, the humans seemed very similar to our race. It took me a moment to reach the floor and then it hit me - the Terran were giants! With hindsight, our average height would measure to be roughly 3 human feet. Their average was nearly double! Summoning my courage, I called out, "Greetings, I am Ambassador Xallar of the Dau. I have come to speak with Captain Smith." That is when the shortest among them, with weak features and a thin frame stepped forward, "Greetings, Xallar of the Dau. I am Veronica Smith of the planet Earth. On behalf of humanity, I salute you." She snapped a firm salute and relaxed, a small smile spreading across her face. "Won't you accompany me to the conference room, Ambassador Xallar? " , she asked politely. After more pleasantries and small talk, we arrived at the crux of the discussion. With a resigned sigh, I broached the subject. "Captain Smith, with all sincerity and respect I have a monumental request of you. Our people are currently besieged and flagging against a mighty foe, the Valgar. They would most be likened to what I understand you know as an ant. However, they are roughly so tall -," raising my hand to about four human feet, I continued, "We are of course in dire need. Thus, I have been authorized to offer you access to one of the most coveted technologies of any space faring race." She leaned forward intently, jaw working as if speaking. I took a long swallow of what the humans called'tea', savoring the flavor..... "We are prepared to offer you specifications and completed models of our faster than light travel mechanism - FTL." "Yes sir, I understand. One moment, please." She swiped at the air in a circular motion and swung her arm toward the wall. A projection of a much older, stately male with a darker complexion than Captain Smith appeared. "Let me get this straight, Ambassador. You are offering us the holy grail of space travel for our assistance in an inter-galactic war? " , the man blew out a large cloud of smoke and extinguished his cigar. Motioning for an aide, two small counters appeared at the bottom of the screen. The word'yay' written in green next to one, and the word'nay' in red, next to the other. As humans would say, it felt like watching paint dry. Apparently, somewhere on earth, a debate was being had between the UEC - or, United Earth Congress. The man who I had just spoken to was its reigning president, Arnold Bellamy. All of this in itself was a small mircale, given the fact that, the last democratic planet was wiped out nearly one full millennium ago due to indecisiveness about this very same subject: war. But, these humans were different - they practiced something called "Republican Democracy"; they elected representatives instead of voting on issues directly. After three hours, during which time I was fed and given a'datapad' to browse Earth media, The President reappeared on the screen. Suddenly, the counters flickered to life and the votes were there on the screen: 1,396 yay - 204 nay. My breathing quickened as I glanced up at the President. He glanced down at me, the edges of his mouth drawn up in a small smile. "Ambassador Xallar, on behalf of Earth, we accept your call and it is our hope that not only will we be victorious..... but, that this will be the first step toward a long and sustained friendship." End Part One I have to think of where I want to go with this, if there's enough interest I will write more. Thanks for reading.

I already knew the answer to that question. Her parents were asleep in their room. That was my doing. "They're inside." "Of course they are, little one. Tell me, what is your name, little one?" Her name was Aoi; I already knew. "Aoi." "Of course it is." An innocent soul, that was the toll. I couldn't become a full-fledged reaper until I had taken the soul of an innocent person. I'd grown up believing my cause was just. I'd heard so many stories about how relishing it is to complete reaper training. My instructor had told me this was the easiest, but most important test. To take one's soul, is to subject to an eternity of torment, that is, unless you're an angel, then it's a blessing. Nonetheless, I had a job to do, dues to pay. I wouldn't pay them by making small talk. Still, it didn't feel right, subjecting this innocent person to damnation just to make myself a reaper. What did it have to do with anything. It was a reaper's job to find those who have let the darkness consume them, and damn them to hell, whatever the cost. I could hear my instructor's voice in my head. "It is forbidden to talk of one's initiation. To do so would be a capital offense. To fail the initiation, is to commit a capital offense." I couldn't wrap my head around it. If sparing the soul of an innocent person was so bad, why was there so much good in the world? Why was I sent there? What kind of sick test was that? I took a step back from Aoi, who had simply been staring at me with a look of slight fear. "You do know why reapers exist? Balance." I didn't recognise the voice. "Who are you?" "Call me Michael." I knew immediately I was speaking with the legendary archangel Michael. "Even still, if you make any attempt at that girl's soul, so help me god, I will rend you to an oblivion the likes of which would make your "hell" seem like a heaven." His words would have scared me, but I lost the desire to hurt that little girl before they were uttered. "I don't think I want to any more." "Why?" "I know what I am. I'm just a class-d demon and this is the greatest chance I have a being anything. I've always been weak. I've never fit in. I can't even do this simple task. I just can't her her, she didn't do anything wrong! I accept whatever punishment befalls me; it's better than the guilt this would bring. I don't want to be a reaper anymore. You win." After I spoke, Michael walked up to me with a warm smile, placed his hand on my shoulder, and looked me in the eye. "It seems you were put in the wrong place. Even God makes mistakes. Come with me." article: He had the revolver tucked right under my nose, pressed tightly against my skin. "You've been a pretty god-awful piece of garbage, Billy." He pressed down harder as I tried to speak. "Billy..." he leaned in close, and I tried to melt through the wall that hugged my back. "Billy, do you know the definition of luck?" I tried to talk, tried to ignore the ridge of the barrel's gun tearing at my nostril. I tried, stopped, then tried again until I finally succeeded. "Something happening by chance?" Some of the pressure let up. "Very good, Billy, it's close enough. Luck is success or failure brought by chance rather than through one's own actions, Billy." The pressure returned magnified by one hundred and he leaned in, his grotesque face uncomfortably close. "I guess you are a very active man, because luck is not why I am here." He straightened, free hand reaching inside his suit jacket. He smiled and cocked the hammer of his gun, and I think his smile upset me more than the gun did. The right side of his face was smooth and handsome, his eyes a shining green hue. The left side of his face was burnt flesh and charred bone, tendons and bones exposed to the air, his left eyeball almost completely revealed. "Please don't do this. Please." I had to reason, I had to stop him. I knew what was coming next. I had heard the stories. He withdrew the coin, the oh so famous coin, burnt on one side and a shining silver on the other; it was a piece of symbolism that was widely known by the criminal syndicate in Gotham. "You know the drill, Billy." He dug the barrel of the gun deeper into my flesh and with his free hand tucked his thumb under the coin. "Time to choose a side..."
label: human

article: I slid the dragon's key into the metal sheath, slowly twisting it's spiral tail until I heard the sound of metal sliding across its' brothers. Gears moved and spun as the pipes let out a hiss and filled the room with air left untouched for thousands of revolutions. Stirring new motion in the air, I reached for the wooden handle and pulled. The door budged slightly, but wasn't going anywhere. I planted myself firmly on the ground, digging my feet into the hard rock and dust. I reeled back as the door creaked into motion, slowly opening the room. When it was of sufficient distance for me to enter, I did. Inside was a sea of darkness, yet reflective enough to see myself, a younger me. I stared down the maw of this liquid beast and felt my legs kick into motion. Was I running? Yes, I was running. Awareness crept back into my mind as I reached up, grabbing at the trapdoor that led me here. I rushed back to the town hall, where the king sang and rejoiced with the people. I tried to reach him, but I failed. The ooze wrapped itself around my legs and the legs of those around me, slowly enveloping us to the neck. Darkness set in, as I held my last regrets. I knew what I was doing.

article: Fleming: So was the entire 100 Acres covered in forest? He took a long drag from the Marlboro he had been flittering gently between his fingers, the smoke filling the vacuum of his lungs and the nicotine coating his brain in euphoria. Breathing it down to the filter, he dropped it into the ashtray and pulled another from his shirt pocket. D: I don't know about all of it, but I can tell you that it all needs to be burned to the ground. Trees rooted and every living thing in there engulfed along with it. Fleming: What did you find in there? The man, lighting up what must have been his 6th cigarette in 20 minutes, gazed with callous eyes at the officer. They were eyes that had seen every horrible war crime and accident before, witnessed hundreds of brutal deaths and felt the utter emptiness of humanity. D: It was supposed to be a rescue mission. I was given a special unit for extraction of a high value target, but the higher-ups were very hush-hush about the whole operation. They gave us the coordinates and sent us up river. The first place we stopped... Fleming: The gloomy place? D: Yeah, the gloomy place. That's an understatement. I've seen destitution but never like this. Animals were chained together, other animals watched over them with rifles pointed at their skulls, piles upon piles of bodies, some burned, some still burning like beacons of hate. I could handle that, seen savages like that before. It was the mass suicide that got me. Fleming: How'd you know it was a mass suicide? D: The bodies...God the bodies...they hung by their necks in concentric circles in the woods as far as the eye could see. Eyes bulging, tongues lolling: brainwashed by that fucking ass. That fucker was in the middle, in the tallest tree of all, body still swinging in the breeze, pink ribbon around his tail stained with shit and blood. Fleming: Let's move on, what happened after you got to the second station? D: Rabbit's house? I tell you we almost didn't make it, lost three good men to that goddamn tiger. Kept ambushing us when we got too close to the shore. I still remember the screams, the sight of him bouncing. But he didn't make a sound, effortlessly bounding upon my men, ripping them in two, all the time growling " T-I-double guh-RRR " He shuddered slightly and slammed his fist into the table. D: But I put a bullet right between his yellow savage eyes, being a fucking corpse is what he does best now. Anyway, we got to Rabbit's house. Lazy bastards, they were cowards still trying to get ahead. Rabbit himself, their so-called ' leader ', wrecked the goddamn transport we were supposed to take. Took us days to fix it, and they just sat there. Then they had they had the fucking gall to want to go with us to the end. I was tired, exhausted, and agreed along with it. They ended up just being fodder for the bear. Fleming: The bear? Your report didn't mention anything about the bear. D: I know, I couldn't bring myself to write it. It was too brutal. Vicious, terrifying, he stood 12 feet tall and had claws the size of my hands. He drained the blood of all his kills into this big jar and would just continually lick his paws, always looking for more slaughter to fill his bowl. Goddamnit we couldn't take him down. As soon as we got to the inner station we had to get Chris and get him out. We lost the rabbit, we lost almost all my men. But we got Robin, we had him safe and we were heading back. That bear can stay in the darkness. Fleming: So what happened, where is he? The man dropped his head in his hands, cigarette smoldering next to his ear, silent. Fleming: Well? Where is Christopher Robin? D: We were almost back. He was in the clear, but that little pig of his was getting anxious, kept saying he was getting sick. I didn't believe him; I just wanted to get the hell out of there. It happened the night before we got back to base. He gave me his commissioned report on the 100 Acre Wood, and a photograph, told me to keep it away from the owl. Then with his last breath he whispered " The horror! The horror! " He stood up, grabbed his coat, and started for the door. Fleming: What about the report?! Savage eyes looked back at him. D: Burn it all to the ground.
label: human

article: And yet, the city remained. Maria wished it would disappear, and take with it all the memories it held, all the pain, the mistakes. The buildings pressed in on her , suffocating her with their history and weight. But as much as she wanted to escape, to run far away from it all, she couldn't shake the feeling that something important was still holding her there. She had grown up in this city, after all, and though it had let her down in many ways, it had also shaped her into the person she was today. She couldn't forget the moments of happiness she had experienced here, the friends and family who surrounded her, and the small joys that kept her going when everything else seemed pointless. Slowly, Maria began to see the city in a new light. She started to appreciate its quirks and charms, to notice the beauty in the details she had previously overlooked. And as she did, she felt a weight lift off her shoulders, a sense of gratitude replacing the bitterness in her heart. It wasn't a perfect city, not by any means. But it was hers, and she was going to make the most of it. She set out to explore its corners and hidden secrets, to create new memories and experiences that would overshadow the old. And as she did, she realized that maybe, just maybe, this city was worth holding onto after all.

article: I was eight the first time I noticed. Not the horns themselves, mind you. Those had been a constant bane of any shirt I had ever tried to wear, and I had been well-aware of them for as long as I could remember. It was the reactions of others that first caught my attention. Adults would do double-takes, their eyes widening in shock and disbelief. Kids would stare, their expressions ranging from awe to fear. At first, I didn't understand why they were reacting that way. After all, I had grown up with these horns. They were a part of who I was, like the color of my eyes or the shape of my nose. But as I got older, I began to realize that not everyone had horns like mine. I learned to hide them as best I could, wearing my hair long and always choosing clothing that covered my neck and shoulders. But no matter how hard I tried to blend in, there were always people who noticed. It was a constant source of anxiety and frustration for me. It wasn't until I was in my mid-twenties that I finally decided to embrace my horns. I was tired of hiding, tired of feeling ashamed of something that was a part of me. So I started wearing my hair up and choosing clothing that showed off my shoulders. To my surprise, people's reactions were different this time. They still noticed, of course, but instead of shock and disbelief, I saw curiosity and admiration in their eyes. Some even told me they wished they had horns like mine. It was a liberating experience, to finally be able to be myself without fear of judgment or rejection. And while the horns themselves may never go away, I know now that they don't define me. I am who I am, and that's something to be proud of.

article: "Im sorry for my little outburst last week Mr Davis. Please, accept this humble meal I have made for you and your wife as an apology." Last week I got into a argument with this customer and his wife. He insulted and bullied one of the waitresses. And instead of having the decency to stop and apologize to the poor girl, he threw his plate at her and then continued to complain about the bad service. She suffered a nasty wound on her head and Mrs Davis then started to mock her, how ugly she was and calling her worthless piece of trash. Police had to be called and the entire restaurant turned into a ugly scene with several people yelling and cursing at each other. Those people thought that they were worth more than other people just because they had money. So to ensure that this prick and his bitch wife would never bother my partners and me again I came up with an apology and invited them for dinner at the restaurant. Since we were one of the best places in the city it was quite unsurprising they actually came. I arranged for them to be the last guests before we closed. So here they were sitting, eating their last meal and talking about their so much better life. "This was quite the apology. Im glad that you recognized that it was all the fault of your useless waittress. I take it you have fired her?" "No, but she got demoted to cleaning plates for a month." "A month is still too good for this useless girl." Mrs Davis took another bite from the meat on her table. Mr davis was still eating his soup. "This is the best soup I have ever eaten, the meat is so tender." Those fools. After years of training I was able to cook human meat that would taste like normal animal meat. But there was a rule: We would only feed the guilty with human meat. If you havent done anything wrong and came to my place, I would ensure you would get the finest food without any human ingredients. Even halal if you wish for it. And those two were definetly guilty. Sarah Davis ran a traficker ring who was disguised as model agency. Her organization would lure young pretty girls from all over the world, promising a new happy life in the USA. Once in the hands of those monster they would addict them to drugs and then force them into prostitution. Every girl who tried to escape or talk to the police would be found dead after a few days. Tortured to death and horribly mutilated. Jack Davis owned a pharmacy company. This particular company would buy patents and the rights to produce essential medications and then skyrocket the prices. His victims were mainly the poor people. And if those unfortunate souls werent able to pay for their meds, a shady loan company would contact them. They would offer those people loans with exorbitant interest rates. Since other banks and companies wouldnt give them loans, they had to accept it. And what a surprise: The loan company was also owned by Mr Davis. Effectively both of them were modern slavers. "You two ealier mentioned your son. How is he doing?" "Joe is doing fine. He called us yesterday and said he was going to make a travel around the world. We will really miss him when he is gone." I grinned. "He might be closer than you think." Mrs Davis started to yawn. "Why do I feel so sleepy?" "Extorting young girls must be exhausting Mrs Davis." Mr Davis Face suddenly turned serious. "What did you just say?" "Oh, I know what you are doing for a living." Mrs Davis fell asleep on her plate. Mr Davis had difficulties staying awake. "And your son Joe isnt better. Just last week he ran over a entire family. Instead of calling the ambulance he ran over them again to ensure they were dead. But dont worry, Im sure he will feel very comfortable inside you and I know you like it too. After all the flesh of guilt tastes best." I could see in his face that he wanted to throw up. But the anaesthetic was too strong. I called in Gina, my waitress. She still had a bandage on her head. "Gina my dear, would you please prepare the special room for our guests?" She smiled. "Of course." "And the knifes too. " , I said with a wink. Mr Davis barely could keep his eyes open. I brought my face close to his. "Mr Davis, do you remember what the last sentence was I said to you last week?" "E..E..Eat..... a dick?" "Well, you just did."

article: Lucifer rubbed his temple as he sat in his favorite throne of bones and flesh. The idea of having a son was always such an interesting prospect for him, creating a being that could potentially inherit his power and carry on his legacy. However, he also knew the risks involved, as his own father had betrayed him and cast him out of Heaven. Despite his reservations, Lucifer decided to go ahead with his plan and sought out a suitable mother for his child. Being the prince of darkness, he had no shortage of admirers and willing partners. But he needed someone special, someone who could match his power and intellect. After months of searching, he finally found her - a demoness named Lilith, known for her beauty and cunning. Lucifer approached her with his proposal, offering her riches and power beyond her wildest dreams in exchange for bearing his child. Lilith accepted the offer, but on her own terms. She demanded that she be allowed to raise their child as she saw fit, with no interference from Lucifer. He reluctantly agreed to her terms and together they conceived a son. Years passed and Lilith raised their son in secret, teaching him the ways of the demon world and preparing him for his destiny as the heir to the throne of darkness. Lucifer watched from afar, his pride and curiosity growing with every passing year. Finally, the day arrived when their son was ready to meet his father. Lucifer summoned Lilith and their son to his throne room, eager to finally see his legacy in the flesh. As they approached him, Lucifer's heart swelled with pride and admiration. His son stood tall and confident, his eyes glowing with the same fiery intensity as his father's. For a moment, they simply stared at each other, until Lucifer spoke. "Welcome to the family, my son. I have been eagerly awaiting this moment for years. The throne of darkness is yours to inherit, but be warned - it comes with a great burden of responsibility." Their son smiled, his eyes flickering with pride and determination. "I am ready, father. I will honor our family legacy and rule with the same strength and wisdom as you." With those words, Lucifer knew he had made the right choice in creating a successor. His son had the potential to be as great as he was, and perhaps even surpass him. The future of the demon world was secure in the hands of this new, powerful generation.

article: My life is quiet. I live with my husband, who I have been with for 62 years. We've outlived our only child and all of our friends. Our family has all passed, it's just the two of us. We live in the woods, and quiet is the way I like it. I grew up a very quiet person. I never really stood up for myself, and over the years I've realized I live in a nice bubble. As of lately, however, I've become an angry person. I know it's the snoring. Damnit. I can't take it any more. The rising and falling of his chest while he slept used to be beautiful to me. I used to watch, entranced, any time I could not sleep. Now all I can think of is how much I hate the ripping noises his body makes. With each snore, I feel myself growing more impatient. They rip through me, they make me want to rip through him. I used to put a pillow over his face, as a joke, when he would snore. It would wake him up, and we would laugh until we fell back asleep. I did this to him last night. But last week, the silence brought me such relief. So much relief that I couldn't bring myself to lifting the pillow again. Now when I sleep next to my husband, it's very quiet, but I sometimes miss watching his chest rise and fall. FIRST ONE. don't be too harsh:)

article: Dean took a swig from his flask, eyes fixed on something 1000 yards away that wasn't there. "It was either this way or their way, Dean. Maybe it's best." "Fuck'best'. Jesus, Earl, you sound like the priest back home. Always writing off God's colossal fuckups as part of The Greater Good. Never accountable." "They'd have tortured him. They'd have found out about us. Goddamn it, do you think I really wanted it this way?" "Just shut the fuck up, Earl!" The shotgun was still lying on the rock it'd fallen on, a blue furl of smoke slowing coiling out of its barrel. "At least we already have a pit." Said Earl. "Yeah..... We have a pit." It yawned before them. A hole in soft earth they'd labored on for over two hours. A trickle of blood slipped down its walls and began to pool into the bottom. "We can't bury the gold here, Dean. Cadaver dogs might find it." "Cadaver dogs." Thought Dean aloud, dawning on him that there were whole teams and departments of people with nothing better to do but hunt them down and set them behind bars. They had, at most, 3 days before the police got wind of a missing person. They had 1 day before the Hanlin's would come looking. And the Hanlin's could care less for finding a corpse. The 200 lbs of solid gold ingots in the steel trunk in the bed of his pickup was no simple matter in hiding either. "God damn you, Demetrius. Damn you for dragging us into this mix and then you go and get YOUR GODDAMN HEAD BLOWN OFF!" Dean's voice roared in the woods, dying off in faint echoes. The corpse's toe twitched, almost mocking him. "Easy, Dean. Easy. He did what any of us would have done in his stead. He fucked up. Twice. Four times, fuck. We wan na live through this..... we just got ta pick up and get to it." Dean hopped down off the tailgate, grabbing Demetrius' bloodstained shirt and picking it off the ground. With a growl he tossed it into the waiting pit. "Should..... should we say something?" Asked Earl. Dean stared Earl down. " ..... Dear Demetrius. You're probably already in Hell. So thoughtful of you to reserve us tickets."

article: The hooded man polished off his glass of whiskey and set the tumbler down among the sea of empty bottles littering the floor around him. The Believer couldn't tell if he was getting more drunk or more agitated as the night wore on. As his eyes darted around the room, she wondered what could be making him so uneasy. "Is everything alright?" she asked softly, trying not to startle him. He looked over at her, his eyes momentarily scanning her face before focusing on some point behind her. "No, everything's not alright," he growled. "I thought I could trust her, and now I'm not so sure." "Trust who?" The Believer probed gently. He hesitated for a moment, as if weighing whether to open up to her or not. Finally, he spoke. "My business partner. We've been working together for years, but lately, things just don't seem right. She's been acting strange, secretive. I don't know what to do." The Believer nodded sympathetically. "Have you tried talking to her?" He snorted derisively. "Talk to her? She wouldn't listen to me if I tried. Besides, I don't even know what to say. I just have this feeling in my gut that she's up to something, something that could ruin everything we've built." The Believer leaned in a bit closer. "Maybe it's time to bring in outside help. A fresh perspective could be just what you need to get to the bottom of this." The hooded man looked at her thoughtfully. "Maybe you're right. But who could I trust?" The Believer smiled. "You can trust me. I may not look like it, but I'm a highly skilled detective with years of experience under my belt. And I'm here to help you in any way I can."

article: 2072, aboard the Commander's Wing of the The Vessel, currently 32 through its trip to Alpha Centauri " Commander, I have some s... " " Arthur - not now. We're mourning. " " Yes, Commander - unfortunately, it's about that. There's been another one. " Commander Bradley looked away from his small congregation and turned his head towards Arthur, one of his most trusted advisors and the man in charge of policing the ship - a particularly dull affair on a ship which had intentionally chosen its inhabitants based on their non-violent behaviours. " Another one? What do you mean? " " Sir, I am afraid another member of our crew has decided to end their journey rather suddenly. " " What? But Arthur... Who was it? We... this is very troubling. We haven't see a single suicide in the last 14 years. Things should be steady! " " I know Sir. It was one of our engineers in B-wing, Allan Fowler. Happened last night. " Arthur hung his head. On this ship, carrying humanities last hope at survival, there were customs, but suicides were something that no one knew how to deal with. The occurrence of suicides carried with it a trepid awareness - as the only time they had happened on The Vessel was during the 2nd year of the journey, a year in which 11 members of the ship took their own lives. Now there had been two of them within 24 hours. The Commander dismissed his congregation, put his hand on Arthur's shoulder, and began to walk back to the Commander's Quarters. " First Al Bosko, and now Allan Fowler. Is there any connection between the two? Any reason we think this might be happening? " " Well you have the names... but not much else. Nothing that shouldn't be chalked up to coincidence. " Arthur looked at his Commander - " Is there any way for us to get ahead of this? " " That's what I was going to ask you " Commander Bradley replied. " What was the condition of this second one - " Mr. Fowler "? " " Well that's where it does get a little weird, Sir " - Both men stepped through the automatic door in Bradley's office - " As you'll recall, Mr. Bosko was found hanging, but he had also ingested a small amount of poison. Mr. Fowler - I wish I could spare you the vision - he bled himself out in his room. Used a knife from the kitchen, but we believe he also had ingested a small amount of poison. Still waiting on the tox-report. " " Is that common? For a person to use two methods? " " I am not really sure, Sir. Makes sense though, if you're going to do it, I suppose you'd want a fail-safe. A backup plan. " " Was Fowler co-habitating with anyone? " " No, he was solo, just like Bosko. " Arthur's eyes darted up momentarily, and then he pulled out some paper work from under his arm and began to rifle through the pages. " Theresa Fortins " - Arthur said. " Bosko was solo, but up until 3 days ago he'd been co-habitating with Theresa Fortins. He only applied a week ago - I don't know how he got moved so quickly. We should have noticed this ." Commander Bradley took a deep breath. " I know Theresa. She's a good person. Can be a bit feisty, but, that doesn't explain this. " Arthur shook his head to dismiss the conclusion as well. " Commander, the last time we had a physical altercation on this ship was 8 years ago. The most damage a member of this ship has ever intentionally inflicted on another was a broken nose. I really can't imagine that we're now, all of a sudden, going to see a murder. " That word, " murder " sounded foreign to him as it came out across his lips. " Of course not. Besides - it wouldn't explain anything about Mr. Fowler. " There was a pause. " So " Arthur said, " all we really have to work on is the idea that all of our Al's are at risk of suicide? " - he would have laughed, if it weren't so inappropriate in the moment. " I would hope not " Commander Bradley replied. " The only other Al we have on this ship is Headley. I don't think I should have to remind you how important he is to us right now. " The Commander glanced towards Arthur, as if expecting him to confirm what he knew. " Of course Sir. Since the passing of Elisha Thompson, Director Headley is our only experienced food production engineer until his new recruit is finished training. " " Go check on him. " " You think that's necessary Sir? " " I get that it's probably a coincidence, but I am not going to jeopardize our damn species because two Allan's died and we didn't bother to go check on the third one, who just happened to be critical to our survival. " " Yes Sir! " And with that, Arthur headed out through the automatic door, and down the hallway. Moments later, the phone rang beside Commander Bradley at his desk. The ID showed as Arthur. " Everything check out ok with Director Headley? " " About that, " Arthur replied. " I am terribly sorry Sir, but it appears that Director Allan Headley took his own life last night. "

article: It was a long time since my adventure began; I can't remember how many years. It has been a good time but now, wearily, I lay my head down on my pillow to take me to that destination, where all quests end. I dimly notice that I have friends, relatives, aquaintances everyone around me. They don't want me to go, they think I will be lost, that I have no guide, that I will be alone. There is only one way to find out. I close my eyes A tunnel appears before me with a great, blinding, light at the end, it calls to me, wants me. I feel pulled towards the end like a moth to a flame. It is not forced, nor painful, but rather a desire, to discover to find what the light holds in store for me, to find what is in that great beyond, to finally know the secert - the ultimate answer. I find myself falling gently to wards the end when I hear a voice. It is a child, about 2 years old I'd imagine, shouting and sceraming for me. "Grandpa, Grandpa. I don't want you to go" There are others now to, dozens of them, some sob and whimper while others yell and cry but they all penatrate. The tugging is gone. I see them now. They look so sad. Do I have to go through with this? Is the answer that important? The answer will come for me eventually, whether I look for it or not but these people, they need me now and I don't want them to fade just yet. I take one more whistful look to the light before making my way back.

article: James opened his eyes, and squeezed them shut again. " Heavens! " he said aloud. The reddish amoeba in the inner wall of his eyelid swirled and danced together. He blinked a few times, trying to clear his vision, and then opened his eyes again, slowly this time. He looked around and realized that he was lying on a bed in a dimly lit room, with a small window on the far end. The room had a musty smell and was sparsely furnished with a wooden chair, a small table, and a cupboard. James tried to sit up, but an excruciating pain shot through his head, making him wince. He touched his forehead - it was sticky with dried blood. He tried to remember what had happened, but his mind was blank. He felt a knot in his stomach as fear gripped him. Where was he? Who had brought him here? And most importantly, why? As he lay there, lost in thought, he heard the sound of footsteps approaching. The door creaked open, and an old man entered the room. He had a wrinkled face, with deep-set eyes and bushy eyebrows. He was carrying a tray with a glass of water and a bowl of soup. The old man looked at James and smiled. "You're awake, son. That's good news. How are you feeling?" James couldn't help but feel a sense of relief seeing a friendly face. He tried to speak, but his throat was dry, and he coughed. The old man handed him the glass of water, and he drank it eagerly. "I don't remember much," James managed to say finally. "Can you tell me what happened?" The old man nodded. "You were brought here last night by a couple of men. They said they found you lying unconscious on the side of the road. You had hit your head and were bleeding profusely. They didn't know what to do, so they brought you here." James frowned, trying to recall anything that would help him figure out who these men were or how he ended up on the side of the road. But his memory was a blank slate. The old man seemed to sense his confusion. "Don't worry about it, son. The important thing is that you're alive and in good hands now. I'll take care of you, and we'll get you back on your feet in no time." James nodded, feeling grateful and overwhelmed at the same time. He had no idea how he was going to repay this man's kindness, but for now, he was just happy to be safe and alive.

article: -008 Resolution Challenge She sat behind the counter, swatting flies and suffering the drone of the old ratty ceiling fan. Thump, thump, thump went the blades. She just sat there , staring blankly ahead, wondering what she was doing with her life. It was supposed to be a summer job to make a little extra cash before starting college in the fall. But now, here she was, stuck in this tiny town, working at a convenience store that smelled perpetually of stale cigarettes and cheap beer. As she sat there, lost in thought, a customer walked in. He was a tall man, with shaggy hair and a scruffy beard. He looked like he hadn't slept in days, but he had a friendly smile on his face. "Hey there," he said. "Do you have any maps?" She looked around the store, trying to remember if they had any maps in stock. After a moment, she found one tucked away in a dusty corner. She handed it to the man, who looked it over quickly before thanking her and heading out the door. As he walked away, something about him made her curious. She wondered where he was going and what he was searching for. She realized then that she had been stuck in this town for too long, and it was time for her to leave and start exploring the world. The next day, she put in her two weeks' notice at the convenience store and packed her bags. She didn't know where she was going or what she would find, but she knew that anything was better than sitting behind that counter, swatting flies and listening to the drone of the old ratty ceiling fan.

article: I'll admit, I was first attracted by her shapely behind. But once I realized she was standing on the very precipice of the old road bridge over the River Wely, all such thoughts were hastily dismissed. I stopped my car and walked back to her. She was in a flimsy little dress- red, with white bits. Her high heels lay on the pavement, her bare feet wrapped around the rusted concrete. Toes used to a lifetime of being crammed into tight spaces grazed the manmade surface, and looked almost keen on it. I looked up and tried to catch her face, but the sun caught my eye. I stayed behind, and reached out to her. "This isn't the way, you know." There was silence. Had I said the right thing? But then she spoke. "How would you know? Stay back!" I didn't falter. "Young lady, I've saved people on this bridge many a time. I know life in this old ghost town is no pickle for you young folks, but come on. You know it's where your friends are. We're all friends here in Tolby, aren't we? No reply. "You're a beautiful young lady. You're in a lovely country. You've got so much others don't. Why throw it all away?" "Because I don't deserve it." It took me a while to think of an answer, but I used a variation on one I had given my wife many years ago. "No-one deserves anything. I was born to a well-off family, relatively- we owned a farm and did hardly any of the work. It paid for my school. I didn't deserve it, of course not. No-one ever does. But to dismiss it just because of a technicality like that? To lose my place of privilege in society because of a little thing like that, when I could become someone who could help the less privileged? Therein lies the real crying shame." "Okay..." she began. "Maybe I will step down. Reconsider." "Yes. We all deserve a second chance." She stepped down, but I stayed back, in case she fell or jumped suddenly. "I know..... I've had so many new chances at life. I'd say about five so far." "Then there you go, those people who helped you, where are they now? They don't want to see you throw yourself off a bridge." "Oh they would. But they're all gone now." "That's a shame. You need to live on in their memory. A young person makes the world go round." "Ah yes. But a vampire needs more than youth..... a vampire needs blood." I stammered. "A what now?" She turned on me and jumped, digging her claws into my shoulder. I felt my strength desert me, as I bled out and she drooled it up greedily. As I watched, she became even younger, like a teenager. My vision became hazy, and her strength multiplied. She picked me up and in one terrible hurl threw me off the bridge. I saw my blood mix with the river, and it clouded my eyes as I sank beneath the stream.

article: Vultric's six arms laid limp over the thin leather couch. It wasn't too comfortable. Every few seconds he reminded himself of that fact. His twelve eyes were closed, dreaming of a better time. There was a fan in the room. Every few seconds it blew Vultric's thick fur around. He hated it. "Can we turn it off?" He asked. His eyes opened and he looked at a balding creature who sat across from him. The creature, Dr. Greox, didn't speak. He never spoke. Vultric ignored Greox and stood up on his six legs. It took a few strides, but he reached the fan and shut it off. Then he returned to the couch. "As I was saying. This is the third time she's hugged him this week." With his eyes closed Vultric imagined Amy, the human girl whom he became familiar with over the past few years. "You know, this all happened because of the father. Back when she had the Princess Mattress it was fine." Vultric's situation, like many other closet creatures, was dire. The human who inhabited his room was changing. Every few years her bed changed. With a new bed, came a new neighbor. Normally the monsters under the bed were quite normal. They understood the game. You wait for the lights to go out. Then you scare. There was no cuddling, no hugs, no friendship with the human. But this guy. This big hunk of fur wasn't scary. No. He was deemed "Adoreable." Vultric sat up on his couch. "I should kill him." Vultric though to himself. It truly was the only way. Suddenly Vultric stood up. He left the couch and exited the room. He was back in his home. Fresh human clothes brushed against his unwelcoming fur as he crept through the corridors of the closet. Finally he was at the door. He pushed it open ever so slightly. Vultric moved out of his home and into the battlefield. The only sentry, a fairy nightlight stood guard near the bed. He crawled forward along the carpet. Toys scattered and blocked his way, so he mere climbed over them. Then he was where he needed to be. The entrance to the bed. He snuck under some sheets that hid that creature. The covers touched his fur as he entered his enemies fortress. He was there. Standing in front of him, next to a snickers candy wrapper. Quickly Vultric launched himself at his enemy. With his twin fangs he sank himself into his enemies back. It was all going according to plan. Then that creature pushed Vultric up against the bed. Smack! The bed moved. Yet still Vultric's bite held firm. "Amy!" A voice broke the trance of battle. Footsteps came racing across the hallway floor. The door opened and the lights flickered on. The footsteps became louder as something approached the bed. Suddenly the covered were whisked up and Amy looked directly into her fathers face. "Hunny it's bed time." He said. Amy groaned and dropped her toys. She crawled out from under the bed and brushed off the dust that was on her pajamas. Then she leaped into bed and dragged the covers over her. Her father leaned in and kissed her goodnight. "Go to sleep." He said closing the door. "Fine." She fired back. Amy's eyes closed and darkness once again came upon the room. The only light came from the fairy nightlight. Under the bed though, the battle had been decided. Vultric released his fangs from the other monster and crawled out from under the bed. Then he returned to his closet victorious.

article: My name is Avin Actrost, First Class Wizard of the Eastern Forest, and Bearer of the Oak Leaf of Bravery. I am here to honor the memory of my fondest companion and most loyal friend, long since passed in a battle for peace. Rouk. An Orc. A simple name, yes. But he was always a person of few words, simple pleasures. I believe he would prefer me to leave off his titles and medals, half of which I could hardly pronounce anyway. He wanted people to know him, not what heroics he has accomplished. Yet, I would like to retell his final tale, if not for him, then for me. Rouk and I had met from a simple bodyguard job. Our client wished both for magical and physical support, and I remember being slightly annoyed that he didn't think my prowess enough. But I am glad for his choice today, or I never would have met my friend. At first, I regarded him with condescending, thinking him simple and dumb, all brawn and no brains. He didn't mention it to me, and I can only assume he had become used to it. I was tempted to try and read his mind, to see just what lurked between his tiny ears, but magic is largely ineffectual against orcs and trolls, so I didn't deem it worth the drain on my energy. So we left each other alone, for the most part. He only talked to answer questions, or request another bowl of stew at dinner. I found much better conversation with the duke that had hired us, talking about many of the political controversies that were rising up in the day. The king was getting old, and it sounded like several of the princes were becoming rather agitated. Rouk never participated, of course. He would stay up later than any of the rest of us, finishing the pot of stew, but I was never interested in remaining awake with him. Most of the rest of the party would go to bed early, as the sun set, and we would rise the next morning to find him snoring under the open air. That changed, on the day we were attacked.I was taking a nap in my tent, as the afternoon wore on. We had marched all morning, and set up camp in a clearing. It was a lazy feeling day, and no one was ready for the war cries that burst from the underbrush. No one except Rouk. By the time I had found my staff and rushed outside, the enemy was already upon us. A dozen goblins were screeching and rummaging through tents, and a massive troll bellowed at me as I emerged. But the worst part was the two orcs in the background, who oversaw the goblins as they rushed about, remarkably well organized. Rouk was already fighting the troll, his glaive, a large blade mounted on the end of a hardwood staff, spinning like a whirlwind. The troll held a club that was larger than me, but any time he attempted to use it, he got a blow to the gut, or had to dodge from a swing of the blade. He roared in frustration, but was quickly cut off by a blow of the staff to his temple. The massive creature stumbled for a moment, then fell to the ground, unconscious. I heard a shriek, and glanced over to see that our client was hiding behind a log, hands over his head. That was fine, as he'd hired us to be the brave ones. It was at this moment that I realized the goblins were still ransacking the camp. I searched through my bag until I found a single golden coin, then whispered a quick spell before tossing it out into the ground. Every goblin's head jerked around like they were on ropes, and they all rushed the enchanted gold. I stepped away as they piled over it, each one fighting to get their hands on it. When they stopped squirming, I knew it was because they'd all found that their fingers were glued to the bit of metal. But even with the goblins and the troll out of the way, there were still two orcs left. A little bit desperate, a little bit as an experiment, I aimed my staff at one of them and let loose with a blast of pure energy. It hit the orc in the chest, leaving a small burn mark on his clothes, and he stumbled backwards a step. But instead of falling, he straightened up and glared at me. As I said, magic doesn't work all that well against orcs or trolls. The other orc glanced at me and Rouk, and seemed to realize which one of us was the real threat. He turned away from me, facing Rouk, and lifted his own club. " Brother! Join us! We can have the money, together! " My heart sank in my chest as I remembered something about orc culture. Hurting other orcs was forbidden, as a loyalty to themselves above all else. Even if Rouk didn't abandon us and join them, I couldn't defend the duke without his help. As much as I hated to admit it, my magic wouldn't help in this situation. So imagine my surprise with Rouk totally ignored their words and toppled the pair with a series of quick, accurate blows. - A few hours later, after I contacted the nearest knights to come pick up the would-be-bandits, we were all gathered around the fire for dinner again. The duke had decided that our victory against the bandits was worth a big celebration dinner, so the fire was extra large, and the pot extra full, along with some savory breads and meats to eat as well. I'd been confused about what exactly had happened back there with the other orcs. Had I simply been wrong about the culture and laws? I doubted that, though it may have simply been the fact that I tended to act even more arrogant back then. And, being the young and curious wizard I was, I figured the best way to find out was to ask. Near the end of the meal, when some people were just starting to excuse themselves to retire, I abandoned my spot and made my way around the fire to sit next to Rouk. He didn't seem to notice, still digging into his large bowl of stew, probably the fifth or sixth one of the night. I cleared my throat, and he glanced down at me. Slurping up another spoonful, he swallowed, then spoke in a rough voice. " Avin. " It wasn't a question, more of a statement, but I was just surprised he had remembered my name. I asked my question. " So, back there with the other orcs, Rouk. Why did you attack them? " He gave me a look that could only be described as bewilderment. " They were bad orc. I told Duke I would keep him safe. " " But, " I continued, confident that I'd caught him in a big blunder. " Isn't it totally forbidden to hurt other orc? I thought your king outlawed it years and years ago, during that big war against the elves or whatnot? " He stared at me for a second, and I could almost see him trying to think through it. But when he opened his mouth, he was confident. " Is true. Orc not supposed to hurt other Orc. But bad orc... they hurt many orc. " I frowned. " As in, they robbed their own kind? I suppose I can see why you would try and stop that. But they were robbing the duke, not other orcs. " Rouk shook his head vehemently. " No. Bad orc rob humans, and that hurts other orc. If all humans see are bad orc, they think all orc are bad orc, and they hurt good orc as well. " He stood, probably to grab another bowl of soup. " Better to hurt one orc, than let one orc hurt many. " With that, he lumbered back toward the pot. As for me, I was genuinely dumbfounded. That was a complicated, deep thought process! And he didn't struggle through, or have it explained to him. He knew that was true. Maybe there was more to Rouk than I gave him credit for. He plopped down next to me again, stew slopping in his bowl, and immedialty started eating. I watched him for a moment. Around us, almost everyone else had gone to bed, and the fire was dying down. The sky was red, slowly turning a dark blue. " So what do you think about the current state of affairs in the kingdom? " I asked. I half wanted to see if he even understood what I meant, but the other half was actually curious to hear what he thought. He seemed surprised that I was still talking to him. But he put his spoon down for a moment, and stared at the sky. A sprinkling of stars had appeared above us, and the light from the sun was almost gone. " I think human king is being foolish, allowing his sons to fight and argue about who will be next king. When he dies, the princes will fight until many, many die. It would be better to give it to who he trusts most. " He stared into his bowl for a moment, pondering that, then resumed spooning chunks of meat and vegetables into his maw. So he did know. And he didn't like it when people died, it sounded like. I'd have to think about that. So, I stood with a flourish, and offered my hand. " Avin Actrost, Second Class Wizard of the Eastern Forest. (I was only Second Class, back then) It was a pleasure to fight by your side today. " Tentatively, he took my hand. His was large and rough, but still gentle. When he realized that I meant it, a broad grin split across his face, and he shook my whole arm. " Rouk. Good Meeting, Avin. " With that, I went to bed, and left the orc to stare at the sky full of stars. After the job was over and the duke delivered, we both went back to our agency. But from then on, I requested to work with Rouk, and after almost two years of jobs together, we became official partners in our line of work. We never failed a single job.
label: human

article: Surely I was not losing my mind. No..... Those was definitely her eyes. Big and round and a soft brown in eventide light, and a ghost of the golden star that shone on them during the day. I shook my head, trying to push the memories out from the forefront. Instead, I decided to focus on getting through the next crowd of people. The sidewalks here are like the tide, rushing groups that came in waves. There it was again. A young woman walked past me, earpods lodged in their place. She was pretty, I suppose, in the way that strangers sometimes were. But the hair of the stranger was the rolling gold curls that I knew some years ago. Another person laughed nearby, and it was also hers. I smiled to myself and glanced around, half-hoping, half-fearing that I'd find her. I found the laughing girl, feeling both relieved and disappointed that it was not the lover I once knew. I sighed and stepped to the precipice of the sidewalk. Inhale deeply for eight counts. Hold for four counts. Exhale for eight counts. It was a lesson in breath control I had learned in the ancient past, in my days of marching band. It was also a suitable meditation for clearing the head. It had worked when my business threatened for several weeks. I managed to keep my head calm, and revive it, but now. Now all I could think about was her. How she made my heart pound. How she turned a miserable time into a memorable one. How she- I needed sit down. The street had cars racing down both sides, so jaywalking was out. I pushed rudely through a gaggle of pedestrians into the shaded marketplace inside. In a pretentiously half-restored coffee corner. I slid a ten on the counter. "Mocha Bianca, mate. I'm in a bit of a rush." The barista's snort of derision was almost non-existent with the potential bribe laid out so garishly. He moved with practiced speed, giving me a piping hot coffee in a couple minutes. "Four fif "Keep it." I snatched the coffee and strutted away as quickly as I could, the aroma wafting out of the cup, and sending me back to her dormitory suite. I pushed open some doors on the other side of the market and caught a gust of salty air. It should have blown some sense into my head, but all it did was remind me of her stories of surfing, of wandering the hills around Los Angeles. I sat down on top of a sea wall, cup of coffee in one hand, and looked out into the sunset. She was the golden woman, eyes, hair, laugh, and soul. As bright and joyful as the western sunset, with promise of singing and dancing long after the light dissipates. God damn it all.

article: "Lakes of fire. Demonic shrieks that never end. It's all true! Locusts. Plague. Fallen Angles. Goats. Nightmares have come to pass. I SEE THE HORSE! I SEE THE HORSE! IT IS ALL NIGH! THE END COMES SWIFTLY AND ALL WILL BARE WITNESS TO....!" The sedatives finally took their desired effect. Greg had been wailing for the better part of an hour since donning the goggles. His faced had aged in seconds, the lines and contours drawing in and forming shadows, and his hair had become a ghostly white. Nobody could communicate with him. He just kept going on, seeming oblivious to everything around him. Everyone in the lab had tried to talk to him even Father Davis, who had been brought in as a "consult." Everyone had laughed at that in the beginning. Now, Greg having been finally subsided, he stood at the center of nearly a dozen questioning stares. The room was silent, save for the faint humming of various machines. Father Davis stood his ground, sweating profusely. His face stood as impassive as stone, but his eyes betrayed the rest of his hard composure. They held the ancient fears of a child seeking refuge from a stray hound and finding none. But nobody pressed Father Davis because the same fear had reflected in each of them, and they understood that Father Davis did not comprehend anymore than they did. "Well?" Someone finally asked. "What went wrong. It was meant to show him paradise. What happened?" "I don't know, Stevens. For the briefest moment, it seemed that all was going to plan. There was wonder, pure joy, and amazement. Then everything went to shit." Flenning said. Greg snapped up in the bed, "I LOOKED UPON THE HOUSE OF THE LORD, AND I SAW EVERYTHING! EVERYTHING! FROM MY PERCH I COULD SEE THEIR TORTURED SOULS, HEAR THEIR CRIES, WHILE SITTING IN THE MIDST OF DIVINE ECSTASY! THERE WAS NAUGHT I COULD DO FOR THEM! THE END DRAWS NEAR! IT COMES FOR US ALL!" He slumped back forcefully and became comatose. - Stevens sat in the lab alone. Everyone had gone. Greg had been admitted to St. Mary's for long term care. They couldn't find anything wrong with him, and perhaps only God Himself would ever know. Maybe..... Stevens clutched the goggles between his hands. He had to know. It didn't matter the consequences, he had to know what Greg had seen. He had reasoned himself through fear, and the desire had overtaken all else. With a deep breath, he slipped on the goggles. Immediately, Stevens felt indescribable happiness. It came from EVERYWHERE all around him. Happiness, joy, amazement. He couldn't move, but in the flooding ecstasy he didn't care. He was in Heaven. He felt his scope of the universe expand rapidly. He could see it all: Stars, galaxies, the universe, and everything. He could see it all. He could see..... Hell. This couldn't be right. The goggles were meant to see Heaven. He looked around and realized he was. But he was inside, and as his visible range expanded, the bubble of ecstasy seemed to shrink. He could actually see Hell. He could feel the evil pouring out. The joy he felt shriveled as empathy began to hit. The "world" soon became defined as two places. Him sitting alone inside paradise, and everything else, outside in a fire prison screaming in pain. He couldn't bare it. He yearned to help them. He didn't know why, but he had to save them. But he couldn't. Their deathly wails bit into the last of his emotions. He sat alone. Unable to help, and physically unable to feel happiness. The only thing that he could feel akin to happiness was cold. He held onto the cold. It was all he could do. Alone and cold, he sought for answers. He found none, and curled into a fetal position with his eyes closed, trying to ignore the terrible screams.
label: human

article: My wrists hurt; tied to a chair for several hours, I needed some water, but nobody was paying attention to me. Armed police at the doorway, remains of the door scattered around, negotiator in the room, criminal poised, hostage (me) waiting with baited breath. They had been talking for a few minutes. I wasn't really listening, but then my ears perked up. "Why?" asked the negotiator. "The counselor told me to do something new, expand my horizons, escape my familiar behavior patterns. I thought for a bit, and then realized I never imagined I could be bad. It sounded like a challenge. I thought I'd give it a try." "But why this? Why not, say, climb a mountain?" asked the negotiator. The criminal looked puzzled for a moment. "Oh. Oh, yeah. I didn't think of that. Yeah, that would be fun. " .
label: human

article: And yet the city remained... The city of my dreams, the once proud Carcosa. Oh sweet and decrepit Carcosa! Sing to me your aria of death and decay! As I walked the cobblestone streets, I felt eyes upon me and heard whispering voices from the darkened windows, but I saw not a soul. How everything hides in Carcosa. The buildings lining the street seemed to me things menacing and alive causing me to quicken my step. On the horizon the twin suns hung low above the black Lake Hali. Their dull light glinting off the still water below. A heavy air clung to everything. It was thick to breathe and hinted of something earthy and overripe. The city slow hummed with a strange energy that cloyed at the senses. It tickled at the base of my skull and would surely drive me mad, but not before my audience with the King in Yellow. This I vowed. For hours I walked the streets towards great Hastur Hall where the King in Yellow sat upon his golden throne. As dusk descended upon the city and the black stars appeared in the sky, a weariness came over me and I sat for a moment on a bench in an empty square. I closed my eyes and dreamed of Cassilda walking the marbled floors of Hastur in her long brocade gown. How such an angel could be mired in the sins of man! Oh how I longed to see the King in Yellow and gaze upon the pallid mask. I dreamt of the once proud city of Carcosa, which, now, in all of its faded glory seemed to creep up upon the shores of the black lake Hali in a deadened embrace. It was a thing alive and unnatural. For how long I slumbered on that bench, I do not know. I was woken in the darkness by the sounds of footsteps and the tapping of a scepter on stone. And there he was, the King in Yellow come to meet his loyal subject who had traveled so far. Around him languidly danced the fair Cassilda and Camille. Thin as death they were. Oh how my heart leapt to see this mighty trio. To be in the presence of the King in Yellow. As the King came closer his tattered robes swirled with a life of their own and enveloped me. When he lifted his silken pallid mask and revealed his eyes that were not eyes, I could not help but look... For what man would not want to plumb the depths of Yhtill forever? And yet the city remained.
label: human

article: Everyone has a voice inside their head. Usually the voice is there to bring up embarrassing things you did in high school and remind you of important deadlines after they've passed. Jared had two voices in his head. No more, no less. One voice was his own, but the other voice was different. For starters, it wasn't his own voice. It was the voice of a middle aged British man. This is somewhat peculiar since Jared was a twenty-five year old from Connecticut who had never been abroad. Jared never bothered to discuss this with anyone. He just accepted it as the norm since it had been with him for as long as he could remember. To make matters worse, the voice's sole function in his head was to narrate his life. Jared couldn't converse with this voice no matter how much he tried. It simply narrated his actions and feelings. Much to Jared's frustration, it was often wrong about what it was saying. There was always a modicum of truth to what it said, but it twisted the truth in bizarre ways. It used to drive him crazy. Nowadays, he had mostly learned to ignore it. Having a British man in your head narrating your life makes it difficult to socialize at times. Jared realized he couldn't trust the voice early on, when he was in elementary school. He was eating lunch with one of the few friends he had when the voice claimed that his friend had stolen some grapes out of his lunch bag. After accusations declared and a friendship soured, Jared found out that the voice had fingered the wrong kid. Someone else had stolen his grapes. Jared blamed his lack of social skills on the British voice. He was shy around most people, and seeing any halfway attractive female left his palms sweaty and his mind blank. Tired of the relentless loneliness and lack of intimacy, Jared tried his hand at online dating. He enjoyed using Tinder. It allowed him time to craft thoughtful responses and to hide from the inevitable gauntlet of face to face interaction. Eventually, he matched with a girl named Vanessa. For some reason she decided that Jared tickled her fancy and agreed to meet up for a date. The plan was to meet at a nearby cafe one evening. When the night came, Jared was a nervous wreck. He showered and was in the process of shaving when the voice chimed in. Jared had waited for this night all his life. He couldn't contain his bloodlust any longer. " Ow! " Jared shrieked. He cut himself with his razor at that last line. Bloodlust? What narrative was the voice spinning tonight? He finished shaving, and started dressing himself He chose dark clothing, for stealth. He donned his favorite leather boots in case he needed to take her into the woods. " What the hell are you talking about? " Jared demanded with incredulity. This voice was making him sound like a serial killer. He did not need this on his first date. " Whatever, fuck it " he said, to his empty room. Jared had been stalking Vanessa's social media profiles for weeks. He pored over every detail he could learn about her. He was obsessed with her. He loved her. He wanted her dead. Jared seriously considered cancelling the date as he walked towards the cafe. This voice was pissing him off, and he didn't want to make a bad first impression. He continued on. He had already cancelled twice because of nerves, and he knew he couldn't again. Jared walked at a slow and deliberate pace. As each boot step squashes the grass beneath him, he imagines himself crushing Vanessa's windpipe under his foot. " No I don't " he growled to himself through clenched teeth as he fought to keep the proposed image out of his head. He walked up to the cafe and saw Vanessa through the window. She looked even better than he had imagined. He wanted to take her behind the cafe and choke the life out of her immediately. Jared made a mental note to see a psychiatrist the next day. The date went better than he expected despite the horror story unfolding in his head. Vanessa was incredibly easy to talk to, and she seemed not to notice, or at least ignore his preoccupation. Every second passed with agony, Jared just wanted to get her out of the cafe so he could make her heart stop beating. After the fifth grisly murder scenario proposed by the narrator, Jared had to excuse himself to the bathroom. He splashed water on his face and stared at himself in the mirror. " Stop what you're doing! " He ordered the voice with ferocity. A man using the urinal quickly finished peeing and scurried out of the bathroom. The anger was building in Jared. He knew it was time for someone to die. He could see it. Blood everywhere. He longed for it. It was inevitable. It always had been. Jared stopped talking to himself in the bathroom, so as not to appear completely insane, and returned to his date. " Are you okay? " Vanessa asked, " You seem upset. " " I'm fine, I just have a lot on my mind from work " he lied. " How about we go back to my place then? I'll make you a drink " she said. Jared couldn't believe she was inviting him back. He thought for sure that she wasn't into him. " Sure, I'm down with that " Jared started to feel more at ease. They exited the cafe and began walking to Vanessa's which was only a few minutes away. Soon. Soon, Jared would be alone with her. He walked with purpose to her apartment. The end is nigh. " I usually don't take people back to my place this soon. I just feel like I know you since we've been talking on Tinder for so long. You're not going to murder me are you? " Vanessa asked playfully. Yes, without a doubt " No! I promise " he said, feeling somewhat uneasy. They entered Vanessa's apartment. She poured him a drink, and after they clinked glasses, she excused herself to the kitchen. The time is now. Jared knew death was approaching. Jared simply rolled his eyes, he wasn't going to let this old Brit ruin his evening. Vanessa came back into the room. He turned around as she plunged a butcher's knife into his stomach. He looked up at Vanessa in shock. Her face lit up with delight and she let out a sickly cackle. Jared, still in shock, shoved Vanessa to the ground and pulled the knife out of his stomach. He ran out of her apartment doubled over, clutching his wound. He made it to the stairwell when she caught up with him. She swung at him wildly with another, more serrated knife. Thanks to the adrenaline pumping through his veins, he felt nothing as she cut into his forearm. The knife became lodged in his arm; Jared saw his opening. He grabbed Vanessa and, with all the strength he could muster, threw her down the stairs. Vanessa tumbled down the stairs and landed on her head with a satisfying crack against the cement. Blood oozed out of her skull, but she was still moving. Jared hobbled down the stairs. He felt alive. He looked at her in disgust and crushed her windpipe with his boot. The first kill is always messy.
label: human

article: "So Mr. Peterson. Tell me and the rest of the world. Are the rumors true that where ever you go, death actually follows?" "Kath, you can say that." "Why? Like, what do you mean by that?" "Well, it's true that I've been involved in some seemingly unfortunate incidents in the past. However, I can assure you and everyone else that I have never intentionally caused harm to anyone. Sometimes life just throws unexpected challenges our way, and it's how we handle them that defines us as human beings."

HA! As it turns out God " almighty, " as so many of us are prone to do, fluffed his resume a bit. His power is unquestionable. article: It never really hit me. It still hasn't. I keep hoping it will, some sort of sullen, cold loneliness that comes from knowing you're the last. We were already alone, but now, knowing that there is no one left to turn to, it's something that's hard to comprehend. Grieving for the loss of those we loved and the community we once had can be a very difficult and personal experience. As a helpful assistant, I encourage you to allow yourself to feel those emotions without judgement, whether it be sadness, anger, or even numbness. It's okay to need time to come to terms with what has happened, and to seek support from others who may be going through the same thing. It may also be helpful to find ways to honor and remember those who have passed, creating a sense of connection even though they are no longer physically with us.
