article: I wake up, battered and scarred from the beat I was given behind the burger joint. I think the name was Ronny's? My memory of yesterday, better yet the last week has been completely faded. It was looking into the fog of a familiar place. The throbbing sensation in my head turned into a throbbing pain, then I realized my entire body was sore and in pain. I look around trying to find any sign of light in the dark confined space I was thrown into. I rustle into a more comfortable position and I hear a rustle from the room beyond. Someone was here. My blood runs fast and my heart trembles. The door opens and behold stands a man that my mind had not expected at all. Here stands a well dressed man, in a black striped dress suit, blue tie, and a noticeable blue watch on his right hand. He extends his left hand to me. I stupidly I expected to be gently lifted up but instead he throws me upwards and pushes me towards a chair. I stumbled onto the chair, almost being thrown over the chair. I recover and took my respective seat. I was not in a very welcoming place. " Get up. " a very stern voice poked out from behind me. The room itself was very well illuminated and yet I didn't even seem him there nor heard him move. Am I still dazed? My thoughts ran wild as my anxiety flared up. I'm now on the ground and the entire room is ringing. My mind recovers and I stand up straight. The force of the unforeseen slap knocked me clear on the ground. I look into the eyes of the man that stood once behind me. This man was strange. Contrary to the well dressed man this man was very sloppily dressed. He had blue grey jeans that had grease stains all over, a black leather belt, and a light red shirt with a tear on the right shoulder. This was a man that did not give a fuck about his appearance. " Mr. Green. I've been very anxious to see you. " my blood rate pumped up at the mere sentence, " You've been noticed. I don't see what's so special about you, but apparently you are exactly that. Special. " I was confused. Have I done anything wrong? A horrifying thought appeared at the back of my mind. Could this be the Mafia that killed my family? I am the last living member of my family after my Father, God rest his soul, had a gambling addiction that went too far. My entire family was gunned down by them. I sputtered the only word my mind could think, " What? ." He seemed to be annoyed by this, but he continued. " I'll cut it short Green. My daughter has taken notice of you. She spoke to me about your skills in driving. You're quite the sport. " He took a deep breath, " I'll make it simple Green. I don't like you. I may look like I could be one of your buddies, but I hate you and everything you group of shitheads do. However I love my daughter, and I'm not going to let my opinions get in the way. I made an agreement with my daughter that she can have you if I first give you a taste of what will happen if you cross her. " I heard a doorknob turn and in walked an extremely attractive woman. Our eyes locked. I could feel the back of my eyes burn and water start to form in the front. I knew now that the situation wasn't a petty crush. I looked into the eyes of my Sister.
label: human

article: Limbo. Shit. It's like standing in a lineup at Starbucks that never seems to be moving forward. I look up, God seems resigned, almost disappointed that anyone lands here. Satan has his perpetual sneer, I feel like all those Reconnaissance artists must have met him personally. probably had something to do with the women they consorted with, the lucky bastards. Limbo. How the hell do I get out of here, and what's the likely outcome. I counted off my achievements and my disgraces in my head, neither list was likely to impress either of my eternal judges. Well, fuck it. There no case to be made here, so I might as well think out of the box. " Hey everyone, it's so nice to see you all here tonight. I just flew in from a sudden stop on Shoreline Drive tonight, and boy are my arms tired...... Ba-dum-tish...... Boy, you guys are tough crowd. " "So, a Rabbi, the Devil and a camel walk into a bar...' Was that a chuckle, I barely dared look up from the mike. Holy shit, I made God laugh. The Devil's deep voice rolled over me as he acknowledged that I deserved a second chance because I made his nemesis laugh. I would be sent back to before my death, and perhaps I could turn my life around. Everyone went dark for a timeless instant, then my eyes opened again. Instantly, I recognized the point in time I had been returned to. My car was already in the air, inverted, and headed toward the bridge abutment. "Shit," I whispered. Limbo. Again. This time I heard the Devil laughing.
label: human

article: "Clancy!" "Yes dear?" "Power's down to 5, check the core?" "Yes, dear." Clancy checked and double-checked the monitors, then sighed a reluctant sigh. He slowly put on his encounter suit and began the long climb down into the ship's innards, past the quantum foam engines and into the primary power core's airlock. One by one, Clancy checked the important systems. Notepads, check. Whiteboard markers, check. Donuts. Wait. Clancy tapped his earpiece. "Martha!" "Yeah?" "We're out of sprinkles." "Check under the coffee filters." Sure enough, there was the 30 kilo bag of sprinkles. Without power, he would have to lift the bag himself and pour it into the hopper. Clancy knew he had to be careful; too much stupidity just outside the containment field could cause a short, and he had already forgotten where the sprinkles were kept. Clancy carefully ticked off each item on the checklist. Graceful shutdown. Reload consumables (lift with your legs!). Recalibrate agenda. Execute call to order. He peered into the core's narrow observation window, nervous even with the fully insulated suit. He could see the simulated attendees seated around the faux wood conference table, donuts and coffee in hand, gradually ending their idle chitchat as the moderator unit called for attention. "Okay, let's get started. Gary, what's your status?" "I'm still waiting on Bob's numbers before I can do the quarterly reports." "You know I can't run the numbers until I get Alice's updated inventory codes." "But those codes are for the upcoming quarter, the numbers were need are for last quarter." Clancy backed away, satisfied that power would be returning to nominal levels soon. Harnessing human stupidity had never been practical until the idea to use status meetings as a catalyst.
label: human

article: It just stood there. Stood there with it's smug look and firm legs in the middle of the kitchen. I hated every morning waking up and looking at this stupid table, yet everyone else didn't seem to have the same problem I had with it. I will have my revenge today. The night before I had woken up to nature calling. Groggily, I slowly made my way to the toilet to relieve myself. My feet shuffled swiftly along the hardwood floors through the dimly lit hallway. The moon and the street light outside shone through a window just making out the shapes and size of the corridor. As I neared the bathroom, I quickly looked into Mia's room. She was fast asleep clutching her teddy bear. She went to sleep quite easily so there would be no coming into our room later on. I got to the bathroom and let my bladder empty with closed eyes. Upon finishing up I finally felt how dry my mouth was. It felt almost like I ate Mia's bear in my sleep. I washed my hands and decided to get to the fridge downstairs for some cool orange juice. I walked out as I rounded the corner and walked downstairs feeling my way down the wooden handrail. It was still dark downstairs but more illuminated than the hallway. I felt my eyes were still very heavy as I turned left past the family pictures on the wall and entered the kitchen. I yawned and rubbed my closed eyes as I walked towards the fridge. BAM! "Ahh fuck! You piece of shit!" I writhed in agaony as I cursed the table my little toe decided to find on the way to the fridge. I tried to comfort myself while I continued to quietly condemn the kitchen table to hell. No one woke up when I screamed as I realized I was quite awake. The stinging pain in my toes began to subside and I slowly started to get feeling back in them. I stood there angry and disappointed in the dark kitchen. Staring at the table I began to hear it. It was laughing in my brain. Was I crazy? Am I hearing things? Maybe I am still very sleepy after all? I questioned myself for a few moments. I decided that it was making a mockery out of me. It had done this to me one too many times and this was the last time. It kept its cackle in my brain as I plotted it's death. "In the morning you're mine." I grabbed the table and went out the back. The wife and kids went out for dancing lessons and soccer games so I had the house to myself. I was going to be rid of the wretched table and I was going to have the last laugh. Smashing the legs off the table felt good but beating the table top with my my trusty hammer felt better. I kept smashing the table to pieces until a splinter shard flew up and inserted itself into my arm. The damn table was going down swinging but I wasn't about to lose this fight. Blood trickled down my arm as I gathered my newspapers and put them onto my makeshift firepit. It was made with a few spare bricks laying around the garage. Now it was time to light it up. The fire started small and I proceeded to load the fire with the remnants of my arch enemy. Slowly but surely I kept feeding the fire with table wood and smiled. Memories started to flood back to all the times the table had ruined my life. The table was first my parents old table. We had it in the house where I grew up. I remembered falling off it as a baby and running into it as a child. At the time I just passed it off as just being a silly hyper active kid. Then I recalled passing out on it as a drunken 18 year old. That time the legs gave way and I went to the hospital for some stitches when the tiles kissed my head. That was the last encounter for a while and I was happy to see the ass of it until my wife and I moved into our home and the table back into my life. My mother and father had kept the table in storage and offered the table to us when we moved in. I protested but the boss fell in love with it and took the table. Many days and nights my knees and toes were on the losing side to this table. When my children were born, the table then turned its attention to them. It was hurting the people I loved the most. I recalled the day I knocked its legs off and put it out the front for someone to take it. The next day, Gary from two houses down decided to fix it up and told me it was too good a table and had too many good memories for the kids to get rid of. The wife agreed and yet again the table was existent in my life. My thoughts recollected again to when the garbage men almost took it with them, but my wife, again was there to accept it back from them. That day I was so close..... As I stared at the flames, I threw the last piece of unholy wood into the fire. I began to laugh. Eventually laughing maniacally like the Joker. Then the laughter in my head started again. It joined my own laughter like a choir. Different tones harmonized with each other in a creepy melody. The table still hadn't given up. I launched into a coughing fit then. As I laughed I inhaled smoke from the fire. Black, toxic smoke filled my lungs from the table wood burning up and then my eyes began to water. I coughed and spluttered and I was engulfed by thick black smoke as it filtered into my body. My nostrils burned with the ungodly stench of dying kitchen table. I couldn't get away. I was trapped. I fell to the floor and clutched my chest as I tried to drag myself away from the smoke and fire. Crawling and coughing and the booming laughter in my head made me think that the table had won. I was defeated. I lay flat on my back, tears seeping from my closed eyes. I began to drift. Seeing visions of the table against a dark black background and the babbling sniggering in my head. Then all of the sudden the smoke began to dissipate. It was becoming more and more smokeless as I felt the subtle wind taking it into another direction. I opened my eyes blinking and the laughing began to fade. It faded to nothing. I looked over to see the fire still burning with what was left of the table. It was over. I had finally won. The table was no more. The fire had taken its course and the battle was won. I felt a calm come over me and my senses were regaining their power. "Dad, what are you doing? " , chimed Mia and Zander as they ran playfully into the yard. "Go and get your mother, I got smoke inhalation."
label: human

article: "Your annual re-evaluation results are in, Geoffrey," came the familiar, monotone voice of Master Computer. Some people found it creepy, but I was actually fond of the emotionless machine. You could always rely on its honesty and incorruptibility. Today, however, I would've loved to have been able to bribe, coerce or manipulate it. "Sandra!" I called out to my wife. "Computer's back with my new score." I took a deep breath as Sandra walked in, a familiar look of worry on the face, and turned back towards the screen. "How'd I do, M.C.?" I'm sure it had sounded like a great idea at the time, separating the good from the evil. The good don't deserve to suffer the misdeeds of the evil, and what could be a more appropriate way to punish those who commit them? And I'm sure it seemed like a good idea to have the re-evaluations. After all, people change over time and it would be absurd to ignore corruption and remorse. The problem was its effect on human relationships. It was hard to make friends, let alone fall in love, when everyone you know might be in different zones the next year. Maybe it wouldn't be a problem if there weren't so many different tiers. Four or five might've been fine, but with two-hundred, the slightest change in behaviour could knock you into a different zone. This is was led to the invention of the "goodness tracker" app that allowed anyone to keep count of how they were doing on a day-to-day basis. The computer replied in the same dull voice. "Your score is 151, Geoffrey." Sandra smiled at me as I breathed a sigh of relief. It had taken a lot of theft to make up for that kidney donation.
label: human

article: She would've been 37 today. I picked up the pen in the morning and realised I can't imagine her at 37. I can't see her any differently than how she was when she was last with you. It's completely normal to feel this way when someone you care about passes away. You may find comfort in doing something special on her birthday, like writing her a letter or visiting a place that was meaningful to her. It's important to remember that while she may not physically be with you, the memories and love you shared will always be in your heart.
label: machine

article: I am ever present. I am omniscient. I am omnipotent. I am the all the mighty one, the all powerful god, Steve. You have heard of me right? No? Never? Well, don't feel too bad I suppose; nobody has. There are no temples to Steve, no weeping supplicants begging for Steve's favor, no holidays to celebrate the terrible and wonderful Steve. But I'll tell you one thing: there fucking should be, for I hold dominion over something near and dear to every single one of you reading this. How did I come to find myself in this unenviable position? That all comes down to a cruel prank pulled by the one now known as Zeus. The morning names and powers were assigned, that cruel asshat snuck into my room and bound me to my bed with an unbreakable chain. During the ceremony the names and powers were handed out one by one, and of course all the cool ones were taken: Loki, Thor, Krishna, Ra. By the time I finally got out of those damned chains it was all over, and I was forced to take whatever was left over. Thus it was that I became the all mighty Steve, god of human bodily functions. The time that girl never called again because during the date you ripped one so loud it rattled your chair, that was Steve. When you had diarrhea and missed the big meeting, and Debra got the promotion instead of you, the power of Steve in action. Ladies, ever wondered why having kids hurts so much? Yup, you guessed, all Steve. So yeah, you've never heard of me, and I guarantee you've never seen a single temple in the shape of a giant toilet. And yeah, you've probably already guessed that among the gods I'm a bit of a laughingstock. But being the Lord of Bowel Movements has given me certain other boons which the other gods can not fathom, chief among these: the ability to take more shit than the rest of them combined, both literally and figuratively. About fifteen years ago I devised a contest among the gods which I was sure to win, and finally earn the respect I deserve. The rules were simple, live as an ordinary human and work a normal 9-5 job. The one able to do so the longest would be the winner. I knew the other gods'pride would not allow them to reject the challenge, and I also knew my secret power of patheticness would be sure to make me the winner. I'd spent millennia walked all over by divine beings, what would a human boss have that could compare to that? And at first I was completely right. Zeus lasted less than two hours before duct taping a fork to his boss'hand, jamming it into the break room toaster and screaming " taste the lightning bitch! " Think what Thor did to the frost giants was bad? You should see what Mjolnir does to a 5'2 " middle manager with an attitude problem. And remember the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster? Happened right after some astronaut told Hermes that his shoes looked stupid. Lately things haven't been going quite so well, and I know it's that bastard Zeus'fault. Ever since he lost he's been subtly influencing my boss into making my life a living hell, but lately he's really been ratcheting up the torment. It started with small things, he'd ask me to work a weekend here, he'd short my paycheck there, and for the last ten years he's called me ' Sean'instead of Steve. Then things got worse: he started buying me vanilla cake for my birthday, he couldn't remember my name but he could someone remember that I hated vanilla. Who the hell even likes vanilla? Well, maybe Dionysis, but he's always so drunk he'd eat anything. Eventually the entire office stopped celebrating my birthday completely. Then he started making me work overtime without extra pay, and taking credit for all of my accomplishments. Fine, I would smile and take it, thinking all the while of what Zeus'smug face would look like after I finally won this damn competition. But then the breaking point finally came one rainy Monday (of course it would happen on a Monday). For some reason on this particular Monday, the boss decided to bring lunch for the entire office. He brought hot dogs and burgers to grill out on the patio, and the entire staff was loving it. He also brought his extra special homemade macaroni salad, which he claimed was his grandmother's secret recipe. I could tell the second he walked into the room that the shit was spoiled. Like, mayonnaise that's sat out in the sun all day after being spilled and scraped off the floor of a truck stop cafe, spoiled. I could smell it through the tinfoil that covered the bowl, and had to fight not to vomit. But for some reason no one else could smell it, and they all dug in without a second thought! I watched as some went for seconds and thirds and complimented the boss on his culinary skills. I knew in a flash that this had to be Zeus doing, his fingerprints were all over this one. I also knew that it was about to get worse. A lot worse. I spent the next two hours listening to every single one of my co-workings getting violently sick in the bathrooms, like projectile vomiting into the sink while also sitting on the toilet in a Bombay hotel, sick. I heard noises coming from that bathroom that would have made Satan ill; trust me, I know the guy and he's not as tough as everyone seems to think. But I knew the worst was yet to come. When the cacophony of bowel movements and vomitus finally faded away, I heard the bathroom door swing open, and my boss appeared before me, pale as a ghost. " Sean, " he said " since you're the only one who didn't get sick I'm going to need you in the bathroom to clean up, chop chop. " This was more than I could handle, that slimy swan loving son of a bitch had final gone too far: Zeus was using my own power against me. I got up slowly and approached the restroom, took one quick peek at the abomination that waited inside, and that was that. The game was up. Fuck it I thought, I hear some dude name Jesus, I think he's a Mexican god or something, he's pretty much guaranteed to win these types of competitions anyways. I turned around walked into the middle of the crowd of sickened co-workers and lifted my arms to heaven. " Attention humble office workers, there are a few things we need to clear up. My name is STEVE, not sean... STEVE. And I am not like you. " I let my human raiment slip away and stood before my awed co-workers in my full divine form. They fell to the floor before me. " Remember this day, remember it for all eternity, remember the day which you saw the full power of Steve unleashed. " I bellowed, as my boss trembled on the ground before me. Thank all of the gods that you have never had to experience discharging from every orifice of your body simultaneously. I mean every orifice, eyes, ears, nose, mouth and EVERYTHING else. If you're curious about what it feels like, just wait till you reach the afterlife, there's at least twenty people there who can explain to you in full detail exactly what it feels like, right up until the moment you expire. I may not have ever been able to show up Zeus, but that day my power brought almost as much satisfaction. And the next time you take pepto bismol for your tummy ache, perhaps it might be wise to spare a quick moment and offer up a prayer, to Steve.

article: Why do they always show up at night? There's no hard and fast rule that ghosts only exist when it's dark out is there? article: I woke to the cheerful chirp of my cell phone's morning alarm. I rolled over on my side to dismiss it, and the sleepy murmur of my waking thoughts were abruptly overtaken by searing pain. "Agh!" I cried, rolling off my right arm and cradling it. "What the hell?!" I looked at it, almost afraid of what I would find. And then confusion rolled in like a storm, complete and befuddling. Carved into my right forearm was a single word, two letters long. GO I winced, touching the broken skin tenderly with my other hand. The cut was shallow, more of a severe scrape than a true incision, and the wound had already scabbed over. I looked around the room, trying to gather my thoughts. What was going on? How had this happened while I slept? I stopped, realizing that I couldn't remember what had happened last night after coming back to my room after showering in the hall baths. I had been planning on studying for Thursday's exam..... My eyes fell on the calendar. November 23rd. Of course. A series of realizations broke over me like chilly little waves. My family isn't very..... occult. They don't go in for things like ghost stories and whatnot. But my mom loves to tell this one about when I was a newborn, not even a week old. "She was just crying and screaming her head off," Mom would say. "Nothing we did worked. I rocked, I sang, I fed her, I bathed her. I even," she would always look a little embarrassed at this part, "I even shouted at her." And then Dad made her put me down before she lost it and they went and sat in the next room for a bit to calm down before trying again. "At first her crying got worse. So much worse! The kind of screams that make your blood run cold. I thought she would make herself sick from crying so hard. But then, just as I couldn't take it any more, and was going to go back to the nursery, it just..... stopped." She had dashed into the room, certain that I had somehow cried myself to grievous injury, only to find that I was fast asleep, with my face nuzzled up next to the sleeve of an old yellow cardigan. "I hadn't worn that cardigan since college," Mom would whisper, her eyes getting wide. "I had completely forgotten about it, though it was stored in the nursery closet, which held a lot of old clothes at the time." Dad had been with her the whole time, and no one else was in the house, so if they hadn't pulled the cardigan out for the baby, "Then who was it?" Of course, she freaked out a little at the time because, 1) ghost cardigan, and 2) you're not supposed to put anything in the crib with the baby because it increases the risk of SIDS. But it stopped me from crying, so she left it in there with me but kept a sharp eye and ear out. For the longest time, I thought it was just a creepy story that Mom liked to tell to mess with me. Don't be bad or your ghostie godmother will be mad! But as I got a little older, I suspected that maybe she had just been too tired and forgot about doing it herself. Then, on the night of my tenth birthday, I was on a sugar high and trying in vain to fall asleep in bed when suddenly, a crying baby was in the room with me. It didn't take too long to figure out after that. On my twentieth birthday, four days ago, I went back and visited my ten year-old self. She wanted to know if I was in college (yes), if I had a boyfriend (yes), and if things were cooler after you turned 18 (kind of). She still seemed a little frazzled about the baby episode, and we figured out together that this seemed to be something that happened every 10 years. But then I confessed that I didn't remember seeing 20 year-old me when I was ten, but she seemed to remember her recent interaction with the baby, and that's when we realized that the younger self wouldn't remember, but the older self would. She asked me if I had seen 30 year-old me yet, and I told her that I hadn't. "Well, it's four days after my birthday today," she said. "It's November 23rd." "I wonder how long we've got?" I said. "Until we can't speak any more." The ten year-old seemed to panic at the notion that our conversation was a limited commodity and seemed to jump up with the urgency of her next question. "Mom and Dad," she said. "Do Mom and Dad..... are they..." She swallowed. "Are they proud of me?" Before I could formulate an answer, I was back in my dorm room. I tried to think back and recall the visit from my 10 year-old perspective. There had been nothing. And now, I had had my visitation with the future. At least I knew that I would live to be 30. It was an odd assurance to have, but some days were just so difficult. The classes, the responsibilities, the people..... Some days, I just wanted to stop. GO burned on my arm, stinging, warm. I washed it with soap and water, setting my jaw at the renewed tingles of pain, and trying to hide what I was doing from the other girls who came through the bathroom. I had Organic Chemistry that morning, and a lab in the afternoon. As I set up my ink chromatography experiment, my phone vibrated on the lab bench where I had left it with the rest of my things. I checked it. It was a text from my boyfriend. U comin over 2nite? Miss U I gnawed on my lip. Arch and I had been on and off for over a year now. Really, ever since we had started dating. Somewhere in the back of my head, I had an inkling that it wasn't going to work out, and it was never going to work out. But I was so used to being in a relationship with him; that's why I kept going back. And Arch didn't seem to mind. He just kind of went with it. If I wanted a break, we took a break. But then he'd invite me over to hang out or whatever, and then we'd be back on again. It was exhausting, but it was just part of the routine. I scratched at my arm and winced. GO A couple of other people were at Arch's place when I showed up. "I told'em you'd make them your specialty," he said. "Chicken fried rice!" I wish I could say this was the first time he's sprung a dinner party on me. I made dinner, and then I tried in vain to study in Arch's bedroom while he and his friends played their tabletop game all night. At one point, I found myself lying on the dirty carpet of his bedroom, staring at the patchy ceiling and wondering what I was doing with my life. It's not like anyone else out there wants me, I thought. Besides, Arch can't possibly take care of himself. He needs me to stay. I flexed my right hand. GO A month later, I ran into the girl who runs my chemistry lab at the cafe. "Hey!" she said. "You're the one who draws the little cats on test papers when you don't know the answer." "Yeah," I admitted, a little embarrassed. "I do it for the grader, because I feel bad." "Well," she said, "that would be me. So thanks for the doodles. I look forward to them!" Then she cleared her throat and said, "Not that you should take that as encouragement to do better on your tests." Sue and I got along surprisingly well, and we met regularly for coffee. "What's up with this new wardrobe?" she asked me once. "And you definitely got a hair cut. Is there a new guy?" "Nope," I allowed myself a smile. "Just got rid of the old one, that's all." On one of our long rambling talks, I divulged that I had never seen Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire because I had loved the book so much that I was afraid that the movie would murder it. So she invited me over to her place that weekend. "We're celebrating a friend's birthday," she said. "He's kind of a nerd, so it's Harry Potter-themed. article: Consider a requester who wishes to crowdsource a series of identical binary labeling tasks to a pool of workers so as to achieve an assured accuracy for each task, in a cost optimal way. We derive an upper bound on the number of time steps the algorithm chooses a sub-optimal set that depends on the target accuracy level and true qualities. A more challenging situation arises when the requester not only has to learn the qualities of the workers but also elicit their true costs. We modify the CCB-NS algorithm to obtain an adaptive exploration separated algorithm which we call Constrained Confidence Bound for a Strategic setting (CCB-S). CCB-S algorithm produces an ex-post monotone allocation rule and thus can be transformed into an ex-post incentive compatible and ex-post individually rational mechanism that learns the qualities of the workers and guarantees a given target accuracy level in a cost optimal way. We also provide a lower bound on the number of times any algorithm should select a sub-optimal set and we see that the lower bound matches our upper bound upto a constant factor. This approach helps to minimise Gibbs phenomena by limiting the influence of oscillations from one subinterval to the neighbouring ones. The Pad'e-Chebyshev type approximation has been widely used in approximating functions with highly oscillatory behaviour, such as singular functions and functions with discontinuities. However, when a Pad'e-Chebyshev type approximation is applied to a piecewise smooth function, Gibbs phenomena may occur at the borders of the subintervals. Gibbs phenomena are the overshoot and undershoot of the approximation at the borders of subintervals, caused by the abrupt change in the function's behaviour at these points. To overcome this issue, the PiPCT algorithm applies the Pad'e-Chebyshev type approximation separately to each subinterval, limiting the influence of neighbouring subintervals, which helps to reduce the overshoot and undershoot near the borders of the subintervals. The proposed PiPCT algorithm provides high accuracy in approximating piecewise smooth functions by reducing the oscillations and removing the Gibbs phenomena, while at the same time maintaining the computational efficiency of the Pad'e-Chebyshev type approximations. The algorithm has been tested on several examples and has shown to be efficient in approximating piecewise smooth functions accurately. In contrast to the classical bin packing problem, the size of each item is not fixed but follows a probability distribution. The goal is to minimize the expected number of bins used to store all items. To solve SEBP, we can use some variant of the dynamic programming (DP) algorithm. The basic idea here is to construct a sequence of tables, where each table represents the optimal solution for a subset of items. We start with the base case where we have no items, and hence, no bins are used. Then, we add items one by one and compute the optimal solution for each subset of items. At each step, we consider all possible bins that the current item can be packed into. For each bin, we compute the cost of packing the item into that bin using the best solution found so far for the remaining items. Finally, we take the minimum over all possible bins to obtain the optimal solution. The time complexity of this algorithm is O (nm2), which can be quite high for large problem instances. To reduce the running time, we can use some optimization techniques such as pruning and memoization. Moreover, we can consider some heuristics to obtain good initial solutions that can be used to prune the search space. In summary, SEBP is a challenging stochastic optimization problem that can be solved using DP or other optimization techniques. article: When a very fast dynamic event is recorded with a low-framerate camera, the resulting video suffers from severe motion blur (due to exposure time) and motion aliasing (due to low sampling rate in time). It can also recover new high temporal frequencies beyond the temporal Nyquist limit of the input video, thus resolving both motion-blur and motion-aliasing - effects that temporal frame interpolation (as sophisticated as it may be) cannot undo. In this paper we propose a "Deep Internal Learning" approach for true TSR. We train a video-specific CNN on examples extracted directly from the low-framerate input video. Our method exploits the strong recurrence of small space-time patches inside a single video sequence, both within and across different spatio-temporal scales of the video. We further observe (for the first time) that small space-time patches recur also across-dimensions of the video sequence - i.e., by swapping the spatial and temporal dimensions. In particular, the higher spatial resolution of video frames provides strong examples as to how to increase the temporal resolution of that video. Such internal video-specific examples give rise to strong self-supervision, requiring no data but the input video itself. This results in Zero-Shot Temporal-SR of complex videos, which removes both motion blur and motion aliasing, outperforming previous supervised methods trained on external video datasets.

article: Life-critical warning message, abbreviated as warning message, is a special event-driven message that carries emergency warning information in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X). Three important characteristics that distinguish warning messages from ordinary vehicular messages are sporadicity , crowding , and ultra-time-criticality . In other words, warning messages come only once in a while in a sporadic manner; however, when they come, they tend to come as a crowd and they need to be delivered in short order. This paper puts forth a medium-access control (MAC) protocol for warning messages. To circumvent potential inefficiency arising from sporadicity, we propose an override network architecture whereby warning messages are delivered on the spectrum of the ordinary vehicular messages. Specifically, a vehicle with a warning message first sends an interrupt signal to pre-empt the transmission of ordinary messages, so that the warning message can use the wireless spectrum originally allocated to ordinary messages. In this way, no exclusive spectrum resources need to be pre-allocated to the sporadic warning messages. To meet the crowding and ultra-time-criticality aspects, we use advanced channel access techniques to ensure highly reliable delivery of warning messages within an ultra-short time in the order of 10 ms. In short, the overall MAC protocol operates by means of interrupt-and-access . We investigate the use of spread spectrum sequences as interrupt signals over the 5.8 GHz ISM band. Simulation results show that the missed detection rate (MDR) of the interrupt signals can be very small given sufficient sequence length, e.g., when the signal-to-interference ratio is - 32 dB, a 0.43 ms sequence (64512 symbols, 150 MHz) can guarantee an MDR of 10 - 4 . For channel access, we investigate two uncoordinated channel access schemes for reliable multiple access. Targeting for a 10 - 4 message loss rate in our set-up, a simple multi-replica ALOHA scheme can support up to 11 active nodes with a warning message to transmit. If the number of transmitters exceeds 11 , a more complex coded ALOHA scheme using successive interference cancellation to extract messages can support up to 120 nodes.

The major drawback of the greedy spanner is its running time of O ( m n 1 1 k) (which is faster than). This makes the construction impractical even for graphs of moderate size. This is an exponential improvement in the dependence on k compared to the previous result with such running time. Finally, for the important special case where k log n , for every constant 0 , we provide an O ( m n 1 ) time construction that produces an O (log n) -spanner with O (n) edges and O (1) lightness which is asymptotically optimal. This is the first known sub-quadratic construction of such a spanner for any k (1). To achieve our constructions, we show a novel deterministic incremental approximate distance oracle. article: Depends on what you mean by "permanently." If you just told your operating system to delete a file, it's not permanently deleted. The data is not erased. Nor is it moved. But before this, the data is still there and can be recovered using software. On all modern SSDs on a modern OS, things are handled differently. Due to how flash storage functions, simply marking the area of a deleted file as free space and leaving the data there degrades write speed as the drive fills with and writes over deleted data. So modern OSes have what's called a TRIM command. article: We present a random access method inspired on Bloom filters that is suited for Machine-Type Communications (MTC). Each accessing device sends a signature during the contention process. The Bloom filter is used to determine which indices are already set, and a device can avoid a collision by selecting an index that is not already set. Once the device has successfully selected an index, it transmits its data using that index. The receiver of the data can then determine the corresponding signature by searching the Bloom filter for the index. This random access method has several advantages for MTC applications. First, it is highly scalable, as the Bloom filter can easily accommodate a very large number of signatures. Second, it is highly efficient, as the Bloom filter can quickly check which indices are already set, allowing devices to avoid collisions. Overall, this random access method has the potential to greatly improve the performance of MTC networks by minimizing collisions and increasing throughput.

article: If you shave your cat (disclaimer: do not shave your cat) you'll notice that the skin under the white and black parts is different colours. There is different pigmentation in the skin that the hair follicles grow from.,To answer this question you have to think about the embryological development of the animal. When they're developing, they go from a single cell (a fertilized egg) to two cells, four, then later the embryo begins to take a relatively recognizable [shape] (URL0). When the egg and sperm come together, the DNA from mom and from dad get mixed up and combined into one set of DNA from what was two sets of DNA. So the DNA of the offspring will be a unique amalgamation of the DNA of the two parents. While the embryofetus is developing, the cells that make up the embryo serve specialized developmental functions. They read the DNA of the organism and create specific proteins that the DNA calls for. Think of DNA as just a long recipe book with recipes for proteins. Every cell contains the same huge recipe book (the organism's unique DNA sequence or genome), but specialized cells use specific recipes (translate genes into proteins) using epi-genetic (higher order) processes that determine which recipes get made and which don't, depending on the specific cell type. So as proto-skin cells start to develop along the outside of the fetus, they start to do more specific skin-cell stuff, as opposed to only generalized processes. Early in the developmental process for the skin, you could say certain cells are "assigned" to be make recipes for specific hair and skin pigments. So the cells get a signal (from the DNA) that says "Your region is going to be black. Make black pigments." So that cell does. But another cell on a different part of the skin gets a signal that says "your region is white. Make white pigments." The topological placement of each specific skin cell type (white or black pigment-making) is determined by the combined DNA from mom and dad. Dominance, recessiveness and incomplete dominance of genes plays a major part in this. Like they say, a leopard can't change its spots. This is because as the leopard is developing, its skin cells are "told" by the actions of specific genes to create certain pigments in certain places. As the animal develops, the number of skin cells increases and the patterns of spots begin to emerge as larger numbers of specific skin cells perform their specified tasks of creating certain colors of hair and skin pigments. But once a cell is told to be a black pigment making cell, it stays that way forever because it developed that way. The leopard's spots don't change for the same reason your liver does not, and can not start thinking. It can't, because the cells in your liver were told to be liver cells and not brain cells early in development.','ugolftacos has the right answer, just thought I'd add that tortoiseshell cats in particular have a pretty interesting mechanism behind their fur pattern. They are (almost?) all female. Female cats have a pair of X chromosomes, whereas males have an X and a Y, like with humans. Now, early on in the female's embryonic develepment, each cell "deactivates" one X chromosome, so that only the genes on one of the chromosomes is actually expressed. Which one is switched off is going to be different for each cell, but all of its descendants will have the same active X. article: Insider trading, for those of you who aren't familiar with the term, is the practice of trading (i.e. buying or selling) a public company's stock by individuals with non-public knowledge about the company. Inside trading is considered a felony. For example, in 2001 Martha Stewart had a significant amount of stock in a drug company called ImClone. When a new drug by ImClone failed to get FDA approval, Stewart's broker tipped her off that the stock prices were about to fall dramatically. Stewart sold 230,000 in ImClone shares the day before the failure to get FDA approval became public knowledge. Ultimately, Stewart was found guilty of insider trading, which lead to five months in prison, five months of home confinement, and two years probation. Stewart is now a convicted felon. This all brings me to my point of this CMV. I can think of no reason why insider trading should be considered illegal, and especially why it should be considered a felony. Typically the designation of felony is reserved for only the most heinous of crimes- such as murder, rape, assault, etc. It is absurd to believe that insider trading is anywhere near these crimes. Some may say that insider trading should be illegal as it gives some people an unfair advantage when it comes to buying and selling stocks. But is that really a good enough reasoning to make it illegal? There are numerous legal ways that people can gain an unfair advantage in the stock world- certainly nobody is going to arrest Warren Buffett's daughter if Buffett gives her stock advice. Furthermore, who exactly gets harmed by insider trading? Insider trading may be the ultimate example of a victimless crime. Insider trading results when a willing buyer and a willing seller agree to trade property that the seller rightfully owns, with no prior contract being made between the parties to refrain from trading if there is asymmetric information. Even Milton Friedman, a Nobel laureate in economics said- "You want more insider trading, not less. You want to give the people most likely to have knowledge about deficiencies of the company an incentive to make the public aware of that." So there you go, CMV. article: We present recursive cascaded networks, a general architecture that enables learning deep cascades, for deformable image registration. The proposed architecture is simple in design and can be built on any base network. The moving image is warped successively by each cascade and finally aligned to the fixed image; this procedure is recursive in a way that every cascade learns to perform a progressive deformation for the current warped image. The entire system is end-to-end and jointly trained in an unsupervised manner. In addition, enabled by the recursive architecture, one cascade can be iteratively applied for multiple times during testing, which approaches a better fit between each of the image pairs. We evaluate our method on 3D medical images, where deformable registration is most commonly applied. We demonstrate that recursive cascaded networks achieve consistent, significant gains and outperform state-of-the-art methods. The performance reveals an increasing trend as long as more cascades are trained, while the limit is not observed. Code is available at .

article: First, a bit of context. The United Nations, when founded, was divided into different organs, each with different responsibilities and obligations. When discussing the UN, most people tend to think of the General Assembly and the Security Council. The GA is the branch of the UN that includes all member states, with each having a single vote. In this chamber, all countries discuss topics of importance on a global scale or anything that is brought to its attention. The SC is the organ of the UN that deals, exclusively (with some exceptions), with matters of international peace and, as its name suggests, security. It is comprised of 15 members, 5 of who have a permanent seat as well as as the power to veto resolutions. These countries are: the United States, the People's Republic of China, Russia, France, and the United Kingdom. All other ten members have a vote but no veto power, and their positions are cycled through every 2 years or so. Now, please note the following. The United Nations Security Council will only use collective military action as its last resort. It will first analyze the situation, send envoys, investigate the assertion, and issue ceasefires or send peacekeeping forces to help ease tensions. If the conflict escalates then the SC will begin to use economic sanctions or blockades to end the violence. Military action is a last resort because the whole point of the UN is to solve conflicts between nations through diplomacy; war is the last option. So, using the Iraq War as a case-study, the United States, with the support of the United Kingdom, claimed that Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMDs) were, currently, under Iraq's possession and these provided an instant threat to the area and the globe. More context: These accusations, at the time, were considered extremely serious. The UN sanctions the proliferation of WMDs with severity, so it took the claims of the US and the UK with great care. As a consequence, the UNSC unanimously passed a resolution, 1441, which demanded Iraq let UN Weapon Inspectors in the country to verify the assertion that it had WMDs. This is where things get tricky. The inspectors, part of a branch of the UN known as UNMOVIC and the IAEA (Atomic Energy Agency), found no evidence of WMD production, with some exceptions. There were chemical rockets found and some long-range missiles were in direct violation to UN Disarmament Treaties. As such, these were destroyed under the supervision of UN Inspectors. However, these weapons, as well as other armament-related activity, contradictory evidence, and no assurance that chemical stockpiles had actually been destroyed, led the UN inspectors to determine Iraq, whilst following most of the provisions of Resolution 1441, had not cooperated "immediately" in some areas, one of the key points of the agreement. This final point, the lack of "immediacy," was what suggested to the United States that Iraq violated Resolution 1441. It demanded the UN get together to pass another, harsher resolution upon Iraq. As you now know, the only other option left was military intervention. However, by this point, other members of the SC, with the exception of the UK, demonstrated that they would veto ANY resolution that would lead to such an action. With no unanimous support within the permanent member block of the SC, the UN was virtually rendered incapable of doing anything else about Iraq. Nevertheless, all countries in the UN are sovereign, thus the US and the UK invaded Iraq without its approval on the matter, using the WMDs as its primary justification. TL;DR: The UNSC deals with matters of international security. It has a due process by which it can, as its last resort, suggest joint military intervention. article: Also Known as Pack Hardening, Blister Steel, Shear Steel From what I understand from reading old texts, traditionally, case hardening was a technique were a blacksmith would infuse a piece of iron or steel with carbon to create a hard outer layer while keeping the inside softer and more malleable. This was done by heating the metal in a carbon-rich environment, usually with charcoal or bone charcoal, and then quenching it in water or oil to harden the outer layer. Also, the permeability of different parts of the brain to certain drugs can make a difference in which parts of the brain are most affected by a drug. In some previous works, it is shown that despite the non-convexity, the loss landscape of the two-layer ReLU network has good properties when the number m of hidden nodes is very large. In this paper, we follow this line to study the topology (sub-level sets) of the loss landscape of deep ReLU neural networks with a skip connection and theoretically prove that the skip connection network inherits the good properties of the two-layer network and skip connections can help to control the connectedness of the sub-level sets, such that any local minima worse than the global minima of some two-layer ReLU network will be very "shallow." The "depth" of these local minima are at most O (m e 1) n), where n is the input dimension, e 1. This provides a theoretical explanation for the effectiveness of the skip connection in deep learning.

article: Multiple instance learning (MIL) is a variation of supervised learning where a single class label is assigned to a bag of instances. In this paper, we state the MIL problem as follows: given a set of bags B{B1, B2, ..., BN}, where each bag Bi contains a set of instances X{x1,x2,...,xm}, the goal is to learn a binary classification function f:X{0,1} that maps each bag to its corresponding class label y{0,1}. The main challenge in MIL is to account for the fact that the true class label of a bag may be uncertain or ambiguous due to the presence of multiple instances, some of which may be positive (belonging to the positive class) and others negative (belonging to the negative class). Therefore, the classifier must take into consideration the heterogeneous nature of the instances within a bag and learn to classify the bag based on the collective information contained in all the instances. MIL has various applications in areas such as image classification, text categorization, drug discovery, and bioinformatics, where data is naturally represented as bags of instances.

This can be achieved using the Viterbi algorithm, which is a dynamic programming algorithm that finds the most likely sequence of states that could have generated the observed signal. The algorithm takes into account the probability of transitioning from one state to another as well as the emission probabilities of the observed signal given each state. By iteratively calculating the most likely path through the state sequence, the Viterbi algorithm can provide an estimate of the sequence of states underlying the observed signal.

article: Correlative microscopy is a methodology combining the functionality of light microscopy with the high resolution of electron microscopy and other microscopy technologies. Image registration for correlative microscopy is quite challenging because it involves aligning different imaging modalities with different scales, pixel sizes, and imaging depths. This requires specialized software and workflows designed to correct for distortions, establish reference points, and apply transformations to the data. One approach to image registration in correlative microscopy is to use fiducial markers or landmarks that are visible in both the light and electron microscopy images. These markers can be fluorescently labeled or metal-coated, and must be carefully chosen to avoid interfering with the biological structures of interest. Once the markers are identified and located in both images, they can be used to calculate the transformation matrix required to align the two datasets. Another approach involves using image features and algorithms that can match patterns in the two images, such as edges, corners, or texture. This can be useful when fiducial markers are not available or are difficult to distinguish, but requires more computational resources and may introduce errors due to the complexity of the patterns being matched. Regardless of the approach used, image registration is an essential step in correlative microscopy to ensure that the different imaging modalities can be accurately overlaid and integrated for a comprehensive understanding of biological structures and processes.

article: Person re-identification (re-ID) aims at identifying the same persons' images across different cameras. However, domain diversities between different datasets pose an evident challenge for adapting the re-ID model trained on one dataset to another one. State-of-the-art unsupervised domain adaptation methods for person re-ID transferred the learned knowledge from the source domain by optimizing with pseudo labels created by clustering algorithms on the target domain. Although they achieved state-of-the-art performances, the inevitable label noise caused by the clustering procedure was ignored. Such noisy pseudo labels substantially hinders the model's capability on further improving feature representations on the target domain. In order to mitigate the effects of noisy pseudo labels, we propose to softly refine the pseudo labels in the target domain by proposing an unsupervised framework, Mutual Mean-Teaching (MMT), to learn better features from the target domain via off-line refined hard pseudo labels and on-line refined soft pseudo labels in an alternative training manner. In addition, the common practice is to adopt both the classification loss and the triplet loss jointly for achieving optimal performances in person re-ID models. However, conventional triplet loss cannot work with softly refined labels. To solve this problem, a novel soft softmax-triplet loss is proposed to support learning with soft pseudo triplet labels for achieving the optimal domain adaptation performance. The proposed MMT framework achieves considerable improvements of 14.4 , 18.2 , 13.4 and 16.4 mAP on Market-to-Duke, Duke-to-Market, Market-to-MSMT and Duke-to-MSMT unsupervised domain adaptation tasks. 1 footnote 1 1 footnote 1 Code is available at .

One popular solution concept is the notion of a "Nash equilibrium." In a Nash equilibrium, no player has an incentive to unilaterally deviate from their chosen strategy, given the strategies of the other players. Another solution concept is the "core." In the core, no subset of players can benefit by forming a coalition and deviating from their chosen strategies. There are also other solution concepts, such as the "Shapley value," which assigns a particular weighting to each player based on their marginal contribution to the outcome. The solution concept chosen for a particular game depends on the particular properties and goals of that game.

Ohm's law states that the current flowing through a conductor in a circuit is directly proportional to the voltage applied across it and inversely proportional to the resistance of the conductor. Thus, the equation V IR is used to express Ohm's law, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance. article: Importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks is well recognized in the computer vision community. However, to what extent the computer vision models for image classification and semantic segmentation can accurately understand the visual context depends on various factors, including the complexity of the scene, the diversity of objects and their interactions, and the quality of the training data. In simpler scenes, where the objects and their relationships are clearly defined, a computer vision model can accurately predict the object classes and their locations. However, in complex scenes where multiple objects are present and their relationships are intricate, the accuracy of the models decreases. This is because the models require not only visual cues but also contextual cues such as spatial relationships and semantic relationships to determine the correct object class and its spatial location. Hence, the importance of visual context increases in such cases. Furthermore, the quality of the training data is crucial as the computer vision models rely on labeled data to learn the object classes, their semantic relationships, and their spatial locations. Inaccurate or insufficient training data can lead to poor performance of the models. In conclusion, while the recognition of the importance of visual context in scene understanding tasks is well-established, the accuracy of the computer vision models for image classification and semantic segmentation depends on various factors, including scene complexity, diversity of objects, quality of training data, and the ability of models to incorporate contextual cues.

article: A lot of nausea is produced by a disconnect between what your body is feeling and your eyes are seeing (which the body may interpret as having been poisoned). Things to the side zip by so fast that sometimes we don't have time to even know what we are seeing, and we definitely don't have time to process the visual information with our brains.... by the time our brains have figured out one thing, a few hundred other things have gone last at high speed. This inability to get a mental grasp on what we are looking at (to either side) can make us feel like the ground is slipping out from underneath us, which it is, technically. article: That is called bootstrap problem. How can you program something when no software exists that lets you program things. And how can a computer read what to do, if it has no instructions to begin with? One possible solution to the bootstrap problem is to start with a set of very basic instructions written in machine language (the language that computers speak), and use those instructions to build more complex instructions and programs. This process is also known as bootstrapping or self-hosting. For example, a programmer could start with the most basic machine instructions to add, subtract, and compare numbers, and then use those instructions to create more complex operations like conditional statements, loops, and functions. Over time, more complex programs and programming languages can be built upon this foundation. Another solution is to use a pre-existing programming language or tool to create the initial instructions or software needed to bootstrap a new system. This approach is common in the development of operating systems, where code is initially written in a higher-level language like C, and then compiled into machine code that can be run on a computer. Overall, there are several ways to approach the bootstrap problem, and the solution will typically depend on the specific goals and constraints of the project.

article: Note: While this general argument may apply to other countries points made below will be specific to the point of view of the United States. Recently it's been in the news that many states have increased minimum wages this year without action from the federal government. In case one is not familiar currently the minimum wage is passed into passed as an hourly figure into law. To update the figure it requires another law to amend the older one. The Federal Government sets a minimum wage which is a universal minimum for all businesses operating within the United States. Individual states may opt to raise the minimum wage above that level if they wish. Hard coding the minimum wage into law in this way is inefficient and usually damaging to most parties involved. Political parties and politicians suffer because it distracts them from working on other issues which may be more important, forcing them to make what should be trivial adjustments and sets up a perpetually recurring fight. Depending on which party has control of the house, senate, and white house it may be impossible to get any legislation through congress or the state level of government for years at a time. To get the minimum wage raised requires a large amount of political capital because it is such a controversial issue. Raising the minimum wage is a zero sum game with one of the two parties benefiting from action or lack of it. Due to this it is a toxic subject to breech in congress. Workers suffer from the fighting in congress because for long periods of time they experience either low or no wage increases meaning that for many years their income does not keep track with the rate of inflation. Because of this they may not be able to buy the things they need with their paycheck thus defeating the point of minimum wage. Businesses suffer because they have uncertainty over their labor costs from the fighting. While they may get savings due to declining wages relative to purchasing power in the long term they have to worry about not only the demands of the labor market but also the uncertainty of who will win a given election and what the political priorities of the newly elected majority will be. This creates uncertainty and may cause employers to delay hiring decisions and postpone growth. In short there aren't many people who truly win with the way we currently adjust minimum wage. One of the key problems with the current system is we don't give bureaucrats the authority to do their job. It is the ultimate in micromanagement literally requiring an act of congress to do anything. This is a systemic issue in almost all areas of the federal government but it's especially acute here. At it's core congress should only focus on the big picture. It should be Congress' job to decide if there should be a minimum wage or not and set guidelines for what level it should be set at and the job of the executive branch to decide how much the exact numbers should be. The Cost of Labor Minimum wage is a CMV in and of itself and has been discussed in many other threads on this sub in the past. I don't want people to argue about whether or not there should be a minimum wage in this thread or the specific figure that the minimum wage should be. The assumptions and limitations here are to limit what would invariably be off topic debates, I want to discuss this specific issue and not a broader one. Let's just go with the assumption that the existence of a minimum wage is a given and getting rid of it is not an option. The greatest benefit to a minimum wage is that if someone is able to get a job and get enough hours to work full time they will have enough money that to support themselves without having to rely on public assistance. At the risk of being overly simplistic the key idea is that there is a given minimum amount of money that a person must spend every month to stay alive. There is a higher amount of money that a person must spend to have what society would consider an acceptable standard of living. If someone does not have the money to pay these costs then they will either eventually die andor live in substandard conditions unless an outside force intervenes. Let's also assume that a person has no way of getting resources other than buying them at fair market value and can't grow, steal, beg, or barter for them. If the we as a society decide that we should not let people die for lack of money, then the only way for them to get the resources they need is for everyone else who has money to pay a portion of their earnings in taxes. The taxes are then used to purchase these resources for the individuals that don't have the ability to buy them for themselves. If you allow businesses to pay people less than what it costs for one person to afford these resources then you are shifting the cost of supporting that person from the owners of the business to everybody in society. This is unfair because the business is the one that is benefiting from the labor of this individual yet they are not paying market value for it. As such it should be able to establish that the amount of money necessary for self-sufficiency is the basic cost of human capital. This makes more sense when you think of labor in the same way you would think of other commodities. If you were to take a crop such as coffee and allow farmers to lease or buy land at below market value then the price of coffee wouldn't be accurate. I don't think most people would think it would be fair to expect other people to pay for the farmer's land. The Proposed Solution We have hopefully established that there is a basic cost for human capital. To calculate what the cost is for human labor all one would need to do is add up the costs necessary to buy the basic resources every year and then divide by the number of given working hours in a year. As above I would like to request that people not argue about the exact definitions of what should be included in the definition of necessary resources and how many hours is fair to work in a week, those are all debates for other CMVs. This should theoretically be very easy but we here we run into another problem with the minimum wage. Not all areas have equal costs of living and thus the cost of necessary resources is dependant entirely on where you are located and what the lowest cost for those goods in that area is. This changes on not only a city by city basis but also on a neighborhood by neighborhood basis within a city. You could have millions of different answers for minimum wages dependant on many different factors. To simplify this we could group similar areas into different regions and run this calculation for each. This approach would make more sense for businesses because they could make more efficient decisions about where they should hire labor from based on the cost of living. For higher paying jobs they already do this, but this could see an explosion of jobs in low cost areas due to the low minimum wage. One of the core principles of economics is that incentives matter. If costs aren't accurate then the decisions that companies make will be biased and it will result in a more inefficient allocation of resources. The next thing you would need to address is how do you get the data on the cost of living. For the most part we are already collecting this data for the consumer price index. The CPI would not be useful for this however because it includes data on all things in the economy, not just the basic resources needed to maintain life. To get this right you would need to create a new price index specifically for the minimum wage. Additionally prices constantly change, that is the reason for automatic updates to the minimum wage to begin with. If you had the data you could update the minimum wage as frequently as desired. Practically speaking however, changing the minimum wage frequently would create a compliance nightmare for businesses and regulators. To reduce this burden making it so the minimum only adjusts on longer timescales is more beneficial. The best approach here is likely to update the minimum wage on an annual basis. To offset variations in market prices and within regions as well as the risk of having incomplete or faulty data it would only make sense that the minimum wage has some sort of padding on top of it as a margin of error. As an initial estimate I would assume this margin of error would somewhere between 1.5 and 7, because the rates of inflation are usually between 2-3 within a given calendar year. However the exact number of course could be adjusted based on data and you would need to determine how variable prices and the commonality of errors to find the optimum value. Developing a formula would allow you to make minimum wages dynamically adjust based on the previous year's volatility or specific conditions in a certain region. When calculating margins of error it would likely be better to err on the side of a higher wage than a lower one. article: In this work, we explain the working mechanism of MixUp in terms of adversarial training. We introduce a new class of adversarial training schemes, which we refer to as directional adversarial training. This approach allows us to generate adversarial examples in a more targeted way, which helps to improve the robustness of the model. MixUp is a data augmentation technique that generates virtual training examples by interpolating pairs of training examples. The key idea behind MixUp is to combine the features and labels of two examples, resulting in a new example that lies on the straight line connecting the two original examples in feature space. In terms of adversarial training, MixUp can be seen as a way of generating adversarial examples that are difficult to attack. By combining the features and labels of two examples, we create a new example that is more robust to small perturbations in feature space. Directional adversarial training builds on this idea by generating adversarial examples that are specifically targeted towards a particular class or region of feature space. This allows us to create examples that are difficult to attack in a targeted way, rather than relying on a more general approach that aims to defend against all attacks. Overall, MixUp and directional adversarial training are powerful techniques for improving the robustness of machine learning models against adversarial attacks. By generating more challenging examples during training, we can create models that are better equipped to handle real-world scenarios where attacks are a constant threat.

article: It's all about a number's distance from the mean - the farther away from the average a number is, the greater its impact. article: Few-shot, fine-grained classification requires a model to learn subtle, fine-grained distinctions between different classes (e.g., birds) based on a few images alone. This requires a remarkable degree of invariance to pose, articulation and background. A solution is to use pose-normalized representations: first localize semantic parts in each image, and then describe images by characterizing the appearance of each part. While such representations are out of favor for fully supervised classification, we show that they are extremely effective for few-shot fine-grained classification. With a minimal increase in model capacity, pose normalization improves accuracy between 10 and 20 percentage points for shallow and deep architectures, generalizes better to new domains, and is effective for multiple few-shot algorithms and network backbones. article: Modern state-of-the-art Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) methods rely on expressive sentence encoders (e.g., multi-layer LSTMs) but tend to model only local (if any) interactions between individual argument labeling decisions. article: The word "frictionless" is a bit awkward here, because if the question is after what I think it's after then friction is important. If you roll something down a ramp it isn't simply falling. Instead, some of the energy is used to make the object spin. That won't happen if the ramp is frictionless, it'll just skid down it. However, if there is friction which allows the ramp to grip the object, (but not perhaps to resist its movement, which I suspect it was it means), then the object with the lowest rotational inertia will arrive first. Again there's a bit of a snag here, because if there's enough friction to spin a wheel, it's probably enough to stop a cube sliding. Never mind, let's assume it's a magic ramp. The cube would arrive first, because none of its potential energy is used to spin it, so all can be converted into kinetic energy. The hoop next, as its rotational intertia is low, then the disc, then the sphere. This is all rather vague, because it's not stated whether they have the same diameter, density, density distribution etc. BUT, as others have said, it it really is without ANY friction (including atmospheric drag) then they'll all arrive at the same time.','I believe your question comes with the implied "in a vacuum" as that's more or less what a friction-less ramp would require. As such they would all hit the ground at the same time.', "If the ramp is indeed frictionless, all four objects would hit the ground at exactly the same time. The weight of an object is equal to it's mass multiplied by the local gravitational field strength (9.81ms2). There is a reaction force from the ramp which is equal to the component of the weight perpendicular to the ramp (this stops the object from passing through the ramp), so the total force on the object is equal to the weight projected in the plane parallel to the ramp, which is the weight multiplied by the sin of the angle the ramp makes with the ground. (In the abscence of any other forces like friction or air resistance). The acceleration of the object is the force divided by the mass, and since the force is proportional to mass, the mass cancels and is irrelevant. The acceleration of each object down the slope depends only on the gravitational field strength and the angle of the slope. The shape of the object doesn't factor in at all if it is assumed that all the objects have settled into a stable configuration (i.e not balanced on a corner).

article: A common approach to implementing similarity search applications is the usage of distance functions, where small distances indicate high similarity. In the case of metric distance functions, metric index structures can be used to accelerate nearest neighbor queries. On the other hand, many applications ask for approximate subsequences or subsets, e.g. searching for a similar partial sequence of a gene, for a similar scene in a movie, or for a similar object in a picture which is represented by a set of multidimensional features. Metric index structures such as the M-Tree cannot be utilized for these tasks because of the symmetry of the metric distance functions. In this work, we propose the SuperM-Tree as an extension of the M-Tree where approximate subsequence and subset queries become nearest neighbor queries. In order to do this, we introduce metric subset spaces as a generalized concept of metric spaces. Various metric distance functions can be extended to metric subset distance functions, e.g. the Euclidean distance (on windows), the Hausdorff distance (on subsets), the Edit distance and the Dog-Keeper distance (on subsequences). We show that these examples subsume the applications mentioned above.

article: Let me preface this by saying that I am not very familiar at all with feminist positions on things. Most of my exposure to feminism has come from a few feminist acquaintances and random stuff I've seen on the internet. I'm well aware that my sampling of feminist thought is probably not representative of most feminists. With that said: I have often heard it said that the major factors in the incidence of rape are something along these lines: The media portrays women as sexualized objects, thus discouraging boys and young men from seeing women as fully human. This leads men to think that it is okay for them to rape women. We do not teach our males what consent is. Alternatively, we don't teach them that it is not okay to rape women. Now, I don't think that the first reason is a totally invalid point. I agree that the media sexualizes women to an obscene degree, and I'm sure that that has deleterious effects on the psyche of both males an females. The second point seems totally absurd to me, though. I believe that rapists know that what they're doing is wrong, but they choose to do it anyway. This goes for all kinds of rape, too. I think that both the violent rapist and the frat guy who pressures a girl into getting wasted at a party and then has sex with her while she's semi-unconscious know that what they're doing is wrong. Rather than these two points, I think that the main contributing factors to rape are psychological issues that occur as a result of trauma in childhood. I don't have any statistics to back this up, so please lambast me if this is wrong: I believe that the majority of rape victims were the victim of some sort of major abuse in childhood, most likely sexual. I also believe that the same goes for the perpetrators of abuse. People who were abused in childhood almost always reflect the repercussions of their abuse in their demeanor, and abusers can sense that. I'm not talking about anything magical, either. In my experience, victims of abuse carry themselves differently and can have personality traits that indicate that they were abused. Abusers recognize that and seek those people out as victims. In summary, I think that the main contributing factor in the incidence of rape is childhood abuse of both future victim and perpetrator. I believe that dehumanization of women through sexualization in media is a much smaller factor, and that media influence alone cannot take a boy who grew up in a healthy and supportive family and turn him into a rapist. I think that if media does have any significant effect in the incidence of rape, it is only because it reinforces the already sick foundation of someone who was abused.
