article: Just over eight years ago there was a solar flare as powerful as the Carrington event; it took down the power grids of many countries in the world. Many of these countries, such as the United States and the United Kingdom, used to be economic powerhouses, but the blackout of 2015 left their populaces struggling to survive in just-turned-third-world countries. The population of Great Britain is now less than twelve million, and only nine million survived these eight long, miserable years. On the second of June in the year 2023, the British government announced that finally over ninety percent of the country, including the area where the twenty-six-year-old man lived, had access to electric power. It used to be considered essential, of course - before 2015 it was essential, as the deaths of over fifty million British people and over seven hundred million people worldwide had shown - but now, as in 1900, it was considered a luxury. Rather aptly, the lights were first turned on in London on the first of May - people had begun to move back there three years earlier - and Prime Minister Williams had said that electric power would be available for all Britons by the end of July. Upon hearing the news, the twenty-six-year-old man, who had moved from the Midlands to the south west eight years ago, took out his hard drive - nearly ten years old, used for the first time in September of 2013 and for the last time, of course, on Walpurgis Night of 2015 - which he had kept safe for eight years just in case something like this happened - an anti-430, if you will - and plugged it in to an old Windows 7 computer. He didn't know why he'd kept the computer, or the hard drive for that matter - the computer had ceased to work and the hard drive had had nothing to work with starting on the night our world ended, and the man had been almost certain in those chaotic first few weeks that, if he'd been lucky enough to be buried, the tombstone would say . But that hadn't happened - he'd witnessed the deaths of his sister and his mother, the only two people he lived with, and he'd lost contact with all of his friends on the last day before the lights went out, but somehow he'd lived to see the ninth and final summer of the blackout, and the twenty-seventh and hopefully nowhere near final summer of his life. He turned the computer on, and he saw a lot of numbers. The numbers all had twelve digits and they all began with "201504"; scrolling up, he saw 201503s and 201502s. These were files, files with information eight years out of date. Some were images: "21:03 30042015," "17:08 30042015," "20:09 29042015....." mostly images of a social media website called Reddit, which had gone down when the solar storm hit on May Day morning. Of course it had been cloudy that night, where the twenty-six-year-old man lived when he was only eighteen: he never saw the aurora borealis even well above fifty degrees north, neither after the event nor before, but most nights he saw a view of stars that would seem wondrous to a person from 2014. The man had slowly got used to the thousands of stars shining brilliantly on those nights - he had wept the night the moon turned blood-red, the night of September 27th, but he had been thankful to still be alive - he had had other things to worry about during that first horrific summer, such as where to find food and clean water. During those first few months he'd seen hundreds die of hunger, thirst and water-borne diseases, but he was certain that the true British death toll was somewhere in the tens of millions. No-one had heard from David Cameron or Ed Miliband - that May morning when all of the electronic ones and zeros had been turned into plain old zeros had been only six days before a general election was due to take place, the first general election under a fixed-term Parliament. Back in the early 2010s, for the first time ever, people had been one hundred percent sure about the date of the next general election: Thursday, 7th May 2015 - that had been planned almost four years previously, but ruined less than a week before it was due to take place. Radios which had ran on grid power, along with televisions and computers, had of course ceased to work that morning just before four o'clock, but there had been no sign of the BBC or the British government on battery-powered or hand-crank radios. On Thursday the seventh, food riots had been commonplace in every major city in the country, and doubtless in many other countries as well: the man reckoned they'd started on about day five and ended in about week five. But during the last eight months of 2015 and the first three or four months of 2016 - during the winter that had been proof of Murphy's Law, with temperatures below freezing on most days from mid-November to early April - the British people didn't see any sign of a government. The number of governments in the formerly-first-world country of England had decreased from a few hundred microstates in early 2016 to one in late 2017; many of the surviving electrical engineers had worked, whenever they had been able to, to form a new National Grid; now, on this Friday evening in early summer, the twenty-six-year-old man saw light that was not from celestial bodies, the burning of oil or an open flame for the first time in more than eight years. Perhaps now, as summer once again turned to autumn, as significant seventeenth, fifty-fourth and twenty-seventh birthdays passed, as the moon turned partially red just before Hallowe'en and as 2023 turned to 2024, life could possibly return to some semblance of normality. People would never return completely to the naive lifestyle of the 2000s and the first half of the 2010s, but perhaps this dark chapter in the history of humanity could finally, after 2,954 days, be closed.

article: Journal Entry: 24th December, 2089. Tomorrow is Christmas. I miss my beloved family, and I miss you, sweet Anna. This war..... This war has gone on for too long, with no end in sight. We fight for what? We win a battle, but then lose, making no progress..... to no avail. Day in, day out, seeing death and suffering of my friends, my comrades, my brothers. I'm not sure where I am any more, nor where I'm going to be. My comrades dread the forthcoming jump. I don't blame them, it's the first time many of them have made the jump to the battle of Falegrass, in the summer of'82. They've all heard the stories, and they know that only a few us made it back. Something so tragic, something that was to be a win for the cause..... something that turned out to be a bloody massacre of women and children. Innocent people caught in the middle of a war between us..... and them. Why in the hell do we keep repeating history? Huh. Funny, that term, "History repeats itself." Such a waste. One of my boys is brand new to the squad. Jim, he's a nice fella. Always has a smile, and something witty to say. But I'm afraid that will change, and soon. Nobody keeps a youthful attitude after their first jump. If you don't die, or go insane, you come back unsure of who you are or where you're at..... Do not worry though, I am fighting my damnedest to keep my sanity. To come home to my family, and you, with my head on straight..... not ever to think of this war again. I promise you, after this jump, things will be normal..... We'll have won. And I will be home with you in my arms. I can't speak much of our mission, except that during our last jump we were able to deport an enemy agent that is ranked highly with the enemy. We've learned the location of their next jump..... and something else. Their commander is jumping this time. We're not sure why, but honestly, it frightens me to my core. Usually, our commanding officers do not go into the battles, instead constantly jumping from one instance to another, in order to keep hidden in time. Thank God we can only jump back in time..... who knows how this war would've been, being able to jump ahead to the future. I'm leaving my journal here. If I am to survive, and we win, I will return for it and erase these horrid memories. For I will not need them anymore..... My heart and my soul is with you, dearest Anna. Merry Christmas, again. I love you. Your Departed Wanderer.

article: The satisfiability problem in real closed fields is decidable. In the context of satisfiability modulo theories, the problem restricted to conjunctive sets of literals, that is, sets of polynomial constraints, is of particular importance. One of the central problems is the computation of good explanations of the unsatisfiability of such sets, i.e. obtaining a small subset of the input constraints whose conjunction is already unsatisfiable. We adapt two commonly used real quantifier elimination methods, cylindrical algebraic decomposition and virtual substitution, to provide such conflict sets and demonstrate the performance of our method in practice.

article: The ICASSP 2021 Acoustic Echo Cancellation Challenge is intended to stimulate research in the area of acoustic echo cancellation (AEC), which is an important part of speech enhancement and still a top issue in audio communication and conferencing systems. Many recent AEC studies report good performance on synthetic datasets where the train and test samples come from the same underlying distribution. However, the AEC performance often degrades significantly on real recordings. Also, most of the conventional objective metrics such as echo return loss enhancement (ERLE) and perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) do not correlate well with subjective speech quality tests in the presence of background noise and reverberation found in realistic environments. In this challenge, we open source two large datasets to train AEC models under both single talk and double talk scenarios. These datasets consist of recordings from more than 2,500 real audio devices and human speakers in real environments, as well as a synthetic dataset. We open source an online subjective test framework based on ITU-T P.808 for researchers to quickly test their results. The winners of this challenge will be selected based on the average P.808 Mean Opinion Score (MOS) achieved across all different single talk and double talk scenarios.

That problem has a name and it's survivorship bias (link below). Survivorship bias indices are available. The bed source is CRSP. 2. The health of an economy goes well beyond the performance of a simple stock index. I recommend you spend some time at URL0 or the St. Louis fed to get a better feel for the data. GDP is a standard go to. Side note. I've never been a fan of the Dow jones industrial average. This is for 2 reasons. 1. The djia consists of only 30 stocks. There are approximately 2500 non reit stocks that are of meaningful size and price that trade on a non otc exchange. Even though the U.S. Market is too heavy (a few hundred stocks represent most of the market's available market capitalization) 30 is a very poor sample. 2. The djia applies a divisor to its index, effective equal weighting the stocks. Ignoring that this is only 30 stocks, this is a problem in that equal weighting doesn't reflect the market. The market is, well, market weighted. A stock can only represent as much as is does in the market place (adjusted for free float normally). This only departs from reality when you look at a specific part of the market (like small caps). In an equally weighted scheme, small stocks can have a disproportionate impact on the performance of the index. Not reflective of reality in my opinion and it creates investing concerns on implementation. If you are looking for a good, survivorship bias free index that represents the performance of the U.S. Stock market, I recommend looking at crsp. Link below. P.s. Total market capitalization price available shares outstanding. Survivorship bias in Wikipedia: URL1 Crsp site: URL2," " Of course their performance will look good over time if you replace the poor performers, right? Only if you assume that the committee that decides on changes to the DJIA have magic future prediction abilities. And even if they did, that still wouldn't invalidate it, it would just mean everyone should use their own money to capture that value. Having performed better in the past doesn't mean they will perform better in the future.," "The DJIA is already a garbage indicator. No serious investor even bothers with it. It is total and complete bullshit. URL5 URL6 URL6 URL4 You might as well be reading tea leaves. It is simply a number that, for some reason, lay-person talking heads tell to completely uninformed consumers. It's cargo cult bullshit. No one on the street gives a fuck about it.

article: Task fatigue. The exact, molecular mechanisms of what is happening inside your brain is not completely understood but essentially the process in your brain that stops it from paying attention to other stimulus and only on the task at hand, in this case studying and not looking at Reddit, gets physically tired and looses effectiveness. The father you push this mechanism without recovery, just like a muscle, the less effective it becomes. Read more about it here: URL0', "When your brain takes the food from the blood your heart pumps around your body, it transforms it into'brain poop' as the cells in your brain (neurons) eat the food. When too much brain poop clogs up in your brain, you need to sleep so your brain can use the dreaming stage of sleep called Rapid Eye Movement (REM) to facilitate the removal of the brain poop so you have room to eat more blood food and poop it. Source: I have narcolepsy and my brain is always filled with brain poop. Also this: URL1," "So if I'm mentally tired and not physically, whats a good way to get mentally rested without sleeping?,Think of it like working out any specific muscle until it get tired and sore. If you do a whole bunch of curls on your right arm it will get tired but most of your other muscles will be OK. Using any muscle causes those cells to release stored energy causing movement of the cells and some chemical waste products that need to be flushed out. Use enough energy fast enough and it take your body time to flush out the waste and supply new energy to the muscle. The same thing happens in your brain. The more you use it the more energy it needs to consume to function. It takes time for your body to clear the waste and refill.','Reading about how my brain gets distracted from homework while I am distracted from my homework by Reddit...','It could be low dopamine or serotonin, that usually feels like a lack of motivation and is why stimulants that increase dopamine are regarded as "smart drugs.

article: In the US, there's already a [mandatory background check] (URL0) to buy a gun in a retail setting (if you buy a new or used gun from a store, you will have a background check). Further, because the federal government can regulate sales of things that cross state lines, it's illegal for two people to sell a gun privately without involving a retail store (and thus a background check) if they don't reside in the same state. There isn't a background check on private sales within most states. So when someone says, we want mandatory background checks on all gun sales, they mean they want them on private, in state gun sales. The opposition points out that we enforce the background checks on retail sales by [very strictly controlling the inventory of retailers] (URL1) (they must keep a log book of every single gun that goes through their store). Gun owners are exceedingly concerned that a similar registration of the guns they own gives the state a tool that's much too useful should it ever wish to seize the guns (since it would know where every single gun in the nation is). This is why there's opposition, the current background checks cover almost all gun sales, and there's too little trust that the means of enforcing private background checks would eventually be the means to facilitate a seizure of private guns.," "Most people that are against them aren't against them entirely for the most part people are ok with the current system of if you buy a gun at a store you get a background check. The debate is usually around whether or not the should be required for personal gun salestransfers. So if I sell you a gun that I own I would be responsible for making sure you are legally able to own a gun. People dont want that responsibility placed on them they feel it could end up hurting them,Many people see it as a slippery slope situation, and they are not wrong, either. There is an element of the gun control crowd that wants to ban all guns. That's not politically tenable right now, so they want to do it in little steps. First background checks, then broaden the prohibited categories until the background check becomes prove to us you really need a gun. So even when a gun control proposal seems reasonable, the pro-gun people will oppose it, because they have no faith it will stop at "reasonable., "Personally I can agree with having background checks in private sales in theory. However were ultimately talking about a mountain out of a molehill argument. So few gun sales would be affected by a law of this nature that it appears to me and many others to be nothing more than a power grab. As it stands you can't legally buy a firearm in any store or gunshow without a background check. I encourage you to YouTube any of the videos of ppl going undercover to try and get a gun at gun show without a check (this is where supporters of laws like to act like a loophole exists. Hint: it doesn't exist). The only firearm sales that would be affected would be private sales or transfers between citizens who are not dealers which makes up a very very small minority of gun sales. Because of how little a law mandating universal checks would actually change things, it is better to oppose what amounts to be a power grab, to prevent further grabs, than to allow the law to go through. It would be a lot better to come up with ways to help treat and prevent a mentally ill person from obtaining a firearm, or to end the root causes of most gun crime aka the war on drugs. As far as the mentally ill are concerned, no background check in the world will ever screen them out because of our medical privacy laws. There are a lot of effective ideas that can be attempted if common ground could be found but it's not likely to happen any time soon. BTW the same amount of ppl are killed yearly from drunk drivers when compared to homicides. That's not including just regular old traffic accident fatalities. And yet we give 16yo kids the ability to drive alone in most states after barely needing to prove any proficiency behind the wheel. Even ISIS has begun to realize that all they need is an automobile to inflict a mass casualty incident. That should scare everyone whole lot more. You will get into a car accident in your life, most will never hear a gun shot fired in anger and many more will never hear a gun shot at all in their lives. Let's solve problems that are real threats to the majority of ppls lives instead of focusing on red herrings given to us by those in political parties. That's just my 2cents on the matter.,Some see it as an infringement, and thus unconstitutional. Some say the constitution entitles all citizens to guns, not just those who can pass some kind of background check. Some feel if you give an inch on the gun issue, even a reasonable inch, the people they feel are "anti-gun" will push the issue down the slippery slope towards total gun confiscation.', "We already have background checks for purchasing guns. The issue surrounds private sales between individual citizens. You'll also notice that most gun owners have no issue with said background checks, but they'd like to do it themselves and have access to NICS (which is the system used to perform the background check). If individual citizens can get access to NICS, there's no record of the sale, which is what we're interested in; having a third party (which would invariably have to be the government) do it means there is a record of the sale, which would invariably have to involve the name of the buyer and the seller. That is, essentially, a gun registry, which is a big concern among gun owners.," "The background check system in Australia varies a little from state to state. But ALL states check for criminal history, mental health and domestic violence. Some also have other listed, as well as addiction, residential and physical. What they mean by those last ones, I don't know. I believe the first two are the most important. But we also have tighter laws here than the USA. For instance, even if you are fully licenced for a particular gun, you CAN NOT just sell that gun to another fully licenced person privately. ALL transactions MUST be done through a licenced dealer. ALL firearms MUST be registered, and the dealer is the one that supplies and files the paperwork with the government body.," "They are mandatory when buying from a retailer. Private sales in some states require background checks on private sales as well The big argument is that it will lead to a national gun registry, making future gun bans a possibility. They'll know who has what, and how many. The problem with increased regulations, is that they never know when to stop.,You have a few assumptions that are erroneous: People are against background checks that stop mentally unstable people from purchasing a gun - That's not true. We already have mandatory checks in place for retail purchases that include, despite claims to the contrary from gun control people, purchases over the internet and gun shows. As it's been pointed out in the other comments, people are against the requirement to conduct a background check if you have a gun of your own that you'd like to sell. Including personal transfers in the background check requirement would stop more gun crimes - The majority of gun crimes are committed either by people who have illegally obtained a gun by theft or by people who had a legal right to purchase a firearm, in which case, why would extending the reach of current checks to include personal sales have any impact on those legal purchases? Current background checks don't bar mentally unstable people from buying guns (based on your comment) - Mentally unstable people are already barred from purchasing firearms. California is a prime example of what happens when you allow gun control politicians to have an unfettered ability to enact the gun control they desire. CA counties require you to [prove you have a pressing need for a concealed carry license] (URL4). At one time, they required gun merchants to send a list of all gun purchasers to the state every month. [They imposed heavy restrictions on the purchase of ammunition] (URL5). CA bans the sale of certain rifles that [use special features on magazines] (URL5). The point is, the gun control politicians know they can't outrightly ban firearms so instead they make it as onerous as possible to own or obtain firearms, accessories, and ammunition. The rifle most gun control groups want to ban is the AR-15 even though handguns are the weapon of choice for mass shooters. Their reason for attacking the AR-15 seems to be that it looks military or scary, not that it's any more lethal than a handgun. Many groups even intentionally or unintentionally misstate that an AR-15 is capable of fully automatic fire. The accessories they try to ban have nothing to do with the lethality of the AR-15 barrel shrouds] (URL4), pistol grips, and flash suppressors. So the argument that there's a "gun show loophole" is false. The argument that the majority of mass shootings occur because there is some flaw in the background check system is false. It's not that people are against mandatory checks, which is why there are in fact mandatory checks. Rather, it's that people object to gun control politicians from trying to make it onerous for legal purchasers to purchase or own something that they have a constitutional right to own.

article: We present an improved combinatorial algorithm for the computation of equilibrium prices in the linear Arrow-Debreu model. For a market with n agents and integral utilities bounded by U, the algorithm runs in O (n 7 log 3 (n U time. This improves upon the previously best algorithm of Ye by a factor of O (n). The algorithm refines the algorithm described by Duan and Mehlhorn and improves it by a factor of O (n 3). The improvement comes from a better understanding of the iterative price adjustment process, the improved balanced flow computation for nondegenerate instances, and a novel perturbation technique for achieving nondegeneracy.

article: "You don't seem to quite understand. We're here to help you. Getting back to your families and such." The man he was speaking to had a sun-kissed complexion and chopped wood into clean halves with matching zest. He was also clean naked. We'll just have to search for those." They went to the town center, adamant in imposing their view on the locals. They took wefies with the people, tried to tell them about drones and virtual reality. "What we have is more real than any of that," they said. "So you can either integrate to our way of life, or take your fanciful gadgets and digital stuff and get out. article: The Crusades are such a weird piece of history from a high-level summary. By the Fourth Crusade it's such a clusterfuck that it doesn't seem possible. The First Crusade Byzantine Emperor: Hey Pope, got a problem over here. Turks are taking over some of my territory. Help a fellow Christian out? Pope: Well, I don't have an army, but I'll see what I can do. Crusaders: Chaaaarge! Hey, cool, we did it. Suck it, Turks. You're welcome, Byzantine Empire. Now that we're here, let's set up four small Christian nation-states before we head home. We'll call'em Crusader States. The Second Crusade Pope: Uh, guys, looks like Muslim forces took one of the Crusader States (Edessa) back. Get on that. Still God's will. FranceGermany: Right-o, we got this. [siege of Damascus] French forces: Yeah, this isn't working, the Germans fucked us over. Retreat to Jerusalem. German forces: Yeah, this isn't working, the French fucked us over. Retreat to Jerusalem. Turkish forces conquer almost all of the Crusader States, minus their capital cities. Shortly after, they join with Egyptian forces and take Jerusalem too. The Third Crusade Pope: Guys are you fucking kidding me? Things are worse than they were when we started! This is all probably God punishing you for being such shitbags. Get back down there and take Jerusalem. For realsies this time. Christ! Holy Roman EmpireEngland: Okay, we're on it. Let's try taking Tyre first. Nope, nope, run away. What about Acre? Yeah, we did it! That worked well, let's try Jaffa. Yeah, we did it! This is totally working, on to Jerusalem, boys! Wait, before that, should we try and work something peaceful out? Nah, screw that, let's publicly execute every prisoner we have. Muslim forces: Yeah you guys can fuck right off back to Europe any time now. Not cool. We're retaking Jaffa. Crusaders: Hey, you retook Jaffa, no way. Now we're retaking Jaffa. Muslim forces: This is getting ridiculous. Okay, look, we'll sign a treaty that says Jerusalem stays under our control, but pilgrims and traders are allowed to visit as long as they keep the peace. Deal? Crusaders: Fine, fine, okay. We're heading home again. Sorry Pope. The Fourth Crusade Pope: Guys. Guys. Seriously. What did I say about Jerusalem. Get your asses back down there and mete out the Lord's will! Was I unclear before that this is your sacred duty, not run-of-the-mill border disputes that got out of hand? Most of western Europe: No thanks, we're busy. Italy: Yeah, okay, I guess so. Wouldn't it be more profitable to attack Egypt than Palestine, though? We'd need a naval force to do that, though. Pope: What? No, the whole point is Jerusalem. Which is in Palestine. Italy: Uh huh. Yeah, we're building a navy to conquer Egypt. This is really expensive, though, it had better be worth it. Actually we're kind of broke now after building all these boats. Byzantine prince: What's that you say? Hey, I'll pay off your debts if you do me a favor... Italy: Oh? What favor? Byzantine prince: Take that shiny new navy to Constantinople instead and overthrow my father so I can be emperor. I'll even let the Pope control the Greek Orthodox branch of Christianity we've got going on over here. Italy: Hmm. Yeah, sure, that sounds doable. [seige of Constantinople] Italy: Ha! We overthrew your emperor. Byzantium: Power now passes to his brother. Italy: Okay great wait wait what? Oh no, that's not going to work for us. You have to make his son co-emperor. Byzantium: Uhhh why? Italy: Shut up, just do it. Former prince, time to pay up! Byzantine prince co-emperor: Yeah, about that.... I don't know if that's going to work for me. Italy: FFFFUUUU Pope: Uh, guys, what's going on over there? You know you're supposed to be fighting a religious war, right? Against the Muslims? In Jerusalem? Italy: Oh uh yeah, totally, we are. That's what we're doing. In fact, these Greeks are the enemies of God, and it is his will that we take all their stuff because Constantinople looks dope as fuck bring them under your control. [sack of Constantinople] Pope: [facepalms so hard his skull flips inside out] Epilogue No further Crusades were officially launched by popes. Every now and again a European monarch would launch a unilateral one, mostly directed at Egypt and mostly unsuccessful. And then there's the Children's Crusade, a whole new level of fuckery.,It's complicated, but the very short answer is it was about the Christian Byzantine Empire losing territory to the Muslim Seljuk Turks. The Byzantine Empire struggled with a very complicated administration framework that made military coordination difficult. You might hear people call elaboratedifficult bureaucracies "byzantine" even to this day! The Seljuk Turks exploited this weakness and expanded into Anatola (the land is now called "Turkey" so you can guess how that turned out!). The Byzantine Emperor called on the Pope in Rome to help. The Pope doesn't have an army though, so he needed to create a religious reason to ask the Catholic kingdoms of western Europe to go fight to protect Byzantium. The answer: Protect pilgrims going to the Holy Land, especially Jerusalem. The crusades included several military victories, but they are generally remembered as a failed religious war. They did irreprable harm to ChristianMuslim relations. They were oppressive of Jews, and they intensified conflicts between the Byzantine church (Orthodox) and the Roman church (Catholic). By the fourth crusade Catholic crusaders were attacking the Byzantines (who were also Christians), which severely undermined the moral authority that the crusades were supposed to be about, and also guaranteed that the Turks would conquer the rest of the Byzantine Empire.', "Political influence, money, territorry. article: This paper investigates the virtualization and optimization of a multi-cell WLAN. We consider the station (STA) -access point (AP) association and airtime control for virtualized 802.11 networks to provide service customization and fairness across multiple internet service providers (ISPs) sharing the common physical infrastructure and network capacity. More specifically, an optimization problem is formulated on the STAs' transmission probabilities to maximize the overall network throughput, while providing airtime usage guarantees for the ISPs. Subsequently, an algorithm to reach the optimal solution is developed by applying monomial approximation and geometric programming iteratively. Based on the proposed three-dimensional Markov-chain model of the enhanced distributed channel access (EDCA) protocol, the detailed implementation of the optimal transmission probability is also discussed. The accuracy of the proposed Markov-chain model and the performance of the developed association and airtime control scheme are evaluated through numerical results.

article: I believe deodorant is a societal norm and it isn't the teacher's place to tell or encourage the student to wear deodorant. article: We propose to combine the robustness merit of model-based approaches and the learning power of data-driven approaches for image restoration. Specifically, by integrating graph Laplacian regularization as a trainable module into a deep learning framework, we are less susceptible to overfitting than pure CNN-based approaches, achieving higher robustness to small dataset and cross-domain denoising. First, a sparse neighborhood graph is built from the output of a convolutional neural network (CNN). Then the image is restored by solving an unconstrained quadratic programming problem, using a corresponding graph Laplacian regularizer as a prior term. The proposed restoration pipeline is fully differentiable and hence can be end-to-end trained. Experimental results demonstrate that our work avoids overfitting given small training data. It is also endowed with strong cross-domain generalization power, outperforming the state-of-the-art approaches by remarkable margin.

article: " The Usual" "So how was work?" Genevieve asked, as she sat on the couch, munching on cheese curls and watching the latest episode of a rather interesting crime drama. She paused the recording, knowing that Aria still had yet to finish the first season. This episode contained few spoilers, but it was especially character-driven, and Aria hadn't even met half of the current cast. "The usual. Hire a guy, fire a guy," Aria answered morosely as she placed her coat on the rack by the door. "More of the latter these days." "Recessions. What can ya do, right?" Genevieve gestured to the TV. "You wan na get caught up?" "Nah." "How'bout a game?" "Sure..... What were we doing? Dragon Keep?" Aria asked, muttering the question more to herself than to Genevieve. She looked up at her wife, and asked, "Where's Tanya? I'll need someone to Res me." "Still have shit for guns, eh? She went out to get some milk; she'll be back in a few." Aria sat down next to Genevieve, and leaned against her heavily-tattooed shoulder. Genevieve reached over and pulled Aria closer, grasping the matching abstract pattern on her shoulder. Everyone in the world was born with a tattoo somewhere on their upper body usually their chest, back, or an arm and each person's tattoo matched that of their predestined soulmate. Whether they were upstanding citizens or murderous sociopaths, a pair of people with identical birth-tats were guaranteed to find happiness together. Genevieve could hear Aria's jaws grinding together, and see her brows and fists tightening in frustration. Aria's job was stressful, soulless, and generally unfulfilling, but today must have been especially awful. "Let it out, Aria." "I'm just so sick of the looks we get all the time! Everyone else can talk about'my husband' this,'my wife' that, but I can't talk about us without people just..... getting things in their heads!" Aria didn't hear a key turning in the front door lock as she continued, "I'm just so goddamn sick of everyone ogling at me! There isn't anyone in my building who can't walk into my office without watching a third-rate porno in their heads starring yours truly! I'm a fucking person and I want to be treated like one is that so fucking much to ask for?!" She felt a familiar hand clamp down on her non-tattooed shoulder, and heard Tanya's sultry voice behind her, saying, "They can dream all they want, but they'll never have the real thing." Aria felt the couch shift as Tanya leapfrogged over the back, brushing against her side as she landed. "Hey, Genny, who's that guy with Finch?" "We'll have to watch it later. Aria's still got ta catch up." "Ah. Maybe a game or two, then? Where were we..... Badass Crater?" "Dragon Keep," Aria corrected her. "Righto." Tanya gave Aria a quick kiss on the cheek before standing up. "Get the game set up. I'll get us some snacks." "I've already got cheese curls!" Genevieve said. "Cheese curls are for bitches!" article: In this article, we investigate self-organizing optimization for cognitive small cells (CSCs), which have the ability to sense the environment, learn from historical information, make intelligent decisions, and adjust their operational parameters. By exploring the inherent features, some fundamental challenges for self-organizing optimization in CSCs are presented and discussed. Specifically, the dense and random deployment of CSCs brings about some new challenges in terms of scalability and adaptation; furthermore, the uncertain, dynamic and incomplete information constraints also impose some new challenges in terms of convergence and robustness. For providing better service to the users and improving the resource utilization, four requirements for self-organizing optimization in CSCs are presented and discussed. Following the attractive fact that the decisions in game-theoretic models are exactly coincident with those in self-organizing optimization, i.e., distributed and autonomous, we establish a framework of game-theoretic solutions for self-organizing optimization in CSCs, and propose some featured game models. Specifically, their basic models are presented, some examples are discussed and future research directions are given.
